## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the proxy's own request-budget skip to use a name that
cannot be confused with an upstream rate-limit rejection, so operators and
analysis tooling stop misreading `rate_limited` as "the local model was rate
limited".

## Why

`rate_limited` is emitted by `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` when a provider
entry's configured `rate_limit_rpm` window is exhausted
(`BudgetDecision(reason="rate_limited")`). It is a **proxy-side, pre-flight
budget skip**, not an HTTP 429 from the provider — upstream 429s are logged
separately as `[remote] upstream error status=429` /
`upstream_http_error`.

The name caused a concrete misreading: `rate_limited` is 61.6% of the
fallback-reason table (6,042 events, all `from=munitoai-free`), yet it was
reported as the per-session "reason for remote fallback" for 11 of 26
sessions that had actually been diverted from local by lease contention. The
local provider has no `rate_limit_rpm` and can never emit this reason (0 of
9,683 archive occurrences are `from=local`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The budget-skip vocabulary is renamed to
  `provider_budget_exhausted`, everywhere it is emitted: the
  `BudgetDecision.reason` values in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
  (retaining the `_after_wait` / `_waiters` / `_disconnect` variants, e.g.
  `provider_budget_exhausted_after_wait`), the `reason=` text in the
  `Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=...` log lines, the
  `fallback_reason = ...` assignments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  (~9028, ~10515), **and the diagnostics attempt `status` values**
  `status="rate_limited"` / `status="rate_limited_waited"` (~9018, ~9038,
  ~10505, ~10525) -> `status="provider_budget_exhausted"` /
  `status="provider_budget_exhausted_waited"`. Producer decision
  (2026-10-25): *full rename everywhere* — no `rate_limited*` literal may
  remain in **newly emitted** code paths, tests, or current documentation.
  The analysis-skill legacy mapping (AC3) and `REFERENCE.md` deliberately
  retain the old spelling as a *historical* name (exactly as
  `warm_cache_bypass` is retained next to `context_too_large`).
- AC2: Internal decisions/behaviour are unchanged: the affinity/reserve/wait
  logic and any cooldown behaviour keep working (the rename must not alter
  decisions — it is a string rename only). `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` is updated
  to key on the new status (`frozenset({"provider_budget_exhausted"})`,
  provider.py ~4181); `status_code=429` in the diagnostic attempt entries
  stays as-is (a numeric HTTP code, not the reason vocabulary); the
  reason-keyed budget-evidence gate `(reason or "").startswith("rate_limited")`
  (~669) switches to the new prefix.
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill normalises legacy logs: `log_parser.py` maps
  `rate_limited*` -> `provider_budget_exhausted*` so historical windows and
  new windows report under one label, with the mapping documented in
  `REFERENCE.md` (add to the existing legacy reason mapping next to
  `warm_cache_bypass` -> `context_too_large`).
- AC4: `reporting.py` renders the new label and keeps the reason table stable
  (no duplicate rows for old/new names in one window);
  `recommendations.py` text that references rate limiting is updated to
  distinguish proxy budget pacing from upstream 429s. Paths verified at plan
  time: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` (legend at
  ~line 545) and `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
  (~lines 478, 544, 731).
- AC5: Tests: parser normalisation tests (old and new spellings) in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`; every test that asserts the old
  reason string is updated. Audited set (verified at plan time by literal
  scan): `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` (20 occurrences — the primary
  decision-reason tests), `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_budget_eval_parse.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py`, `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`,
  `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`.
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py` were named in the original
  draft but contain **no** `rate_limited` literal — confirmed listed in error
  (producer decision 2026-10-25), nothing to change there.
  With the full rename the attempt-`status` assertions also move:
  `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` (~1187), `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py`
  (~75, ~169, ~397), `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py` (~357),
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py` (~360). Test-function names describing the
  old vocabulary are renamed in the same change (see implementation notes).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`. Historical artifacts are
  deliberately left untouched: `.worklog/analysis/report.md` (regenerated by
  the analysis skill, which normalises legacy names via AC3) and
  `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/RESULTS_NOTE.md`
  (archival run note quoting a then-current log line) — record this
  classification in the commit message.
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the vocabulary split (proxy budget skip vs
  upstream HTTP 429) so the two are never conflated again.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.
- AC9: Current documentation examples that show the reason *or* attempt-status
  strings are updated (`proxy/README.md` exhaustion-diagnostics example at
  ~lines 534-536 and table ~934, `proxy/docs/routing.md` routing table at
  ~lines 154-158, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` attempt example at ~lines 284-285) so
  no current doc advertises `reason=rate_limited` or `status: "rate_limited"`
  after the rename. `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` (~275) and
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_config_docs.py` (~44) cite the renamed test
  function `test_rate_limited_entry_still_skipped_under_surge` and are
  updated in lock-step with it.

## Notes

- **Deferral cleared:** renaming alone does not fix mis-attribution, it only
  removes a misleading label — so this was deferred behind the
  session-attribution fixes. The prerequisite LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES (*Add
  session + attempt + budget evidence to `Fallback triggered` log lines*) is
  now `completed`/`in_review`, so the report is correct regardless of naming
  and this rename is unblocked.
- **Scope decided (producer, 2026-10-25): full rename everywhere.** The
  rename covers the budget-skip *reason* values **and** the diagnostics
  attempt *status* values, plus `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES`, test assertions,
  fixtures, test-function names and documentation examples. **Boundary:** the
  rename targets the proxy budget-skip vocabulary only. It does **not**
  rename configuration knobs that describe a real RPM budget
  (`rate_limit_rpm`, `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`,
  `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_waiters`), the rate-limiter machinery
  (`rate_limiter`, its tests), upstream-429 vocabulary, or unrelated
  quota/lease status values — those keep their accurate names, and renaming
  them would change configuration semantics.
- Coordinate: dashboards/UI that display reason strings (the log tail in
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` shows raw lines) need only a display sanity check.

## Implementation notes (verified at plan time)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` carries all four reason variants —
  `rate_limited` (~120, 553, 561, 755, 765),
  `rate_limited_after_wait` (~121, 647, 655),
  `rate_limited_waiters` (~122, 569, 578),
  `rate_limited_disconnect` (~123, 617). Rename to
  `provider_budget_exhausted{,_after_wait,_waiters,_disconnect}` (keep the
  `_waiters` / `_disconnect` suffixes exactly as AC1 requires).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: `fallback_reason = "rate_limited"` at ~9028
  (new-session pass-through) and ~10515 (in-progress pass-through) — both
  become `provider_budget_exhausted`. The reason-keyed budget-evidence gate
  `(reason or "").startswith("rate_limited")` at ~669 must switch to the new
  prefix (otherwise budget evidence silently stops being emitted).
  Docstrings/comments at 636, 659, 7767, 7841, 8261, 8880, 9531 mention
  `rate_limited*` and should follow the new vocabulary.
- Diagnostics attempt status sites (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`): `status="rate_limited"`
  at ~9018 (new-session pass-through) and ~10505 (in-progress pass-through)
  -> `provider_budget_exhausted`; `status="rate_limited_waited"` at ~9038 and
  ~10525 -> `provider_budget_exhausted_waited`. Leave `status_code=429`
  untouched (numeric HTTP code, not vocabulary).
- `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES = frozenset({"rate_limited"})` (~4181) keys on the
  *diagnostics attempt status* and must be updated in lock-step to
  `frozenset({"provider_budget_exhausted"})` — otherwise
  `_budget_window_retry_after` (~4184) silently stops deriving a retry_after
  from budget-skipped entries (a behaviour change AC2 forbids).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`: mirror the existing
  legacy-mapping pattern (`CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE` / `LEGACY_WARM_CACHE_BYPASS` /
  `_normalize_reason`, ~lines 255-271) — add a `PROVIDER_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`
  constant plus a prefix-aware legacy mapping so `rate_limited*` normalises to
  `provider_budget_exhausted*` while preserving the four variant suffixes.
- Consumers keyed on the **line prefix** rather than the reason value need no
  code change (verified): `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` and
  `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py` match
  `"Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=..."`, and the benchmark's
  `reason=([A-Za-z0-9_ ]+?)` regex accepts the new name unchanged.
  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py` has no `rate_limited` literal.
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` has no literal (only its test does).
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py:80` is a comment describing field
  placement after `reason=` — wording update only.
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` renders raw log lines — display sanity check only.
- Test-function names carrying the old vocabulary (rename with the change;
  each currently asserts the old string/status):
  `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py` ~3136
  `test_plan_fallback_reaches_go_tier_when_free_tier_rate_limited` and
  ~5489 `test_budget_evidence_emitted_for_rate_limited`;
  `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` ~389
  `test_rate_limited_waited_attempt_is_not_a_blocker`; and
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py` ~336
  `test_rate_limited_entry_still_skipped_under_surge` — whose name is
  cross-referenced in `proxy/tests/test_quota_config_docs.py` (~44) and
  `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` (~275), so update all three together. Optional
  (descriptive only): `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` ~154
  `test_fallback_rate_limited_line_parses_budget_snapshot`. **Do not** rename
  tests that describe genuine rate limiting / the config knob
  (`test_unset_rate_limit_is_unlimited`, `test_rate_limiter.py`,
  `test_account_429_rate_limit_exceeded_*`).
- Test-first order: (1) parser normalisation tests (old + new spellings) in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`; (2) proxy decision/log-text tests
  (`test_provider_budget.py` first — it holds the four-variant reason and
  attempt-status assertions); (3) analysis-skill fixtures and assertions;
  (4) docs (AC9 + REFERENCE.md); (5) full suite via the test skill.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — all four `BudgetDecision.reason` values and their log lines.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `fallback_reason` assignments (~9028, ~10515), reason-keyed evidence gate (~669), `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` (~4181), docstrings.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — legacy reason normalisation.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — renders the reason label (legend ~545).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py` — rate-limit wording (~478, ~544, ~731).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` — legacy mapping + "Interpreting the report" (~490-553).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — parser/analysis assertions.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — legacy and current log fixtures.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` — four-variant reason assertions (20 occurrences).
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py` — budget evidence line assertion.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` — attempt fixtures carrying the reason.
- `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_budget_eval_parse.py` — benchmark fallback-reason parsing.
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py` — diagnostics attempt status assertion.
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py` — parametrised status fixture.
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py` — reason-field docstring/assertions.
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py` — script reason tally.
- `proxy/README.md` — diagnostics/log examples.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — routing table log/attempt examples.
- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — attempt-status example.
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py` — comment about field placement.
- `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py` — fallback-reason extraction.
- `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` — budget-skip line matching.
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` — raw log tail display check.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- ~~OPEN QUESTION 1~~ **ANSWERED (producer/Map, 2026-10-25): "full rename
  everywhere."** Decision: the rename covers the emitted *reason* values
  **and** the diagnostics attempt *status* values (`provider_budget_exhausted`
  / `provider_budget_exhausted_waited`), plus `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES`, the
  status assertions in the proxy tests, fixtures, test-function names and
  documentation examples. The plan's earlier preferred option (reason-only)
  is **superseded**; AC1/AC2/AC5/AC9 and the implementation notes were
  rewritten accordingly. Scope boundary recorded in Notes (config knobs for
  the real RPM budget, the rate limiter and upstream-429 vocabulary are not
  renamed). **Final: full rename.**
  Q: Does the rename cover only the emitted *reason* value, or also the
  diagnostics attempt `status="rate_limited"` / `status="rate_limited_waited"`
  fields in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` plus `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES`?
  Context: AC1 names the reason and the `fallback_reason = ...` assignments
  only, while AC2 says "*Internal status/behaviour is unchanged:
  `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` ... keep working*" **and** "*Update any internal
  constant that keys on the old string*" — the second clause only has a
  referent if the diagnostics status is also renamed. The Notes mention UI
  consumers of "reason strings" only.
  Preferred option (plan assumption): **reason-only** — rename
  `BudgetDecision.reason` values, the `reason=` log text, the
  `fallback_reason` assignments and the reason-keyed
  `startswith("rate_limited")` gate; leave the diagnostics
  `status=` values, `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` and the
  `test_quota_surge_bypass.py` / `test_quota_state.py` status assertions
  alone. Rationale: this removes the misleading label from the
  fallback-reason table (the cited 61.6% misreading) with no change to the
  diagnostics payload other tools already consume.
  Alternative: rename the status vocabulary too (`provider_budget_exhausted`
  / `provider_budget_exhausted_waited`) and update `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES`,
  the status assertions in `test_provider_budget.py` (~1187),
  `test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` (~75, ~169),
  `test_quota_surge_bypass.py` (~357), `test_quota_state.py` (~360) and the
  `status:` examples in `proxy/README.md` / `proxy/docs/routing.md` /
  `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`.
  Answer: **awaiting producer**.

- Q: `AC5` listed `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`, but neither contains a
  `rate_limited` literal today, while `test_provider_budget.py` (20),
  `test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` (6) and
  `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py` (6) were unlisted.
  Answer (plan, evidence: repository literal scan at planning time):
  expanded AC5 to the audited set. Follow-up (producer/Map, 2026-10-25): the
  two zero-occurrence files are **listed in error** — full rename leaves
  nothing to change there. **Final: audited set stands.**

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 (plan skill, skip path — effort Extra Small / risk Low):
  pre-check returned `decision: skip`; six automated review stages run
  against existing content — no child items created (single atomic
  rename, leaf task).
  1. *Requirements & AC alignment*: all 9 ACs trace to the goal; AC5's test
     list was incomplete (two zero-occurrence files named, the main
     assertion file omitted) → expanded to the audited set.
  2. *Completeness*: added the previously absent `**Key Files:**` section
     (format-validated) and `## Implementation notes (verified at plan
     time)`; corrected AC4's `reporting.py` / `recommendations.py` locations
     (they live under `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/`).
  3. *Sequencing & dependencies*: no children; the deferral prerequisite
     LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES is completed/in_review → deferral cleared in Notes;
     test-first order recorded in the implementation notes.
  4. *Scope sizing*: leaf task, Extra Small — no decomposition needed.
  5. *Acceptance & testability*: added AC9 for stale documentation examples
     (a completeness gap, not a new requirement) so every renamed string has
     a pass/fail check; all ACs remain mechanically verifiable.
  6. *Polish & handoff*: added exact code site line references, the
     reason-keyed `startswith` gate warning, and the verified no-change list
     for prefix-keyed consumers.
  AC coverage review: no children → coverage trivially complete.
- 2026-10-25 (resume after producer answer): producer decided **full rename
  everywhere** (reason + diagnostics attempt status). Rewrote AC1 (status
  values), AC2 (`_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` must move; `status_code=429` stays),
  AC5 (status assertions + test-function renames), AC9 (status examples +
  cross-referenced test name), AC6 (historical-artifact classification) and
  the implementation notes; added the scope boundary (config knobs / rate
  limiter / upstream-429 vocabulary unchanged); resolved both Appendix
  questions; cleared `needsProducerReview`.

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer and as the proxy-usage analyst, I want every `Fallback
triggered` log line to identify the session and the attempt it belongs to, so
per-session fallback attribution stops relying on a "nearest line within 60
seconds" guess.

## Why

`Fallback triggered` is now the only structured decision line with no session
context. `routing_skip_local`, `routing_skip_provider_context`, `routing_hop`,
`Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `local_dispatch_denied` and even
`[local] POST` all carry a session id.

Consequence observed in the 2026-10-23/24 window: a session with no
`routing_skip_local` line of its own inherited an unrelated
`munitoai-free -> opencode-go` spill as its fallback reason. 11 of the 26
sessions that used local were labelled `rate_limited` this way, while the real
cause was `local_dispatch_denied` (lease held by another session). Example:
herdr-1792767061-1282111-17770 has no skip and no fallback line at all, only
lease denials.

The session id is already available in scope: `_budget_session_id` is resolved
in `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (proxy/proxy/provider.py ~line 8177).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The three `Fallback triggered` emit sites (proxy/proxy/provider.py
  `_handle_streaming_success`, `_build_fallback_success_response`, and the
  third site `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` around line 7563) include
  `session=<uuid|unknown>` on the log line, threaded from the request's
  resolved session id.
- AC2: The same line carries an attempt/step index (e.g. `attempt=N`) so two
  fallbacks from the same session in the same second are distinguishable.
- AC3: When `reason` is budget-driven (`rate_limited*`), the line also carries
  the budget evidence already computed by
  `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`: `limit=`, `remaining=`, `waited=` (only
  for those reasons; no behaviour change to the decision itself).
- AC4: Existing lines keep their current prefix and key=value shape where
  possible; any consumer regex tolerant of extra trailing fields continues to
  work (verify, don't assume).
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill consumes the new fields:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` (parse `session`,
  `attempt`, budget fields on the fallback event),
  `aggregation.py` (`_attribute_fallback` uses the session's own fallback line
  before any nearest-line heuristic), `reporting.py` (per-session reason is
  sourced from own evidence; expose explicit `no remote fallback` /
  `lease/concurrency denied` / `unattributed` states instead of inheriting),
  and `recommendations.py` where reason counts are cited.
- AC6: Skill tests updated/added: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`
  (`fixtures.py`, `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `test_availability_classification.py`) cover session-bearing fallback
  lines, attempts, budget fields, and the no-inheritance rule. Proxy tests
  that assert log text are updated:
  `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`.
- AC7: All other log-consuming scripts are audited and updated where they
  parse `Fallback triggered`: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`, and
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`. Non-parsing pass-through consumers
  (the log tail in `proxy/proxy/ui.py`) are verified unaffected.
- AC8: Documentation updated: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`
  (log contract + attribution precedence) and any comment in provider.py that
  describes the line format.
- AC9: Full suite passes via the test skill.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — three `Fallback triggered` emit sites:
  `_handle_streaming_success` (~7071), `_build_fallback_success_response`
  (~7136), `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` (~7563)
- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — budget evidence already computed
  (`limit_rpm`, `remaining`, `waited_seconds`)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_availability_classification.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`
- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`
- `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`
- `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` (pass-through only)

## Implementation notes (verified at plan time)

- The emit-site helpers are called from **two sibling fallback cycles** (7
  call sites total): `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (line 8109; session
  var `_budget_session_id`) and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (line 8748;
  session var `_session_id`). Thread the session id into the three helpers
  from each caller — do not assume `_budget_session_id` is in scope at every
  call site.
- AC4 "verify, don't assume" answers: three consumers are **end-anchored**
  and will break unless updated — `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`
  (`RE_FALLBACK`, `reason=([\w ]+)$`), `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`
  (line 46, `reason=[A-Za-z0-9_ ]+)$`), `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want local prompt-eval (prefill) throughput increased so that
large cold prompts become cheap enough to serve locally, unlocking real local
utilisation instead of diverting work to paid remote providers.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This item must only be executed once we have had a successful night of local
LLM consumption, meaning >60% GPU utilisation across a full night.** Until
local actually carries sustained work (>60% local busy), tuning prefill
throughput is premature: there is no sustained workload to measure against and
no evidence that prefill latency — rather than routing policy — is the binding
constraint. Verify the gate with the `proxy-usage-analysis` report's
`## Local model utilization` section for a night window (e.g. 22:00-07:00):
it must show busy >= 60%. Record that evidence in a comment on this item
before starting work; if the gate is not met, leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Prompt-eval speed (llama-server eval timing, Qwen3, fast bucket): median
  **90.7 tok/s**, p90 316.7, p10 24.9 (532 samples, 24h window
  2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52).
- Per-stream prefill (dispatch -> first byte): p50 4.4s, p90 35.3s, max 73.7s.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 90` — a slow prefill can be cancelled, and
  prior incidents show cancelled prefills re-dispatching identical prompts
  (the prefill-thrash cooldown exists because of this).
- The prefill-ETA admission guard refused **478** local admissions in the
  window on projected prefill cost, and only **34** requests were admitted by
  the idle override despite local being idle 89.8% of the time.
- Current llama-server launch flags (Qwen3 child):
  `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024
  --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0
  --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation
  for a full night, taken from the usage-analysis report, before any change is
  made. Work does not start without it.
- AC1: A measured baseline is captured first: prompt-eval tok/s distribution
  (p10/p50/p90), prefill phase duration, prefill-ETA admission refusals, and
  prefill-thrash events over a fixed window, all from the
  `proxy-usage-analysis` artifacts.
- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch
  configuration (candidates: `--ubatch-size` 1024 -> 2048/4096, `--batch-size`,
  `--mlock`, thread count, SWA/checkpoint settings) and/or the prefill-related
  proxy knobs (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, the ETA guard budget). Each
  changed value is justified by measurement, not by guesswork.
- AC3: The optimisation is measured with the same method as AC1 and the
  before/after comparison is recorded on this item, including any effect on
  decode speed (no regression to decode tok/s median) and on stability
  (`slot_save failed`, prefill cancellations, HTTP 400/503 rates).
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's
  configuration and documentation are updated together, and the
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill is updated if new or changed log evidence is
  needed to measure the improvement
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/{llama_log_parser.py,log_parser.py,
  reporting.py}`, `REFERENCE.md`), and any other log-consuming script that
  reads llama-server eval timings or prefill evidence is audited
  (`proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_lease_verification.py`).
- AC6: Launch-flag changes are documented in `models.ini` / start-proxy
  documentation so the settings are reproducible, and any start-proxy script
  or test asserting the flags is updated.
- AC7: Full suite passes via the test skill.

- This item is downstream of routing policy: raising local demand (thresholds,
  serve-first admission) comes first, otherwise there is nothing to optimise

- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (evaluate increasing local ctx-size) and the
  slot-geometry experiment (1 slot vs 2) — decide ctx/slot geometry before

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a measured comparison of **1 llama-server slot with
262,144 ctx** versus **2 slots with 131,072 ctx each**, so we can choose the
geometry that maximises local work served without unacceptable queueing.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This experiment can only be carried out when we have a full night of GPU use
(>60% busy).** With local currently at ~10% busy, a 1-vs-2 slot comparison
measures noise, not saturation: the trade-off only shows up when demand
actually contends for slots. Verify the gate with the
`proxy-usage-analysis` report's `## Local model utilization` section for a
complete night window: busy must be >= 60% for the full night. Record that
evidence in a comment on this item before starting; if the gate is not met,
leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Current geometry: `--parallel 2` with `--ctx-size 262144` = **131,072 tokens
  per slot**.
- Measured concurrency: **avg 1.04 while busy, peak 2** — demand is nearly
  serial today, so 2 slots are rarely both used.
- The routing hard cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 120000`)
  sits just under the 131K per-slot limit. In the 24h window **2,064 requests
  were skipped as `context_too_large`** (estimated > 120K), including 105
  skips from sessions that were already warm (cache ratio 0.92-1.00, only ~4K
  new tokens, total 126K-137K). A single 262K slot would move that ceiling
  from ~120K to ~258K.
- Local was idle **89.8%** of the window, serving only 225 turns across 26
  sessions, so spare capacity is not the current constraint — but slot
  geometry determines what will be servable once demand is raised.

## Hypothesis to test

- **1 x 262K**: ~2x per-slot context → far fewer `context_too_large` skips and
  larger conversations stay local; cost: requests serialise when two sessions
  overlap (today: peak 2, avg 1.04, so the cost may be small).
- **2 x 131K**: current state; parallel but capped at ~120K per request; the
  evidence above shows warm sessions being cut off at the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment records the measured >60% GPU busy for a full night
  from the usage-analysis report, before any configuration change.
- AC1: A repeatable measurement protocol is defined and written on this item:
  identical workload window length, same metrics, same report tooling for both
  arms.
- AC2: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a
  comparable period at the gate, with llama-server `--parallel` / `--ctx-size`
  changed together (and `session_slot_pool_size` plus the warm/cold thresholds
  adjusted consistently, since per-slot ctx and slot count interact — see
  LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP on the band collapsing to zero
  width).
- AC3: Results compare, for each arm: local busy %, turns served locally,
  requests diverted per fallback reason (especially `context_too_large` and
  `large_context_bypass`), queue wait / `fallback_after_queue` counts, time to
  first token, prefill and decode phase slot-seconds, and any errors
  (`slot_save failed`, HTTP 400/503).
- AC4: A decision is recorded on this item: keep 2 slots, move to 1 slot, or
  make it mode-dependent, with the data that justifies it. If 1 slot wins, the
  follow-on config change is filed (or implemented if in scope).
- AC5: Findings feed the configuration documentation (`models.ini` launch
  flags, `proxy/config.yaml` slot/ctx comments) and the usage-analysis skill's
  interpretation section if the guidance changes
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`), plus any log-consuming
  script that assumes a fixed slot count or per-slot ctx.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill for any config/code change made.

## Notes

- Depends on demand having been raised first (thresholds / serve-first
  admission); that is why the >60% busy gate exists.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (local ctx-size evaluation), and the
  prefill-latency optimisation item — decide geometry before micro-tuning.


---

## Plan (2026-10-25, /skill:plan)

Sequenced features in dependency order (execution order for `wl next`):

1. **Gate: verify 60% local busy night** (LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG) — parent AC0 evidence; blocks the arms.
2. **Geometry A/B protocol and reporter** (LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP) — `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` (protocol, window, metrics, pre-registered gate), `scripts/slot_geometry_ab_report.py` + fixture tests, `scripts/slot_geometry_arm.py` apply/verify helper. Test-first; can start while the gate is unmet.
3. **Arm A capture: 2 slots 131K** (LP-0MVNCME7Y009KC9K) — blocked by 1+2.
4. **Arm B run: 1 slot 262K** (LP-0MVNCMEJ6004A2QY) — blocked by 3; warm ceiling raised to the 258,048 clamp, cold unchanged, band non-collapsed.
5. **Arm comparison and geometry decision** (LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY) — blocked by 4; applies the pre-registered gate, records verdict + follow-on item.
6. **Propagate geometry decision to docs** (LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7) — blocked by 5; models.ini / config.yaml comments, usage-analysis REFERENCE, log-consumer audit.
7. **Suite green and geometry assertions** (LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP) — blocked by 6; `/skill:test` green + slot/ctx alignment assertions.

Reuse: env plumbing already exists (`LLAMA_PARALLEL`, `LLAMA_CTX_SIZE` in start-llama.sh; `session_slot_pool_size` drives it); per-slot clamp/band logic is in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` with existing unit coverage; usage-analysis report already emits busy/prefill/decode metrics. Precedent harness: `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py`.

Pre-registered decision-gate defaults (proposal — confirm at implement time unless overridden by the producer): adopt **1 x 262K** when, relative to Arm A, (a) turns served locally does not decrease, (b) `context_too_large` + `large_context_bypass` diverts fall by >= 50 %, (c) p90 dispatch→first-byte does not worsen by > 30 %, (d) local busy % does not regress by > 10 points; otherwise keep 2 slots (or choose mode-dependent with the recorded numbers).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (2026-10-25)

- Q: "Arm B's warm threshold: raise to the new per-slot clamp (~258K) or keep ~120K?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: raise the economic ceiling ratio so warm = clamp (258,048), cold unchanged (38,000), band non-collapsed (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP). Rationale: leaving it at 120K means the extra slot context is never routed to, defeating the arm. Final confirmation delegated to implement time unless the producer overrides.
- Q: "What makes 1 x 262K 'win'?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed pre-registered gate above (mirrors the ubatch A/B precedent LP-0MVNBJXR6002OSPD). Confirmation delegated to implement time.
- Q: "Arm window length?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: one full night (22:00 → 06:00 local, >= 8 h), Arm A then Arm B on the same weekday type, identical length for both. Delegated to implement time.
- Q: "Write the protocol while the gate is unmet?" Answer (plan): yes — child 2 has no dependency on the busy gate (desk work), so implementation can begin immediately and the gate evidence decides when the arms may run.

- 2026-10-25Z (plan session herdr-1792903336-2608898-6919): superseded the placeholder auto-skip verdict (XS/0.00 h) with a genuine estimate (Medium effort/Medium risk); ran full /skill:plan decomposition. Created 7 children (LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG gate, LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP protocol+reporter, LP-0MVNCME7Y009KC9K Arm A, LP-0MVNCMEJ6004A2QY Arm B, LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY comparison+decision, LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7 docs propagation, LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP suite green) in test-first order with dependency edges C3<-C1,C2 / C4<-C3 / C5<-C4 / C6<-C5 / C7<-C6. Ran the six automated review stages (trace bullets added; Key Files validated), AC coverage review proceeded (7/7), stage advanced to plan_complete. ## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy to record real prompt/completion token usage
for local streams, so that (a) local cache-credit and context accounting can
work from measured data and (b) the usage-analysis report can measure actual
local prompt sizes instead of showing them as unknown.

## Why (evidence)

Local `Stream finished` lines **never carry `tokens=`**:

- 225 of 225 local `Stream finished` lines in the window 2026-10-23 10:52 ->
  2026-10-24 10:52 have no token field;
- **0** lines with `tokens=` exist in the entire log archive (2026-10-17 ->
  2026-10-24) for `provider=local`.

Consequences:

1. **The usage-based cache-credit path is dead for local.** In
   `proxy/router.py` (~line 566) `update_cached_ratio()` and
   `record_prompt_prefix()` are only called when the response carries a usage
   block with `prompt_tokens > 0`. Because local never reports usage, the
   expected-reuse credit (`LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV`) can never be earned from
   measured tokens. Credit today comes only from the slot-snapshot seeding
   path (655 `slot_save success` events in the archive), so a session whose
   first local dispatch did not produce a snapshot stays permanently "cold"
   (ratio 0.00) and is then bypassed by the 38K cold-cache rule on every later
   turn.
2. **The report cannot measure local context.** In the window, 3 of the 26
   sessions that used local had no context size at all, and the per-model
   token table attributes local tokens only via sessions whose *initial*
   provider was local — not via actual local streams.
3. Two current analysis outputs are therefore guesses rather than
   measurements: per-session local prompt sizes, and the cache-state
   attribution used in the skip-reason explanation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Local `Stream finished` lines include `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
  with values taken from llama-server's reported usage (its response/`usage`
  payload or `/slots` accounting — whichever is authoritative), for
  non-streaming and streaming paths.
- AC2: `update_cached_ratio()` and `record_prompt_prefix()` therefore fire for
  local streams with measured values, so the expected-reuse credit is earned
  from data rather than only from a saved slot snapshot. Verify with a test
  that a 30K local turn followed by a 40K total / 10K new turn routes local
  (the intended cold-cap semantics: the cap applies to NEW, uncached tokens).
- AC3: A regression test proves the sequential-caching case explicitly:
  turn 1 total 30K -> local; turn 2 total 40K with ~10K new -> still local
  (new tokens below the 38K cold cap). This is the behaviour the design
  intends and it currently cannot be demonstrated from the logs.
- AC4: The usage-analysis skill consumes the new data:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` and
  `aggregation.py` attribute tokens to local streams, `reporting.py` reports
  real local prompt sizes and a "streams without usage" count, and the
  limitation text that currently explains missing local context is updated.
- AC5: Other log consumers relying on `tokens=` are audited:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`.
- AC6: Tests: skill fixtures/tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` plus proxy-side tests for the emit
  path.
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents local token reporting and the cold-cap
  semantics (cap applies to new/uncached tokens; total context is bounded
  separately by the warm cap).
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Complements LP-0MVMBM6N400541EH (`tokens=missing` marker): that item makes
  absence explicit; this item fixes the root cause (local usage is never
  reported at all, so the marker would fire on every local stream).
- Do not change routing thresholds here — this is measurement plumbing, and it
  is a prerequisite for measuring any later routing change honestly.

data.description:
## Problem statement

Local admission is scheduled **per request** against a 2-slot llama-server pool
with no session→slot tenancy and no check of the *actual* reusable prefix, so
any session can land on another session's slot and lose the resident KV. 27
distinct sessions cycled through 2 slots in ~5.4 h on 2026-10-24; aggregate
prefix reuse was 26.1 % and the median for prompts >20k tokens was **15.6 %**
(28 of 227 fully cold), and 160 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` cancellations in
5.4 h wasted ~780k prefill tokens (~93 % of local compute in the window).

The routing estimator cannot see this: `cached_ratio` is predicted from the
session's own snapshot sidecar (`proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`) and is
structurally wrong under contention (`cached_ratio ≈ 0.99` predicted for
requests that then prefilled from `n_past=738`), which is why the 38k cold cap
never fired. The counter-example that proves it is slot churn rather than
GPU incapacity: the identical 49,103-token prompt scored `n_past=738` on its
first attempt (deadline-cancelled) and **100 % reuse (`n_past=49103`)** on the
immediate same-prompt retry, before another session trashed the slot.

## Users

- **Primary — local-work sessions (herdr / opencode clients):** multi-turn
  coding sessions with large, mostly-resident context that today lose their
  prefix on nearly every turn.
- **Secondary — the proxy operator:** needs local throughput without paying
  remote tokens for work the GPU could have done, and needs a truthful signal
  when local admission declines.
- **Tertiary — the capacity/usage analyst:** consumes the usage report to
  attribute local vs remote dispatch and resident-vs-evicted reuse.

User stories:

- *As a multi-turn local session*, my second and later turns should resume
  from my resident prefix instead of a cold prefill that consumes my whole
  deadline.
- *As the proxy operator*, a cold prompt that cannot finish inside the prefill
  deadline must not be admitted just because a prediction said it would be
  cheap.
- *As the operator*, I want to see, per admission decision, the measured
  reusable prefix and which session owned the slot, so residency regressions
  are visible without forensics.
- *As a client whose connection died*, I must not leave a dead session holding
  the pool; the proxy alone reaps me within a bounded window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Resident-prefix admission gate.** Before a local dispatch of a large prompt is admitted, the router computes the session's *actual* reusable prefix from live slot state and admits only when `reuse_ratio = min(context_tokens, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens` is `>= local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` (default `0.5`, `0` disables). Otherwise it skips local with reason `resident_prefix_insufficient` and the chain falls through as it does today. Cold prompts above the admission budget from non-resident sessions are never admitted. *Measured by:* unit tests over stubbed slot snapshots + a replay fixture of the 2026-10-24 window asserting zero over-budget cold admissions.
- **AC2 — Session tenancy ("N tenants, 2 slots").** At most `local_session_tenants` distinct sessions (default: the slot count, i.e. 2) may hold a local reservation for a large prompt at once. A new session's large prompt is admitted only when a slot is free of other sessions' prefixes, or when the resident session's tenancy has idle-lapsed (`local_session_tenancy_idle_seconds`, default derived from the existing adaptive dispatch lease). Beyond that bound the request follows the normal chain rather than evicting a resident session.
- **AC3 — Live-prefix pricing (re-scoped).** The cold-cache gate (`provider._should_skip_local`) prices `new_tokens` from the **live** measurement used by AC1 rather than the predicted sidecar ratio, so the new-token cap is evaluated against real prefill work. The budget constant itself is owned by `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` (25k) and is consumed, not redefined, here. *Measured by:* zero admissions whose live `new_tokens > cold threshold` unless idle-exempt.
- **AC4 — Deadline/thrash regression (re-anchored), verified by a mandatory follow-up work item.** On a 24 h window measured **after** `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is deployed, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are >= 90 % below that window's own re-anchored baseline; genuine GPU-speed misses are out of scope. A cancellation counts as *scheduling-attributed* when either the live `reuse_ratio` at admission was below `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`, or `slot_owner_session` changed between admission and the deadline event (i.e. the prefix was evicted by another session). The 2026-10-24 figures (160 events / 5.4 h, ~780k wasted tokens) remain the historical reference only. **Verification is executed by a separate follow-up work item, and creating that item is a deliverable of this one (not optional):**
- Title format: `24 h AC4 verification of resident-prefix admission — run no earlier than <ISO-8601 UTC instant>`. The instant in the title is the earliest the review can run: the **later** of this item's deploy and `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`'s deploy, **+ 24 h**. Until this item ships, the title carries the provable lower bound (now + 24 h); the implementing agent MUST retitle it with the concrete deploy-derived instant on ship.
- Description records the pinned measurement window (start/end UTC), the baseline re-anchoring query for that window, the `proxy-usage-analysis` invocation, and the scheduling-attributed classifier above.
- Linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and related to `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`; assigned to the operator's triage queue.
- AC4 is **not** satisfied by the implementing agent's own measurements: it is satisfied only when the follow-up item reports its 24 h result.
- **AC5 — Observability.** Every admission denial and admission logs `n_past_actual`, `estimated_tokens`, `reuse_ratio`, `slot_owner_session`, and the decision (`admit` / `resident_prefix_insufficient` / `tenant_limit`) at `routing_skip_local` / `routing_hop` level, and the `proxy-usage-analysis` report surfaces resident-vs-evicted reuse splits and slot-owner churn per session.
- **AC6 — Tenancy reservations are leases, not locks.** Reservations follow the existing dispatch-record lease pattern: held only while real activity is observed (data chunks, prefill progress, or a live client confirmed by the poll-cadence `request.is_disconnected()`), TTL refresh bounded by the 180 s no-progress watchdog and the 900 s lifetime ceiling, never extended by a merely open upstream socket. Reclaim uses the existing ~10 s `_dispatch_cleanup_loop`: within seconds when a disconnect is observed (release record, pop prefill marker, free slot assignment, cancel the captured upstream `stream_cm`) and within <= 180 s for a silent half-open drop; no path leaves a dead session gating the pool beyond those bounds (the 2026-10-23 ~5.5–6 min `local_lease_active` window is the regression baseline). On reclaim the evicted session's KV snapshot is saved (`slot_<id>.bin`, subject to pool-size and busy gates) so a returning client restores warm instead of prefilling cold. The proxy is the sole owner of abandonment reaping; no client protocol change is required.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit coverage for: resident accept / non-resident reject, ratio boundary, tenancy bound, unknown-`context_tokens` fallback ladder, predicted-vs-actual divergence, and both reclaim bounds. Integration coverage replays the 2026-10-24 thrash fixture and asserts (a) no cold admission above the budget without a resident prefix and (b) task 92383/92422 classify as resident on retry. All tests run through the test skill.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** `proxy/config.yaml` documents every new knob (defaults, 0-disables semantics, interaction with `local_idle_admit_*` and `contention_queue_*`); `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `docs/dev/cached-ratio-prefix-credit.md` and `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` describe the admission ladder and the "read the cached slot snapshot, never a synchronous `/slots` call" constraint.
- **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (dev-push gate).
- **AC10 — Occupancy-aware deadline admission (re-scoped residual, producer decision 2026-10-25).** With the scheduler live, a within-budget admitted local dispatch is not cancelled by `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` while another session's prefill is in flight — occupancy-aware admission refuses (falls through) instead. The deliverable half is implemented here: the admission deadline bound is priced from the *projected time to first byte* (own calibrated prefill + the remaining service of in-flight prefills, read from the occupant's own dispatch record), unit-tested against the measured 2026-10-25 residual shape. The measurement half — zero user-traffic `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events over a >= 24 h post-landing window — is executed by `LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I` AC3, the residual's tracking item, which closes on that window.

## Constraints

- **`/slots` must not be queried on the admission hot path.** Under a
  prompt-processing batch llama-server holds `/slots` for >15 s (measured 8.7 s
  then >15 s, vs the 1 s status timeout) — see `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`. AC1 must
  therefore read the in-memory snapshot already maintained every ~1 s by
  `_periodic_broadcast_loop()` (`observability._last_slot_details_cache`,
  TTL-coalesced `/slots` poll, 5 s failure backoff) plus
  `session._slot_owners`; any synchronous upstream call is prohibited.
- **Fail-open on unknown state.** A missing/stale snapshot, an unreported
  `context_tokens` (llama b8782 dropped `n_past`), or a cache older than the
  freshness bound must not turn into a hard local outage: fall back to the
  session-owns-slot check, then to today's predicted-ratio decision.
- **No change to** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (stays a backstop;
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` owns the 90→110 change) and no change to
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills`.
- **No live slot-count change** here: widening the snapshot pool is evaluated
  separately in `LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`, and adding llama slots shrinks per-slot
  context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots), excluding the long-context sessions
  that dominate this workload.
- **Idle-awareness must keep working.** `local_idle_admit_enabled`
  (`LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`) deliberately overrides the economic bypass when the
  GPU is idle; the new gate must not silently disable that behaviour.
- `contention_queue_*` semantics are unchanged: a request denied by AC1/AC2
  does not consume the queue budget differently from today's bypass path.

## Existing state

- Admission is per-request: `router_helpers._try_acquire_local_dispatch()`
  keeps N concurrent dispatch leases (`local_active_queries`,
  `local_dispatch_records`, no-preemption cooldown), which bounds *in-flight*
  requests but not *which* sessions occupy the pool over time.
- The economic gate is `provider._should_skip_local()`: a hard
  `warm_cache_threshold` cap plus `new_tokens = estimated_tokens *
  (1 - cached_ratio)` compared to the cold threshold, where `cached_ratio`
  comes from `_last_cached_ratio` and the snapshot sidecar
  (`slot_cache_ratio.py`, safety margin 0.9, prefix-fingerprint validated).
- Slot ownership/persistence already exists: `session._slot_owners`
  (`(endpoint, slot_id) -> session_id`), `_slot_id_for_session`,
  `_free_slot_assignment`, `_save_slot_snapshot` / `_restore_slot_snapshot`
  with per-slot failure cooldowns and `session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`.
- Live slot state is already collected: `observability._query_slots_detail()`
  (single-flight, 1 s TTL, 5 s failure backoff) feeds
  `_last_slot_details_cache`; log-derived progress (`_slot_progress_cache`,
  60 s max age) supplements builds that dropped `n_past`.
- Mitigations already shipped: post-deadline thrash cooldown
  (`LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL`, 10 min default), no-progress watchdog + prefill
  liveness extension (`LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF`, `LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O`),
  atomic reservations (`admission_reserve.py`).
- Measured gap: none of the above consults the *live* resident prefix, and
  none bounds the number of distinct sessions contending for the pool.

## Desired change

1. **Residency view (shared, in-memory).** Build a small read-only projection
   of `(slot_id, owner_session, context_tokens, is_processing, age)` from
   `_last_slot_details_cache` + `session._slot_owners`, exposed as one function
   used by AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5. No new poller, no upstream call, no lock
   inversion (read under a snapshot copy).
2. **Admission ladder** in `_should_skip_local` / the local dispatch path:
   (i) hard `warm_cache_threshold` cap (unchanged); (ii) **resident-prefix
   gate** (AC1) with the fallback ladder — `context_tokens` known → measured
   ratio; unknown but session owns the slot → treat as resident (restore
   path); otherwise → non-resident; (iii) **tenancy** check (AC2); (iv) cold
   pricing from live `new_tokens` (AC3); (v) existing idle-exempt override
   stays last, so an idle GPU still serves cold work.
3. **Tenancy as a lease** registered alongside the existing dispatch records
   (AC6), reaped by `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` and the no-progress watchdog, so
   no new lifecycle machinery is introduced.
4. **Logging + report** (AC5) using the existing structured log lines rather
   than a new sink.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_should_skip_local()` cold pricing (AC1/AC3),
  local dispatch path, `_last_cached_ratio`; new admission ladder entry point.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `_last_slot_details_cache`,
  `_query_slots_detail()`, `_slot_context_tokens()`, `_slot_progress_cache`
  (source of the live residency view; TTL/backoff invariants).
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_owners` registry, `_slot_id_for_session`,
  `_free_slot_assignment`, `_save_slot_snapshot` / `_restore_slot_snapshot`
  (tenancy ↔ slot ownership, AC6 reclaim + snapshot on eviction).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch()` tenancy
  bound, `_release_local_dispatch()`, `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch()`,
  prefill-thrash cooldown interaction.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — reservation verdict should consume the
  same residency view so `POST /llama/local/reserve` and the guard agree.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `evaluate_admission` ETA unchanged, but the
  admission verdict feeding it carries live `new_tokens`.
- `proxy/proxy/disconnect_reaper.py` — abandonment observation used by AC6.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — new `server.*` knobs: `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`
  (0.5), `local_session_tenants` (default = slot count),
  `local_session_tenancy_idle_seconds`.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `test_session_slot_affinity_continuity.py`, `test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`,
  `test_local_idle_admission.py`, `test_lease_truthfulness.py`,
  `test_prefill_thrash_cooldown.py`, `test_prefill_eta_occupancy.py` —
  extend for AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6.
- `proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py` — extend as the 2026-10-24
  replay fixture driver (AC7).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — AC5
  resident-vs-evicted report section.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `docs/dev/cached-ratio-prefix-credit.md`,
  `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` — AC8.

## Non-goals

- No change to `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` or
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills`.
- No live slot-count increase (see `LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`) and no change to the
  snapshot pool size here.
- No client-side cooperation for abandonment (proxy-owned reaping only).
- No attempt to make llama.cpp's native context-checkpoint restore rate a
  scheduling signal (`docs/dev/restore-rate-metric-fix-ranking.md`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: admission starvation.** A strict residency gate could refuse local
  for most large prompts, shifting cost to remote. *Mitigation:* the idle-exempt
  override stays last in the ladder, the gate is configurable (0 disables),
  and AC5 logging makes the shift visible within one report cycle.
- **Risk: stale snapshot decisions.** A 1 s TTL snapshot can be wrong exactly
  at a slot switch. *Mitigation:* reason about ownership (authoritative
  in-process registry) rather than throughput, and fail-open on unknown state.
- **Risk: `/slots` unobservability repeats** (`LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`), leaving
  `context_tokens` unknown. *Mitigation:* the fallback ladder + log-derived
  progress cache; the feature must remain correct when the number is absent.
- **Risk: tenancy + single-flight interaction** can make a session wait behind
  its own earlier turn; *Mitigation:* same-session re-acquisition is always
  permitted (existing lease semantics), and the tenancy check only gates
  *new* sessions.
- **Risk: the 0.5 default is aggressive for this workload.** Measured median
  reuse is 15.6 % for prompts >20k, so a 0.5 default may refuse most large
  prompts initially. *Mitigation:* one knob, `0` disables, staged observation
  via AC5 logs before the AC4 window; the ladder still admits same-slot
  residents and idle-exempt work.
- **Assumption:** the local pool stays at 2 slots and
  `session_slot_pool_size: 2` for the duration of this work; a pool-size change
  (`LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`) invalidates the tenancy default and the AC4 baseline.
- **Assumption:** `session._slot_owners` stays accurate under churn — verified
  by `LP-0MTIHWYGJ006YS6X` continuity tests; new tests extend them.
- **Assumption:** the 25k budget from `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is the constant
  consumed by AC3; if that item changes scope, AC3's threshold follows it.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "more slots", snapshot-pool widening, and checkpoint
  tuning are adjacent opportunities — they stay linked work items
  (`LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`), not additions to this brief.

## Testability

Unit tests stub the residency view (slot snapshot + owner map) and assert the
ladder: resident accept, non-resident reject, ratio boundary at exactly
`local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`, unknown-`context_tokens` fallback, tenancy
bound with same-session re-entry, live-vs-predicted divergence (predicted 0.99,
actual 0.015 → reject), and both AC6 reclaim bounds (observed disconnect
releases within one cleanup cycle; silent drop released by the 180 s watchdog,
never the 900 s ceiling). Integration replays the 2026-10-24 thrash window
fixture through the guard and asserts no over-budget cold admission without a
resident prefix, and that task 92383/92422 classify as resident on the retry.
The 24 h AC4 comparison is a post-deploy analysis (`proxy-usage-analysis`)
executed by the mandated follow-up work item, not a test-suite gate and not a
deliverable of this item's implementation session beyond creating that item.

data.description:
## Goal

Stop admitting local prefills that cannot possibly finish before the prefill deadline, and widen the deadline enough to admit the largest genuinely feasible prompt:

1. **Cold-prefill admission budget = 25,000 tokens** of *new* (uncached / to-be-prefilled) tokens — a cap on what the GPU must actually compute, not on prompt size.
2. **`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`: 90 → 120 s.** Operator decision: keep the 25k budget and widen the time budget rather than reducing the prompt budget. At the measured 20–30k band rate (249 t/s) a 25k prefill is ~100 s, i.e. ~16 % margin under 120 s (and ~93 s / ~23 % margin at the band's p75 rate of ~270 t/s).

## Why (measured on this host, 2026-10-24/25)

Prompt-eval rates from `llama-server` logs (268 samples), size-dependent with a knee at ~27k:

| Prompt | Median rate | Prefill |
|---|---|---|
| 10–20k | 281 t/s | 36–71 s |
| 20–30k | 249 t/s | 80–100 s |
| 30–40k | 181 t/s | 165–210 s |
| 48k | 152 t/s | ~320 s |
| 63k | 114 t/s | ~563 s |

Consequences measured in the 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 window: **160 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events**, 45 local tasks cancelled mid-prefill, **~780k of ~840k prefill tokens computed then discarded (~93 % waste)**. A 38k cold prefill (~210 s) can never fit a 90 s deadline; 25k (~100 s) fits 120 s with ~16 % margin.

## Concrete configuration proposal

All changes are in `proxy/config.yaml` (server section); nothing else changes.

| Key | Now | Proposed | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` | 90 | **120** | 25k cold ≈ 100 s at the measured 20–30k band rate (249 t/s): 90 s cancels it, 120 s admits it with ~16 % margin (~23 % at p75). Ordering stays `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds (60) < deadline (120) < local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds (840) < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds (900)` and below the client's 900 s queue deadline. |
| `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` *(new)* | — | **25000** (0 = disabled/rollback) | Hard cap on **new (to-be-prefilled) tokens** at admission, enforced on **every** admission path including `routing_idle_admit` (the economic bypass admitted 38 oversized requests in the window and is a direct leak). Refuse at admission with `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`; never dispatch-then-cancel. |
| `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens` *(new; currently the hard-coded `CONSERVATIVE_MIN_TOKENS = 32_768` in `prefill_eta.py`)* | 32768 | **20000** | Extend the existing p75 ETA percentile pricing down to cover the 25k budget band. p75 ≈ 270 t/s for 20–30k → 25k ≈ 93 s ≤ 0.95 × 120 = 114 s ✓ admitted; 30–40k band p75 ≈ 190 t/s → 132 s ✗ refused. This is what stops a band-slow 25k from slipping past the flat cap. |
| `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction` *(new)* | — | **0.95** | Admit only when `eta_prefill_p75 ≤ 0.95 × deadline` (= 114 s at 120 s). Makes the budget deadline-relative instead of a bare token count, so future deadline changes stay consistent. |
| `local_admission_guard_reference_tokens` | 32000 | **25000** | Align the published-status reference prompt with the budget (one number instead of two). |
| `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` | 600 | **600 (unchanged)** | Now a backstop only; leave as-is. |
| `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` / `contention_queue_max_depth` | 60 / 8 | unchanged | Budget refusal happens before the queue. |
| Slot count / `session_slot_pool_size` | 2 / 2 | unchanged | Out of scope (see LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5). |

Left deliberately untouched: `cold_threshold` is *derived* (38000, from `_effective_large_context_thresholds` over per-slot ctx) and becomes a non-binding upper bound once the 25k measured budget exists; `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile` stays at 75 (it is simply applied from 20k upwards now).

Expected effect from the measured rates:

- >25k cold prompts (the 49k–93k thrash set): refused at admission → **zero** deadline cancellations for them (baseline: 160 events / 5.4 h, ~780k wasted tokens).
- 25k cold: 93–100 s, admitted and completed under the 120 s deadline.
- Warm requests (cached_ratio ≥0.9, e.g. 47k prompt / 549 new tokens): unchanged — the budget never binds.
- Residual deadline events: only genuine GPU-speed misses near the cap, priced at ≤114 s (p75).

Accepted trade-off of the 120 s choice: a near-budget prompt that *is* admitted and then lost consumes up to 114 s before the detour (vs 90 s today), +27 % worst-case waste per failed attempt — acceptable because the budget removes the systematically-doomed attempts, which were the source of the 93 % waste.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Budget:** `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000` caps the **new (prefilled) tokens** admitted for a local dispatch, on all admission paths (including idle/economic bypass). Over-budget requests are refused at admission (skip local, chain detours), never dispatched and never cancelled at the deadline.
- **AC2 — Deadline:** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`. Enforce and assert the ordering `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds (60) < deadline (120) < local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds (840) < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds (900)`, and keep the deadline strictly below the client's 900 s queue deadline (config-load assertion).
- **AC3 — Deadline-relative pricing:** budget admission uses p75 percentile ETA pricing from 20k tokens upwards (`local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens: 20000`) and admits only when `eta_prefill ≤ 0.95 × deadline` (114 s), so 25k at the 20–30k band is admitted and 25k in the 30–40k band is refused.
- **AC4 — Regression evidence (re-scoped 2026-10-25 by producer decision, option (b)):** over the certified post-deploy window — the >=24 h window starting at the first restart that carries the whole change, **2026-10-25 20:17:00 UTC → 2026-10-26 20:17:00 UTC** — the **admission-budget** criteria hold:
  1. **Zero over-budget admissions** — no local dispatch is accepted with `new_tokens > local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (25 000); over-budget prompts are refused at admission (`reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`) on every path.
  2. **Deadline rate <=10 % of baseline excluding audit loads** — scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events **from user traffic** are <=2.4/h (10 % of the 24.3/h measured baseline, 125 events / 5.15 h). Proxy `audit-*` sessions are excluded because they are agent audit traffic from parallel gate runs, not the user workload this item is priced for; the all-traffic rate is recorded alongside for transparency.
  3. **Wasted prefill tokens <=25 % of baseline** — the sum of cancelled dispatches' `new_tokens` is <=~38k/h (baseline ~151k/h).
  4. **No increase in client-visible 503s / provider-exhaustion errors** versus the equal-length pre-deploy window.

  The **eviction-counter** criterion is narrowed to what this item owns: `local_evictions_after_acceptance` must be **zero for the instrumentation reasons owned here** (`slot_assignment_freed` false positives, fixed in LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D) and otherwise contain **only** `prefill_deadline` events of the **second-slot head-of-line residual**, which is explicitly **out of scope for this item and is an acceptance criterion of the scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG** (tracked by LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I). No zero-tolerance requirement applies here to admitted-then-HOL-blocked prompts: this item deliberately does not reschedule requests or add slots (see Relationships), so a residual that no admission-budget change can prevent is not a failure of this AC.
  5. Every one of the four checks is recorded with its measured number and verdict.
- **AC5 — Warm path unchanged:** warm requests remain admissible when total prompt size exceeds 25k (assert e.g. 47k prompt / 549 new tokens stays local).
- **AC6 — Documentation + rollback:** config comments state units, interaction with `cold_threshold`/`warm_threshold` and the admission guard, and the rollback values (budget 0, deadline 90, percentile-min 32768, safety fraction off).
- **AC7 — Record post-acceptance eviction as an ERROR (defect signal, not noise):** any local dispatch that was **accepted** (admitted, dispatch record created) and then **evicted before producing a first byte** must be recorded at **ERROR** log level — never WARNING/INFO — with a structured, machine-parseable event carrying at least: `session`, `reason` (`prefill_deadline` | `no_progress_watchdog` | `idle_timeout` | `orphan_cleanup` | `lease_evicted` | `slot_assignment_freed`), `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `elapsed_s`, `slot_id`, and the llama task id where known. This covers every release path an accepted dispatch can suffer, so eviction after acceptance is unambiguously an error condition rather than expected churn; refusals **before** acceptance stay at their current level (a budget/ETA refusal is normal operation, not an error). Ship with: (a) a dedicated monotonic counter and per-reason breakdown exposed in the `--json` summary and the `proxy-usage-analysis` report (`local_evictions_after_acceptance`), (b) an alerting threshold of >0 for evictions of within-budget prompts, and (c) a documented triage rule that any such ERROR is treated as a defect and filed as a `test-failure`-class work item — it is exactly the signal that the budget/pricing model is wrong for a prompt band.

## Tests

- Unit: budget boundary (24,999 admitted / 25,001 refused); warm bypass above 25k prompt size; deadline ordering assertion rejects a violating config; safety-fraction maths (114 s at 120 s); band-slow 25k refused via p75 pricing.
- Integration: fixture replay of the 2026-10-24 thrash window → zero admitted cold prompts >25k; every refused request detours with a logged reason.
- AC7 (eviction-after-acceptance is an ERROR): for **each** release path an accepted dispatch can take (`prefill_deadline`, `no_progress_watchdog`, `idle_timeout`, `orphan_cleanup`, `lease_evicted`, `slot_assignment_freed`), assert exactly one ERROR-level structured event is emitted with the required fields (session, reason, estimated_tokens, new_tokens, eta_prefill_s, elapsed_s, slot_id, llama task id where known), and assert none is emitted at WARNING/INFO. Assert the inverse too: a **pre-acceptance refusal** (budget / ETA / admission-guard) produces **no** ERROR (normal operation, no false alarms). Assert the counter increments once per eviction and that `local_evictions_after_acceptance` appears in the `--json` summary and in the `proxy-usage-analysis` report with its per-reason breakdown. Replay the 2026-10-24 thrash window as a regression fixture: with AC1/AC3 in force the counter must be 0 for within-budget prompts (any non-zero count fails the test, because it means the pricing model admitted a doomed dispatch).

## Producer decision log

- **2026-10-25 — AC4 re-scoped (option (b)).** The post-deploy measurement (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I) delivered the budget half of AC4 (zero over-budget admissions; deadline rate -88 %; wasted prefill tokens -83 %; no 503 increase) but could not satisfy AC4's literal "eviction counter is zero for within-budget prompts": 94 of 116 counter events were instrumentation false positives (fixed and shipped in LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D) and the remaining 12 user-traffic events in 7.4 h are second-slot head-of-line blocking, which this item explicitly scopes out (no slot-count change, no rescheduling). Producer decision: re-scope AC4 to the admission-budget criteria above and make the HOL residual an acceptance criterion of the scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG. `needsProducerReview` cleared.

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (resident-prefix/tenancy admission). This item delivers the *budget* half of that item's AC3 ahead of the scheduler work and must ship independently; AC3 of LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG is to be re-scoped to the live-prefix pricing half when this lands.
- Do not increase the number of live slots in this item (per-slot ctx shrinks 131k → 87.4k at 3 slots).
data.title: Cold-prefill admission budget 25k tokens + prefill deadline 90s -> 120s, with post-acceptance eviction logged as ERROR

## Goal

Evaluate (with measurements, go/no-go) whether widening the **per-session KV snapshot pool** (`session_slot_pool_size` 2 → 4, snapshots under `session_slot_save_path/slot_<id>.bin`) raises local prefix reuse for the small/medium working set — as the recommended alternative to adding live llama slots, which would shrink per-slot context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots) and exclude the long-context sessions that dominate this workload.

## Why

- Measured prefix reuse is poor: aggregate 26.1 %, median **15.6 %** for prompts >20k tokens (227 prompts), 28 fully cold; 27 distinct sessions cycled through a 2-slot pool in ~5.4 h.
- More live slots buy *residency*, not throughput (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills), and cost per-slot address space for a long-context workload.
- The snapshot mechanism already exists (per-session save/restore, `session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds: 0.0015`, capped at `session_slot_max_timeout_seconds: 60`, pool capped by `session_slot_pool_size: 2`) but is degraded under load (`session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`, circuit-breaker cooldown). Restore cost estimate: ~50k tokens ≈ 75 s → capped 60 s, so the mechanism currently helps only the <40k band.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Benchmark:** measure save/restore latency (and disk footprint) per prompt-size band (10k / 25k / 40k / 60k+) on the production GPU host, including under load (another session streaming), against the 0.0015 s/token timeout model.
- **AC2 — Go/no-go with evidence:** with `session_slot_pool_size: 4` in a replay/bake-off on the 2026-10-24 thrash window (or equivalent fixture), report the reuse uplift (baseline 15.6 % median for >20k prompts) and the restore-success rate (skip_when_busy / cooldown exclusions).
- **AC3 — If go:** ship the config change plus retention/eviction semantics for 4 snapshots (pool eviction policy, disk cap, failure cooldowns unchanged) and any report/observability fields (restore-hit rate per session, snapshot pool occupancy) so the proxy-usage-analysis report can monitor the effect.
- **AC4 — If no-go:** record the measured blockers (latency, skip rate, restore failures) as a comment on this item so the decision is reproducible.
- **AC5 — No change to live slot count or per-slot ctx in this item** (that remains the separate 3-slot "fast" profile discussion).

## Tests

Bake-off harness replaying fixture logs + real save/restore micro-benchmark on the host; unit tests for pool-size > 2 retention semantics; report-schema tests for the new fields.

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (slot-churn / tenancy investigation, option 3a of the recommendation).
- This is an evaluation/deliberation item, not a mandate to change configuration.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD** – Slot-count benchmark: find optimal session_slot_pool_size for Qwen3 (completed)
- **LP-0MPOL5S7W007GRWB** – Include router model in slot save/restore requests (completed)
- **LP-0MU03AL730000B5W** – Slot counts: default and fast -> 1 slot, cheap -> 3 slots (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mvn1iqtf0037wtg, 20k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+140 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: 10k, 50k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+134 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: 10k, 50k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+134 more)

## Appendix — Open question from child LP-0MVOG8T9F0031JP5 (pool-4 semantics)

> **OPEN QUESTION (producer):** Parent AC5 states "no change to live slot count or
> per-slot ctx in this item". Candidate A (`session_slot_pool_size: 4`) necessarily
> changes both — 2 → 4 live slots and 126,976 → 61,440 per-slot clamp — because in this
> codebase that one key is the llama-server `--parallel` value, the lease cap, the slot-ID
> space and the persistence gate (see
> `docs/dev/slot-snapshot-pool-sizing-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` §1). Candidate B (a
> decoupled retained-snapshot pool, live slots fixed at 2) satisfies AC5 and is the only
> reading under which "4 snapshots" means what this item's title says.
>
> **Question:** does AC5 forbid candidate A outright — i.e. is candidate B the required
> interpretation of AC3's "4 snapshots"? Or is a geometry change acceptable here? Until
> answered, C6/C7 (go/no-go record, retention/eviction semantics) remain conditional.

## Objective

Execute the **24 h post-deploy verification of AC4** for `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`
(resident-prefix admission + session tenancy) on a restart-free production
window and record whether **scheduling-attributed** `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
cancellations fell by **≥ 90 %** against that same window's own re-anchored
baseline — plus the AC5 observability and AC6 lease-watchdog checks.

This item only measures and reports; it changes no scheduling logic.

## Problem statement

The epic's AC4 cannot be verified inside the implementing session: it needs a
full 24 h production soak on code that is actually running. Verification also
silently invalidates itself — the proxy restarted **six times on 2026-10-25**
(log rotations at 11:01:54, 11:21:20, 11:46:48, 18:57:27, 20:16:58 and
21:18:04 UTC), and each restart resets the in-memory residency/lease state, so
a window that contains a restart measures nothing. Without a pinned window,
attested uptime, and a window-scoped baseline, the ≥ 90 % claim is
unfalsifiable.

As the implementing agent for `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`, I need the failing-first unit
tests for the residency-aware admission ladder so that AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6 and AC7
(unit half) are pinned by executable, meaningful assertions before any production
code changes.

Store-of-truth fixtures: a stubbed `_last_slot_details_cache` snapshot (slot_id,
is_processing, context_tokens, timestamp) and a stubbed `session._slot_owners` map.
No HTTP, no `/slots` call, no sleeps — every matrix cell is a pure function call.

- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit coverage for: resident accept / non-resident reject, ratio boundary, tenancy bound, unknown-`context_tokens` fallback ladder, predicted-vs-actual divergence, and both reclaim bounds (this item authors those tests first).
- **AC7 (unit) — resident accept / non-resident reject:** tests assert the ladder admits a large prompt when the session's measured `reuse_ratio` is at/above `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` and skips local with reason `resident_prefix_insufficient` when below it.
