# Implementation: wire capacity verdict into refusal builder, 429 body and log line

Parent: LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6.

## Goal

Make `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` the only source of the classification at every local-route refusal exit in `provider.py`, surface the verdict in the 429 body and in exactly one log line, and change nothing else (no timing, queue, lease, header or promotion change).

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
  - `_build_local_only_refusal_response(attempt, config, preference=None)` computes the verdict **exactly once** via `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` using evidence already on `attempt` (`reason`, `new_tokens`, `budget_tokens` from `_local_admission_evidence` / `_admission_token_evidence`); no reason table, no second estimator, no re-derivation (parent AC1/AC3). The preference parameter defaults so existing direct unit-test callers keep working.
  - Body: add `"verdict": "deferrable" | "too_large"` to the 429 JSON payload — additive only; `reason`, `retryable`, `eta_prefill_seconds`, `budget_seconds`, `projected_wait_seconds`, `retry_after`/`retry_at`, `suggested_action` and `X-Local-Route: refused` stay byte-identical (parent AC2/AC3).
  - Log line: extend the existing single-per-refusal line (`local_only_refused reason=%s preference=%s`) with `verdict=%s`, keeping the `local_only_refused ` prefix so existing greps in `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py` (`startswith("local_only_refused ")`, `_parse_kv`) stay green. The line names the **parsed** preference (threaded in from the call sites), verdict and reason and is emitted exactly once per refusal, not per skip branch (parent AC4). The parent deliverable's `local_capacity_verdict ...`-prefixed alternative is acceptable only if the reflecting tests are updated with it.
  - Thread the resolved preference from the choke point `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote` (both dispatch cycles) and the two `refused_local_only` branches (queue and lease denial paths) into the builder so the log line names the actual preference (parent AC4/AC5).
  - Comments/docstrings updated at every call site that now consults the verdict — builder docstring, choke point, both `refused_local_only` branches — stating the single-implementation contract (parent AC6).
  - Flip the `xfail(strict=True)` verdict assertions from the test child.

## Boundaries (explicitly out of scope)

- `_build_exhausted_response` / `_build_local_admission_reject_response` (chain-exhausted path; the "All providers exhausted" wording is LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ) and the direct free-slot local-only branch that returns the exhausted response — unchanged here.
- `_refusal_retry_timing` untouched (no timing change); no queue/lease/slot change; no new header (`X-Local-Verdict` header work belongs to LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 if wanted); no `too_large` remote promotion (LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE).
- Fail-safe preserved: an unclassifiable exit keeps today's pin-local refusal; the verdict never promotes a request to remote.
- The **second** `_log_local_only_refusal(...)` caller — the free-slot local-only branch that returns `_build_exhausted_response(...)` (`provider.py:11536`) — is out of scope: it keeps its current two-key line (`reason=… preference=…`, no `verdict=`) and must not gain a verdict field here.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (~6526), `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` choke point (~6686), `_log_local_only_refusal()` (~6506), both dispatch-cycle call sites (~10057 remote-first, ~10742 local-first, `refused_local_only` ~10931 and ~11946).
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — read-only: the `local_capacity_verdict` helper and vocabulary (delivered by dependency LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — flip the xfail markers written by the test child.
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py` — the existing `startswith("local_only_refused ")` + `_parse_kv` greps (`~743-790`) constrain this item's log format; `reason` / `preference` stay in place and only `verdict=` is appended, so those assertions keep passing (re-pinned only if the vocabulary alias has already made the parsed preference `local-preferred`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 The only verdict computation in `provider.py` is the `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` call inside the refusal builder; the choke point and both `refused_local_only` branches route through it (no reason table, no re-derivation).
- AC2 A deferrable refusal returns 429 with body `verdict: "deferrable"`, `reason` unchanged, `X-Local-Route: refused`, and retry timing exactly as `_refusal_retry_timing` already produced it (no timing change).
- AC3 A too-large refusal returns 429 with body `verdict: "too_large"` and the existing `reason` (`prefill_budget_exceeded` or `context_too_large`).
- AC4 Exactly one log line per refusal names preference + verdict + reason (the extended `local_only_refused` line; asserted with `caplog`).
- AC5 `prefer-local` and `remote-ok` behaviour is unchanged (existing tests keep passing) and no promotion to remote is introduced.
- AC6 Comments and docstrings are updated at every call site that now consults the verdict.
- AC7 The `xfail(strict=True)` verdict assertions from the test child are flipped green; changed-scope test gate passes (full suite enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- Import the helper; never copy its rules (`provider.py` must not contain a verdict `if reason in (...)` table).
- Verdict is additive in the 429 body; no existing field is renamed or removed; no double header stamping.
- No retry-timing change, no queue/lease behaviour change, no config-default change.

## Design decisions (plan session 2026-10-28)

| # | Decision | Reason / trace |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | The verdict is computed **once**, at the top of `_build_local_only_refusal_response()`, into a single `admission_reserve.CapacityVerdict`; that one object feeds **both** the 429 body field and the log line. | Two calls (one for the body, one for the log) could disagree and would already be a second computation (AC1/AC4). |
| D2 | The builder passes the helper only evidence already on `attempt` — `reason`, `new_tokens`, `budget_tokens` (from `_local_admission_evidence()` / `_admission_token_evidence()`). It does **not** read `config` for `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` and never estimates tokens. | The guard's own numbers are already on `attempt`; re-reading config would create a second envelope source (parent AC1/AC3). The helper's raw `estimated_tokens` / `context_limit` form is for the dispatch cycles and is not needed here. |
| D3 | No `try/except` around the helper call inside `provider.py`. | The helper is pure and total — its own AC4 makes an unknown/absent input fail safe to `deferrable`. A provider-side fallback verdict would be a second fail-safe implementation (AC1). |
| D4 | Signature `_build_local_only_refusal_response(attempt, config=None, preference: str \| None = None)`; `preference=None` resolves to today's `_PREF_LOCAL_ONLY`, so every existing direct unit-test caller keeps its current `preference=local-only` line byte-for-byte. All four production call sites pass the parsed `_preference` explicitly. | Backwards compatibility for direct callers (deliverable requires the default). In production the line names the **parsed** preference, which becomes `local-preferred` once the alias child LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 lands — that drift is expected; behaviour is unchanged (AC5) and only the logged value follows the parse. |
| D5 | `_log_local_only_refusal(reason, preference=None, verdict=None)` appends `verdict=%s` **only** when a verdict is supplied. | Keeps the out-of-scope free-slot/exhausted caller byte-identical (two keys) while the refusal builder gains the third key (AC4). The `local_only_refused ` prefix and the `reason=` / `preference=` keys stay in place, so `startswith("local_only_refused ")` and `_parse_kv` in `test_routing_preference_logging.py` keep working. |
| D6 | Preference threading: `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` forwards its existing `preference` parameter; both `refused_local_only` branches forward `_preference` (verified in scope at both). | AC4/AC5 — the line names the actual intent rather than a constant. |
| D7 | `payload["verdict"]` is added next to `reason`; `verdict=` is appended **after** `preference=` in the log line. No header is added. | Additive-only (parent AC2/AC3); a `X-Local-Verdict` header belongs to LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 if it is wanted. |
| D8 | The xfail flip lands in the **same** change as the wiring, not as a follow-up. | Removing `strict=True` before the behaviour exists would silently lose the assertion; removing it together keeps the TDD gate meaningful (AC7). |

## Existing state (verified during planning)

# Test: single-implementation spy — both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder

Parent: LP-0MVSMI7JK002FKUF (child of LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6).

## Goal

Pin the single-implementation contract (parent AC1) with a failing-first spy
test: replace `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict` with a recording
wrapper that returns a **sentinel** verdict, drive every call site, and prove
each one routes through the helper exactly once and that the 429 body carries
the sentinel verbatim.

## Deliverables

`proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` (focused addition; the module already
imports `proxy.provider` and `proxy.admission_reserve` and drives
`proxy.proxy_with_fallback`):

- A small spy helper, e.g. `_spy_capacity_verdict(sentinel="spy-sentinel-verdict")`,
  returning `(wrapper, calls)` where `wrapper` records each call's
  `args`/`kwargs` and returns a real `CapacityVerdict`-shaped object carrying the
  sentinel verdict (so the builder's normal path runs and the body is produced).
  Patch it at `proxy.admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict` — the module
  `provider.py` imports it from — never at the builder, or the contract is not
  exercised.
- Four assertions, each `== 1` call and each asserting
  `json.loads(response.body)["verdict"] == sentinel` on the 429:
  1. **Remote-first cycle** — `provider.proxy_with_remote_fallback` on a
     remote-only chain with `X-Local-Preference: local-only` (the
     `local_only_no_local_route` refusal). Mirror the harness of
     `test_remote_fallback_cycle_enforces_the_local_only_choke_point` in
     `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`.
  2. **Local-first cycle, choke-point row** — `provider.proxy_with_fallback`
     with a chain-cooldown exit (`_provider_unavailable_until[local] = now+60`).
  3. **Local-first cycle, `refused_local_only` branch** — a queue-expiry or
     admission-reject exit (reuse the row fixtures already in
     `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` semantics: contention-queue wait
     expiry, or the calibrated-gate denial on the free-slot path).
  4. **Refusal builder called directly** — `provider._build_local_only_refusal_response({"reason": ..., "eta_prefill_seconds": 31.7, "budget_seconds": 60.0})`.
- A negative/guard assertion: with `prefer-local` and `remote-ok` (and an
  absent header) the spy records **zero** calls (no verdict is produced for a
  non-refusal path) — this is the observability counterpart of parent AC5 and
  prevents the helper being called per skip branch.
- Module docstring note stating the contract this file now pins ("one call per
  refusal, verdict never re-derived in `provider.py`").

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — the spy test (new content only).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — **read-only** reference for
  the dispatch harness (`_issue`, `_DummyRequest`, `_model_config`, `_config`,
  `_MutableConcurrency`); copy the minimal harness into the new test rather
  than importing across test modules.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only: `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote`
  (~6686), `_build_local_only_refusal_response` (~6526), both dispatch-cycle
  call sites (~10057 remote-first, ~10742 local-first, `refused_local_only`
  ~10931 and ~11946).
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — read-only source of
  `local_capacity_verdict` (delivered by dependency LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 Exactly one implementation is used by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder: a patch/spy test replaces admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict with a recording wrapper returning a sentinel verdict, and proves each call site — the remote-first dispatch cycle, the local-first dispatch cycle and the refusal builder — routes through it exactly once, with the 429 body carrying the sentinel verdict verbatim (no re-derived verdict, no second reason table).
- AC2 Tests are written before the wiring implementation (TDD): the new spy verdict assertions start xfail(strict=True) and are flipped by the implementation child.
- AC3 Changed-scope test gate passes with the xfail markers (expected failures are green); full suite enforced at the dev-push gate.
- AC4 With `X-Local-Preference: prefer-local` and `remote-ok` (and an absent
  header) the spy records **zero** calls — no verdict for a non-refusal path
  (the observability counterpart of parent AC5); the module docstring note pins
  the contract ("one call per refusal, verdict never re-derived in
  `provider.py`").

## Constraints

- Status note (plan run 2026-10-28): the helper has landed —
  `local_capacity_verdict` is at `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` (~222,
  delivered by LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB), and `provider.py` does **not** call it
  yet, so the four spy assertions fail with zero calls today and must start
  `xfail(strict=True)` (AC2) — flipped green by the wiring child
  LP-0MVSMINPR006SWT6.

- Test-only change: `provider.py` and `admission_reserve.py` are **not**
  modified here (wiring is the sibling LP-0MVSMINPR006SWT6; the helper itself
  is LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB).
- Patch the helper, never the builder: stubbing the builder would pass while
  the single-implementation contract was violated.
- Do not modify or weaken any existing test in the file; the addition is
  purely additive.
- The spy must return a *real* verdict object (not a mock) so the 429 body is
  produced by production code and the sentinel can travel through it verbatim.
- Run tests via the test skill (`run_tests.py`, changed scope), never ad-hoc
  `pytest`.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator reading the daily proxy usage report, I want the GPU busy-time
figure to reflect the *hardware's* actual compute activity (measured from GPU
power draw at 15-second resolution) rather than only the proxy's logged slot
occupancy, so I can tell how hard the GPU really worked and spot gaps between
proxy accounting and reality.

## Context

The report's `## Local model utilization` section computed "busy" entirely from
proxy logs (`aggregation.BusyStats`): it pairs `Stream started`/`Stream
finished` events, extends each back to its dispatch time, clips to the window
and unions the intervals. That measures *slot occupancy* — including queued
time and excluding GPU work the proxy did not log — not hardware utilisation.

On this Strix Halo APU `gpu_busy_percent` is pinned at 100% and is unusable
(LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP). Power draw is the discriminating signal; the
`gpu:computing:bool` recording rule (`power >= 90 W`) is evaluated by
Prometheus every 15 s from the node_exporter hwmon series
(`monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`).

## Change

Add a hardware-side, power-based GPU busy measurement alongside the log-based
figures:

- New module `gpu_busy.py` queries `avg_over_time(gpu:computing:bool[Nh])`
  (raw 15 s series) and the 5-minute-smoothed `gpu:power_watts:avg5m` trace.
- `reporting.run_analysis` populates `AnalysisResult.gpu_busy` best-effort
  (None if Prometheus is unreachable — the report never fails).
- The utilization table gains a `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` row, the
  `--json` summary gains a `gpu_busy` block, and the CLI text summary names
  the power-based figure.
- Docs: `SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` describe the method and the 15 s cadence.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` row appears in the `## Local model
   utilization` table with the power-based busy time and %, and is omitted
   (no crash) when Prometheus is unavailable.
2. `--json` exposes `gpu_busy` with `computing_fraction`, `busy_pct`,
   `busy_seconds`, `idle_seconds`, `total_seconds`, and the `smoothed_power`
   trace; `gpu_busy` is `null` when the query fails.
3. The computation uses `avg_over_time(gpu:computing:bool[Nh])` over the raw
   15-second series (not a down-sampled 1-minute pull of a smoothed series).
4. Unit tests cover: instant (`value`) and matrix (`values`) response formats,
   Prometheus-unreachable, empty result, invalid/out-of-range values,
   zero/negative window, JSON round-trip, and report row rendering.
5. `ruff check` is clean and the proxy-usage-analysis test suite passes.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_gpu_busy.py`

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`

## Goal (user story)

As an operator reading the proxy usage report (and any gate or alert that quotes
a "busy" percentage), I want the **non-GPU, log-derived local busy time**
(`dispatch → finish` slot union) used as *the* local model utilisation figure,
so that decisions are made on proxy-measured slot occupancy rather than on the
power-based hardware `GPU busy` proxy, which counts GPU activity the proxy does
not serve and therefore overstates local model utilisation.

## Problem statement

The usage report currently publishes two incompatible "busy" percentages and
the operator-facing surfaces do not consistently say which one is the local
utilisation figure. For the 2026-10-27 22:10 → 2026-10-28 22:10 window they
diverge by ~27 points (log-derived 12.6 %, power-based 39.3 %), and the
`LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG` gate quotes the power figure in its precondition/AC0
while its AC1 reads the log-derived section — so a decision can be made on the
wrong number. `REFERENCE.md` already names the log union as primary; the code
and the gate wording have drifted from that intent.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** deciding whether local capacity is contended
  (e.g. the ">60 % local busy night" gate) — needs one authoritative number.
- **Analyst** reading `## Local model utilization` and the stdout summary —
  needs the hardware power figure kept, but clearly marked as *not* local model
  utilisation.
- **Machine consumer** of `--json` — needs stable, separately-named keys with
  unambiguous semantics.

Example user story: *"As a producer gating a slot-geometry experiment, I want
the report's busy % and the gate's precondition to mean the same thing (log
slot occupancy), so that a 12.6 % busy night cannot be recorded as 39.3 %
contended."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Every decision-facing "busy %" in the report and its JSON summary is the log-derived `local_busy` (`dispatch → finish`); the power-based `gpu_busy` value remains available but is never presented as the local utilisation figure (it is labelled `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` and carries an explicit "not local model utilisation" note).
- AC2: The CLI stdout summary states the log-derived busy percentage as the local busy figure and, when `gpu_busy` is present, reports it separately with a label that distinguishes hardware activity from served local work.
- AC3: LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG's precondition/AC0 wording is corrected to quote the log-derived `local_busy` (documented via a comment on that item; this item does not change its status).
- AC4: `REFERENCE.md` states which busy figure is authoritative for decisions, when to prefer each, and why the two differ (log gaps, unfinished streams, GPU work outside the proxy's slot accounting) — matching the code.
- AC5: A regression test asserts that the summary/JSON busy figure used for decisions is the log-derived one and that `gpu_busy` remains a separate, clearly-labelled key (fixtures from real log lines, no live Prometheus dependency).
- AC6: A re-run of the analysis for the same 24h window produces the log-derived 12.6% figure in the decision-facing position, with the power figure still visible but no longer leading.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, and any relevant docs entries.
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Existing state (verified against the code, 2026-10-30)

- `scripts/reporting.py::_append_busy_section` already **leads** with
  `Busy time — upper bound (dispatch → finish)` and appends the hardware row as
  `| GPU busy — power-based (hardware) |` — so the table ordering is already
  compliant. Gap: the note under the table calls the power figure "the
  authoritative hardware-side busy measure" without stating it is **not** local
  model utilisation (AC1's explicit note is missing).
- `scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` stdout already prints the log-derived
  `local model busy (dispatch → finish) X%` first and appends
  `GPU busy (power-based, 15s sampling) Y%`. Gap: the appended label does not
  distinguish hardware activity from served local work, and does not say the
  figure is not local utilisation (AC2).
- `reporting.summary_to_json` already exposes `local_busy` (with an explicit
  `definition` marker) and `gpu_busy` as **separate keys**, and
  `_gpu_busy_json` returns `None` when Prometheus is unreachable — already
  compliant in structure; the gap is wording/labels and the absence of a
  regression test pinning the precedence.
- `REFERENCE.md` § *GPU busy time from power (Prometheus)* says the log union is
  "primary" and the power row "authoritative hardware-side", and explains why
  the two differ — but never states which is authoritative **for decisions**
  nor when to prefer each (AC4).
- `SKILL.md` (lines ~89–105) documents the power row as hardware-side; needs a
  matching "not local utilisation / decisions use `local_busy`" statement.
- `tests/test_gpu_busy.py` covers `gpu_busy` computation and `_gpu_busy_json`
  rendering; **no test** asserts that the decision-facing figure is the
  log-derived one (AC5).
- `LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG` (Gate: verify 60% local busy night) AC1 reads the
  report's `## Local model utilization` section, but its *Parent AC0 trace* says
  ">60% GPU busy" — the wording to correct in AC3.
- Log retention for the AC6 window is confirmed present: `/var/log/llama-proxy/`
  holds `proxy.log.2026-10-27_22.gz`, `proxy.log.2026-10-28_04.gz`,
  `proxy.log.2026-10-28_10.gz`, `proxy.log.2026-10-28_16`, … (checked
  2026-10-30), so the 2026-10-27 22:10 → 2026-10-28 22:10 window can be
  re-analysed.

## Desired change

Make the log-derived `local_busy` the single decision-facing utilisation
figure on every operator surface, while retaining the power-based figure as
clearly-labelled, non-leading, supplementary hardware telemetry:

1. Report note + row label: state explicitly that `GPU busy — power-based
   (hardware)` is hardware activity, **not** local model utilisation, and that
   `local_busy` is the decision figure.
2. stdout summary: label the log-derived figure as *the* local busy figure and
   label the power figure as hardware-only (e.g. "GPU busy — power-based
   (hardware, not local model utilisation)").
3. `REFERENCE.md` + `SKILL.md`: a short authoritative-figure subsection —
   decisions use `local_busy`; prefer `gpu_busy` only for hardware questions

4. Regression test (fixtures, no live Prometheus) asserting the precedence and
   the separate `gpu_busy` key/label.
5. Comment correcting `LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG`'s precondition/AC0 wording (no

- No live Prometheus dependency in tests; use real-log fixtures

data.title: Use the non-GPU (log-derived) local busy time as the decision-facing utilisation figure

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As an operator reading the proxy usage report, I want the question "should GPU
utilisation come from `amd-smi` (or a tool like `amdtop`) instead of power
draw?" answered **once, with measured evidence, in the place I would look** —
so the power-based `gpu:computing:bool` measurement is not replaced by a
counter that saturates on this APU, and nobody re-litigates the decision.

## Answer (measured on this host, 2026-10-28)

**No — do not switch.** Two separate facts, both measured here:

1. `amd-smi` returns `N/A` for every metric the report needs on this
   `gfx1151` APU; `rocm-smi` and `amdtop` reach a value only by reading the
   **same** `gpu_busy_percent` sysfs counter this repo already samples.
2. That counter is **not a utilisation measure**: it latches to ~100 % as soon
   as the GPU draws more than ~20 W and only falls back at < 20 W. Over 7 days
   of Prometheus history it read ≥ 90 % for 93.8 % of samples while the GPU was
   at compute power (≥ 90 W) only 28.1 % of the time — i.e. **45 % false-busy**.

### amd-smi / rocm-smi / amdtop probes

| Probe | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GPU inventory | `amd-smi list` | one GPU, BDF `0000:c5:00.0` (the APU) |
| Engine usage | `amd-smi metric --usage`, `amd-smi monitor` | `USAGE: N/A`; `GFX% = N/A` |
| Power | `amd-smi metric --power`, `amd-smi monitor` | `SOCKET_POWER: N/A`, `POWER = N/A`, `PWR_CAP = N/A` |
| Clocks / thermals | `amd-smi metric --clock -t`, `amd-smi monitor` | `GFX_CLK: N/A`, `GPU_T/MEM_T: N/A` |
| Energy counter | `amd-smi metric --energy` | `energy: "N/A"` |
| Memory | `amd-smi monitor --json` | `vram_used 0.3 GB / vram_total 1.0 GB` — VRAM only; an APU serves from GTT, so this misdescribes the host |
| `rocm-smi` (same family) | `rocm-smi --showuse --showpower` | power `108 W` (same `hwmon` node), `GPU use 100%` (the `gpu_busy_percent` counter) |
| `amdtop` (Linux) | source: `linux.go:151` — `os.ReadFile(gpuDevPath + "/gpu_busy_percent")` (`zyoung11/amdtop` @ `5e500c3`) | "GPU usage" **is** `gpu_busy_percent`; power/temp come from the same `hwmon` `power1_average`/`temp1_input` the report uses; VRAM from `mem_info_vram_*` (not GTT). Windows uses ADLX, a Windows-only driver library — irrelevant here |
| Working alternative (already in use) | `hwmon5/power1_average` | 11–26 W idle, 91–120 W under decode/prefill — live and discriminating |
| No joule counter | `ls hwmon5/energy*` | absent, so no energy accumulator either |

`amdtop` therefore adds no new signal: it renders the same counter the pinned
`gpu_busy_percent` caveat already covers.

### Why the counter cannot be the utilisation figure (7-day evidence)

Prometheus has scraped `gpu_busy_percent` "for continuity only" since the
monitoring stack shipped, so the premise could finally be quantified instead of
asserted. Query: `gpu_busy_percent` vs `gpu:power_watts:amdgpu`, 5-min steps,
7 days to 2026-10-28 23:40 UTC (904 paired samples).

| GPU power band | samples | mean `gpu_busy_percent` | share ≥ 90 % |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–20 W | 44 | 2.3 % | 2 % |
| 20–40 W | 414 | 98.9 % | 99 % |
| 40–60 W | 90 | 100.0 % | 100 % |
| 60–80 W | 7 | 100.0 % | 100 % |
| 80–90 W | 96 | 100.0 % | 100 % |
| 90–100 W | 175 | 99.1 % | 98 % |
| 100–125 W | 78 | 95.7 % | 95 % |

It is a **bang-bang indicator that saturates at ~20 W**, not a graded
utilisation measure: once the GPU draws > 20 W it reads ~100 % no matter
whether that is 25 W (idle-with-resident-context) or 120 W (prefill). Summary
statistics: mean 94.5 % vs 28.1 % power-derived computing time; Pearson
`r(busy, power) = 0.28`; false-busy (`busy ≥ 90 %` ∧ `power < 40 W`) 45.2 % of
samples, longest continuous run **5.3 h**; false-idle (`busy < 90 %` ∧
`power ≥ 90 W`) 0.8 % — it never *under*-reports, which is why a short
observation (it does ramp 0 → 55 → 83 → 99 under load and decays afterwards)
looks convincing while an hour-scale view exposes the latch.

Consequence: the report's power-derived `gpu:computing:bool ≥ 90 W` figure
stays the discriminating hardware signal; `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` and `amdtop`
are all the same saturated counter (or `N/A`), and neither adds history — a
24 h window needs a time series, which the existing 10 s sysfs sampler →
node_exporter → Prometheus pipeline (90 d retention) already provides.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Why is GPU utilisation measured from power and not
  from AMD's own tool (or `amdtop`)?" — wants the documented, evidence-backed
  answer where the measurement is described (`monitoring/README.md`, the
  usage-analysis `REFERENCE.md`), not a restated assertion.
- **Agent working a usage/observability question (secondary).** Needs the
  decision pinned so it is not "improved" into an `amd-smi`/`amdtop` shell-out
  that would silently report a saturated number as utilisation.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-28)

| Capability | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Power-based GPU busy in the usage report | `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` (`avg_over_time(gpu:computing:bool[Nh])`), row `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` | Done (LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4) |
| Power recording rules | `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` (`gpu:power_watts:amdgpu`, `gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`) | Done (LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48) |
| Rationale "why not `gpu_busy_percent`" | rule-file header, `monitoring/README.md` §527, `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` §107, `REFERENCE.md`, `SKILL.md`, doc-guard test `test_documents_the_pinned_busy_counter_caveat` | Done — but worded as an unexplained **"pinned at 100 %"** assertion |
| Quantified characterisation of the counter (latch at ≥ 20 W, 45 % false-busy) | — | **Missing** (this item) |
| Rationale "why not `amd-smi` / `rocm-smi` / `amdtop`" | — | **Missing** (this item) |
| Guard preventing an `amd-smi`/`amdtop` shell-out | — | **Missing** (this item) |

## Desired change

Document the measured decision and pin it with a test — **no behaviour change**:

1. `monitoring/README.md`: replace the bare "pinned at 100 %" assertions (§202
   rationale, §273 series list, §527 troubleshooting) with the measured
   statement (bang-bang at ~20 W, 7-day figures, dated) and add a "Why not
   `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`" subsection carrying the condensed `N/A`
   table and the `amdtop` source finding.
2. `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` (§107 series table) and the header of
   `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`: same correction, keeping the "must not
   be used in a rule" wording intact.
3. `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` (§ GPU busy time from power)
   and `SKILL.md` (same section): one sentence each stating that `amd-smi`
   reports `N/A` and `amdtop`/`rocm-smi` just read the saturating
   `gpu_busy_percent`, cross-linking `monitoring/README.md`.
4. `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`: extend the doc-guard coverage
   (pattern: `test_documents_the_pinned_busy_counter_caveat`) so the docs must
   record the `amd-smi` `N/A` finding and the measured saturating behaviour,
   and assert `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` contains no
   `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi` subprocess call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The work item records the decision and its measured evidence: the `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi`/`amdtop` probe table (with the `amdtop` source line reference `linux.go:151`, commit `5e500c3`), the 7-day power-band table, and the two structural reasons (no history; same saturating counter) — each reproducible with the listed commands/queries.
- AC2: `monitoring/README.md` no longer asserts an unexplained "pinned at 100 %": every GPU-utilisation rationale there states the measured behaviour (latches to ~100 % above ~20 W; ≥ 90 % in 93.8 % of 7-day samples vs 28.1 % at compute power; 45 % false-busy) with the measurement date, and a "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`" subsection records that `amd-smi` is `N/A` on this APU and that `amdtop`/`rocm-smi` read only `gpu_busy_percent`, naming `hwmon` → Prometheus `gpu:computing:bool` as the retained source.
- AC3: `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` and the `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` header carry the same measured statement, and both keep an explicit prohibition on selecting `gpu_busy_percent` in any rule.
- AC4: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` § GPU busy time from power and `SKILL.md` § GPU busy time from power each state that `amd-smi` is not the source on this APU (`N/A`) and that `amdtop`-style tools only surface the saturating counter, cross-linking `monitoring/README.md`.
- AC5: A test in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` asserts the docs record the `amd-smi` decision and the measured saturating behaviour, and asserts `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` contains no `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi`/`amdtop` subprocess call; it fails if the doc statement is removed (verified by temporarily deleting it), and `test_documents_the_pinned_busy_counter_caveat` still passes with the corrected wording.
- AC6: No behaviour change: `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24 --json` still returns a non-null `gpu_busy` with the same keys (`computing_fraction`, `busy_seconds`, `idle_seconds`, `busy_pct`, `idle_pct`, `total_seconds`, `smoothed_power`), and the report still shows the `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` row; no rule expression, threshold or exporter config changes.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Documentation + guard tests only.** No new dependencies, no new sampler, no
  `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi`/`amdtop` invocation in the report path, no change to the
  `gpu_busy` JSON contract, the 90 W threshold, the recording rules or the
  wedge-detector behaviour (its disable remains justified — the counter
  saturates at ≥ 20 W, so `gpu_busy_percent >= 90` fires while idle).
- Measured evidence must be reproducible offline; the guard test must not shell
  out to `amd-smi`/`amdtop` (neither exists on every host) — it inspects source
  text and docs only.
- Edits to `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` are in scope because the
  operator's question concerns that project skill; the global install
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills`) is not touched.
- UK English throughout.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: doc rot.** Kernel 7.0.0-34 already changed the counter's behaviour
  relative to the 2026-07-31 "pinned from boot" observation (kernel 7.0.0-28),
  so the wording must be dated and phrased as a measurement with the query
  used, making a re-measure obvious. *Mitigation:* AC1/AC2 require the date and
  the commands; the 7-day analysis is repeatable from Prometheus history.
- **Risk: over-claiming.** The latch could be a sampling artefact of the
  textfile sampler. *Mitigation:* the band table uses 15 s scrapes (the sampler
  writes at 10 s) and the 5-min step samples the instant value, so the latch is
  the counter's own behaviour; AC2 cites the figures rather than a mechanism.
- **Risk: over-broad guard.** A source-text test could ossify the
  implementation. *Mitigation:* assert only the absence of an
  `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi`/`amdtop` shell-out in `gpu_busy.py`, not its structure.
- **Assumption (pending producer confirmation):** the desired outcome is to
  *record the measured decision*, not to build an alternative
  hardware-utilisation sampler. The remaining avenue
  (`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`, struct 264 B, format revision 3.0,
  populated and live — the interface that yields real GFX-activity
  accumulators) is filed as **LP-0MVSQT7YC0045HFW** rather than folded in here.
- **Assumption:** "medium" priority (operator-specified) — the current
  measurement is correct, so this is decision hygiene plus a documentation
  correction, not a defect.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `monitoring/README.md` — rationale (§202), series list (§273) and troubleshooting (§527) corrected; new "Why not `amd-smi`/`rocm-smi`/`amdtop`" subsection
- `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` — series-table wording correction (§107)
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — header comment: measured statement replaces the bare pinned assertion
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` — cross-reference in § GPU busy time from power
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — same section, one sentence
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — doc-guard additions + no-shell-out assertion
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` — no change expected; the module whose docstring must state the decision

## Related work

- LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4 — Proxy usage report: hardware power-based GPU busy time (15 s sampling) — implemented the row this item defends.
- LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48 — GPU utilisation must come from power (rules, threshold, dead alert groups) — the precedent rationale, now quantifiable.
- LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP — GPU-wedge detector false positives — origin of the pinned-`gpu_busy_percent` finding (2026-07-31, kernel 7.0.0-28); still valid, with a better explanation.
- LP-0MVSQT7YC0045HFW — `gpu_metrics` as a true GFX-activity signal (discovered-from this item).
- LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation history — where a *new* signal belongs.
- LP-0MVSPWLLP008AQXZ — Use the log-derived local busy time as the decision-facing figure — related "which busy number is authoritative" decision.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`, `monitoring/prometheus.yml`, `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` — the pipeline that stays.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (operator, 2026-10-28):** "In the usage report skill we estimate GPU use by measuring power consumption. This is an AMD GPU and we can use the `amd-smi` CLI — should we switch to using that? (priority medium)." — **Answer:** researched on the live host: no. `amd-smi` 26.2.2 / ROCm 7.2.4 reports `N/A` for usage, socket power, clocks, thermals and energy on the single `gfx1151` device. Source: operator request + local measurement.
- **Q (operator, follow-up, 2026-10-28):** "The github project `amdtop` has GPU usage — check its source to see how it gets it (`https://github.com/zyoung11/amdtop`)." — **Answer:** cloned at `5e500c3`; Linux "GPU usage" is `gpu_busy_percent` read directly from sysfs (`linux.go:151`), power/temp from the same `hwmon` files, VRAM from `mem_info_vram_*` (not GTT); Windows uses ADLX. So `amdtop` surfaces exactly the counter this repo already samples — no new information. Source: cloned source + `grep`; corroborated by `rocm-smi --showuse` reporting the same 100 % figure.
- **Q (agent → operator):** scope — (a) record the measured decision in docs + guard tests, or (b) also build a new hardware-utilisation sampler on `gpu_metrics`. **Recommended:** (a) — the existing measurement is correct; a new sampler already has an owner in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W. **Answer (operator, 2026-10-28):** (a) — land the docs. Scope confirmed; this item proceeds to implementation as documentation corrections plus guard tests, with no behaviour change. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q (agent → operator):** should the `gpu_metrics` follow-up (LP-0MVSQT7YC0045HFW) be raised from `low`? **Recommended:** yes — the saturating counter leaves a real measurement gap. **Answer (operator, 2026-10-28):** yes, make it high. Applied: `wl update LP-0MVSQT7YC0045HFW --priority high`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Research summary:** the counter does respond to load within seconds (0 % idle → 55 → 83 → 99 % during decode, decaying after), which is why `amdtop`/`rocm-smi` look plausible in a live demo; but over 7 days of Prometheus history it saturates at ~100 % for any draw above ~20 W, giving 93.8 % "busy" against 28.1 % at compute power and 45 % false-busy samples. Effective resolution of the retained pipeline is the 15 s scrape interval; the report's power threshold (90 W) sits inside the genuinely-computing band (91–120 W observed under decode/prefill).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVSQT7YC0045HFW** – Investigate /sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics as a true GFX-activity signal on gfx1151 (open)
- **LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4** – Proxy usage report: hardware power-based GPU busy time (15s sampling) (completed)
- **LP-0MS91D782006XIR6** – GPU wedged at 100% busy by hung KV-cache slot save/restore - severe inference slowdown (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+389 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+389 more)

data.title: Evaluate amd-smi as the GPU utilisation source for the usage report (record the decision)

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator I need a **measured, reproducible verdict** on whether
`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` (the `amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob, the
interface `amdgpu_top` reads) carries a *graded* GFX-activity signal on this
Strix Halo APU — one that separates compute from idle the way the
power-derived `gpu:computing:bool` rule does but `gpu_busy_percent` does not —
and, only if such a field passes an explicit discrimination bar, to have it
published as a Prometheus series through the existing 10 s textfile sampler.
A negative verdict, recorded with numbers so the path is never retried, is an
equally valid outcome.

## Problem statement

The usage report's GPU busy time infers activity from power draw
(`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot tell GFX work from any other
power draw. `gpu_busy_percent` was eliminated as a utilisation signal
(2026-10-28: 45.2 % false-busy, Pearson r = 0.28 against power,
LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), leaving `gpu_metrics` as the last candidate hardware
activity source. **Intake measurements (2026-10-29) show that candidate is very
probably dead too**: `average_gfx_activity` read **100 % on every one of 120
samples across two captures** while package power moved between 42 W and 123 W
and DRAM bandwidth between 0.7 and 59.5 GB/s. This item therefore exists to
settle the question with evidence and a stated bar, not to assume the answer.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Is the GPU actually doing work right now, and was it
  busy between 17:00 and 19:00?" — needs a utilisation figure that is a direct
  measurement, not a power-draw proxy.
- **Agent answering a usage/incident question (secondary).** Needs to know which
  hardware fields are trustworthy on this host so it cites a real signal instead
  of re-litigating `gpu_busy_percent`.

User stories:

- As an operator I can run one command that decodes `gpu_metrics`, samples it
  alongside power and `gpu_busy_percent`, and prints per-field discrimination
  statistics — so the verdict rests on numbers I can reproduce.
- As an operator I am told plainly whether the interface gives a graded signal,
  with the capture date, kernel, sample counts and band means, so I never
  re-investigate it.
- As an operator, if a field does pass, the series appears next to the existing
  `gpu_*` textfile series without a new daemon, port or scrape job.

## Existing state (measured during intake, 2026-10-29, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic)

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Is the file live and readable? | `-r--r--r-- 4096` root:root; 264 bytes of content; values change between reads; no root, no ROCm, no `amd-smi` needed |
| Which structure? | Header decodes to `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` → `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; the same header text is vendored in `libdrm_amdgpu_sys`'s `wrapper_gpu_metrics.h`) |
| Does the layout check out? | Field sizes under `#pragma pack(4)` sum to 260 B; 4 B tail padding = **264 B**, matching `structure_size` exactly. Cross-checks: `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW vs hwmon `power1_average` 95.06 W (0.1 % agreement); `average_gfx_power` 11.3–44.2 W; `average_gfxclk_frequency` 2 711–2 900 MHz; `average_dram_reads` 0.7–59.5 GB/s; `average_vcn_activity` 0; `average_ipu_activity` all 0; `temperature_gfx` 56–69 °C |
| Does the activity field discriminate? | **No.** Capture A (60 samples @1 s): power 44–123 W, DRAM 1.8–59.5 GB/s → `average_gfx_activity` = 100 on all 60. Capture B (60 samples @1 s): power 42–66 W (idle band), DRAM 0.7–3.5 GB/s → 100 on all 60. Spot samples earlier: 97, 99, 100 at 41–57 W |
| How does it compare with the rejected counter? | Identically saturated: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 on all 120 samples of both captures; `rocm-smi --showuse` reports `GPU use 100 %` at 54 W. GFX clock is pinned at its 2 900 MHz maximum in *both* bands, so the GFX domain is never gated while the proxy holds the device |
| What *does* vary with load? | `average_dram_reads`/`average_dram_writes` (memory bandwidth, 0.7 → 59.5 GB/s), `average_gfx_power` (11.3 → 44.2 W), `average_socket_power` (42 → 123 W), `average_core_c0_activity` (per-core C0 residency) |
| Are the values instantaneous? | No — they are SMU **time filtered** (`time_filter_alphavalue` = 1 000 000); the filter window is undocumented, so no claim finer than the sample interval is supportable |

Existing pipeline this would plug into: `gpu-metrics.service` runs
`~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` every 10 s, writing `gpu.prom` into
node_exporter's textfile collector (`gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_*`,
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes`, label `gpu="card0"`), scraped every 15 s by Prometheus;
documented in [docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service](../../docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service)
and [monitoring/README.md](../../monitoring/README.md).

## Desired change

1. **A reproducible probe CLI** — `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py`: decode the
   v3.0 blob from a sysfs path (default
   `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`), sample every candidate activity
   field alongside the two reference signals (amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` and
   `gpu_busy_percent`) at a configurable interval for a configurable duration,
   and emit CSV or `--json`. A `--verdict` mode prints the per-field
   discrimination statistics against the bar below.
2. **A recorded verdict** — the measured numbers plus a pass/fail decision per
   candidate field, written into the work item and the two monitoring documents,
   so the interface is either adopted once or closed off permanently.
3. **Conditional publication** — only if a field passes the bar, publish it
   through the existing 10 s textfile sampler (new `# HELP`/`# TYPE` series with
   the `gpu="card0"` label, atomic write, nothing written on read failure). If
   nothing passes, publish nothing and record why.
4. **A regression guard** — a saturated activity field must not be usable as a
   utilisation input in any rule or report query without a test failing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decodes `gpu_metrics` into named fields
  using the pinned v3.0 layout and validates the header
  (`structure_size` == layout size, `format_revision` == 3); unit tests cover a
  real 264-byte capture committed as a fixture, a truncated buffer, and an
  unknown `format_revision`/`structure_size`, which must be rejected with a
  clear error rather than misparsed.
- [ ] A capture (`--duration`/`--interval`, defaults documented) writes one row
  per sample containing a timestamp, every candidate activity field,
  `power1_average_watts` and `gpu_busy_percent`; a test drives the sampler
  against fixture sysfs trees (fake `/sys/class/drm/card0/device` and hwmon
  directory) and asserts row count, monotonic timestamps and fixture-derived
  values, without sleeping.
- [ ] `--verdict` reports, per candidate field, the idle-band mean (< 60 W), the
  compute-band mean (≥ 90 W), their separation in percentage points, Pearson r
  against package power, and the idle-band false-busy share (samples ≥ 90 %
  while power < 60 W); a field passes only if separation ≥ 30 pp **and**
  r ≥ 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy ≤ 10 %. Unit tests drive synthetic
  saturated, graded and noisy series and assert the exact pass/fail decision and
  the printed statistics.
- [ ] The measured numbers and the resulting verdict — positive **or** negative
  — are recorded in `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`,
  `monitoring/README.md` (the "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`?"
  section gains a `gpu_metrics` row) and the work item, including capture date,
  kernel version, sample counts and band statistics; a negative verdict is a
  complete outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] If a field passed, the 10 s textfile sampler publishes it (series name,
  `# HELP`/`# TYPE`, `gpu="card0"` label) with the existing atomic-write and
  write-nothing-on-failure behaviour, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
  documents the series and its meaning; a test runs the sampler against fixture
  sysfs and asserts its emitted series set exactly matches the set the
  documentation table lists (so docs and behaviour cannot drift). If no field
  passed, no new series is added and the test asserts the sampler's series set is
  unchanged.
- [ ] The pinned-counter guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`) is extended so a saturated activity field cannot
  appear as a utilisation input — `gpu_busy_percent` always, and the
  `gpu_metrics` activity fields when the verdict is negative — with a regression
  test that fails if any `monitoring/*.yaml` rule expression or the probe's own
  utilisation expressions select one.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, docstrings, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` and
  `monitoring/README.md`; the probe's re-measure procedure (how to re-run the
  capture after a kernel, firmware or driver change) is documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- **No new daemon, port or scrape job.** Reuse `gpu-metrics.service` →
  node_exporter textfile collector; the sampler's 10 s cadence and Prometheus's
  15 s scrape interval are the resolution floor and must be stated as such.
- **Host state is part of the deliverable.** The sampler script lives in
  `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` and is documented in
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`; any change to its series must be reflected
  there so a clean clone can reproduce it.
- **Repository boundary.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`gpu_busy.py`,
  `reporting.py`) is not edited — adopting a passing field in the daily report is
  a follow-up item, mirroring the constraint recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W.
- **The layout must be pinned in-repo.** The struct is not shipped in the
  installed `linux-headers` packages on this host, so the field table must be
  transcribed with a cited source (`struct gpu_metrics_v3_0`) and validated
  against the observed 264-byte `structure_size`; it must fail closed when the
  kernel reports a different revision.
- **No instantaneous claims.** The values are SMU time-filtered with an
  undocumented window; the output must say so rather than imply per-second
  fidelity.
- **Read cost.** One 264-byte sysfs read per sample; world-readable, no root, no
  ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. v3.0 decoder (field table + header
  validation), paired sampler for `gpu_metrics` + hwmon power + `gpu_busy_percent`,
  band statistics and the pass/fail verdict; CSV and `--json` output.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. Decoder fixtures (real 264-byte
  capture, truncated, unknown revision), fixture-sysfs sampling, verdict
  arithmetic and boundary cases (power exactly 60 W / 90 W, activity exactly
  90 %).
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` — New. One committed real capture so the
  layout assertion is reproducible.
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — Record the verdict, the decode layout and
  (conditionally) the new series; extend the verification section with the probe
  command.
- `monitoring/README.md` — Add `gpu_metrics` to "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi`
  or `amdtop`?" with the measured band statistics; note the re-measure recipe.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — Header comment records the `gpu_metrics`
  verdict (no rule change expected; the power rule stays authoritative).
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`
  so saturated activity fields are rejected as utilisation inputs.
- `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` — Only if a field passed: emit the new
  series from the same atomic write.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the premise is false.** Intake evidence already shows
  `average_gfx_activity` saturated at 100 % from 42 W to 123 W. Mitigation: the
  negative verdict is an explicit, accepted outcome (AC4) and the probe records
  which fields *do* discriminate (DRAM bandwidth, GFX power) for a follow-up.
- **Risk: decoder drift after a kernel or firmware upgrade.** Mitigation: header
  validation plus a committed real capture; the probe refuses unknown revisions
  and the docs carry the re-measure procedure.
- **Risk: undocumented APU field semantics.** `average_gfx_activity` may mean
  "GFX domain powered" rather than "GFX busy" on SMU 14. Mitigation: the bar and
  band statistics decide it, and the interpretation limits are documented.
- **Risk: a capture that misses one band.** A verdict computed only from idle
  samples would be meaningless. Mitigation: AC3 requires both bands, and the
  probe reports per-band sample counts so a one-sided capture is visible.
- **Risk: scope creep** into report integration, new daemons or a full GPU
  telemetry redesign. Mitigation: those are explicit constraints/follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption:** amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` remains the reference compute
  signal (idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W) per
  LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; this item does not re-derive the threshold.
- **Assumption:** the discrimination bar (≥ 30 pp separation, r ≥ 0.6, ≤ 10 %
  idle false-busy) is strict enough — it is far stricter than
  `gpu_busy_percent`'s measured 45.2 % false-busy — and is recorded here so the
  producer can tighten or relax it before implementation.
- **Assumption:** both bands occur on this host within a short window (intake saw
  idle at 42–66 W and compute at 90–123 W within ~15 minutes), so a 30-minute
  capture is sufficient; longer captures are supported by the same CLI.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `high` — the verdict decides whether a direct
  hardware utilisation measure is possible at all on this host, which the usage
  report's honesty goal depends on — even though the likely outcome is a short
  negative report rather than a code change.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** — Evaluate `amd-smi` as the GPU utilisation source
  (completed). Quantified `gpu_busy_percent`'s saturation (45.2 % false-busy,
  r = 0.28) and filed this item as the remaining avenue. Parent context.
- **LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W** — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation
  history (in review). Owns the *workload* half (per-slot busy/idle, in-flight
  tasks, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI). **Partial overlap only**: that item
  attributes power to llama-server slots; this one judges a *hardware* activity
  field. No CLI or slot work is duplicated here — this item produces a probe and
  a verdict, and its publication step (if any) extends the existing sysfs
  sampler.
- **LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT** — Monitoring: deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus
  with honest GPU utilisation (completed) and children: LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48
  (power-derived utilisation rules), LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G (docs for the deployed
  stack). The sampler, units and docs this item extends.
- **LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP** — Fix GPU-wedge false positives (completed):
  established that `gpu_busy_percent` is unusable and power is the
  discriminating signal; the proxy's wedge detector was disabled because of it.
- **LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T** — Grafana dashboard GPU VRAM panel queries series no
  exporter publishes (in progress): the precedent for asserting *published*
  series against documentation, which AC5 reuses.
- **LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX** — Cross-check report slot-time against llama-server
  eval timings (independent): the other half of validating the report's busy
  figures.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive operator was available for this intake (auto-dispatched by the
herdr downtime worker at 2026-10-29T03:54:28Z), so each question below was
resolved from host and repository evidence; none is blocking. Each carries the
agent's **Recommended** option, which the producer may override.

- **Q1: Given that `average_gfx_activity` already measures as saturated (100 %
  from 42 W to 123 W), is a documented negative verdict an acceptable
  deliverable for this item?**
  **Recommended:** yes — record the numbers, close the path permanently, and file
  follow-ups for the fields that do discriminate.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the item was written to test the hypothesis,
  not to assume it; the file decodes correctly (264 B v3.0, cross-checked
  against hwmon power) yet its activity field does not respond to load, so the
  honest outcome is a negative verdict with evidence. Source: two 60-sample 1 s
  captures (power 44–123 W and 42–66 W, DRAM 0.7–59.5 GB/s, activity 100 on all
  120 samples), `/tmp` probe using the `kgd_pp_interface.h` v3.0 layout.
- **Q2: If a field does pass the bar, should it replace the power-derived
  `gpu:computing:bool` as the report's GPU busy measure, or be published
  alongside it?**
  **Recommended:** publish alongside; keep power-derived authoritative until its
  own calibration item justifies switching.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): `gpu:computing:bool` is referenced by the
  report (`gpu_busy.py`, `reporting.py`), the alert `GpuComputingSustained` and
  `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`; changing its meaning inside an
  investigation item would break three consumers at once. Publishing an additive
  series keeps the comparison visible, and report adoption stays a follow-up
  (same boundary recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W). Source:
  `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`, `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py`.
- **Q3: Where should the probe live, and how should a passing field reach
  Prometheus — extend the deployed bash textfile sampler, or add a Python
  sampler?**
  **Recommended:** a repo `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decoder plus a one-line
  call from the existing bash sampler; no new unit.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the sampler is a documented 10 s bash loop
  writing `gpu.prom` atomically, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` embeds
  the script verbatim; a second sampler would duplicate the unit, the textfile
  directory and the docs. Decoding a 264-byte binary blob in bash is not
  testable, so the field table belongs in Python with fixture tests. Source:
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`, `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh`.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator of the LLM proxy, I want a 24 h post-deploy measurement proving the contended-pricing fix (parent LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3, AC4) drops the abandoned-queue-wait share below the 85 % baseline without new post-acceptance evictions — measured deterministically at the exact moment the window elapses, so the epic can close.

## Context

Parent AC4: "Post-change, the share of queued local waits ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` drops below the 85 % baseline measured 2026-10-19/20 over a 24 h window, with no new `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events."

- The contended-pricing fix was **deployed on 2026-10-29 00:10:18 UTC** (proxy restart, pid 1081749; code = local `dev` HEAD `52085f09` (committed 2026-10-29 00:07:08 UTC, i.e. before the restart), which contains the contended rate bucket `cc840d3d`, occupant-remaining rebase `91eab34d`/`9a866fc7`, baseline harness `a843e62c`, docs `323fe680`, decision-log/report surface `bb4bcb3c`).
- **Runnable at/after 2026-10-30 00:10 UTC** (24 h of post-deploy traffic).
- Pre-change baseline committed by the baseline child: `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion.{md,json}` (24 abandoned / 65 queued waits = 36.9 % abandoned share; per-band conversion table).
- Consumes the harness from the pre-change measurement child and the extended report from the parser child.

## Scope

- Capture a 24 h post-deploy window through `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py` (per-band conversion + abandoned-wait shares) and the proxy-usage-analysis report.
- Sanity gate before the verdict: the window must contain at least one `rate_bucket=contended`/`solitary_fallback` admission (proves the deployed code is actually pricing contended admissions) — if the bucket is still all `unknown`, the deployment did not take and the window is void.
- Compute the queued-local-wait share ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` and compare against the 85 % baseline and against the pre-change window.
- Count `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events in the window and triage any occurrences into an explanation or a follow-up item.
- Commit the measurement record (`docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.{md,json}`), labelled with the deploy hash (`52085f09`, local `dev` HEAD at restart) and window bounds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The post-change window's share of queued local waits ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` is below 85 % (parent AC4) — or, if it is not, a follow-up work item is created recording the failure with the numbers.
- AC2: Zero new `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events in the window, or every occurrence is explained and links to a triage item.
- AC3: The committed record shows the pre-change and post-change windows side by side (per-band conversion, abandoned shares, count of local admissions), with the AC verdict and the deployed commit hash (`52085f09`).
- AC4: The record is produced by the committed tools (no one-off analysis), reproducing the exact numbers without manual steps for the named logs; the window's `rate_bucket` distribution is reported (must not be all `unknown`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py` (from the baseline child)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion.md` + window JSON (pre-change baseline)
- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md` + window JSON (this item's record)

## Dependencies

- Pre-change baseline + harness child (terminal); contended rate bucket child (terminal); occupant-remaining rebase child (terminal); parser/report child (terminal); **deploy = proxy restart performed 2026-10-29 00:10:18 UTC (completed)**.
- Supersedes LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA (the original time-blocked AC4 item, currently open and detached from the parent); this item carries the concrete runnable schedule.

## Deployment verification (2026-10-29 00:13 UTC)

Restart completed 2026-10-29 00:10:18 UTC (proxy pid 1081749, `/health` =
`healthy`, llama-server + TTS healthy). The contended-pricing code is provably
serving: `local_admission_guard` decision lines written after the restart carry
the new fields, e.g.

```
00:13:02 local_admission_guard decision=admit reason=within_budget ... eta_prefill_s=3.7 eta_occupancy_s=18.1 projected_wait_s=21.8 rate_bucket=solitary_fallback contended_samples=1 busy_slots=1 ...
```

(`rate_bucket` is `solitary_fallback` because the contended window has only 1

Before the restart every decision logged `rate_bucket=unknown`, so this is a
hard before/after signal for AC4.

- **Runnable from:** 2026-10-30 00:10 UTC (24 h of post-deploy traffic) —
  recommended `--since "2026-10-29 00:10:18" --until "2026-10-30 00:10:18"`.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator evaluating the 60 s → 30 s contention-queue sweep
(LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R), I want a windowed report that separates ticket-backed
dispatches, residual queue wins and residual queue losses (with a lease-active
`reason` split), so the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline and the post-flip verdict are
measured with one definition.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers parent AC3 (residual-queue telemetry) and
the AC1 trigger precondition (a ≥24 h baseline at 60 s / depth 8 must exist
before the sweep is applied).

## Scope

- New `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py`: CLI with `--log-dir`, a
  stated window (`--since`/`--until` or `--hours`), `--sweep-budget-seconds`
  (default 30), `--json` and a human/markdown render; modelled on
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`.
- Reuse `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` (`discover_proxy_log_files`,
  `parse_line_timestamp`, `iter_proxy_log_lines`) and import
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` as a **read-only**
  library where practical (never edit that skill's files).
- Report sections for the window:
  (a) ticket-backed dispatches — `local_admission_reserve_claimed` count
      (reported, **not** a flip gate);
  (b) residual queue wins — `contention_queue_dispatch ... queued_duration=`,
      count, share at or below the sweep budget, and a wait distribution
      (p50/p75/p90/max);
  (c) residual queue losses — `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue ...
      queued_duration=`, count, aggregate wait, wait-per-hour, and a split by
      `reason` (`local_lease_active` vs `none`/other).
- Only the two lease-retention emit sites carry `reason=local_lease_active`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py` ~12312 and ~12358); a missing `reason=` is
  counted as `none`, never dropped.
- Exit codes mirror `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`: 0 = measurement complete,
  2 = incomplete (no logs / thin window / coverage gap; never silently pass),
  1 = invalid input.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC3 — residual-queue telemetry.** A windowed report (script + test) emits
   ticket-backed dispatches, residual wins and residual losses split by reason.
2. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py --log-dir <dir> --hours 24`
   prints a report containing all three sections (ticket-backed count, win
   count/share/distribution, loss count/aggregate wait/reason split) for the
   stated window; `--json` emits the same numbers machine-readably.
3. Unit tests in `tests/test_contention_queue_sweep_report.py` drive the CLI
   against synthetic proxy-log fixtures (mixed wins/losses, lease-active and
   reason-less losses, empty window, window filtering) and assert every
   section, the reason split, the at-or-below-budget share, and the 0/2/1 exit
   codes — no live logs required.

5. A short runbook `docs/dev/contention-queue-sweep.md` documents the

6. Changed-scope tests for the new script and its log parsing pass.

## Constraints

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the contention queue to be a bounded straggler net
(30 s, depth 2) instead of a 60 s parking lot, so dead local wait stops
competing with real local work, while a slot that frees within seconds is
still usable.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers parent AC2 (single-source budget) and
AC4 (tests/validation).

## Change

```yaml
contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30   # was 60 (was 120 in LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO)
contention_queue_max_depth: 2           # was 8
```

Evidence (proxy.log*, 2026-10-22 19:00→22:18, 3.3 h at 60 s / depth 8): 180
queue events — 38 wins (21 %) / 142 losses (79 %), every loss at the full
60 s, 8 705 s aggregate dead wait; wins retained by budget: 20 s → 24 %,
30 s → 34 %, 45 s → 60 %. Trigger, flip criteria and the two-line rollback
live on the parent item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, flip criteria and rollback.
2. `proxy/config.yaml` ships 30 s / depth 2 and the surrounding comment block
   (~lines 1740-1800) records the new evidence, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline
   requirement, the 7-day observation window, the three flip criteria and the
   two-line rollback (revert to 60 / 8, restart the proxy).
3. **AC2 — single-source budget.** The shortened budget reaches the admission
   guard and the reservation endpoint through one resolver
   (`prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds`); no second constant, no per-call
   default. Tests assert `wait_budget_seconds(merged config, "medium") ==
   30.0`, the guard's refusal payload and `X-Local-Admission-Budget` header
   report 30 s, `POST /llama/local/reserve` prices against the same 30 s, and
   `high` priority still resolves to 0 s — all through
   `_get_contention_queue_config`.
4. depth 2 is accepted unchanged; clamping happens only outside [1, 16]
   (values 1 and 16 pass through unchanged).
5. **AC4 — tests / validation.** Unit tests cover the swept values end to end:
   resolver 30 s, depth 2, 30 s timeout. A third waiter with 2 parked falls
   back immediately without enqueueing, and a parked waiter that is not
   served falls back at 30 s (tiny/mocked caps — never a real 30 s sleep).
6. Stale fixtures/tests that assert the shipped 60 s / 8 defaults are updated
   (`proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py::test_{cheap,fast}_config_declares_queue_policy`
   and any other shipped-config assertions), not left stale. The code-level
   defaults for a missing key stay as the inert no-config fallback and are
   documented as such (absent queue key ⇒ policy `fallback` ⇒ nothing queues).
7. Code comments in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (module docstring still says
   60 s), `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` and `proxy/proxy/router.py`
   state the single-budget contract; no behavioural change beyond the two
   config values.

## Constraints

- Fail-open semantics of the admission guard are unchanged (uncalibrated ⇒
  admit).
- One budget, one resolver: no new knob, no per-reason budget.
- Out of scope: queue removal, slot count, ctx-size, the ETA guard's model,
  client reservation adoption (`WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`).
- The config change requires a proxy restart; deployment happens in the
  observation child after a quiet-window restart, not in this item's session.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the post-flip window measured against the ≥24 h pre-flip
baseline and a keep/rollback verdict recorded, so the sweep is judged by its
own flip criteria instead of by assumption.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers the evaluation half of parent AC1
(trigger, observation window, verdict) and AC3's "run the report and record the
numbers".

## Nature of the task

This is a **scheduled measurement task, not code work**. It starts only after
the sweep child has shipped to `dev`, been released, and the proxy has been
restarted in a quiet window. It is expected to stay open for the 7-day
observation window; it must not be implemented inside a code session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, window, flip criteria and rollback, verified against the
   deployed state before the flip is announced.
2. Preconditions verified and recorded on this item: the reservation endpoint
   is live, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline exists (report/baseline child), the
   sweep is deployed (config 30 s / depth 2 active after a quiet-window
   restart), and the flip is announced in a comment with the restart
   timestamp.
3. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` is run over the 7-day post-flip
   window (≥1 000 queue events), with numbers recorded: dead wait per hour vs
   baseline, residual wins as a share of queue events, remote dispatch volume
   change, ticket-backed dispatch count, and the lease-active vs `none` loss
   split.
4. A keep/rollback verdict is recorded against the three flip criteria —
   ≥50 % fall in dead wait per hour, residual wins ≥20 % of queue events,
   remote dispatch volume rise <20 % relative. A rollback reverts the two
   values to 60 / 8, restarts the proxy, and records the observed numbers.
5. If the window is incomplete (fewer than 1 000 queue events, a log-coverage
   gap, or no restart yet), the item stays `blocked`/`open` with the shortfall
   and the missing days stated — never a verdict from partial data.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (consumed)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (rollback only)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sweep child (30 s / depth 2 deployed) and the report/baseline
  child (baseline + tool).

## Relationship to LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R

Spun out of `LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R` (contention-queue sweep) as a **top-level,
standalone measurement item** on 2026-10-31 (operator decision), so the sweep
parent can reach `in_review` at code-complete while this scheduled observation
runs on its own calendar. Recorded as `discovered-from:LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R`;
the parent is no longer a dependency. The sweep's three implementation
children are already on `dev`: `LP-0MVT110PJ003XYLP` (report + ≥ 24 h pre-flip
baseline, `65621b8b`), `LP-0MVT1146V007WXA4` (30 s / depth 2, `6a6e2f38`),
`LP-0MVT114HU009UNML` (docs as straggler net, `47f973e0`).

## Earliest run date

**Earliest run: 2026-11-07** — i.e. restart date + 7 days. The window starts
only once the swept config is live (dev→main release, then a quiet-window proxy
restart that loads 30 s / depth 2). If the release/restart lands later than
2026-10-31, this date moves with it: the item is runnable on restart date + 7
days, and never earlier than ≥ 1 000 post-flip queue events (AC5 forbids a
verdict from partial data).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py::test_remote_first_cycle_routes_through_the_helper_once
- Failing commit: 15aeabccd1c7d821baefe04ad03c605953d784b1
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
@pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_remote_first_cycle_routes_through_the_helper_once():
        """AC1: the remote-first cycle consults the helper once and echoes it."""
        spy, patcher = _spy_capacity_verdict()
        calls: list[str] = []
    
        async def _remote(_req, _path, _pc):
            calls.append("remote")
            return _ok_response()
    
        with patcher, patch("proxy.server.proxy_to_remote", _remote):
            result = await provider.proxy_with_remote_fallback(
                _DummyRequest(headers={"X-Local-Preference": "local-only"}),
                "v1/chat/completions",
                _remote_only_chain(),
                _cfg(),
            )
    
        assert result.status_code == 429
        assert calls == [], "the refusal must precede any remote dispatch"
>       assert len(spy.calls) == 1, f"exactly one helper call; got {spy.calls!r}"
E       AssertionError: exactly one helper call; got [{'args': (None,), 'kwargs': {'reason': No
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 15aeabccd1c7d821baefe04ad03c605953d784b1`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py::test_remote_first_cycle_routes_through_the_helper_once` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py::test_remote_first_cycle_routes_through_the_helper_once` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. Any documented single-verdict claim is kept truthful and updated where the implementation changes it — specifically the "computed once by `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict` / only verdict computation in `provider.py`" statements in `proxy/docs/routing.md` (`:1280`, `:1327`) and the call-count contract paragraph in the module docstring of `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Root-cause lead (plan review, 2026-10-29)

The contract pinned by this module (`proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`, module
docstring lines 24-31) is that `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict` is
consulted **exactly once per refusal**. The failing commit
`15aeabcc` (work item LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2) added
`_local_capacity_verdict_for_request()` / `_local_preference_pins_local()` in
`proxy/proxy/provider.py` and wired the predicate into three additional exits:

- `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` (contention-queue gate; produces `refused_local_only`),
- `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (free-slot admission-guard exit),
- `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote` (the historical sole call site).

Each consultation of the predicate re-invokes the helper (the docstring states the
verdict is deliberately **not** cached, because the stamped reason changes as the
cycle walks its exits), so a refusal now records 2-3 helper calls instead of 1.

### Sibling failures with the same root cause

The triage comments on this item record the same assertion failing in two more
tests in the same module — `test_refused_local_only_branch_routes_through_the_helper_once`
(3 calls) and `test_local_first_choke_point_refusal_routes_through_the_helper_once`
(2 calls). AC3 (full suite green) therefore also covers them; no separate work
item is needed unless the fix is intentionally scoped to the remote-first cycle only.

### Documented contract to keep truthful

`proxy/docs/routing.md` (`"computed once by admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict"`,
`"the only verdict computation in provider.py"`) states the single-computation
contract. Whichever fix shape is chosen, that sentence must stay true (AC2).

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — `_CapacityVerdictSpy` / `_spy_capacity_verdict()` (`:1084`), `_issue_local_first_cycle()` (`:1136`), the three failing single-call tests (`:1219`, `:1239`, and the remote-first cycle test).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_capacity_verdict_for_request()` (`:6516`), `_local_preference_pins_local()` (`:6570`), `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` (`:7103`), `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (`:7555`), `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle()` (`:11983`).
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — `local_capacity_verdict()` (`:222`), the single helper the contract names.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the "computed exactly once / only verdict computation in `provider.py`" sentences (`:1280`, `:1327`).

## Appendix: clarifications (plan session)

- Q: Is this a duplicate of LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 (the commit that broke it)? —
  Answer: **no**. That item is `completed/in_review` and its scope was wiring the
  pin predicate; this item is the call-count regression it introduced. No
  overlapping completed item satisfies AC1.
- Q: Should the sibling failing tests get their own work items? — Answer: **no** —
  AC1 names the reported test and AC3 (full suite green) already requires the
  siblings to pass; they share one root cause. Recorded here rather than creating
  duplicate critical items.
- Q: Which fix shape — memoise the verdict per request, or collapse the call
  sites? — Answer: **left to implementation (OPEN QUESTION, non-blocking)**. Both
  satisfy the contract; memoisation must key on the evidence tuple
  (`decision`, `reason`, `new_tokens`, `budget_tokens`) because the existing
  docstring warns a stale verdict would re-route the request.
