data.description:
# Daily resets on MinutoAI (LP-0MVT8SAZE00570J5)

## Problem statement

MunitoAI's free tier answers HTTP 429 with an **absolute** daily-reset
timestamp (`error.type = "insufficient_quota"`,
`error.code = "free_daily_limit_exceeded"`), but the proxy recognises neither
the type/code nor the timestamp form: it falls through to the generic
per-entry cooldown (60 s + exponential backoff), so `munitoai-free` is
re-probed roughly every minute for the rest of the UTC day and, once the
other tiers are unavailable, the client receives the raw upstream 429 body
(`Error: Unrecognized error: The daily free limit of … is reached. It resets
at 2026-10-30 00:00 UTC.`).

(Naming: the work item title/description say "MinutAI"/"MinutoAI"; the
gateway is MunitoAI, `https://api.munito.ai/inference`.)

Evidence from the live proxy log (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`,
2026-10-29):

```
2026-10-29 09:39:41,532 - WARNING - [remote] upstream error status=429
  url=https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions
  body={"error":{"message":"The daily free limit of
  deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash is reached. It resets at 2026-10-30 00:00 UTC.
  Add credits to continue now.","type":"insufficient_quota","param":null,
  "code":"free_daily_limit_exceeded"}}
2026-10-29 09:39:41,533 - WARNING - All providers exhausted for
  model=v1/chat/completions; unavailable={'munitoai-free': 44,
  'opencode-go-2': 51961}; usage_limit_reset={'opencode-go-2': 51961}
```

Measured impact for that one day: **128** `free_daily_limit_exceeded` 429s
between 06:10 and 10:04 UTC, and **222** chain-exhaustion lines listing
`munitoai-free` in `unavailable=` — i.e. ~14 hours of pointless re-probing and
avoidable fallback pressure on the paid tiers and local model.

## Users

- **Operator / herdr downtime worker**: wants the free tier quarantined until
  its advertised reset so the chain stops re-trying a dead account and the
  capacity it is spending on retries goes to tiers that can serve.
  *As an operator, when MunitoAI reports a daily free limit with a reset
  timestamp, the proxy skips `munitoai-free` until that instant and logs one
  clear `usage_limit_reset` line instead of 128 blind retries.*
- **Fallback chain (paid sibling `munitoai` on the same gateway)**: the daily
  limit is a free-tier/per-key limit, so the paid key with independent credit
  must stay eligible in the same request.
  *As the router, a free-tier daily-limit 429 must not poison the shared
  `api.munito.ai/inference:deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` failure domain.*
- **Pi client**: wants the raw upstream body surfaced only when nothing else
  can serve — with the exhausted chain carrying an honest `retry_after`
  derived from the daily reset.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Detection.** A remote HTTP 429 whose JSON body carries
   `error.type == "insufficient_quota"` **or**
   `error.code == "free_daily_limit_exceeded"` (case-insensitive, nested under
   `error` and at top level) is classified as a usage-limit error and takes the
   usage-limit reset path — never the generic `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`
   path. Unit test reproduces the verbatim MunitoAI body above.
2. **Absolute-timestamp parsing.** A message of the form
   `… It resets at 2026-10-30 00:00 UTC.` is parsed into seconds-until-reset
   (UTC), and the resulting quarantine lasts until that instant **plus** the
   existing 2-minute `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS`. Unit test asserts the
   parsed duration against a fixed injected `now` (no wall-clock flakiness) and
   covers at least: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC`,
   ISO-8601 with `Z` and with an explicit offset.
3. **Quarantine is account-scoped, persisted and visible.** The reset is
   recorded through `_set_usage_limit_quarantine(_usage_limit_account_key(…),
   …)` (persisted to `provider-state.json`), recorded as a `usage_limit_reset`
   attempt diagnostic with `reset_in_seconds`, appears in the exhausted-chain
   `usage_limit_reset=` map, and feeds `_compute_retry_after`. The routing skip
   logs `Skipping provider=munitoai-free: usage_limit_reset_pending
   (account=…, reset_in=…)`. Unit test asserts the persisted reset survives a
   `_restore_provider_state()` round trip.
4. **Bounded safety.** An absolute-timestamp quarantine is hard evidence
   (`explicit=True`: exempt from the 24 h guess cap and from probe
   revalidation) **but** bounded to the period the payload names
   (`free_daily_limit_exceeded` / "daily … limit" → 24 h) plus margin, so a
   malformed, far-future or clock-skewed timestamp cannot lock the account out
   indefinitely. A timestamp in the past, an unparseable timestamp, or an
   `insufficient_quota` body with no reset information falls back to the
   existing guessed-period rules (guess cap + self-healing probe). Unit tests
   cover all three fallbacks and the bound.
5. **Sibling isolation.** `insufficient_quota` is per-account, not per-endpoint:
   the failing entry poisons only `_usage_limit_account_key` in the per-request
   exclusion set, so the paid `munitoai` entry (same endpoint **and** model,
   different `api_key_env`) stays eligible. Test: a chain of
   `munitoai-free` → `munitoai` where the free entry returns the daily-limit 429
   must route the **same** request to the paid entry, and the endpoint failure
   domain must not be excluded.
6. **No regressions in existing quota handling.** `GoUsageLimitError`,
   `FreeUsageLimitError`, window-aware snapshot quarantine,
   `x-ratelimit-*` header quarantine and generic 429/non-429 handling behave
   exactly as before; a non-429 response carrying `insufficient_quota`, and a
   429 carrying only `rate_limit_exceeded`, are unchanged. Covered by new
   boundary tests plus the existing `test_usage_limit_reset.py`,
   `test_ratelimit_account_quarantine.py`, `test_ratelimit_headers_cooldown.py`
   and `test_failure_domain_grouping.py` suites.
7. **Test coverage.** New tests are added first (TDD) for detection, parsing,
   quarantine persistence, bounding/fallbacks and sibling isolation; each test
   asserts one externally observable behaviour (log line, attempt diagnostic,
   persisted state, or routing decision) against a fixed clock.
8. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `proxy/README.md` (usage-limit quarantine section) and
   `proxy/docs/routing.md` (error taxonomy + account-key table).
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing machinery in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: extend
  `_usage_limit_reset_info()` / `_parse_resets_in()`, return the existing
  `_UsageLimitReset` NamedTuple, and go through `_set_usage_limit_quarantine()`.
  No parallel quarantine mechanism, no new state file.
- No per-request network I/O: the reset is derived from the error body alone
  (MunitoAI sends no `Retry-After`, and its `x-ratelimit-*` headers describe the
  per-minute window, not the daily one).
- Ordering matters: the usage-limit check already runs **before**
  `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` /
  `_apply_ratelimit_account_quarantine()`, so the daily reset wins over the
  ~60 s header-derived cooldown; keep that precedence and prove it with a test.
- Preserve per-account semantics (LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW,
  LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N, LP-0MVFA1VRT007T9HT): never quarantine a gateway, only
  an `api_key_env@endpoint:model` account.
- Both remote paths must be covered: the streaming resolver
  (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, ~`provider.py:10919`) and the
  non-streaming resolver (`_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`, ~`provider.py:12959`)
  — both reachable from `proxy_with_remote_fallback` (`provider.py:11120`) and
  both call the same helpers — add the assertion for each only if the code
  diverges.

## Existing state

- `_usage_limit_reset_info()` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:8777`) recognises only
  `error.type ∈ {gousagelimiterror, freeusagelimiterror}` and returns `None`
  otherwise (`provider.py:8854` guard), so `insufficient_quota` never reaches
  the quarantine path.
- `_parse_resets_in()` (`provider.py:8412`) parses **relative** durations only
  (`Resets in 22hr 43min`); there is no absolute-timestamp parser in
  `provider.py`. `quota_state._parse_resets_at()` (`provider.py`'s neighbour
  module `quota_state.py:321`) parses ISO-8601 with offsets, not
  `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC`.
- `_is_account_rate_limit_error()` (`provider.py:8364`) matches only
  `rate_limit_error` / `rate_limit_exceeded` (plus a raw-body substring
  fallback), so an `insufficient_quota` 429 is
  **not** account-scoped: it poisons the shared failure domain
  (`api.munito.ai/inference:deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`), which
  `munitoai-free` and `munitoai` share.
- `munitoai-free` and `munitoai` both declare
  `respect_ratelimit_headers: true` (`proxy/config.yaml:448`, `:563`), so a
  quota 429 today can be quarantined for the **rolling** header reset (seconds)
  rather than the daily reset — the wrong window for this error.
- `_PERIOD_DEFAULT_SECONDS` (`provider.py:210`) already maps
  `daily → 24h`; `_usage_limit_guess_cap_seconds()` (`provider.py:8482`)
  bounds guesses at 24 h.
- Existing quarantine observability already emits everything needed:
  `_usage_limit_pending_diagnostics()`, the `usage_limit_reset=` exhaustion
  field, `Skipping provider=…: usage_limit_reset_pending`, and
  `POST /admin/clear-usage-limit` (`handlers.py:1484`).

## Desired change

1. Add `_parse_resets_at_timestamp(message) -> float | None` (name indicative):
   parse `resets at <timestamp> UTC` into seconds until that instant using an
   injectable `now` (default `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`). Support
   `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[(:SS)] UTC`, trailing `Z`, and explicit `±HH:MM` offsets;
   return `None` for anything else, and treat past/near-zero results as "no
   usable timestamp".
2. Extend `_usage_limit_reset_info()` detection to accept
   `err_type == "insufficient_quota"` and
   `code == "free_daily_limit_exceeded"` (kept as a separate code check so
   gateway variants that omit `type` still match). Today the function reads
   `type`/`message` **only** from the nested `error` dict
   (`provider.py:8841`-`8849`, and `code` is not read at all); AC1 requires top-level markers too, so reuse
   the two-candidate (`payload` then `payload["error"]`) pattern already used
   by `_is_account_rate_limit_error` rather than adding a second reader. Keep
   the existing `status != 429` guard first, then resolve the reset in
   this order: explicit duration (`_parse_resets_in`) → absolute timestamp
   (`_parse_resets_at_timestamp`) → named period guess (existing behaviour).
   Absolute-timestamp results are `explicit=True` and bounded by the period the
   payload names (daily → `_PERIOD_DEFAULT_SECONDS["daily"]`) plus the 2-minute
   margin; add a distinct `source=timestamp` log line so the report can
   distinguish it.
3. Extend the account-scope predicate (`_is_account_rate_limit_error()` or a
   clearly named sibling used at both call sites) so `insufficient_quota` /
   `free_daily_limit_exceeded` poisons only the account key.
4. Add the tests described in ACs 1–6, then update `proxy/README.md` and
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`.
5. Keep the change surgical: one helper, one detection extension, one predicate
   extension, tests, docs. No refactor of the surrounding cascade.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_parse_resets_at_timestamp()` (new);
  `_usage_limit_reset_info()` detection + timestamp branch (`source=timestamp`);
  `_is_account_rate_limit_error()` (or sibling) extended for
  `insufficient_quota`; docstrings for `_UsageLimitReset.explicit` bounds.
- `proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py` — detection + absolute-timestamp
  parsing (fixed clock), bounding and fallbacks, both remote call paths.
- `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_account_quarantine.py` — sibling isolation and
  precedence over the header-derived cooldown.
- `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` — assert the shared endpoint
  domain is not poisoned by an `insufficient_quota` 429.
- `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_quarantine_diagnostics.py` — assert the
  `usage_limit_reset=` / `reset_in_seconds` diagnostics for the new source.
- `proxy/README.md` — usage-limit quarantine + FreeUsageLimitError paragraphs
  (`:801`-`:802`).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — error taxonomy (`:1628` onward) and the
  429/account-key table row (`:294`), including the daily-window precedence.
  That table row currently reads `api_key_env@endpoint` and should be
  corrected to the implemented `api_key_env@endpoint:model`
  (`_usage_limit_account_key`, `provider.py:8072`).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — comment beside the two `munitoai*` entries noting the
  daily-reset quarantine (comment-only, no behaviour change).

## Related work

- **LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ** (completed) — introduced
  `_usage_limit_reset_info()` and account-level quarantine; this item extends
  its detection and parsing, it does not replace it.
- **LP-0MVDNP36J006430L** (completed) — respect `x-ratelimit-*` reset headers
  on MunitoAI quota 429s; the daily window is **not** covered by those headers.
- **LP-0MVFA1VRT007T9HT** (completed) — reset-aware account quarantine
  (`_apply_ratelimit_account_quarantine`), the precedence this item must beat.
- **LP-0MVPAE77Z002VGIA** / **LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8** (completed) — window-aware
  and bounded-guess quarantine rules reused here (including the
  `explicit=True` exemption).
- **LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N** / **LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW** (completed) — per-account
  (not per-endpoint) rate-limit isolation, preserved by AC5.
- **LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL** / **LP-0MVGGI4Y0003K4AZ** (completed) —
  `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` budget; the daily quarantine sits above it.
- Potentially related docs: `proxy/README.md` (usage-limit section),
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` (error taxonomy), `docs/dev/quota-surge.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **A1 (detection key shape).** `insufficient_quota` is treated as a
  usage-limit error for **any** provider, not just MunitoAI: an out-of-credit
  account genuinely cannot serve, and it is bounded (AC4) with
  `POST /admin/clear-usage-limit` as the escape hatch.
- **A2 (scope of the quarantine).** The existing
  `_usage_limit_account_key` (`api_key_env@endpoint:model`) is kept as-is, so
  the quarantine is naturally per-model as well as per-key — matching the
  message's "daily free limit **of deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash**".
- **A3 (timezone).** Only explicit timezone evidence is honoured (` UTC`
  suffix, `Z`, `±HH:MM`); a bare timestamp with no zone is treated as
  unparseable and falls back rather than guessing local time.
- **R1 (over-long lockout).** A malformed/far-future timestamp could lock the
  free account out. Mitigation: AC4 period bound, explicit-past fallback, the
  admin clear endpoint, and a unit test per branch.
- **R2 (under-long lockout).** Upstream clock skew or a rounded timestamp could
  release the account marginally early; the 2-minute margin and the existing
  cooldown backoff absorb this, and the next 429 re-quarantines.
- **R3 (scope creep).** The Pi-visible string `Error: Unrecognized error: …`
  (client-side error mapping) and any `proxy-usage-analysis` recommendation
  tuning are **out of scope**; if they prove necessary they are recorded as
  separate linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **R4 (paid tier exhaustion).** The paid `munitoai` key can independently
  return `insufficient_quota` (out of credits); it is quarantined on its own
  evidence only, never inherited from the free tier.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive round was required: the seed description named the exact
upstream error, and the payload, frequency and current handling were
established directly from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` and
`proxy/proxy/provider.py`, so every question below was answerable from
repo/log evidence rather than from the producer (interview conduct rule 1:
do not ask questions answerable by repo search).

- Q: "What shape does the upstream MunitoAI daily-limit error have?" —
  Answer (evidence: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log:5139`, 2026-10-29):
  HTTP 429, body `{"error":{"message":"The daily free limit of
  deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash is reached. It resets at 2026-10-30 00:00 UTC.
  Add credits to continue now.","type":"insufficient_quota","param":null,
  "code":"free_daily_limit_exceeded"}}`. Not a producer question.
- Q: "Is the reset duration or an absolute timestamp?" — Answer (same log
  line): an absolute UTC timestamp (`resets at 2026-10-30 00:00 UTC`),
  which `_parse_resets_in()` (relative durations only) cannot parse.
- Q: "Should the paid `munitoai` key be quarantined too?" — Answer
  (evidence: `proxy/proxy/provider.py:8072` `_usage_limit_account_key`,
  `proxy/config.yaml:448/:563`): no — limits are per `api_key_env`; the
  account key already isolates free from paid. Recorded as AC5.
- Q: "How long should the quarantine last?" — Answer (evidence:
  `provider.py:203` `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS`, `provider.py:210`
  `_PERIOD_DEFAULT_SECONDS`): until the advertised reset + the existing
  2-minute margin, marked `explicit=True`, bounded to the named daily period.
  Recorded as ACs 2 and 4.
- Q: "Does a client-visible message fix belong in this item?" — **ASSUMPTION**
  (agent decision, no producer input — item was auto-dispatched by
  `herdr-downtime` and the description scopes the work to "detect these and put
  the provider into cooldown until the reset"): no, out of scope (R3); the
  quarantine alone removes the repeated raw 429s because the exhausted chain
  carries the reset in `usage_limit_reset=`.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-29 (plan skill, Map) — Auto-plan review applied; no decomposition
  created because the description already carries testable ACs, an ordered
  implementation sketch and predicted key files. Corrections made:
  (a) corrected the two remote-resolver call sites to the enclosing
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` / `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`
  functions; (b) noted that `_usage_limit_reset_info()` reads
  `type`/`message` only from the nested `error` dict today, so AC1's
  top-level requirement needs the existing two-candidate pattern;
  (c) noted the raw-body substring fallback in
  `_is_account_rate_limit_error()`; (d) flagged the stale account-key
  spelling in `proxy/docs/routing.md:294`; (e) retitled the item from

## Summary

Follow-up split out of LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 intake answer Q1 (scope = guard-only, `B`). Attribution of individual router-responder `GET /slots ... 400` events is currently impossible from `llama-server.log` because llama.cpp's router access line omits the query string (`srv log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 400` is identical with and without `?model=`, verified empirically 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`_query_slots_detail` and `_query_slots_progress` (`proxy/proxy/observability.py:695`/`:773`) swallow non-200 responses silently — no failure metric, debug-level logging only — so a 400 on those paths is invisible in `/metrics` and `proxy.log`. Only `_query_slots` records `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}`.

## Desired change

- Record `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}` (and other non-200 reasons) from the detail/progress query paths, aligned with the existing `_query_slots` precedent.
- Add a cheap caller/tag label (e.g. `path=status|sse|availability|progress|detail`) so a router 400 can be attributed to a call site without per-request log scanning.
- Optionally emit one throttled WARNING carrying the exact URL + model string on a router-responder 400.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A router-responder `/slots` 400 on any proxy query path increments a metric carrying the call-site tag.
- Tests assert the metric/label is emitted on non-200 for the detail and progress paths.
- Alert rules in `monitoring/slots_query_alerts.yaml` are reviewed so the added series does not create alert noise.
- Documentation (`proxy/README.md` slots-status section) mentions the metric and label.
- Full project test suite passes.

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC1 (decision half) and AC6 (unit half).

**Goal:** As a proxy maintainer, I want the local→remote boundary compaction contract written down as failing tests before any production code exists, so that the trigger gates, the slot pin and the release ordering are specified by executable assertions rather than prose.

**Target outcome:** a single new test module, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py`, that expresses the whole boundary-compaction contract and currently fails for the right reason (missing symbol / missing behaviour), not because of an unrelated import error.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - The module collects cleanly and every test fails only because the boundary symbols do not exist yet.
  - Decision tests cover: fires for a session with recorded local provenance routed to a `type: remote` provider; does **not** fire for a session with no prior local service; does **not** fire below the minimum-size guard; does **not** fire when `server.remote_boundary_compaction` is `false`.
  - Decision tests assert the machine-readable reason token for every skip path (`boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`, plus the disabled token).
  - Slot-pin tests assert the summariser request body carries the session's assigned `id_slot`.
  - A release-ordering test asserts the session's local lease release precedes the remote stream start.
- Automated tests: the module is run through the test skill (`/skill:test` changed scope) and its red state is recorded on this item.

**Constraints**

- Test-only change: no production behaviour may change in this item.
- Follow the conventions of the existing compaction tests (`proxy/tests/test_compaction_bypass_wiring.py`, `proxy/tests/test_router_helpers_compaction.py`): `pytest` classes, injected fakes for the summariser and estimator, no live llama-server or GPU dependency.
- Tests must be deterministic and fast; no sleeps or network calls.

**Risky assumptions**

- One module can host both the decision unit tests and the later dispatch integration test without becoming unwieldy; if it grows past ~600 lines, split the integration half into its own module during the integration item.
- The summary marker (`<!-- compaction-summary -->` style) and the retention invariant (system prompt + first user message verbatim) stay exactly as `plan_session_compaction` implements them today, so the tests can assert against them.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — new test module holding the full contract.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_bypass_wiring.py` — reference for fakes/wiring style.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — the module whose new helper the tests will target.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` exists and the boundary compaction decision is covered by unit tests that fire only for a session with recorded local provenance, a remote provider type and an estimate above the minimum-size guard.
2. Unit tests assert each skip reason token for the boundary decision, including below-guard suppression and the disabled-knob case.
3. Unit tests assert the summarisation call is pinned to the session's assigned `id_slot` (the slot pin contract), and an ordering assertion proves the release precedes the remote stream start.
4. The new tests are TDD-red before implementation: they fail only because the boundary symbols are absent, and that red state is recorded on this work item.
5. Tests run deterministically with injected fakes — no live llama-server, GPU or network access.

data.description:
Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC1 (decision + provenance half) and AC5 (config gating).

**Goal:** As an agent operator, when a long session that has been served locally is about to be dispatched remote, I want the proxy to *decide* to compact that session's history — driven by recorded local provenance and a size guard behind an independent, default-off knob — so the trigger exists before any dispatch wiring.

**Target outcome:** a pure boundary-decision helper plus the provenance signal it reads, all inert by default.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `decide_boundary_compaction(...)` in `proxy/compaction.py`: takes provider type, session provenance, estimated tokens and config; returns `{should_compact, reason, est_before, guard_tokens, enabled}`. Fires only on `remote` + provenance + `est > guard`.
2. Provenance: add `locally_served_turns` (or equivalent) to `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py::Session`, `mark_locally_served()` / `has_local_provenance()` on `SessionManager`, and call the marker from the successful local-dispatch completion path in `proxy/proxy/router.py` (next to the existing `update_messages` block). Provenance is never derived from a live slot assignment.
3. Config: resolve `server.remote_boundary_compaction` (default `false`) and `remote_boundary_compaction_min_tokens` (defaulted, e.g. 20000) in `compaction_config()`; validate both in `validate_compaction_config()` (booleans/positive ints) without touching `compaction_trigger_ratio`.
4. Document the knob in the `--- Session compaction config ---` block of `proxy/config.yaml`, shipping `false`.
5. Green the C1 decision tests plus new tests for provenance recording, the size guard and the disabled knob.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - The decision fires exactly on (remote type ∧ provenance ∧ above guard ∧ knob enabled).
  - With `remote_boundary_compaction: false`, the decision is `should_compact: false` with a `boundary_disabled` reason and no summariser is ever built.
  - A session whose slot was released, evicted or save/restored still qualifies: provenance comes from the session store, not `_slot_owners`.
  - `validate_compaction_config` rejects a non-boolean knob and a negative/zero guard with a `FATAL:`/`WARNING:` prefixed message consistent with the existing validators.
- Automated tests: the C1 decision tests turn green; new provenance/guard/validation tests added and green.

**Constraints**

- Do not re-enable assembly-time compaction: `compaction_trigger_ratio` stays `0` in the shipped config and the new knob must not read or write it.
- No dispatch-path behaviour change in this item — the helper is called by the follow-on hook item only.
- `compaction_config()` is the single resolution point; no ad-hoc `config.get(...)` for the new keys elsewhere.

**Risky assumptions**

- The minimum-size guard default (~20K estimated tokens) is a reasoned starting point, not a measured one: it is above trivial sessions and well below the ~180K assembly trigger. It is configurable so the operator can tune it; the value and the reasoning are recorded in `proxy/config.yaml`.
- Recording provenance on every local completion is cheap (one counter increment inside the existing `update_messages` block) and does not alter session-history semantics.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — new `decide_boundary_compaction` helper beside `decide_session_compaction`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `compaction_config()` resolution; `validate_compaction_config()` additions.
- `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py` — `Session.locally_served_turns`, `mark_locally_served()`, `has_local_provenance()`.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — provenance marker call on the successful local-completion path.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `remote_boundary_compaction: false` + `remote_boundary_compaction_min_tokens` with comments.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — decision/provenance/guard tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Boundary compaction is decided by a helper that fires only for a request about to be dispatched to a `type: remote` provider for a session with at least one prior locally-served turn recorded in the session store, and above the minimum-size guard.
2. Provenance is recorded in the session store and never derived from a live slot assignment, so a released or save/restored slot does not disqualify a session; a session with no prior local service is unchanged.
3. The boundary compaction is controlled by its own independent knob `server.remote_boundary_compaction` (default `false`) plus a configurable minimum-size guard, resolved in `compaction_config` and validated at startup, and it does not re-enable or read the assembly-time `compaction_trigger_ratio`.
4. `proxy/config.yaml` ships the knob disabled by default with explanatory comments, and the guard value and its reasoning are documented inline.
5. Unit tests cover the boundary decision (fires / does not fire by session provenance and size) and the config validation, and the module docstring describes the boundary trigger.
data.title: Boundary compaction decision helper, knob and local provenance

data.description:
Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC2 and the release half of AC3.

**Goal:** As the local model's capacity, I want the boundary summarisation to run on the slot the session already owns and that slot to be free the instant the summary is produced, so a session being served remotely never holds local GPU capacity and never borrows another session's warm slot.

**Target outcome:** a slot-pinned local summariser callable and an immediate-release step, both unit-tested in isolation.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`: a slot-pinned builder (e.g. `build_slot_pinned_summarizer(config, slot_id, llama_port=...)`) that posts to the **local** llama-server chat-completions endpoint with `id_slot: <slot_id>` and the **session's own local model** — not `summarizer_model.llama_model`, because slot ids are per llama-server instance and the Qwen2.5-7B summariser backend has its own slot space (see Risky assumptions). Reuse the existing prompt/transcript/retry/fail-open machinery (`EmptySummary`) rather than reimplementing it.
2. `id_slot` is threaded into the request body and asserted in tests; a `None` slot returns a summariser that never fires and reports `boundary_no_slot`.
3. `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: a small async helper that, given `srv` and a session id, returns the session's assigned slot (read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session`) and, after the summariser returns (success, failure or timeout), calls `_release_local_dispatch` immediately — before the remote stream starts.
4. Green the C1 slot-pin tests; add release-ordering tests (release recorded before the remote request is issued) and a no-leak assertion on the lease registry.
5. Docstrings state the KV caveat: prefilling the summariser prompt overwrites that slot's KV, acceptable only because the session is leaving local.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - The summariser request body carries `id_slot == _assigned_slot_for_session(session_id)` and targets the local endpoint.
  - No assigned slot → no summariser call, `boundary_no_slot` reason, and the release helper is still invoked so no stale lease survives.
  - Release happens on summariser completion (success / failure / timeout), not on remote response completion — proven by an ordering assertion.
  - The lease registry holds no entry for the session after the helper returns.
- Automated tests: unit tests for the pin, the no-slot path and the release ordering; all green.

**Constraints**

- Never pin to another session's slot: only the read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session` lookup, never `_slot_id_for_session` (which assigns).
- Never fall back to `models.compact` or a dedicated summariser model on this path (parent AC4).
- Reuse `SlotLockCoordinator` ordering; do not add a second lock.
- Bounded by `compaction_summarizer_timeout`; no new timeout knob.

**Risky assumptions**

- **Slot ids are per llama-server instance, so "the session's own slot" means the main local model's slot, not the Qwen2.5-7B summariser backend's slot.** The summariser therefore runs with the main local model's name against the local endpoint. This is the reading of parent AC2 ("reuses the session's own disposable slot instead of taking another session's slot or a separate summariser model"); it is recorded here so the follow-on wiring item does not silently reinterpret it.
- The slot is idle at the boundary (the session is leaving), so the summariser prefill does not queue behind a long generation; if it does, the timeout bounds the wait and the request fails open.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — slot-pinned builder reusing the existing prompt/retry/fail-open machinery.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — slot lookup + immediate `_release_local_dispatch` helper.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session` (reuse, no change expected).
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py` — reference for summariser test style.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — slot-pin and release-ordering tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The summarisation call is pinned to the local llama-server slot currently assigned to that session (`id_slot` from the session→slot registry), so it reuses the session's own disposable slot instead of taking another session's slot or a separate summariser model; verified by asserting the summariser request carries the assigned `id_slot`.
2. When the session has no assigned slot the summariser is not called and the skip is reported with the `boundary_no_slot` machine-readable reason token.
3. The session's local dispatch lease / slot ownership is released immediately after the summariser returns (success, failure, or timeout) and before the remote response is streamed, verified by an ordering assertion plus a no-leaked-lease assertion on the lease registry.
4. Unit tests cover the slot pin, the no-slot path and the release ordering with injected fakes; no live server or GPU required.
5. Docstrings record the KV-overwrite caveat and the per-instance slot-id reasoning that makes the session's own local model — not the dedicated summariser model — the summarisation target.
data.title: Slot-pinned boundary summariser and immediate lease release

data.description:
Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC1 (dispatch half), AC3, AC4.

**Goal:** As an agent operator, when a session that has been served locally falls back to a remote provider, I want the compacted history actually dispatched upstream — and when compaction cannot run, I want the untouched history sent with a WARNING that names why.

**Target outcome:** one gated, idempotent, fail-open hook at the remote dispatch point(s), reusing `evaluate_and_apply_compaction` where its semantics fit.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: `async def evaluate_boundary_compaction(srv, config, body_json, session_id, provider_cfg, ...) -> dict` — resolves the knob, reads provenance and the estimate, calls `decide_boundary_compaction`, builds the slot-pinned summariser, runs the summarisation in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread`, matching `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`), releases the lease immediately, and rewrites `body_json["messages"]` on success (setting `cache_prompt` and `result`-style metadata keys so the existing `X-Compaction-*` bridge headers can mirror them).
2. `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: call the hook immediately before the remote POST in **both** remote dispatch points — the remote-only cycle (`ptr(...)` near ~:10798) and the mixed local+remote cycle (`ptr_remote(...)` near ~:12430) — after the priority/chain resolution and before `_maybe_record_provider_affinity`.
3. Never double-summarise within one request cycle: reuse the `compaction_evaluated`-style per-request flag (a boundary-specific flag if the assembly flag would mask it) and prove it with a test.
4. Fail-open: any exception, timeout, blank/`EmptySummary` return or absent slot leaves the body byte-identical and dispatches remote; log at **WARNING** with a stable token from `boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`, `boundary_disabled`. No remote summariser fallback.
5. Emit a structured boundary compaction event (`boundary_compaction` / `compaction_event`-style) recording session, slot, est_before/est_after, turns summarised, duration_ms and outcome — reuse `log_compaction_event` rather than a new log format where it fits.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - Fires once per request when the gates pass, and the compacted list is the body sent upstream (asserted on the object handed to the remote dispatcher).
  - Summariser failure / timeout / empty / exception → identical outgoing body, remote dispatch still happens, one WARNING with the correct token.
  - Knob disabled → hook returns immediately, no provenance read cost worth logging, no summariser call.
  - Second invocation in the same cycle is a no-op.
- Automated tests: unit tests for fire-once, fail-open per failure mode, token correctness, and no-double-evaluation.

**Constraints**

- No client-protocol change: behaviour stays inside the proxy; response headers may mirror the existing `X-Compaction-*` bridge (LP-0MU44KSMS002DBWA / LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8).
- Do not re-enable or call the assembly-time path; if `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`'s trigger semantics do not fit, call `decide_boundary_compaction` directly and record why.
- Latency is charged before remote TTFT: keep the guard and timeout bounds from the earlier items; do not add unbounded waits.
- Fail-open in every branch — the hook must never raise into the dispatch loop.

**Risky assumptions**

- Both remote dispatch points are reachable through a shared helper without a third call site (e.g. `proxy/ui.py` embedding routes); if a third site dispatches remote chat traffic, it is added to the same helper and noted here.
- The request body is the authoritative history at the boundary (the session store may lag by the current turn); the hook therefore compacts `body_json["messages"]` and stores the compacted history via `session_manager.update_messages` + `mark_compacted`, inheriting the post-compaction delta heal (LP-0MTXEED8E003EDM8).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `evaluate_boundary_compaction` hook beside `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the two remote dispatch call sites (~:10798, ~:12430).
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — reason tokens / event logging reuse.
- `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py` — compacted-history update + anchors.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — hook tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a request for a session with at least one prior locally-served turn recorded in the session store is about to be dispatched to a `type: remote` provider, the proxy evaluates boundary compaction before the remote request is sent and dispatches the compacted message list upstream when compaction succeeds.
2. Summariser failure, timeout, empty/blank summary, absence of an assigned slot or an exception leaves the outgoing history byte-identical to today and still dispatches remote — an empty summary is never injected and turns are never silently dropped (existing `EmptySummary` / `remote_with_guidance` guarantees preserved).
3. No remote summariser fallback: every skip is logged at WARNING with a stable machine-readable reason token (`boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`) and the request proceeds remote untouched.
4. A structured compaction-event log line records session, slot, est_before/est_after, turns summarised, duration and outcome for every boundary evaluation.
5. Boundary evaluation is idempotent per request cycle (exactly one summarisation, no re-evaluation), and unit tests cover fire-once plus each fail-open failure mode.

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC6 (integration half) and the default-off regression half of AC5.

**Goal:** As a proxy maintainer, I want an integration test that drives the real failure-to-remote path — session served locally, then escalated — so the trigger, the summariser call count, the compacted body on the wire and the slot release ordering are proven end-to-end rather than only in unit isolation.

**Target outcome:** one integration test module (or a clearly separated section of `test_compaction_boundary_remote.py`) that exercises the dispatch cycles with stubbed HTTP transports, plus the default-off regression test.

**Minimal implementation**

1. Build a harness that (a) creates a session, (b) runs a local completion through the mixed cycle so the session records local provenance, (c) makes the next request bypass local (size or explicit remote-only chain) so it routes remote, with `httpx` transport stubs for the local summariser POST and the remote POST.
2. Assert exactly one summarisation call, that its body carries the assigned `id_slot`, and that the remote POST body carries the summary marker plus the retained system prompt and first user message verbatim.
3. Assert ordering: release of the local lease is recorded before the remote stream starts, and the lease registry holds no entry afterwards.
4. Regression: with `server.remote_boundary_compaction: false`, assert zero summariser calls and a dispatch body identical to the pre-change behaviour.
5. Cover the two unchanged cases: a session with no prior local service, and a session below the minimum-size guard.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - Exactly one summarisation call per boundary evaluation (no double evaluation in a cycle).
  - Remote request body contains the summary marker and the verbatim retention set.
  - Release precedes remote stream start; no leaked lease.
  - Knob disabled → identical dispatch body, no summariser call (byte-comparison against the un-compacted body).
- Automated tests: the integration module is green via the test skill; no live backend, GPU or network.

**Constraints**

- Use the repo's existing stubbing patterns for `httpx` and the provider/remote cycles; do not add a live-endpoint test.
- Do not weaken or delete existing compaction tests; this item adds coverage only.
- Keep runtime under a few seconds — no sleeps, no retry waits.

**Risky assumptions**

- The mixed cycle can be made to bypass local deterministically (size threshold or a remote-only chain) without depending on GPU state; if not, the remote-only cycle is used and the local provenance seeded through the session manager plus a prior local-dispatch unit path.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — integration + regression tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_bypass_wiring.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_integration.py` — harness patterns to reuse.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the cycles under test.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the hook under test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An integration test drives a session that is served locally and then routed remote, asserting exactly one summarisation call for the boundary compaction.
2. The integration test asserts the compacted body (summary marker plus the verbatim retention set) is what reaches the remote provider on the wire.
3. The integration test asserts the session's local dispatch lease is released and, with an ordering assertion, that the release precedes the remote stream start.
4. The boundary compaction is controlled by its own independent knob `server.remote_boundary_compaction` (default `false`) that does not re-enable assembly-time compaction, ships disabled by default in `proxy/config.yaml`, and leaves request handling unchanged when disabled — the regression test asserts no summariser call and an identical dispatch body.
5. A session with no prior local service, and a session below the agreed minimum-size guard, are asserted to dispatch unchanged.

# Provide retry timing for refused admission (LP-0MVTETXU2007FBGC)

**Status: closed as duplicate.** The producer confirmed (2026-10-30) that the
payload observed was the **`Local admission refused` 429**
(`code: local_admission_reject`), whose retry timing is already delivered,
tested, documented and released. The one refusal that still lacks timing —
the local slot-exhaustion `429` (`code: all_slots_exhausted`) — was split out
to **LP-0MVUXY1CL005KWCC** so the useful residue is not lost.

## Original request

> When returning the refused admission error (below) provide a retry after
> field as well so that clients can auto-recover:

(The body that followed was not stored; the producer has since identified it
as the `Local admission refused` 429.)

## Producer answer (Q1)

**Answer (producer):** (b) — the `Local admission refused` 429,
`code: local_admission_reject`.

## Verification — every acceptance criterion of the request is met

The refusal body carries the retry story for both refusal builders (the
pin-local refusal and the admission-reject refusal), via the single
reason→timing decision `_refusal_retry_timing()`
(`proxy/proxy/provider.py:4756`):

- `retry_after` (body) + `Retry-After` (header) — identical values, ≥ 1 s,
  capped by `server.max_retry_after_seconds`.
- `retry_at` — the same instant as an absolute RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, exactly
  when `Retry-After` is present.
- `retryable` — `true` for ETA/occupancy/cooldown/lease/queue-expiry reasons;
  `false` (with compaction guidance and no timer) for
  `prefill_budget_exceeded` / `context_too_large`, where waiting cannot help.
- Token evidence (`new_tokens` / `budget_tokens`) so a client can size a
  compaction, and `suggested_action` naming the remedy.

Reason-specific values (evidence over the older ETA-only formula):

| Reason | `Retry-After` | `retryable` | `retry_at` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `eta_exceeds_budget`, `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget` | `ceil(projected_wait − budget)`, ≥1 s, capped | `true` | RFC 3339 UTC |
| `cooldown` / lease-held / contention-queue expiry | real expiry remainder | `true` | RFC 3339 UTC |
| `prefill_budget_exceeded`, `context_too_large` | absent (by design) | `false` | absent |

Delivered by, and pinned by tests and docs, in:

- **LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X** — truthful, reason-specific retry time (`429`
  `Retry-After` / `retry_at` / `retryable`); the per-reason contract.
- **LP-0MVQ23B80009OZ9V** — non-admission exits (cooldown, lease, queue
  expiry) derive the timer from the real expiry, not the ETA formula.
- **LP-0MVSM06BK008FZUE** — deferral `429` on queue-budget expiry, carrying the
  measured expiry through `advertised_retry_after`.
- Tests: `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (header/body
  agreement, `retryable`, RFC 3339 `retry_at` coherence on queue exits and
  deferrals), `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_error_code.py`.
- Docs: `proxy/docs/routing.md` → `### Per-reason retry contract
  (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X)`; `proxy/README.md` exhaustion section.

**Release check.** The fixes landed on `dev` on 2026-10-28 (commit `0466f5db`)
and reached `main` in **v0.1.26** (tag on `a9772b00`, released 2026-10-29 21:17
UTC). The pre-fix body (`git show 93e2f66d:proxy/proxy/provider.py`, v0.1.25)
advertised the *untruthful* `1 s` timer for a permanently over-budget prompt —
the exact "client cannot auto-recover" symptom. If a client still sees no
timing, the running proxy predates v0.1.26: restart it with
`/skill:start-proxy --restart` rather than changing code.

## Why closed rather than re-scoped

Every behaviour the request asks for on the identified payload is already
present, covered by tests and documented — a second implementation slice would
be redundant work. Two genuinely-remaining timing gaps surfaced during the
intake were recorded separately instead of silently absorbed here:

- **LP-0MVUXY1CL005KWCC** — retry timing for the local slot-exhaustion `429`
  (`code: all_slots_exhausted`), the only admission refusal with no timing.
- **LP-0MVUHR1LB009Q0CF** — `Retry-After` header / `retry_at` parity for
  `POST /llama/local/reserve` refusals.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — which payload did you mean?** Description referenced an error body
  that was not stored ("the refused admission error (below):"). **Answer
  (producer, 2026-10-30): (b) the `Local admission refused` 429
  (`code: local_admission_reject`).** Research: `git show
  93e2f66d:proxy/proxy/provider.py` (v0.1.25) already carried `retry_after` in
  that body but with the untruthful `1 s` value for `prefill_budget_exceeded`,
  which LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X replaced with the reason-aware contract; `provider.py:6049`
  shows the slot `429` with no timing at all; `proxy/README.md:905` documented
  that absence. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — is a timer meaningful for slot exhaustion?** **Answer (repo
  evidence):** yes; slots free when the occupying prefill/decode completes, and
  the router-level slot `503` already advertises
  `server.slot_unavailable_retry_after`. Source:
  `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:876-906`, `proxy/config.yaml:2317`. Recorded in
  LP-0MVUXY1CL005KWCC.
- **Q3 — should the compaction gate gain a timer?** **Answer (repo evidence):**
  no; waiting cannot change a context-too-large verdict — compaction is the
  remedy. Source: `proxy/docs/routing.md` per-reason retry contract.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVUHR1LB009Q0CF** – Retry timing parity for POST /llama/local/reserve refusals (open)
- **LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ** – Local-only admission refusal must not report 'All providers exhausted' (open)
- **LP-0MVSS435600370D6** – Feature: capacity verdict on the admission-reject/exhausted refusal payload (open)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mu56zm0k005f69g, 0mv0mm5r60025xze, 0mvntt4x8009io2x, 0mvq23b80009oz9v, 0mvsm06bk008fzue (+405 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance (+366 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance (+366 more)

# Investigate what happens if I switch to a single slot

## Problem statement

The operator is considering serving the local model from a single llama-server
slot (`session_slot_pool_size: 1`, i.e. 1 x 262,144 tokens instead of 2 x
131,072) and needs to know two things before deciding: which routing and
balancing metrics adjust themselves and which stay put, and what a single slot
would do to throughput. Today the answer is spread across `provider.py`
derivation helpers, static config constants, log-consuming analysis scripts and
one heavily-gated measurement experiment, so there is no single, auditable
answer.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** deciding the local slot geometry.
  *"As the operator, I want to know exactly which mechanisms follow a 2 -> 1
  slot change by themselves and which I must change by hand, so I do not
  switch geometry and silently get the old routing behaviour."*
- **Work-item pipeline owner** judging whether single-slot serving would slow
  the herdr work-item cadence.
  *"As the pipeline owner, I want a reasoned, quantified prediction of turns
  and tokens served locally over time, so I can tell whether fewer slots cost
  throughput or only latency."*
- **Agent maintainer / on-call** relying on metrics to spot a single-slot
  regression.
  *"As on-call, I want the audit to tell me which existing metric would reveal
  single-slot starvation, and which ones would stay silent, so I know where the
  blind spots are."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A single-slot impact report exists at `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`
  with a complete inventory table of every routing/balancing mechanism and
  metric on the local dispatch path. Each row records: its current value at 2
  slots, its computed value at 1 slot, its classification
  (`derived-auto` / `static-needs-manual-change` / `not-applicable`), and
  `file:line` evidence. The inventory must cover at least: per-slot context,
  physical per-slot clamp, economic warm ceiling, absolute warm cap, cold
  threshold, hard-routing cap, `session_slot_tenants`, the dispatch lease pool
  (`max_local`), `local_max_concurrent_prefills`, contention-queue
  wait/depth/lease-grace/ETA-ordering, slot-exhaustion retries, `/health` and
  `/llama/local/status` counts plus per-slot detail, the usage-analysis report
  metrics (local busy %, turns served locally, input/output tokens processed
  locally, diverts by reason, queue waits, dispatch-to-first-byte, prefill and
  decode slot-seconds, decode tok/s), the Prometheus `llama_slots_*` counters,
  and herdr's consumption of the status endpoint.
- AC2: The report states the headline answer explicitly: how many inventory
  items auto-adjust, which items stay static, and the exact
  `key: old -> new` list required for a coherent single-slot switch. It must
  state that the configured absolute warm cap (120,000) and economic-ceiling
  ratio (0.4578) keep the effective warm ceiling at 120,000 even though the
  physical per-slot clamp doubles to 258,048, so doubling the per-slot context
  routes nothing extra on its own. The one-line verdict is also recorded as a
  comment on this work item.
- AC3: A reasoned throughput-impact analysis at request level, **including
  tokens processed locally**, with a named mechanism and a sourced baseline for
  every conclusion: turns served locally and tokens processed locally
  (prompt/completion), per-session first-byte and decode latency,
  head-of-line blocking and queue waits, slot reuse/thrash and re-prefill
  volume, and concurrency headroom. Each conclusion identifies the metric and
  the A/B arm comparison that would confirm or refute it. Token figures must
  state their provenance: the report's `Stream finished`
  `tokens=prompt/completion/total` lines (authoritative) versus any derived
  estimate, and how local versus remote turns are split.
- AC4: A metrics-gap list: for each single-slot conclusion, state whether an
  existing metric can detect it. Every blind spot is filed as a follow-up work
  item (e.g. the blocked slot-occupancy metrics LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL) rather
  than implemented in this item.
- AC5 (testing/validation): New or extended unit tests pin the derivations the
  audit relies on — at 1 and at 2 slots, the physical clamp, effective warm
  ceiling (including the absolute-cap dominance), cold threshold and
  hard-routing cap resolve to the values the report documents — so the report's
  claims are executable and future config drift fails the suite.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular,
  cross-links and any comment that asserts a fixed 2-slot pool are corrected in
  `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`,
  `proxy/config.yaml`, `models.ini` and `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/
  REFERENCE.md`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Desk analysis only** (producer answer 1A). No live geometry flip, no
  proxy/llama-server restart and no arm measurement: the measured comparison
  belongs to LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN, whose arms are gated on a >= 60 % busy night.
- Read-only runtime inspection is limited to the existing `/health` and
  `/llama/local/status` endpoints and must not add GPU load or contend for a
  slot.
- Every claim cites `file:line` or a measured baseline with its window and
  source. No unsourced numbers.
- No new metrics and no configuration-value changes in this item (producer
  answer 3B): gaps become follow-up items, behaviour changes become separate
  items. Factually wrong comments may be corrected.
- The report is a prediction plus an auto-adjustment audit. It must not be
  written as, or pre-empt, the A/B verdict.

## Existing state (seed evidence to verify and extend)

- Current base geometry: `session_slot_pool_size: 2`,
  `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, warm cap 120,000, cold 38,000, economic
  ratio 0.4578 (`proxy/config.yaml:1685`, `:1332`, `:1297`, `:1410`). The
  per-mode overlays are retired, so `config.yaml` is authoritative
  (`proxy/proxy/config_merge.py`).
- Per-slot context is derived, never configured:
  `effective_per_slot_threshold(ctx, slots) = ctx // slots - 4096`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:1816`), i.e. 126,976 at 2 slots and 258,048 at 1.
- WARM resolves through the 3-term model
  (`provider.py:1930`-`2010`): economic ceiling
  `round(ratio x ctx)` capped by the absolute warm config, then clamped by the
  physical per-slot threshold and the hard-routing cap. With today's constants
  `min(round(0.4578 x 262144) = 120,010, 120,000) = 120,000`, so warm stays
  120,000 at one slot.
- COLD is an economic new-token threshold and is explicitly **not** scaled or
  clamped (`provider.py:1955`-`1968`); the `(cold, warm]` band must not collapse
  (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- Queue and prefill knobs are static, not slot-derived:
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60`, `contention_queue_max_depth: 8`,
  `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300`, ETA ordering on
  (`proxy/config.yaml:1756`-`1788`), and `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`
  (`:1706`), so prefill is already serialised with two slots and a second slot
  only overlaps decode.
- Auto-adjusting items already identified: `session_slot_tenants` defaults to
  the resolved slot count ("N tenants, N slots", `config.yaml:1378`); the
  dispatch lease pool `max_local` reads `session_slot_pool_size`
  (`provider.py:6172`); runtime counts and per-slot detail come from
  llama-server `/slots` / `/props` (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`) and are
  consumed by `/health`, `/llama/local/status` and herdr's per-slot dispatch
  (LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ, cross-repo WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F).
- Per-slot occupancy metrics are **not** published yet
  (LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL, blocked) — a likely gap for detecting single-slot
  starvation.
- The single-slot (Arm B) threshold values are already defined:
  warm 258,048, economic ratio 0.9844, cold 38,000
  (`docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` section 3.1).
- Baselines available for the throughput reasoning: a 24 h window with 2,064
  `context_too_large` diverts, 105 of them from already-warm sessions at
  126-137K tokens; local idle 89.8 % serving 225 turns over 26 sessions;
  measured concurrency average 1.04 while busy with peak 2; prefill dominating
  local response time (prompt-eval p50 16 s, p90 189 s, max 591 s); 43.8 M
  tokens/day re-prefilled (`docs/dev/slot-reuse-gap-final-report.md` section 3).
- Known counter-evidence for fewer slots: inter-session slot thrash invalidates
  cached prefixes (`docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`, "cache preservation:
  poor") and 27 sessions were observed cycling through 2 slots in 5.4 h
  (`proxy/config.yaml` comment at `:1371`).

## Desired change

A decision-grade, evidence-cited analysis of single-slot serving: (a) the
derived-vs-static inventory and the exact coupled config changes a coherent
switch needs, (b) a request-level throughput prediction including tokens
processed locally, with the confirming metric named for each claim, (c) a
metrics-gap list with filed follow-ups, and (d) unit tests pinning the
derivations, plus documentation cross-links. No runtime behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` — the new report (main deliverable)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `effective_per_slot_threshold`,
  `_effective_large_context_thresholds`, `effective_large_context_economic_ceiling`,
  `compute_hard_routing_cap`, `_get_active_local_slots`, dispatch lease pool
- `proxy/config.yaml` — slot/ctx/threshold/queue keys and their comments
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `/slots` counts, per-slot detail,
  `/llama/local/status` payload
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — status endpoint consumers
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `aggregation.py`, `reporting.py`, `REFERENCE.md` — request/token/divert/queue
  metric sources
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_per_slot_ctx.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_hard_routing_cap.py`, `tests/test_ctx_slot_validation.py` —
  existing threshold tests to extend
- `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` —
  protocol/design docs to cross-link
- `models.ini` — launch-flag comments describing per-slot context

## Risks & assumptions

  different windows. Mitigation: every baseline carries its window and source.

  serialisation cost of one slot is under-observed today; the report must say
  so rather than extrapolate a cheap conclusion.
- **Risk (mis-attributed tokens):** "tokens processed locally" can be computed
  only from `Stream finished` lines carrying provider plus token counts; a

- **Assumption:** "single slot" means `session_slot_pool_size: 1` with
  unchanged `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, i.e. 1 x 262,144 per-slot context

  **LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN** (3-term warm model),
  **LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP** (band collapse),
  **LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95** (warm cap vs economic ceiling).
- Queue behaviour under one slot: **LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6** (ETA ordering),

  **LP-0MTH7JX82000YS5N** (generating-only occupancy).

## Goal

Close parent AC4 (LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG): every log line that decides "not local" must name the parsed preference, so a local-preference violation is attributable from `proxy.log` alone.

Parent: LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG. Blocks the parent's closure (audit finding AC4, 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`_record_provider_context_skip()` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:3311-3347`) emits

```text
routing_skip_provider_context provider=<name> type=local status=provider_context_exceeded
estimated_tokens=<n> limit=<n> reason=provider_context_exceeded session=<id>
```

with **no** `preference=` field. Every sibling skip line carries one (`routing_skip_local`, `routing_check`, `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`, `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback`, the chain-resolution `Skipping provider=<local> …` lines), and `proxy/docs/routing.md` claims "Every 'not local' line also carries `preference=<parsed>`". The per-entry context-ceiling exit therefore breaks both the parent's AC4 and the documented invariant, so a `local-preferred` request that leaves the local route via the entry `max_context_tokens` cap cannot be attributed by preference.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_record_provider_context_skip` emits `preference=<parsed>` on its `routing_skip_provider_context` line, resolved through the single parser (`_request_local_preference(request)` / `admission_reserve.parse_preference`) — no second header parse.
- The field is **additive**: every pre-existing key (`provider`, `type`, `status`, `estimated_tokens`, `limit`, `reason`, `session`) keeps its name and order; a `key=value` parser assertion proves it.
- An absent header logs `preference=prefer-local`, never an empty or missing value.
- Both call sites are covered (`provider.py:10518`, `provider.py:12098`).
- A `caplog` test asserts `preference=` for each of the three values (`local-preferred`, `prefer-local`, `remote-ok`) on this line, following the existing pattern in `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py`.
- Full suite green via the changed-scope gate first.

Parent-AC traceability: covers parent AC4 — "Every skip/fallback line that decides 'not local' logs the parsed preference (`preference=local-preferred|prefer-local|remote-ok`) so an intent violation is visible in `proxy.log`; `priority_routing` keeps its existing fields (additive change only)."

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_record_provider_context_skip` (`:3311`), call sites (`:10518`, `:12098`), `_request_local_preference` (`:6305` for reference).
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py` — caplog + key=value additive assertion pattern.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the "Every 'not local' line also carries `preference=<parsed>`" claim this item makes true (do **not** edit the sibling wording; that is the docs child's scope).

## Notes

- Log-grep tooling (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `.pi/skills/proxy-log-debug/SKILL.md`) parses these lines; the change is additive so their parsers keep working. Verify read-only; do not edit skill files (repository boundary).

## Goal

Close parent AC7 (LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG): `proxy/docs/routing.md` must state the **deferrable vs too-large split** instead of the now-false universal claim that every local-route exit refuses.

Parent: LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG. Blocks the parent's closure (audit finding AC7, 2026-10-29).

## Problem

Two statements in the document contradict each other and the code:

- § "Local-only is enforced on every exit from the local route" (`proxy/docs/routing.md:1219-1229`): "every exit from the local route is an exit into the refusal, and a `local-only` request is either completed locally or refused, never silently served by a paid provider".
- The token table 25 lines later (`:1254`) lists `context_too_large` with the log line `routing_skip_local ... → skipping local, routing to next remote provider`.

The code implements the split: a `too_large` capacity verdict strips the local entry from the chain and remote serves the request with HTTP 200 and `X-Local-Route: remote`; no local-capacity 429 is produced (`_local_preference_pins_local`, `provider.py:6554-6589`; `_promote_too_large_local_request`, `provider.py:6610-6712`). A client that reads the document today is told the opposite of what the proxy does.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The universal "every exit is an exit into the refusal / never served remotely" claim is replaced by an explicit two-outcome statement: **deferrable ⇒ 429 refusal** (`X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: <token>`), **too-large ⇒ promotion** (200, `X-Local-Route: remote`, no `Retry-After`, no local-capacity refusal, with the reason that promotion happened).
- The `X-Local-Preference` section states that `local-only` is a **legacy alias** of `local-preferred` (LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16) and that `local-preferred` means "local while the request fits local capacity, remote beyond it".
- The exit table marks each row as refusing or promoting, so `context_too_large`, `prefill_budget_exceeded` and the per-entry `max_context_tokens` cap are visibly **promoting** rows while cooldown / residency / thrash / queue / lease / quota rows are **refusing** rows.
- The `X-Local-Route` section documents the `remote` value (promotion) alongside `refused` and local success, and states that a chain with no non-local entry is never stripped (it keeps deferring/refusing).
- A test asserts the documented split matches the implementation (extend `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`; it already pins docs-vs-implementation correspondence).
- Full suite green via the changed-scope gate first.

Parent-AC traceability: covers parent AC7 — "`proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the deferrable/too-large split explicitly … and a client can tell the two apart without parsing prose."

## Key Files

- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — § "Local-only is enforced on every exit from the local route" (`:1219`), the exit/token table (`:1245-1275`), the `X-Local-Preference` semantics (`:1158`), `X-Local-Route` values (`:1173`), the verdict/`too_large` prose (`:1279`, `:1324`).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py` — docs-vs-implementation pin.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_preference_pins_local` (`:6554`), `_promote_too_large_local_request` (`:6610`) as the behaviour of record (read-only).

## Coordination

The epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY has a blocked docs child LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 ("Docs: local-preferred semantics, wire compatibility and client migration"). If that child lands first, this item reduces to verifying that its wording covers the refusal/promotion split and the `context_too_large` table rows; record the overlap rather than duplicating prose.
