data.description:
## Goal

Give clients a preference value that encodes a **hard cost ceiling**: never
dispatch a non-local provider, for any reason and under any capacity verdict —
and refuse truthfully when the request cannot be served locally.

discovered-from:LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG (producer decision 2026-10-29).

## Problem statement

The current `X-Local-Preference` vocabulary has no "never leave local" value:
`prefer-local` (default) falls through to remote on any exit, `local-preferred`
(and its legacy alias `local-only`) deliberately **promotes** an oversized
prompt to a remote tier so the client is not handed a useless capacity 429, and
`remote-ok` strips local entirely. A client whose requirement is **zero remote
spend** — e.g. a herdr worker pinned to the local GPU — therefore has only two
options: a silent paid dispatch (`local-preferred`) or no pin at all
(`prefer-local`). The 2026-10-25 incident (session
`herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152`, billed by OpenCode Go) was exactly that
client.

"Do not give me a useless 429" and "never spend my remote budget" are different
policies. Overloading `local-preferred` for both is what produced the
LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG audit conflict; this item adds the missing value **beside**
`local-preferred` without weakening its promotion.

## Users

- **A cost-capped local-only worker** (herdr worker pinned to the local GPU):
  *"As a worker whose budget is zero remote spend, I want the proxy to refuse
  rather than quietly bill me on OpenCode Go, and I want the refusal to tell me
  what to change, so I never pay for a request I did not authorise."*
- **The operator on call:** *"As the operator, I want each hard-pin refusal to
  appear as one attributable log line carrying the reason and the preference,
  so I can prove from `proxy.log` that no remote dispatch happened."*
- **A client that wants the work done regardless of cost** (today's
  `local-preferred` client): unchanged — it keeps its promotion on a too-large
  verdict (AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (vocabulary)** `X-Local-Preference: local-exclusive` parses to a new canonical constant in `admission_reserve.py` (`VALID_PREFERENCES` + documented in the module docstring); unknown values still fall back to `prefer-local`; the existing `local-only` → `local-preferred` alias is unchanged.
- **AC2 (no remote dispatch, any verdict)** With `local-exclusive`, no non-local provider is ever dispatched: not on a deferrable exit (cooldown, residency, thrash, queue cap/expiry, lease/gate denial, quota) **and not on a too-large verdict** (`context_too_large`, `prefill_budget_exceeded`, per-entry `max_context_tokens`). Asserted by a fake transport that records every upstream call (`calls == []`) across both row families.
- **AC3 (chain never stripped)** Unlike `local-preferred`, a `local-exclusive` request's chain is **not** filtered: the local entry stays so the refusal can report truthful diagnostics, and a remote-less chain behaves exactly as today.
- **AC4 (truthful refusal shape)** Deferrable exits keep the existing retryable refusal (429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: <token>`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at` per LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X). Too-large exits return the **same stable shape** (429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: <too-large exit token>`) but with `retryable: false`, **no `Retry-After`**, and body guidance to compact the prompt — a capacity retry hint for a prompt that can never fit is the untruthful-timer defect LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X exists to prevent.
- **AC5 (traceability)** Each refusal emits exactly one `local_only_refused reason=<token> preference=local-exclusive verdict=<deferrable|too_large> retryable=<bool>` line; `priority_routing` continues to carry `preference=` and `session=`.
- **AC6 (no regression)** `prefer-local`, `local-preferred` and `remote-ok` behave byte-identically to today on every path, including the too-large promotion for `local-preferred`; the existing matrix rows pass unmodified.
- **AC7 (tests)** Table-driven rows for both verdict families × `local-exclusive` (refusal, token, no upstream call, no `Retry-After` on the too-large row), a parser/vocabulary test, and an assertion that the preference appears on the refusal line. Full suite green via the changed-scope gate first.
- **AC8 (docs)** `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents `local-exclusive` in the `X-Local-Preference` section, the too-large refusal (`retryable: false`, compact guidance) and its contrast with `local-preferred`'s promotion; docs asserted against implementation by the existing docs test.
- **AC9 (documentation hygiene)** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments/docstrings, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC10 (suite)** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (changed-scope gate during development; the full suite is enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Existing state (verified)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:63-79` — `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED` /
  `PREF_PREFER_LOCAL` / `PREF_REMOTE_OK`, `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` (deprecated alias),
  `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES = {local-only: local-preferred}`,
  `VALID_PREFERENCES` (3-tuple), `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = prefer-local`.
  `parse_preference()` (`:649`) normalises through the alias table and falls back
  to `prefer-local` for unknown values — the only parse site.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:6741-6769` — `_local_preference_pins_local()` is the
  **single pin predicate**: every local-route exit that would hand the request to
  a non-local provider asks it. Today it returns `False` for a `too_large`
  verdict, which is precisely the behaviour `local-exclusive` must invert.
- `provider.py:7608-7725` — `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` is the
  loop-head choke point in both dispatch cycles; it already forwards the
  recorded exit reason, the token evidence and the parsed preference to the
  builder, so the too-large refusal needs **no new path**.
- `provider.py:6969-7075` — `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` computes the
  verdict once (`admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict`), resolves timing via
  `_refusal_retry_timing()` and emits the single refusal log line. It already
  yields `retryable: false`, no `Retry-After` and the compaction guidance for
  the two too-large tokens (`NOT_TIME_RETRYABLE_REFUSAL_REASONS`,
  `provider.py:4477`; `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE`, `:4484`) — reused, not rebuilt.
- `provider.py:6819-6899` — `_promote_too_large_local_request()` early-returns
  unless the preference is exactly `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED`, so the capacity strip
  cannot fire for `local-exclusive`. `priority.apply_local_preference()`
  (`priority.py:413`) is the single chain filter (preference **or** capacity)
  and is the second place to keep verdict-blind for the new value.
- `provider.py:6926-6966` — `_log_local_only_refusal()` is the only refusal log
  emitter; its 3-key form (`reason`, `preference`, `verdict`) is the one to
  extend with `retryable`.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py:592` —
  `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES = (LOCAL_ONLY, LOCAL_PREFERRED)` parameterises *both*
  matrix families; the too-large family asserts **promotion**, so
  `local-exclusive` must not simply be appended to that tuple.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py` pins the
  `### local-preferred: pinned while deferrable, promoted when too large`
  section's exit table and its Outcome column; a new preference needs its own
  documented subsection rather than editing that pinned table.
- Related, in flight: LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN rewrites `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` and
  the refusal `detail` string. No blocker — this item reuses whatever guidance
  is current — but the two must not both edit those strings without rebasing.

## Desired change

Add a fourth canonical value `local-exclusive` that is **verdict-blind**: it
pins the request to the local route on every exit, including the too-large
family where `local-preferred` intentionally promotes. The refusal is produced
by the existing choke point and the existing builder; the only new decision is
"is this preference a hard pin?" — answered in `_local_preference_pins_local()`
(and its chain-filter analogue) so the choke point, the admission refusal and
the free-slot guard cannot drift apart.

## Constraints

- Reuse, do not rebuild: `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`provider.py:6969`), `_refusal_timing_headers()` (`:6905`, the no-`Retry-After` rule), `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (`:7214`), `_note_local_fallback_reason()`, and `admission_reserve.LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS` as the single token table. No new refusal builder, no new token vocabulary, no new config knob.
- Keep one stable client-facing refusal shape (429 + `X-Local-Route: refused`), per LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ; `retryable: false` carries the "do not retry, compact" signal without introducing a second status code.
- Do not weaken the `local-preferred` promotion: this item adds a value beside it, it does not change that policy.
- Repository boundary: log-grep consumers under `.pi/skills/` are verified read-only; breakage is reported as a work item, not edited.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — `PREF_LOCAL_EXCLUSIVE` constant, `VALID_PREFERENCES`, module docstring; no new tokens.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_preference_pins_local()` becomes verdict-aware per preference; `_log_local_only_refusal()` gains `retryable=`; `_promote_too_large_local_request()` / `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` docstrings state the new carve-out.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `apply_local_preference()` keeps the capacity strip for a hard pin (defensive, alongside the entry guard at `provider.py:6823`).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — `local-exclusive` rows for both verdict families; `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES` left alone.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — parser/vocabulary row for the new value.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — `### X-Local-Preference` table row plus a `### local-exclusive: …` subsection; the pinned `local-preferred` section untouched.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py` (or a sibling doc-contract test) — asserts the new documented value/refusal shape against the implementation.
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py` and `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — both pin the `local_only_refused` log-line contract (key-presence only, so the additive `retryable=` key is safe; re-read them before editing the emitter).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** clients can act on `retryable: false` + compact guidance (the herdr workers already compact; the 2026-10-25 incident shows they retry blindly on a `Retry-After: 1`, so an explicit non-retryable signal is the right affordance).
- **Assumption (AC4 token spelling):** the `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` on a too-large hard-pin refusal is the **exit token that actually fired** (`context_too_large` *or* `prefill_budget_exceeded`), not a hard-coded `context_too_large`. This is forced by the existing single-token-table contract ("the header, the refusal body `reason` and `proxy.log` cannot drift") and by the Constraints' "no new token vocabulary". AC4's `context_too_large` reads as the representative token.
- **Assumption (where the refusal fires):** the too-large hard-pin refusal fires **when the loop reaches a non-local candidate**, not pre-loop, so a local model that can actually serve an estimated-oversized prompt still serves it (the estimate is conservative; an early refusal would refuse a servable request).
- **Risk:** a `local-exclusive` client on a permanently oversized prompt now gets a hard 429 instead of a served answer. That is the requested behaviour (hard cost ceiling), and the refusal names the compaction remedy; document it prominently.
- **Risk:** vocabulary growth (fourth value) complicates reasoning. Mitigation: the value is strictly "pin + never promote"; every existing value keeps its documented behaviour, and unknown values still degrade to `prefer-local`.
- **Risk:** the new `retryable=` log key widens an observability line other tooling greps. Mitigation: additive-only key appended after `verdict=`, matching the precedent set when `verdict=` itself was added; log-grep consumers under `.pi/skills/` are verified read-only before merging.
- **Risk:** `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py` pins the `### local-preferred: pinned while deferrable, promoted when too large` exit table and its Outcome column (promoting ⇔ `CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE_REASONS`). Mitigation: document `local-exclusive` in a **sibling** subsection plus the `### X-Local-Preference` table row, leaving that pinned section untouched (AC6/AC8).
- **Scope-creep guard:** a "per-preference quota/budget accounting" feature, a second status code for hard-pin refusals, and migrating existing `local-preferred` clients to the new value are **out of scope** — record as linked work items if they surface.

## Related work

- LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG — audit that surfaced the split and the need for a distinct hard-pin value (parent by discovery; completed).
- LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY — epic introducing `local-preferred` and the deferrable/too-large split.
- LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 — docs pass that renamed the pinned section and owns the `### local-preferred: …` prose this item must not disturb (AC8 adds a sibling subsection).
- LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4 — too-large promotion (must stay intact).
- LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X — truthful retry timing / non-retryable refusals (contract reused).
- LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ — refusal shape contract (reused).
- LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN — open: refreshes `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` / refusal `detail` strings this item reuses (no dependency; rebase if both land).
- LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM — the single per-request routing-outcome line (`pinned` / `promoted` vocabulary reused).
- LP-0MQ0Q24BX007C0QB — remote selection logic (chain filter context).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were required: the seed context (AC1–AC8, Constraints,
Risks) was sufficient to draft the brief, and the three ambiguities found were
resolvable from repository evidence. Three research-resolved entries are
recorded below for auditability.

- Q: "AC4 spells the too-large refusal token as `context_too_large`, but AC2 also lists `prefill_budget_exceeded` and per-entry `max_context_tokens`. Which token does `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` carry?" — Answer (research, not producer): the token that actually fired, verbatim. Evidence: `constraints` mandate "`admission_reserve.LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS` as the single token table… no new token vocabulary", and `provider.py:7670` already forwards `getattr(request, "_local_fallback_reason", None)` into the refusal body/header/log. Resolution: AC4's spelling is representative, not exclusive.
- Q: "Must the too-large hard-pin refusal be produced before the dispatch loop (like `local-preferred`'s pre-loop strip) or when the loop reaches a remote candidate?" — Answer (research): at the loop head, via the existing choke point. Evidence: `_promote_too_large_local_request()` (`provider.py:6823`) early-returns for any preference other than `local-preferred`, so nothing strips the chain for the new value; `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` then refuses the first non-local candidate. This also preserves local serving when the conservative estimate over-predicts the prompt size. No new pre-loop path (Constraints: reuse).
- Q: "Does AC4's 'body guidance to compact the prompt' need new text?" — Answer (research): no. `NOT_TIME_RETRYABLE_REFUSAL_REASONS` (`provider.py:4477`) already covers both too-large tokens → `retryable: false`, no `Retry-After`/`retry_at`, and `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` (`:4484`) already carries the compaction remedy. Note the in-flight overlap with LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN which rewrites that string.
- OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, resolved by assumption above): none — the operator may override either assumption; implementation will state both in the commit/PR description.

## Duplicate-work check

`wl search "local-exclusive"` and `wl search` keyword sweep: the only item
naming the value is this one plus LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG (completed), which
explicitly defers the new value to this item ("a distinct hard-pin value
(`local-exclusive`) is tracked separately (discovered-from this item)"). No
duplicate; partial-overlap items are linked as related work.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN** – Proxy: refresh stale client-facing refusal strings for local-preferred deferral (open)
- **LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM** – Feature: one routing-outcome line per request (completed)
- **LP-0MVTF2WLQ008BNYK** – Fix: preference= on every not-local skip line (per-entry context ceiling) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mvntt4x8009io2x, 0mvsm06lb001pru4, 0mvsm06z8003uqtm, ac1, ac2 (+424 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+396 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+396 more)

## Plan (2026-10-29) — one vertical slice, no child items

**Decision: no decomposition.** Effort is Small (PERT E=6.58 h, recommended
10.58 h) and the change is one cohesive slice — vocabulary → single pin
predicate → refusal reuse → tests → docs — that cannot be reviewed or merged
in independent pieces. Splitting would manufacture artificial children whose
ACs would restate AC1–AC9. Recorded per the plan skill's step 5 (phasing not
required for an item this size); the AC-coverage review confirms nothing is
uncovered.

**Ordering (test-first within the slice).** Test rows are added first against
the new constant, then the production change makes them pass:

1. `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — parser/vocabulary row for
   `local-exclusive` (AC1), next to
   `test_alias_table_and_canonical_set_cannot_drift` (~`:455`), which already
   asserts `local-only` is *not* canonical.
2. `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — a `local-exclusive`
   parameterisation: the existing `_DEFERRABLE_ROWS` refusal test reused
   verbatim (`calls == []`), plus a **new** too-large test asserting
   *refusal* (`429`, token, `retryable: false`, no `Retry-After`, `calls == []`)
   where `test_too_large_exits_promote_instead_of_refusing` asserts promotion
   (AC2/AC4/AC7). **Do not append to `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES`** (`:592`): that
   tuple drives the promotion assertions too.
3. `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — `PREF_LOCAL_EXCLUSIVE`, add to
   `VALID_PREFERENCES` (`:78`), module docstring vocabulary paragraph
   (`:56–79`). No alias entry, no new reason tokens.
4. `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_preference_pins_local()` (`:6735`)
   becomes verdict-aware **per preference**: `local-exclusive` returns `True`
   regardless of verdict; `local-preferred` keeps its existing
   `verdict != CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE` test. Update its docstring (the
   "``too_large`` … must fall through" paragraph is now preference-specific).
   `_promote_too_large_local_request()` (`:6771`, guard `:6826`) and
   `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` (`:7608`) docstrings state the
   carve-out.
5. `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `apply_local_preference()` (`:413`): the
   capacity strip never applies to a hard-pin preference (defensive; the only
   caller passing a verdict is `provider.py:6873`, already gated on
   `local-preferred`). AC3's "chain is never filtered" then holds at both
   places.
6. `proxy/docs/routing.md` — `### X-Local-Preference` table row
   (`:1315–1319`) plus a **new `###` section placed after
   `### Per-reason retry contract (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X)` and before
   `## Stream Error Handling`** (i.e. outside *both* pinned ranges, see the
   doc-test hazard below). Records `retryable: false`, no `Retry-After`,
   compaction guidance, and the contrast with `local-preferred`'s promotion.
7. Sibling doc-contract assertion (new test, or an added case in
   `test_local_only_exit_docs.py`) tying the documented `local-exclusive`
   value + too-large shape to `admission_reserve.PREF_LOCAL_EXCLUSIVE` (AC8).

### Corrections to the brief (verified in the tree today)

- **Line drift**: the pin predicate is at `provider.py:6735` (brief says
  `:6741–6769`), the promotion guard at `:6771`/`:6826` (brief: `:6819`).
  Implement against the **symbols**, not the line numbers.
- **The pin predicate has five call sites, not three.** Besides the two
  loop-head choke points (`:7590`, `:7666`) it decides the routing-outcome line
  (`:7135`), the admission-reject classification (`:8108`) and the free-slot /
  direct-guard fall-through (`:12895`). Making it verdict-blind for
  `local-exclusive` is what satisfies AC2 on the admission-guard exits — and
  all five must be re-read, because each turns "promote/fall through" into
  "refuse" for the new value.
- **AC5 gap at the free-slot guard**: `_log_local_only_refusal(_direct_reason)`
  (`:12903`) passes neither preference nor verdict, so the line defaults to
  `preference=local-only` — untruthful for a `local-exclusive` request. The
  call site must thread the parsed preference (its caller already holds
  `_preference` at `:12895`). Keep the 2-key shape byte-identical for
  every pre-existing preference; add `retryable=` only where the builder
  computes the timing (`:7071`).
- **Doc-test hazard (decides AC8's placement).**
  `test_local_only_exit_docs.py` slices routing.md from
  `### `local-preferred`: …` to `### Response headers`, and
  `_documented_outcomes()` maps *token → outcome* with later rows overwriting
  earlier ones. A second table inside that range naming
  `context_too_large | … | refusing` would silently flip the pinned
  "promoting == `CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE_REASONS`" assertion. The
  `local-exclusive` section must therefore live **outside** that range — hence
  the placement in step 6, rather than the brief's "sibling subsection" inside
  the `local-preferred` section.
- **Refusal `detail` prose** (`:7038`) still spells
  `X-Local-Preference: local-only`. AC4 needs no new prose, and
  LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN rewrites these strings — do **not** edit them here;
  rebase if that item lands first.
- **Log-grep consumers verified read-only**: no file under `.pi/skills/`
  matches `local_only_refused` (only worktree copies of proxy sources do), so
  the additive `retryable=` key has no out-of-repo consumer to break.
- **Docs hygiene (AC9)**: `proxy/docs/routing.md` is the only Markdown file in
  the repo mentioning `local-preferred`; no README or wiki table restates the
  vocabulary, so AC9 adds nothing beyond step 6 + step 4 docstrings.
- **`local-exclusive` on an unservable prompt** is a hard 429 by design; the
  new section must say so prominently and name compaction as the remedy
  (brief's documented risk).

### Open questions

None blocking. The brief's three research-resolved assumptions stand
(the `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` carries the exit token that fired; the
too-large refusal fires at the loop head, not pre-loop; compaction guidance is
reused as-is).

# Log the resolved snapshot and sidecar paths in `slot_ratio_seed`

## discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want each `slot_ratio_seed` line to carry the snapshot path it
resolved (or the candidate paths it tried) and whether the sidecar was present,
so the remaining per-session cause of `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot` is
attributable from logs instead of inferred from code inspection.

## Why (evidence)

The verdict on LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (docs/dev/slot-ratio-seed-verdict-LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3.md)
proved from 4,488 decisions that the seed path always fails at the lookup
(`missing_sidecar` 75.8 %, `missing_snapshot` 24.2 %; `found`, `expired`,
`prefix_mismatch` all 0). It identified two provable writer-side gaps (the
eviction save path writes no sidecar; the request path skips the sidecar when no
usage block was measured) but could not split the 31 affected sessions between
them, because `missing_sidecar` records `stored_messages=0` by design and logs
neither the resolved `slot_<session>.bin` path nor the sidecar path.

## Scope

**In scope:** one extra field on the existing INFO line (behaviour-neutral) plus
tests/docs. **Out of scope:** any change to the credit decision, `prefix_matches`,
the TTL, or the sidecar format (those belong to LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E).

## Proposed change

1. In `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, extend `log_seed_outcome()` with an
   optional `slot=<basename>` field (basename only — no absolute paths in logs)
   and pass the resolved candidate for `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot`,
   so a later grep can tell which directory/endpoint variant resolved.
2. Cover every outcome branch in `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`.
3. Document the extra field in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every `slot_ratio_seed` line names the resolved snapshot basename (or the
  first candidate tried when none exists), covered by a unit test per branch.
- No behaviour change: the existing outcome vocabulary and credit decision are
  untouched, and the full seed-outcome test suite passes.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the field.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (verdict could not split the
  `missing_sidecar` sub-causes from logs)
- feeds: the post-fix re-measurement on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E

# Slot-cache cleanup: protect recent orphan sidecars from the orphan sweep

## Problem statement

`scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` rule 3 (orphan sidecars, added by commit
`5502ee44` under LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC) deletes **every** `.ratio.json` sidecar
whose `slot_<session>.bin` snapshot is gone, with no age guard. Every other
deletion rule in the script protects a recent artefact (`--min-age-days`, the
size rule's protective window), so the orphan rule is the one path that can
delete a file written moments ago — for example a sidecar whose snapshot is
momentarily absent while a save/restore is settling, or a save that failed
between writing the sidecar and the snapshot. The original acceptance criteria
for LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC required "a sidecar whose snapshot is missing and which
is older than `--min-age-days` is deleted; a recent orphan is kept"; only the
first half shipped.

## Users

**Operator (primary).** Wants orphan pruning to be aggressive on genuinely
stale files while never racing a live save: "When I raise `--min-age-days` to
protect active sessions, I expect that protection to cover sidecars too, not
just snapshots."

**Maintainer (secondary).** Wants the script's three deletion rules to share
one mental model: age-bounded, never deleting anything inside the protective
window.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, I want a just-written orphan sidecar to survive one cleanup
  cycle, so a transient missing snapshot does not destroy the routing ratio
  that the next save is about to re-pair.
- As a maintainer, I want `--min-age-days 0` to disable the protection for a
  one-off aggressive sweep, consistent with the size rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (guard).** An orphan sidecar whose mtime is **older** than
  `--min-age-days` is deleted; an orphan sidecar **newer** than
  `--min-age-days` is kept and reported as kept. Proven by a test in both
  suites (see AC5).
- **AC2 (dry-run).** `--dry-run` reports both categories (deletable orphan and
  kept-recent orphan) and deletes nothing; exit code stays `0`.
- **AC3 (no regression of `5502ee44`).** Endpoint-subdirectory scanning,
  snapshot+sidecar pair deletion, root-layout support, and orphan pruning for
  aged orphans all stay green. The existing pytest pin
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py::TestCleanupScriptRetention::test_orphan_sidecars_are_pruned_with_no_snapshots_present`
  writes orphans with mtime "now" and asserts they are deleted — it must be
  updated to age those orphans beyond `--min-age-days` (so it keeps testing
  the same rule rather than being weakened), not deleted or skipped.
- **AC4 (output & exit codes).** Existing output lines, summary lines and exit
  codes are unchanged; any new "kept" reporting is additive (only printed when
  the count is non-zero) and still reports `SUMMARY`/`DRY-RUN SUMMARY`. The
  script exits `0` when the cache contains only recent orphans.
- **AC5 (testing).** Behaviour is asserted by executable tests that run in the
  project suite: extend
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py::TestCleanupScriptRetention`
  (pytest-collected, the authoritative pin) **and** the standalone shell
  harness `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` (parity for manual runs).
- **AC6 (docs).** Documentation is updated: the script header's rule-3 comment
  (`scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`), the "Retention and pairing" paragraph in
  `proxy/docs/routing.md`, and the "Slot Cache Retention" section in
  `proxy/README.md` all state that the orphan sweep honours `--min-age-days`.
- **AC7 (suite).** The full project test suite passes with the change,
  including `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py`'s line-number citations
  of `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh:27-28`.

## Constraints

- **Scope is one rule.** Do not re-ship or re-litigate `5502ee44`; no changes
  to recursion, pair deletion, `--dry-run` structure, arg parsing or the
  writer side (`proxy/proxy/session.py`, `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`).
- **Keep the age semantics identical to the size rule:** protection applies
  when `age_seconds < min_age_seconds` (`--min-age-days 0` ⇒ no protection).
  Compare the **sidecar's own mtime** — the snapshot is gone, so there is no
  other timestamp available.
- **Citation-drift budget.** `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py` pins
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` lines 27 (`MAX_AGE_DAYS=7`) and 28
  (`MAX_SIZE_GB=20`) with `CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE = 60`. The guard belongs in
  the orphan loop near the end of the file, so do not shift those two
  assignments by more than ~60 lines (i.e. no large new preamble). See
  LP-0MVTHK9090067ESU for the durable fix to this fragile guard — do not
  attempt that fix here.
- **Defaults stay as they are:** `MIN_AGE_DAYS=1` (1 day). The
  `proxy/benchmarks/slot_snapshot_band_report.py` parser
  (`^\s*MIN_AGE_DAYS=(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$`) and
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_snapshot_band_report.py` assert exact default values,
  so the assignment must remain a plain `MIN_AGE_DAYS=<n>` line.
- **UK English** in all code comments and docs.

## Existing state

- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` — rule 1 (age), rule 2 (size, min-age
  protected), rule 3 (orphan sidecars, **unprotected**). `MIN_AGE_DAYS=1` is
  parsed and already used only by rule 2. `all_sidecars` is collected over the
  cache root plus one level of `{host}-{port}/` subdirectories.
- `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` — 9 shell tests, 7 assertions from
  `5502ee44`; `test_orphan_sidecars_pruned` writes orphans with "now" mtime and
  asserts they are pruned.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py::TestCleanupScriptRetention` —
  5 pytest tests invoking the script via `subprocess`; the orphan test has the
  same "now"-mtime assumption and is the pin that will go red if AC3 is missed.
- Docs: `proxy/docs/routing.md` ("Retention and pairing in
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`", plus the orphan-count `find` recipe at
  ~line 757), `proxy/README.md` §"Slot Cache Retention".
- Related rationale: the sidecar TTL is `session_slot_ratio_ttl_seconds`
  (default 86 400 s = 1 day, `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py:68`), so an
  orphan younger than the default `--min-age-days` is still inside the window
  where it could legitimately be re-paired; an older one can never be credited.

## Desired change

1. In the rule-3 loop, compute the sidecar's age from `stat -c %Y`; if
   `age_seconds < min_age_seconds`, skip it and count/report it as kept
   (in `--dry-run` and in real runs alike). Keep the existing
   `[[ -f "$snapshot" ]] && continue` guard first, and preserve the
   `rm -f`/`WARNING` error path and the `errors` counter.
2. Add an additive summary line (e.g. `SUMMARY: N orphan sidecar(s) kept (newer
   than --min-age-days)`) printed only when `N > 0`, in both the real and
   `--dry-run` summary blocks.
3. Extend the pytest pin `TestCleanupScriptRetention` with: stale orphan
   deleted, recent orphan kept, `--dry-run` reporting both and deleting
   neither; fix the existing orphan test's mtime assumption.
4. Extend `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` with the same three assertions.
5. Update the three doc locations named in AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` — rule-3 loop (age guard + kept counter),
  summary blocks, header comment for rule 3. Nothing above line 27 changes.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — `TestCleanupScriptRetention`:
  add orphan age-guard tests; age the orphans in the existing pruning test
  (`_run` already forwards `*extra`, so `--min-age-days` is easy to pass).
- `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` — `test_orphan_sidecars_pruned` plus new
  cases; needs a `make_orphan`-style helper that sets the sidecar mtime.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — "#### Retention and pairing in
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`" paragraph.
- `proxy/README.md` — §"Slot Cache Retention" default-policy bullets and usage
  examples.

## Verification commands (copy-paste ready)

```bash
# Behaviour by hand (stale orphan deleted, recent orphan kept)
tmp=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$tmp/cache/localhost-8080"
echo '{}' > "$tmp/cache/slot_stale.bin.ratio.json"
touch -d "3 days ago" "$tmp/cache/slot_stale.bin.ratio.json"
echo '{}' > "$tmp/cache/localhost-8080/slot_fresh.bin.ratio.json"
./scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh --path "$tmp/cache" --dry-run   # both categories, deletes nothing
./scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh --path "$tmp/cache"             # stale gone, fresh kept

# Suite-visible pin
/skill:test --scope changed        # exercises TestCleanupScriptRetention

# Standalone shell harness (manual parity)
bash tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh
```

## Related work

- **LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC** (completed, commit `5502ee44`) — shipped recursion,
  pair deletion and orphan pruning; this item is its residual AC.
- **LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3** (completed) — the diagnosis that measured 139
  orphans / 0 snapshots and 24.2 % `missing_snapshot` seed decisions; this item
  was discovered from it.
- **LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB** (open) — the ≥24 h re-measurement of the seed fix;
  its `missing_snapshot` counter now decays over `--min-age-days` instead of
  instantly (see Risks).
- **LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E** (open) — writer-side sidecar/snapshot coupling and
  the restored-prefix warmness gap; adjacent but out of scope.
- **LP-0MVTHK9090067ESU** (open) — durable fix for the pool-sizing doc
  citation-drift failures; constrains AC7 here but is not addressed here.
- **LP-0MS91DHQE006CJC4** (completed) — the original "slot-cache GC
  ineffective / 97 GB" episode that established the age+size retention rules.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the guard could mask a real orphan leak.** Recent orphans stay on
  disk for up to `--min-age-days`, so `slot_ratio_seed outcome=missing_snapshot`
  counts decay over that window instead of dropping immediately. Mitigation:
  the kept-orphan summary line keeps the residual visible; LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB
  should read the count after the window, not the day of deploy.
- **Risk: an existing test goes red silently.** The pytest orphan pin asserts
  deletion of "now"-aged orphans; AC3 makes fixing it explicit. Mitigation:
  update it in the same commit, never `skip`.
- **Risk: citation drift.** Covered by the constraint above (guard lives near
  the end of the file; <60 lines of preamble change).
- **Risk: scope creep** — the `proxy/README.md` section also documents a
  non-existent `--keep-recent 3` flag (stale since before `5502ee44`). Do
  **not** fix that here; it is a separate documentation defect (candidate
  follow-up item, not filed by this intake).
- **Assumption:** "kept" reporting is additive and conditional (`> 0`), so
  existing log-scraping and the `DRY-RUN SUMMARY` format keep working.
- **Assumption:** the protective comparison is the same `<` used by the size
  rule, so `--min-age-days 0` disables the guard.
- **Assumption:** no writer-side change is needed — `_retire_session_slot_snapshots()`
  already deletes snapshot and sidecar together, so the guard only narrows the
  cleanup script's blast radius.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does the orphan sweep need the age guard at all, given the writer now
  retires pairs atomically?**
  Answer (Map, 2026-10-30, from repo evidence): Yes. The writer path
  (`proxy/proxy/session.py::_retire_session_slot_snapshots`) is atomic for
  *retirement*, but a save that fails or is in flight can still leave a
  sidecar without its snapshot, and the original LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC AC
  explicitly required the recent-orphan case. Research: read
  `_retire_slot_snapshot` / `_retire_session_slot_snapshots`; no temp-file +
  rename in the save path, so a transient absence is possible. Source: repo
  inspection.
- **Q: Which mtime defines an orphan's age — the sidecar's or the (missing)
  snapshot's?**
  Answer (Map): the sidecar's own mtime; the snapshot does not exist, and the
  sidecar is written after the snapshot, so its mtime is the conservative
  (later) timestamp. Source: `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` rule 3 +
  `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` write path.
- **Q: Is `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` executed by the project suite?**
  Answer (Map): No — the full suite is `pytest` (`.pi/test-config.json` adds no
  `suiteCommands`; the runner resolves `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`),
  and `.sh` files are not collected. The suite-visible pin for this script is
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py::TestCleanupScriptRetention`.
  Both are extended (AC5) so manual shell runs keep parity. Source: test runner
  resolution + repo grep for wrappers.
- **Q: Should the default `--min-age-days` change?**
  Answer (Map): No. It stays `MIN_AGE_DAYS=1`, which also matches the sidecar
  TTL default (86 400 s), so the protection window coincides with the period in
  which an orphan could still be re-paired and credited. Changing the default
  would also break `proxy/tests/test_slot_snapshot_band_report.py` and the
  operator-facing retention docs. Source: `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py:68`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/slot_snapshot_band_report.py`.
- **OPEN QUESTION (deferred, non-blocking):** whether the stale `--keep-recent`
  flag documented in `proxy/README.md` should be corrected in this item. Not
  included in scope; recorded as a candidate follow-up.

## Related work (automated report)

> `/skill:find-related` output, recorded for auditability. Relevance is
> keyword-driven and low here — the curated **Related work** section above is
> authoritative. Full unmatched output:
> `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-LP-0MVTFJ04T001VW47.md`.

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** – Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO (measure before fixing) (completed) — *relevant*: defines the `missing_snapshot` outcome vocabulary this rule affects.
- **LP-0MR4XEDEY009JGVC** – Implement: pi session log retention script (completed) — *not relevant*: different retention script.
- **LP-0MRAWF4SZ001MCGD** – Implement: session recording cleanup script (completed) — *not relevant*: different retention script.

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts*.txt` — matched only on generic
  prose tokens (`acceptance`, `added`, `age`, `ago`, …); a vendored dataset, not
  related to this item.

## Plan: changelog

## Goal

Update the two client-facing refusal strings that still describe the pre-deferral
`local-only` semantics, so the remedy the proxy advertises matches the shipped
`local-preferred` contract documented in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## What is stale

- `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`, the `suggested_action` for
  `retryable: false`): still ends with "or send X-Local-Preference: prefer-local to
  allow a remote fallback". After LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE a `too_large` `local-preferred`
  request is already promoted to the remote tiers automatically, so that clause is
  redundant for a pin-local client and misleading for a `prefer-local` one (which
  falls through without any preference change). The compaction half (compact to
  `budget_tokens` and resend) is correct and should stay.
- The deferral 429 body `detail` in `_build_local_only_refusal_response()`: still
  reads "X-Local-Preference: local-only forbids remote fallback" — a deprecated
  spelling, and a description that contradicts the retryable deferral the same
  response now carries.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` names the compaction remedy and the token target, and
  no longer tells the client to change its preference to reach a remote tier.
- AC2 The deferral 429 `detail` names `local-preferred` (or no preference value at
  all) and describes the deferral rather than an unconditional refusal.
- AC3 The strings stay consistent with `proxy/docs/routing.md`'s per-reason retry
  contract (`suggested_action`, AC2 of LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57) — a doc-contract or
  unit test pins the wording/remedy so it cannot drift again.

- Strings only: no routing, timing or refusal-shape behaviour change.

## Problem

`proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py::TestCitationsStillResolve` has produced a
**critical `test-failure` work item four times in two days**:

| Item | Created | Cited symbol that drifted |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MVS0CU4V006FLLC | 2026-10-28 | `router.py::_get_local_max_concurrent_queries` 150 → 152, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` call site 1264 → 1304 |
| LP-0MVREECR9009UN78 | 2026-10-28 | `router.py` citations again |
| LP-0MVSFCP59004XXCG | 2026-10-28 | `router_helpers.py` 2697 → 2764, 2370 → 2430 |
| LP-0MVTHCT8W003VAGE | 2026-10-29 | `router_helpers.py` 2430 → 2631, 2764 → 2965 |

Each item's only change is renumbering `file:line` citations in
`docs/dev/slot-snapshot-pool-sizing-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` and the matching
`CITATIONS` tuples in the test. No cited behaviour changed in any of the four
occurrences — only line numbers moved.

## Why it keeps happening

The test pins **absolute line numbers** for 36 citations and tolerates
`CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE = 60` lines of drift. Every unrelated commit inside
`proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
(a 6,415-line module that grows fastest of the three) shifts the cited symbols.
Headroom is already thin as of 2026-10-29: `proxy/proxy/router.py:152`
(`def _get_local_max_concurrent_queries`) sits at **drift 55 of 60** — roughly five
inserted lines above it in `router.py` reddens the tree again. The `provider.py`
citations sit at a uniform drift of 16.

Verification (plan session 2026-10-29, read-only): all 36 citations resolve; max
drift 55 (`router.py:152`), next 25 (`provider.py:6127`), next 16 (`provider.py` ×6).

## Options (producer to choose — do not pre-empt)

- **A. Symbol-anchored citations (recommended).** The doc cites `file` + symbol
  (e.g. `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`effective_per_slot_threshold`)) without a line
  number, and the test asserts the symbol exists in that file (and, where useful,
  that the occurrence is unique / inside the expected enclosing definition). A move
  inside a file can no longer fail the suite; removal or rename still does.
- **B. Generated citation index.** Keep line numbers but stop hand-maintaining them:
  a small script derives each cited line from the symbol and rewrites the doc block;
  the test (or a check step) runs the generator and fails only if the committed
  block differs from regenerated output — a one-command fix instead of a new
  critical work item.
- **C. Raise/parameterise tolerance.** Cheapest, but knowingly keeps the treadmill;
  it also weakens the check (a symbol that genuinely moves far away is no longer
  caught). Acceptable only as a stopgap.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 The sizing-doc citation check can no longer fail solely because a cited symbol
  moved *within* its file: a test moves a synthetic symbol down a synthetic source by
  more than the current tolerance and asserts the check still passes.
- AC2 The check still fails when a cited symbol is removed or renamed in its file

- AC3 All existing citations are migrated to the chosen scheme, in the same commit as

  `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py`), with no cited behaviour dropped.
- AC4 The doc remains readable by an operator: each citation still names a file and a
  symbol precise enough to locate the behaviour by search (no bare "see provider.py").
- AC5 The decision (option A/B/C with rationale) is recorded on this item, including
  what happens to `CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE`.
- AC6 Full project test suite passes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change; docs + test only.
- Do not weaken the check into a no-op — AC1/AC2 must both hold.
- The test's doc-table fidelity assertions (`TestProductionGeometry`,

# Pre-push full-suite gate validates the main checkout, not the pushed commit

## Goal (user story)

As an operator relying on the dev-push integration gate, I want the pre-push
full-suite run to test **the tree being pushed**, so "green push" actually
means "the pushed commit is green" — instead of validating a stale main
checkout whose cached result is then reported as a pass.

## Evidence (observed 2026-10-29, LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC)

- `implement.py finish` reports `push: {success: true, hash: 5502ee44}` after a
  push window of **~28 s**, far too short for the ~400 s full suite.
- `phase_finish` calls `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)` — i.e.
  with `cwd` = the **main checkout**, not the item's worktree (the same
  function's non-fast-forward recovery explicitly rebases "where it is
  checked out (the worktree)", so the asymmetry looks unintentional).
- The pre-push hook resolves `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` and
  runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`.
  From the main checkout that is the main checkout's working tree, whose git
  state was `55c1c15a` — 4 commits behind `origin/dev` and **not** containing
  the pushed commit. A full-suite cache entry for `55c1c15a` existed, so the
  gate returned "pre-push: full suite green (cached runs make repeat pushes
  cheap)" in well under a second without testing the pushed tree.
- Direct invocation of the same hook with a simulated `refs/heads/dev` stdin
  line *does* run the gate, so the hook logic itself is correct; the problem is
  the working directory the push (and therefore the gate) runs in.
- Corroborating symptom: `implement.py finish`'s own fast-forward step
  ("Fast-forward dev in main checkout") frequently fails with
  `Diverging branches can't be fast-forwarded`, leaving the main checkout
  permanently behind; every subsequent push then validates that same stale tree.

## Impact

The dev-push gate is the **only** full-suite enforcement point in the
implementation workflow (changed scope runs earlier, full scope at the push).
If it silently validates a stale checkout, a red tree can be pushed to `dev`
as "green", and the pushed commit has no audit-acceptable full-suite cache
entry, which degrades the audit skill's F3 auto-verification for every item.

## Proposed change

1. Push from the worktree (`cwd=worktree_path`) in `phase_finish`, so
   `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` inside the pre-push hook resolves to the tree
   whose commit is being pushed. Keep `repo_root` only for the main-checkout
   fast-forward and lock.
2. Make the hook fail closed when the tested tree's `HEAD` is not the pushed
   `local_sha` (defence in depth): the hook already reads `local_sha` from
   stdin, so it can assert `git rev-parse HEAD == local_sha` (or run the suite
   against a checkout of `local_sha`) and refuse otherwise.
3. Consider making the suite-cache key include the pushed sha rather than the
   working-tree state, so a cached result can never be reused for a different
   commit.
4. Regression test: a `finish` push whose commit differs from the main
   checkout's HEAD must cause the gate to execute (or fail), never to report a
   cache hit.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `finish` push of commit `X` runs the pre-push full-suite gate against a tree
  at `X`; the run takes the full suite's duration (or fails closed) when no
  cache entry for `X` exists.
- No path exists where the gate reports "green" from a cache entry recorded for
  a different commit than the pushed `local_sha`.
- A test pins the behaviour (simulated push from a worktree over a stale main
  checkout).
- The workaround is documented in `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` until fixed.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC (observed while pushing commit `5502ee44`)
data.title: Pre-push full-suite gate validates the main checkout, not the pushed commit

## Goal

Close the last residual of parent AC4 (LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG): the in-cycle chain-resolution "not local" skip lines for a **failure domain**, a **usage-limit account** and a **proactive quota** state still emit no `preference=` field, so a `local-preferred` request that leaves the local route via one of them cannot be attributed by preference from `proxy.log` alone.

Parent: LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG. Blocks the parent's closure (audit finding AC4, 2026-10-29 — "the failure-domain/usage-limit-account skip lines emit no `preference=` at all").

## Problem

`_resolve_provider_with_exclusions()` is the chain resolution both dispatch cycles call. Its cooldown / quota-hard-stop / usage-limit-reset / available-times skip lines already end with `_preference_log_suffix(preference)` (LP-0MVRMC275000R2W6), but three sibling lines in the same loop do **not**:

```text
proxy/proxy/provider.py:8502  Skipping provider=%s: same failure domain as an already-failed entry (domain=%s)
proxy/proxy/provider.py:8516  Skipping provider=%s: same usage-limit account as an already-exhausted entry (account=%s)
proxy/proxy/provider.py:8526  Skipping provider=%s: %s            (proactive quota state — _quota_unavailable_reason)
```

A local entry can be dropped by the failure-domain line: local entries key their failure domain on the provider **brand** (no `endpoint`), so a failed local entry excludes every other local entry of the same brand. `proxy/docs/routing.md` claims "Every 'not local' line also carries `preference=<parsed>`", and parent AC4 requires exactly that, so these three lines break both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The three skip lines in `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions()` (`provider.py:8502`, `:8516`, `:8526`) end with `_preference_log_suffix(preference)` — the same additive suffix the sibling lines in that loop already use.
- The value comes from the function's existing, already-parsed `preference` parameter — no second parse of the `X-Local-Preference` header.
- The change is **additive**: every pre-existing key of each line keeps its name and order, proven by a `key=value` parser assertion.
- An absent/unknown header never yields an empty or missing value (`preference=prefer-local`).
- A `caplog` test asserts `preference=` on each of the three lines for each of the three parsed values (`local-preferred`, `prefer-local`, `remote-ok`), following the existing pattern in `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py`.
- No behavioural change: `prefer-local` and `local-preferred` chains still resolve to the same providers; the routing decision is untouched (log-only change).
- Full suite green via the changed-scope gate first.

Parent-AC traceability: covers parent AC4 — "Every skip/fallback line that decides 'not local' logs the parsed preference (`preference=local-preferred|prefer-local|remote-ok`) so an intent violation is visible in `proxy.log`; `priority_routing` keeps its existing fields (additive change only)."

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions()` (`:8360`), the three skip lines (`:8502`, `:8516`, `:8526`), `_preference_log_suffix()` (`:8040` for reference).
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py` — caplog + additive key=value assertion pattern (`_NOT_LOCAL_LINE_ROWS`, entry-context-cap block).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the "Every 'not local' line also carries `preference=<parsed>`" claim this item makes true (read-only unless the wording needs no change).

## Notes

- Out of scope, recorded deliberately: `resolve_provider()` (`provider.py:3607`) is the public **pre-dispatch** helper (used by `compaction_summarizer` and tests). It has no request object and therefore no parsed preference; its skip lines are not request-scoped "not local" decisions and are left unchanged. Say so in the completion comment so a future audit does not re-open it.
- Log-grep tooling (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `.pi/skills/proxy-log-debug/SKILL.md`) parses these lines; the change is additive so their parsers keep working. Verify read-only; do not edit skill files (repository boundary).
data.title: Fix: preference= on the remaining not-local chain-resolution skip lines (failure domain, usage-limit account, quota state)

## Goal

Ensure the pre-push full-suite gate always validates the exact commit being pushed to `dev`, never a stale main-checkout HEAD.

## Observed failure

Discovered during `LP-0MVT4SMIU0046OTB` (commit `27c76a3e`); `discovered-from:LP-0MVT4SMIU0046OTB`.

The main checkout's local `dev` had diverged from `origin/dev` (local `55c1c15a` vs origin `c25bf665`, a rebased equivalent from another work item). `implement.py finish` logged: "Fast-forward dev failed (Diverging branches can't be fast-forwarded); push will proceed from the stale checkout", then "Push to dev succeeded".

`git_push_to_dev()` pushes with `cwd=<main checkout>`, so `.githooks/pre-push` resolves `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` to the main checkout at the **stale** HEAD `55c1c15a` — not the pushed commit `27c76a3e`. That stale state already had a cached green full-suite entry (`git_state` = `a1982b0b...`), so the gate was a cache hit and the entire push completed in ~14 s. The full suite never executed against `27c76a3e`; a manual `run_tests.py --scope full` at `27c76a3e` was required afterwards (6512 passed, 0 failed).

## Impact

A red commit can reach `dev` while the pre-push gate reports green, because the gate validated a different tree. This bypasses the primary integration safety net rather than merely slowing it down.

## Key Files

- .githooks/pre-push
- scripts/install_git_hooks.sh
- docs/dev/git-hooks.md

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A push to `dev`/`main` from a checkout whose HEAD is not the pushed commit either (a) aborts with an actionable error, or (b) runs the suite against the pushed commit (worktree at `local_sha`) — a green result from the current, unrelated HEAD is never accepted.
2. A cached full-suite entry only satisfies the gate when its `git_state` fingerprints the pushed commit's tree; a stale-HEAD cache hit is reported as a miss.
3. A regression test pins the behaviour (push from a diverged checkout does not pass the gate using the stale HEAD's cache entry).
4. Full project test suite passes with the change, via the test skill (`/skill:test`).

## Notes

- `implement.py` lives in the global skill install; the fix may span both this repo's `.githooks/pre-push` and the framework's `git_push_to_dev`/`phase_finish` (prefer pushing from the branch worktree, or abort on divergence).
- Effort/risk to be estimated in intake/plan.

data.description:
Discovered while implementing LP-0MVT8SAZE00570J5.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` calls `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)` (main checkout) rather than pushing from the worktree where `branch` is checked out. The dev-push pre-push hook (`.githooks/pre-push`) runs its full-suite gate with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` as `--project-root`, so the suite is fingerprinted and executed against the **main checkout's HEAD tree** (local `dev`), not against the commit being pushed.

Consequences:

- The gate can be satisfied by a cached green entry for the main checkout's own state, so a push carrying an unvalidated feature commit completes in seconds instead of running the suite.
- When the main checkout's `dev` is dirty, behind or diverged, the tested tree is not the pushed tree at all — the "full suite first runs at the dev-push gate" contract (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) is not actually enforced for `implement.py finish` pushes.

## Evidence (LP-0MVT8SAZE00570J5)

- The push of `45a15fb3` succeeded 9 s after the finish lock was acquired.
- `.worklog/cache` holds no full-suite entry for `45a15fb3` (git state `62c7e218…`); the newest matching entry (`d37b4bc2…`, completed 12:30:47) is the main checkout's HEAD tree.
- A manual `sh .githooks/pre-push` probe with a stub `python3` shows the gate does run — it prints "full suite green" for a cache hit on the main checkout's state.
- The first push attempt of the same run was rejected non-fast-forward, so the run took the `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` retry path, which also pushes from `repo_root`.

## Expected

The push MUST run from the worktree (or otherwise make the pre-push gate evaluate the pushed tree), so a cache miss runs the suite instead of validating an unrelated tree.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `implement.py finish` pushes from the worktree that holds `branch` (or otherwise makes the pre-push gate evaluate the pushed commit).
2. A test proves the gate input equals the pushed tree (gate project root == worktree root / pushed commit fingerprint) for both the first push and the non-fast-forward retry path.
3. Regression test: when the correctly computed full-suite entry is absent, the push records a new full-suite cache entry for the pushed commit.
4. `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` and the implement skill describe the guarantee.

Discovered-from: LP-0MVT8SAZE00570J5 (a manual full-suite run was performed for that item's AC9).

# Goal

Make a green `dev`-push gate mean *the pushed commit's tree* passed the full suite. The
observed fail-open is now covered by the committed pre-push pushed-commit guard and the
framework push-cwd fix; the only residual this item can still own is **cache-identity
hardening** (pin the suite cache key to the pushed `local_sha`). Whether that residual is
worth doing, and where it lives, is an **open producer question (Q1)** — see below.

# Scope decision (RESOLVED — Q1 = A, 2026-10-30)

Duplicate-work analysis during intake (2026-10-30) found that the outcome this item was
filed for is now owned elsewhere:

- **LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9** (`in-progress`, `intake_complete`) — parent design for a
  repo-local fail-closed guard in `.githooks/pre-push`, with four children:
  LP-0MVU94IPT009SICZ (regression tests, `open`), LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0 (guard, `blocked`),
  LP-0MVU94RD1000IE7P (verify gate evidence at the pushed commit, `blocked`),
  LP-0MVU94RN9006Z28Y (document the contract + fix the malformed simulate recipe, `blocked`).
- **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** (`open`, framework) — `implement.py finish` pushes from the tree
  it is pushing (first attempt *and* non-fast-forward retry), plus rollout.
- **SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB** (`blocked`, framework) — *Tree-fingerprint cache binding*: adds an
  explicit fingerprint override to `test_cache.run_cached` / `lookup` and a
  `compute_tree_state()` tree-SHA fingerprint. It is the framework mechanism this item's
  cache-identity idea would build on; it currently leaves the pre-push consumer on the
  default `HEAD`-based fingerprint.

The guard route deliberately buys identity through a **precondition** (`HEAD == local_sha`
and a clean tree), not through a different cache key. At a clean checkout of the pushed
commit, `compute_git_state()` hashes exactly `rev-parse HEAD` (no dirty entries), so the
resulting fingerprint *is* the pushed commit's fingerprint — the cache-identity outcome is
achieved without touching `test_cache.py`.

**Q1 — what should this item do?** *(answered: A — close as covered, no repo code)*

- **(A) Close as covered (no repo code).** The guard + push-cwd fix make the fail-open
  unreachable; the cache-pin residual is already owned by SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB. Record the
  AC→owner mapping in a closing comment and cross-reference the three items above.
- **(B) Keep only the residual, as a framework item.** Wire the pre-push hook to pass the
  gated `local_sha` as the explicit cache fingerprint (depends on SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB
  landing a `run_tests.py` passthrough). This cannot be implemented in this repository:
  `test_cache.py` and `run_tests.py` live in `~/.pi/agent/skills`, outside the LP worktree,
  so it becomes an `SA-` item (or a child/AC of SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB).
- **(C) Fold the wiring into SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB's scope** and close this item against it.

**Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): (A) close as covered.** No repo code; close against the
guard family and cross-reference the framework owners. Options (B)/(C) are not pursued.

**Recommended:** **(A)** — the fail-open this item recorded is fixed by the guard family,
the only remaining idea already has a framework owner, and this defect has already been
filed five times across two worklogs (LP-0MVTI2K2A002HCGT, LP-0MVTJ2B3H00258U1,
LP-0MVTIYY1D009Y23Q, LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3, LP-0MVTJROWY005HMNA); one further record that redescribes it adds tracking churn, not safety.

Options (B)/(C) are drafted in full in *Residual design* below so the decision is
actionable without a second intake pass.

# Problem (observed, evidence)

discovered-from:LP-0MVTI957W006KS0P (its push of `69909a0a` was reported green without the
tree ever being tested).

Mechanism (as observed 2026-10-29):

- `.githooks/pre-push` reads every pushed ref from stdin
  (`.githooks/pre-push:82`) but uses only `remote_ref`; `local_sha` is discarded
  (`.githooks/pre-push:80-86`).
- The gate then runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`
  (`.githooks/pre-push:145`), where `repo_root` is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the
  `git push` cwd. `implement.py` pushes with `cwd=repo_root` (the main checkout), not the
  worktree.
- `test_cache.compute_git_state()` (`~/.pi/agent/skills/test_cache.py:128`) fingerprints
  `git rev-parse HEAD` of that cwd plus dirty content; it has no pushed-sha input.
  `run_tests.py` exposes no `--git-state`/`--pushed-sha` override (its argparse block,
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py:2030-2133`).
- When `implement.py finish`'s pre-push `git merge --ff-only <commit>` fails
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py:5197-5201`, a warning only), the main
  checkout stays on the older commit while the feature-branch push still succeeds — the gate
  then keys on that stale `HEAD`.

Observed 2026-10-29:

- push of `69909a0a` (LP-0MVTI957W006KS0P) succeeded;
- no full-suite cache entry existed for `69909a0a`'s git state (`5bce0ec4…`), proving the
  gate never ran the suite at that commit;
- the gate was served the 12:30 entry keyed `d37b4bc2…` = clean tree of `f720f762` (the
  main-checkout HEAD at push time), `exit_code 0`;
- a direct `--scope full` run at `69909a0a` then found a real failure
  (`proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py::TestCitationsStillResolve::test_citation_resolves[proxy/proxy/router.py-152-def _get_local_max_concurrent_queries]`,
  citation drift 61 > 60) — i.e. the gate passed a red tree.

# Existing state (verified 2026-10-30)

- The committed hook is still `# worklog:pre-push-hook:v3` (`.githooks/pre-push:2`) — the
  guard is **not yet landed**; it is specified in LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0 (AC1 mismatch refusal,
  AC2 dirty-tree refusal, AC4 POSIX `sh`, AC6 cache plumbing unchanged).
- The guard's regression tests are specified in LP-0MVU94IPT009SICZ; the real-clone evidence
  run in LP-0MVU94RD1000IE7P; the docs contract (including the current malformed five-field
  simulate-a-push recipe in `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`) in LP-0MVU94RN9006Z28Y.
- Framework-side: SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3 (push from the pushed tree) is `open`/`intake_complete`;
  SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB (explicit cache-fingerprint binding) is `blocked` behind its test and
  temp-index siblings.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` currently documents the gate as "runs the full suite and refuses a
  red suite" and does not state *which tree* is measured; the pushed-commit contract is the
  docs child's deliverable.
- Changed-scope (`--scope changed`) dev-time validation is a separate path and is unaffected
  by any option here.

# Closure evidence (verified 2026-10-30)

The gate's cache fingerprint at the guard's precondition is exactly the pushed commit's
fingerprint — no cache-key change needed:

```
$ git status --porcelain | wc -l
0
$ git rev-parse HEAD
5d295fd00d6b177e5f24c55538dee9c540e99567
$ PYTHONPATH=~/.pi/agent/skills python3 -c 'from test_cache import compute_git_state; print(compute_git_state("."))'
98565b81b9b23c3477198e904be51c6353a4428ca9387fb4e44a42fa7ef98438
$ python3 -c 'import hashlib; print(hashlib.sha256(b"5d295fd00d6b177e5f24c55538dee9c540e99567").hexdigest())'
98565b81b9b23c3477198e904be51c6353a4428ca9387fb4e44a42fa7ef98438
```

`compute_git_state()` hashes `rev-parse HEAD` and then only dirty-path content, so on a clean
checkout it is the sha256 of the commit sha itself. With the guard enforcing
`HEAD == local_sha` and a clean tree before the suite runs, a green gate entry is therefore
always keyed to the pushed commit — the observable fail-open (`69909a0a`, 2026-10-29) becomes
unreachable.

# Users

- **Agent implementers** running `implement.py finish` in a repo with a busy main checkout:
  they need a push that is either genuinely verified or loudly refused — never a green gate
  that proves nothing.
- **Producers / release reviewers** relying on `run_tests.py --summary` as the
  "the pushed commit was full-suite green" evidence trail.
- Example story: *As a producer reviewing a `dev` push, I want a green gate to mean the
  pushed commit's tree passed the full suite, so that I can trust `dev` without re-running
  the suite manually.*

# Desired change

Under **Q1 = A**: no code change in this repository. Close the item with the AC→owner
mapping and evidence that a clean checkout at the pushed commit produces the pushed commit's
fingerprint (`compute_git_state()` == hash of `rev-parse HEAD` with no dirty entries).

Under **Q1 = B/C** — *residual design*: pin the suite cache key to the pushed sha so a
wrong-tree run can never be *stored or accepted* as evidence for a commit, even if a future
caller pushes from the wrong directory:

1. Framework (`test_cache.py` / `run_tests.py`): an explicit fingerprint override for
   `run_cached`/`lookup` (SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB) plus a CLI passthrough so callers can supply
   the expected fingerprint.
2. `.githooks/pre-push`: pass the captured gated `local_sha` as that fingerprint, so the
   gate's cache lookup/store is keyed to the pushed commit rather than the checkout
   `HEAD`.
3. Absent the override every other consumer keeps today's `HEAD`-based keys (no cache
   invalidation for the test skill, audit or changed-scope runs).

# Acceptance criteria

Set **A** (closure — verified by comment evidence, no code; **selected by Q1 = A**):

- [x] The AC→owner mapping is recorded (guard LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9 + children,
  push-cwd SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3, cache mechanism SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB) and the item is closed
  against it.
- [x] Evidence recorded that a clean checkout at the pushed commit yields that commit's
  fingerprint: `compute_git_state()` output equals a hash over `rev-parse HEAD` alone (no
  dirty entries), so a green gate run at the guard's precondition *is* evidence for the
  pushed commit.

Set **B/C** (residual — **not pursued**, Q1 = A; retained as the design record should the
decision ever be revisited; framework parts would land under the named `SA-` items):

- [ ] AC1: `run_tests.py`/`test_cache` accept an explicit expected fingerprint and use it for
  both cache lookup and store; without the override, keys and behaviour are unchanged
  (regression test in `tests/test_test_cache.py`).
- [ ] AC2: `.githooks/pre-push` passes the gated `local_sha` as that fingerprint for
  `refs/heads/dev|main` pushes, so a green entry keyed to a stale checkout `HEAD` can never
  satisfy the gate.
- [ ] AC3: A regression test reproduces the concurrent-finish shape — main-checkout `HEAD`
  ≠ pushed `local_sha`, with a pre-seeded green entry for the main-checkout fingerprint ⇒
  the gate must not accept it (runner is invoked; no green from stale evidence).
- [ ] AC4: A red pushed tree is still refused with an actionable message naming the failing
  tests (existing gate behaviour preserved).
- [ ] AC5: `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` documents the pinned-fingerprint contract; the
  changed-scope dev-time gate and all non-gated pushes are unaffected.
- [ ] AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Constraints

- **Repository boundary:** `.pi/`, `skill/` and agent-infrastructure files must not be edited
  from an `LP` worktree; `test_cache.py`, `run_tests.py` and `implement.py` are framework
  files at `~/.pi/agent/skills`. Options B/C therefore require an `SA-` item (or producer
  approval to relax the boundary).
- Fail closed, loud and actionable: never a silent pass; refusal messages name the pushed
  sha, the measured tree and the recovery step.
- `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` and `--no-verify` remain the explicit, documented escape hatches.
- No duplicate tracking: do not re-specify guard tests or the docs contract that
  LP-0MVU94IPT009SICZ / LP-0MVU94RN9006Z28Y already own.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — gated `local_sha` capture and runner invocation (guard in
  LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0; fingerprint passthrough only under Q1 = B/C).
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — pushed-commit contract (owned by LP-0MVU94RN9006Z28Y).
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — stale/dirty gate-tree regression home (owned by
  LP-0MVU94IPT009SICZ).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test_cache.py` (`compute_git_state`, `run_cached`, `lookup`) —
  framework cache identity (out of repo scope; SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — CLI fingerprint passthrough (framework).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` /
  `phase_finish` push cwd (framework; SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3).

# Related work

- **LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9** — *dev-push full-suite gate verifies a stale main checkout when
  the pre-push fast-forward is skipped* (parent design; producer chose Q1=A repo-local
  fail-closed guard, Q3=B refuse dirty trees as well).
- **LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0** — fail-closed pushed-commit guard implementation.
- **LP-0MVU94IPT009SICZ** — regression tests for the stale/dirty gate tree.
- **LP-0MVU94RD1000IE7P** — verify gate evidence at the pushed commit on the real clone.
- **LP-0MVU94RN9006Z28Y** — document the pushed-commit contract and fix the malformed
  simulate-a-push recipe.
- **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — `implement.py finish` pushes from the tree it is pushing.
- **SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2** — finish gate tests the tree the commit produces (parent of the
  cache-binding work).
- **SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB** — tree-fingerprint cache binding (explicit fingerprint override);
  the framework lever for the residual.
- **LP-0MVTHCT8W003VAGE** — owns the *separate* pre-existing citation-test failure that the
  red tree in the observation (above) exposed; this item is only about the gate's evidence.
- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3** — investigation of the non-fast-forward retry path (closed
  against SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3).
- Closed duplicates of this defect: LP-0MVTI2K2A002HCGT, LP-0MVTJ2B3H00258U1,
  LP-0MVTIYY1D009Y23Q. (LP-0MVU94RD1000IE7P references `LP-0MVMC1AD0013HND` as the
  2026-10-28 observation, but that id is not present in either worklog store — a dangling
  reference, not a live record.)

# Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** the guard family expands into hook hardening, docs and framework
  pushes; keep this item to the cache-identity question and file anything else as linked
  work.
- **Assumption (option A):** the guard's `HEAD == local_sha` + clean-tree precondition is
  sufficient for evidence identity. It is only sound while the guard is installed and not
  bypassed; a clone without `core.hooksPath` has no gate at all, so the cache key adds no
  protection there.
- **Assumption (option B/C):** SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB lands an explicit fingerprint override.
  Until it does, a pre-push passthrough has no framework API to call.
- **Risk (option B/C):** a hook-pinned fingerprint that disagrees with the runner's own
  fingerprint would make every lookup a miss (cache never hit → slow pushes) or, if
  mismatched the other way, could accept foreign evidence; the store/lookup paths must use
  the same explicit value and legacy entries must miss (fail closed).
- **Risk:** editing framework files from this repo violates the repository boundary and
  would be flagged at audit.

# Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (ANSWERED, 2026-10-30 — producer):** Given the guard family
  (LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9 + children) and the framework push-cwd fix (SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3)
  already make a green `dev` push mean the pushed tree ran the suite, and the explicit
  cache-fingerprint mechanism is owned by SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB — should this item (A) close
  as covered with no repo code, (B) keep only the residual cache-identity wiring as a new
  `SA-` framework item, or (C) fold that wiring into SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB's scope?
  **Answer (producer): (A) — close as covered; no repo code.** Source: interactive reply to
  the intake question (2026-10-30). The agent's recommendation was (A), on the evidence that
  the guard's precondition makes a clean checkout fingerprint equal the pushed commit's, that
  the residual cache-pin mechanism already has a framework owner
  (SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB), and that this defect already has five records across two worklogs.
  This supersedes the 2026-10-29 consolidation note's "confirm at plan time" deferral now
  that SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB exists.
- **Q0 (answered, 2026-10-29 — previous intake):** Should the fix be a repo-local guard or a
  framework push-cwd change? — Answer (producer, recorded on LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9): Q1=A
  repo-local fail-closed guard in `.githooks/pre-push` with regression tests; framework
  follow-up out of scope. Q3=B: refuse a dirty tree as well as a `HEAD` ≠ `local_sha`
  mismatch. Source: LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9 comment trail.

  `cache_state=restored`), plus the ≥24 h pre-fix window in
  `docs/dev/slot-ratio-seed-verdict-LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3.md`.

## Proposed change

1. Confirm the deployed proxy still runs `5502ee44`-or-later (`git log -1 dev`)
   and that no restart happened inside the window (a restart resets the
   in-memory ratio but not the sidecars — note it if it happens).
2. Run the measurement tool over the post-fix window (and the same-length
   pre-fix window for the before/after):

   ```bash
     --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
     --slot-cache-dir /home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache \
     --window "post-fix=2026-10-29T12:58:32,<post-fix end>" \

     --json
   ```

   shorthand: for a 24 h post-fix window the pre-fix window is
   `2026-10-28T12:58:32 → 2026-10-29T12:58:32`. Save the `--json` output next to
   the report (e.g. `docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-30.json`,
   mirroring `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-metrics-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.json`)
   so every count quoted in the report is reproducible.

3. Aggregate the seed-outcome vocabulary for the same window (the tool emits
   `windows[].seed_outcomes`; raw recipe in `proxy/docs/routing.md`).

   dispatches are still zero, say so honestly, explain the outcome counts, and

   stays unmet).

   resolves them):

   ```bash
   find . -name '*.bin' -exec basename {} \;  | sed 's/\.bin$//' | sort > /tmp/snaps
   find . -name '*.bin.ratio.json' -exec basename {} \; | sed 's/\.bin\.ratio\.json$//' | sort > /tmp/sides

   comm -23 /tmp/snaps /tmp/sides | wc -l   # orphan snapshots (no sidecar)
   ```

   orphans pre-date the fix — the success signal is **no orphan growth for
   sessions saved after the deploy**, not an absolute zero.

## Problem

The automated code-quality review (epic LP-0MVTJXBKO00843I8, tag `Refactor`) filed three work items — one CRITICAL, one HIGH, one MEDIUM — against `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`, a **gitignored, untracked** local analysis scratch script:

- LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA (critical, F401 unused `sys`)
- LP-0MVTJXC1D003NS8F (high, E401 multiple imports on one line)
- LP-0MVTJXCCL008DOEO (medium, I001 unsorted import block)

`.worklog/` is excluded by `.gitignore` (rule `.worklog/`, confirmed with `git check-ignore -v`), and `ruff` itself honours `.gitignore` on directory recursion. Findings on untracked scratch files cannot be remediated by a commit, so each becomes a verification-only no-op item — scheduling noise, and a CRITICAL-tagged one competes with real defects in `wl next`.

## Root cause

The review scan enumerates files by explicit path (or walks the tree without honouring `.gitignore`), so gitignored paths enter the lint scope.

## Proposed fix

- Scope the scan to git-tracked files (`git ls-files`), or add explicit exclusions for gitignored paths / `.worklog/`.
- Optionally suppress findings whose file is untracked (no committable remediation path exists).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The code-quality review emits no findings for files excluded by `.gitignore` (verified by a scan covering `.worklog/analysis/` and observing no findings for it).
- [ ] A regression check covers the scan scope (test or documented scope assertion).
- [ ] No severity inflation: a finding on a gitignored path is either not filed, or filed at `low` with an explicit "untracked scratch file" note.

## Provenance

Discovered while implementing LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA (no-op verification close of the F401 finding for the same gitignored file).

## Scheduling

- **Runnable at/after `2026-10-30 00:10:18 UTC`** — 24 h after the fix was deployed.

Proxy logs rotate roughly every 6 h (00:10 / 06:10 / 12:10 / 18:10) with gzip retention back to 2026-10-15, so the window stays readable for days — but rotation and prefix-based naming mean the exact file list is not stable; rely on `--log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy` and the timestamp filter, not on file names.

## Procedure (exact commands)

```bash

  --since "2026-10-29 00:10:18" \

EOF

# 3. Eviction events with reasons, for the AC4 second clause

import re, gzip, os
start, end = "2026-10-29 00:10:18", "2026-10-30 00:10:18"
import collections; c = collections.Counter()
for f in os.listdir("/var/log/llama-proxy"):
```
