Found while measuring LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 (24 h post-fix window
2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z; evidence in
`docs/dev/router-slots-500-window-2026-10-27-to-28.md` / `.json`).

## Summary

The residual router-responder `GET /slots ... 500` responses are **not** any
more slot-polling call site falling back to the router. They are the proxy's
**`GET /health` reachability probe**, which deliberately queries
`/slots?model=<current_model>` on the router port:

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py:1170` — `health_check()` calls
  `srv._probe_backend_reachable(llama_port)` on every `/health` request.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py:725` — `_probe_backend_reachable()` builds
  `probe_paths = ["/slots?model=<current_model>", "/models", "/health"]` and
  hits `http://localhost:<router_port>...` directly.

Because the probe never calls `_resolve_local_slots_target()`, it neither
increments `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` nor logs
`slots_child_port_unavailable` — which is exactly the observed shape: many
router `/slots` 500s with (almost) zero fallback signals.

## Evidence

- Window superset (`llama-server.log-2026-10-28.gz` + `-2026-10-29.gz`,
  2026-10-27T00:00Z → 2026-10-29T00:00Z): **1,171 router-responder
  `GET /slots` 500s** (128 + 1,043), all from `127.0.0.1`, each preceded by
  `srv proxy_reques: proxying request to model Qwen3 on port <child>` — i.e.
  the router proxied the poll into a busy chat-model child and converted the
  cancellation into a 500. Child instances themselves answered 135,028 × 200
  and **0** × 500.
- In-window fallback signals: **1** throttled warning (for `gpt120`, see
  the sibling bug) and a counter that was 0 at 2026-10-28T04:40Z — far too
  few to explain 1,171 router 500s.
- Live reproduction (2026-10-30T19:18Z, current proxy pid 3224511): 10
  sequential `curl -s -o /dev/null localhost:8000/health` calls produced
  exactly one router-responder `GET /slots` line each, of which **6 returned
  HTTP 500**, 3 returned 200 and 1 was indeterminate.
- Only the proxy process holds connections to `localhost:8080` (300/300
  `ss` samples over 60 s), so the router `/slots` traffic is proxy-originated.

## Why it matters

- The router `/slots` 500 rate is the regression signal the parent fix was
  validated against ("router:500 == 0 is the target"), so a permanent
  non-zero floor makes the signal unusable and keeps masking any genuine
  polling regression.
- Each probe also serialises behind a busy child (5–7 s), so `/health`
  latency degrades under prefill (the same defect class as
  LP-0MTDGBRPU003Z7KU) and the router logs a spurious 500 per probe.

## Proposed change (scope to confirm at intake)

1. Drop `/slots?model=` from `_probe_backend_reachable()`'s router probe
   list — `/models` and `/health` already answer reachability without
   serialising behind the child; or
2. Route the `/slots` probe through `_resolve_local_slots_target()` so it
   targets the discovered child port like every other proxy-initiated poll;
3. Either way, assert the router-responder `/slots` 500 rate returns to 0 in
   a fresh 24 h window (re-run the LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 recipe).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — A unit test proves `_probe_backend_reachable()` does not issue a
  `GET /slots` against the local router port (either the path is removed, or
  the request is rewritten to the discovered child port, with the rewrite
  covered by a test).
- **AC2** — `/health` continues to report `backend_reachable=false` for an
  unreachable backend and `true` for a healthy one (existing behaviour
  preserved; assert via the public `/health` response).
- **AC3** — **Deployed and delegated, with the window dated.** The fix is
  live in production (commit `ac8dc504`; proxy pid 3944027 restarted
  **2026-10-31T00:41:55Z**, i.e. after the fix), and the running code is
  verified: 5 sequential `/health` calls produced **0** new router-responder
  `GET /slots` lines (pre-fix: exactly one per call). The 24 h zero-500
  confirmation is carried by the **root** follow-up item
  **LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6** — *"…— earliest run 2026-11-01T00:41:55Z (window
  2026-11-01T00:41:55Z → 2026-11-02T00:41:55Z)"* (`depends-on` this item),
  which reuses the recorded recipe. This item's own evidence is the unit-level
  proof (AC1) plus the documented target signal (AC4).
- **AC4** — All related documentation is updated (including
  `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`, whose "Observability signal" section
  currently states router:500 should trend to 0).
- **AC5** — Full project test suite passes with the change.

> **AC3 traceability.** AC3 cannot be satisfied before the fix is deployed, so it is
> tracked by the dependent measurement item **LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6**
> (`depends-on` this item), which reuses the LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 recipe. AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5
> are satisfied by the fix itself.


## Scope decision (2026-10-31, at implementation)

AC3 as originally written required a **post-deploy** 24 h window. That cannot
be measured before this fix ships through `dev`→`main`, so keeping it as a
gate on *this* item deadlocks the item (it could never close until after the
release it enables). The verification was therefore split out, mirroring the
parent bug's pattern (`LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF` → `LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57`):

- **LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6** (root item, `depends-on` this item) carries the
  24 h zero-500 measurement, restart integrity, the evidence format and the
  RED → linked-bug path, reusing the recorded recipe. Its title now records
  the earliest run (**2026-11-01T00:41:55Z**, derived from the post-fix proxy
  restart at 2026-10-31T00:41:55Z) and the window
  (2026-11-01T00:41:55Z → 2026-11-02T00:41:55Z).
- AC3 here now points at that item; AC1 / AC2 / AC4 / AC5 remain this
  item's own evidence.

Recorded so the split is auditable, not a silent AC redefinition.

## Constraints

- No production restart is required for the analysis; the fix itself ships
  through the normal dev→main release.
- The probe must stay cheap and must not recurse into the child-port
  discovery path in a way that can block `/health` on a slow log scan
  (discovery is cached and TTL-bounded; validate the added latency).

data.description:
# Chat-model child-port fallback fires for unloaded local models (gpt120) — polls the router and pollutes the fallback signal

**Priority:** medium · **Type:** bug · **Scope decisions (producer, 2026-10-31):** **Q1 = A** (guard every proxy-initiated `/slots` poll through the shared path) · **Q2 = B** (router `/models` loaded set behind a short-TTL cached snapshot) · **Q3 = B** (block on LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW + LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL, then reuse both)

## Problem statement

When a chat request names a local model that is **not currently loaded** (e.g.
`gpt120` while `Qwen3` is resident), the proxy's slot-availability check still
tries to discover that model's child port, fails, and falls back to the router
— which then answers `GET /slots?model=gpt120` with HTTP 400. The fallback is
recorded as a genuine discovery regression (counter +
`slots_child_port_unavailable` warning), so an unloaded-model poll is
indistinguishable from the real regression signal the parent fix
(LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC3) was built to expose.

## Evidence (measured)

- **Direct cause, reproduced from the production log**
  (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-28_10.gz`, lines 8204–8205):

  ```text
  2026-10-28 10:45:00,400 - INFO - [local] POST .../v1/chat/completions
    body={"model":"gpt120", ... "reply OK" ...} session_id=b87b8e0c-...
  2026-10-28 10:45:00,404 - WARNING - slots_child_port_unavailable: no model
    child port discovered for model=gpt120; falling back to router port 8080 ...
  ```

  The warning fires **4 ms after** the chat request and `current_model=Qwen3`
  is reported by `/status` two seconds later — i.e. the caller is the chat
  dispatch path, not a status poll.
- **Call path:** `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`_check_slot_availability` call) →
  `router_helpers._check_slot_availability()` →
  `_resolve_local_slots_target(srv, model="gpt120", ...)` →
  `_discover_local_child_port()` finds no signal for `gpt120` →
  `_warn_child_port_fallback()` increments
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  and emits the throttled WARNING, then the poll goes to the **router**.
- **Scale (from LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 window evidence):** 2,407 router-responder
  `/slots` 400 responses across the 48 h superset (243 on 2026-10-27, 2,164 on
  2026-10-28, vs 86 on 2026-10-26). The 400 side is owned by
  LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8; this item owns the *fallback-signal* side and the
  needless request.
- **Counter readings:** unreadable for the window (serving pid replaced
  2026-10-30T10:35:07Z); post-window pid 3224511 read `2` in its first
  ~8.7 h. The live pid 3944027 emitted one warning at
  `2026-10-31T00:42:00.198Z` for `model=mxbai-embed` — a **loaded** model with
  no discoverable child port, i.e. exactly the shape AC2 must keep counting.
- **Behavioural equivalence of skipping:** in `_check_slot_availability()` only
  a `200` with zero free slots produces a 503; every non-200 (including the
  router's definitive 400) already falls through to `return None`. Skipping the
  poll for a definitively unloaded model therefore **does not change the
  admission decision** — it only removes the request, the counter increment and
  the warning.

## Users and impact

- **Operator / observability consumer** — user story: *As the operator, I want
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` and the
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning to fire only when a **loaded** model's
  child port cannot be discovered, so that a real child-port discovery
  regression cannot hide behind unloaded-model noise.*
- **herdr dispatcher / capacity signal (`/llama/local/status`)** — user story:
  *As the dispatcher, I want proxy `/slots` polling to stay off the router for
  models that are not loaded, so polls do not queue behind the busy child or
  add 4xx noise to the router access log.*
- **Router access-log reader** — user story: *As an operator triaging
  `llama-server.log`, I want the router-responder `/slots` 400 population to be
  attributable to genuine external probes, not to the proxy polling for models
  that are not loaded.*

## Existing state

- All proxy-initiated `/slots` queries route through
  `_resolve_local_slots_target()` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`), which
  rewrites the local router endpoint to the discovered child port and, on
  discovery failure, calls `_warn_child_port_fallback()` (counter + throttled
  warning; LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC2/AC3).
- `_discover_local_child_port()` correctly returns `None` for a model with no
  child instance — the defect is that "no child instance because the model is
  not loaded" is treated as a *discovery failure* rather than a definitive
  non-stale answer.
- An authoritative "is this model loaded" primitive already exists:
  `srv.router_is_model_loaded()` / `srv.router_list_models()`
  (`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py:997–1075`), reading the router's `/models`
  (`status.value` = loaded/ready/running/active), with presence-with-no-status
  treated as loaded.
- `srv.current_model` is set to the loaded llama model name in router mode
  (`lifecycle.py:2383`) **but** at startup it is first set to
  `router_preload_list[0]` (`server.py:949`), which can be a non-chat preset
  (`mxbai-embed`) — see the live warning above.
- The `/health` reachability probe no longer queries `/slots`
  (LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0), which is why the residual fallback signal is now
  dominated by this chat-path case.

## Desired change (scope settled — see Appendix)

1. **Guard before polling.** Before issuing `GET /slots?model=<m>` against the
   local router, establish whether `<m>` is loaded. When it is **definitively
   not loaded**, skip the poll entirely: no router request, no
   `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` increment, no
   `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning. There is no slot state to learn for
   a model with no instance. **Q1 = A:** the guard lives in the single shared
   `/slots` resolution path, so *every* proxy-initiated poll inherits it —
   chat-dispatch availability check, per-model poller, and the status/SSE
   paths.
2. **Keep the genuine signal.** A `/slots` poll for a **loaded** model whose
   child port cannot be discovered must still increment the counter and emit
   the throttled warning (AC2).
3. **Source of truth for "loaded" (Q2 = B).** Use the router's `/models`
   loaded set (existing `router_is_model_loaded()` / `router_list_models()`)
   behind a short-TTL cached snapshot; when the probe fails or the name cannot
   be resolved, **poll as today — never skip**. A false skip would remove a
   legitimate availability gate.
4. **Reuse, don't duplicate (Q3 = B).** The cached `/models` id snapshot is
   delivered by **LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** and the `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`
   section AC4 edits here overlap **LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL**; this item is blocked
   on both and reuses their artefacts.
5. **Observability of the skip (AC6, agent-proposed).** A dedicated counter
   (e.g. `llama_slots_child_port_skipped_total{reason="model_not_loaded"}`) or
   an equivalent documented signal so a skip is distinguishable from "never
   polled" when verifying AC1 on a live proxy.
6. **Docs.** `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` (observability / target-signal
   sections) and the resolver docstring plus the `proxy/README.md`
   child-port-discovery section must describe the unloaded-model skip and its
   signal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Unloaded model is not counted.** A `/slots` poll for a model that
      is not currently loaded does **not** increment
      `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
      and emits no `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning (asserted via the
      counter/warning in a test; the router is not contacted).
- [ ] **AC2 — Loaded-model regression still pinned.** A `/slots` poll for the
      loaded chat model whose child port cannot be discovered **still**
      increments the counter and emits the throttled warning (regression test,
      must fail if the guard swallows loaded-model discovery failures).
- [ ] **AC3 — `/status` capacity truth preserved.** `/status` continues to
      report truthful capacity (existing "definitive model absent" behaviour:
      fail-open on the configured pool, no resurrected fossil counts).
- [ ] **AC4 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` observability
      section and the `_resolve_local_slots_target()` /
      `_discover_local_child_port()` docstrings in
      `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` describe the unloaded-model skip; the
      `proxy/README.md` child-port-discovery section agrees.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full suite green.** Full project test suite passes with the
      change (run through the test skill; changed-scope gate first).
- [ ] **AC6 — Skip is observable (agent-proposed; no producer objection).**
      Live/`/metrics` evidence distinguishes a skipped poll from a poll that
      was never attempted (new counter or documented log line), so AC1 can be
      verified post-deploy.
- [ ] **AC7 — Admission outcome unchanged.** A test pins that skipping the
      availability check for an unloaded model returns the same admission
      result (`None`) as the current definitive-400 fall-through — the fix must
      not start refusing or blocking requests.

## Constraints

- **No new router `/slots` traffic** and no new blocking call on the chat hot
  path: the "is it loaded" probe is `/models` only (never `/slots`), behind the
  short-TTL cached snapshot supplied by LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW.
- **Fail open, never fail closed:** when loadedness cannot be determined, poll
  as today. A wrong skip would remove a real availability gate and allow
  over-subscription of the slot pool.
- The guard is shared (Q1 = A): `_resolve_local_slots_target()` is
  **synchronous** while `router_is_model_loaded()` is **async** — the cached
  loaded snapshot must therefore be readable synchronously (refreshed by the
  async callers / a background refresh), or the resolver takes the loaded set
  as an argument supplied by its call sites.
- `_discover_local_child_port()` semantics stay unchanged (a missing signal is
  still "no port"); the definitive "model not loaded" classification is layered
  above it.
- Do not weaken the LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC3 guarantee for the loaded model.
- Do not build a second `/models` cache: reuse LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW's snapshot
  (Q3 = B); if that slice's API turns out to be unusable for a synchronous
  guard, raise it as a blocker rather than forking the cache.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — add the unloaded-model guard at the async
  `_check_slot_availability()` call site (and `_resolve_local_slots_target()`
  docs/metric plumbing); keep `_warn_child_port_fallback()` for loaded models.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — reuse `router_is_model_loaded()` /
  `router_list_models()`; add a short-TTL loaded-set cache (router pid keyed)
  if the guard needs one.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `poll_slots_for_model()` (the per-model poller
  resolves through the same path and must obey the same skip rule).
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — fallback counter (unchanged) plus, if AC6 is
  accepted, the `skipped` counter.
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_query_target_call_sites.py` — extend the shared
  resolver/call-site suite.
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_unloaded_model_skip.py` — new focused tests for
  AC1/AC2/AC7 (unloaded skip, loaded-model regression pinned, admission
  outcome unchanged).
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_availability_dedicated_client.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_child_port_discovery_rotation.py` — verify the guard did
  not disturb existing availability/discovery contracts.
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` — observability + "target signal going
  forward" sections.
- `proxy/README.md` — "Child-port discovery" / fallback-observability section.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF** — *Residual router-proxied `/slots` 500s: audit
  remaining call sites and enforce direct child-port polling* (done). Parent of
  the shared resolver, counter and throttled warning this item refines.
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — *Router `/slots` HTTP 400s: `?model=` resolution
  path* (plan_complete). Owns the 400-response side; its intake answer Q2=A
  established that a `?model=<unloaded>` 400 is *expected truth* — this item
  removes the proxy's **own** such polls without changing that stance. Its
  six slices (all `intake_complete`, blocked) overlap in two concrete places:
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** — *Resolve the model id from `/models` instead of
    hard-coding Qwen3* (slice 4). Delivers a **TTL-cached `/models` id
    snapshot** that the unloaded-model guard should reuse rather than
    duplicate (see Appendix Q2/Q3).
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZ7M002D9GT** — *Thread the resolved model through the
    model-less `/slots` probes* (slice 3). Its "skip the query when no model is
    known" is a **different** condition (empty model name) from this item's
    "model known but not loaded" — no AC overlap, but the same call sites.
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL** — *Document the model-resolution rule and 400
    semantics* (slice 5) touches the same `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`
    section AC4 edits here — sequence or coordinate to avoid a doc conflict.
- **LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12** — *Static audit: enumerate every `/slots` 400 call
  path* (child of LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8, intake_complete). Shares the call-site
  inventory this item needs.
- **LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0** — *Proxy `/health` reachability probe polls router
  `GET /slots?model=`* (completed). Removed the previously dominant
  fallback/500 source; that is why the chat-path case is now the visible one.
- **LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57** — *Verify `router:500 == 0` over 24 h after the
  child-port discovery fix*. Supplies the window evidence quoted above.
- **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** — *False "saturated" capacity signal starves herdr
  downtime dispatcher* (completed). Source of the definitive-model-absent /
  fail-open contract that AC3 and AC7 must preserve.
- **LP-0MTP1FQXH004JYEF** — model-filtered child-port discovery (`mxbai-embed`
  vs `Qwen3`), i.e. the reason a model name is passed to discovery at all.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (high impact): false "not loaded" ⇒ a real availability gate is
  skipped** and the pool can be over-subscribed. *Mitigation:* require an
  explicit `not loaded` answer from the router's `/models`; fail open to
  polling on any probe error or unresolved name; AC2 + AC7 tests pin both
  directions.
- **Risk: extra `/models` call per chat dispatch.** *Mitigation:* the shared
  short-TTL cached snapshot (LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW) — no new round trip on the
  hot path beyond one cache lookup.
- **Risk: name aliasing** (client model id ≠ llama model name ≠ router preset
  id). *Mitigation:* compare the already-resolved llama model name
  (`_resolve_slot_model_name`) case-insensitively; treat "unknown/not present"
  as *not* evidence of unloaded and poll as today.
- **Risk: `srv.current_model` is not a reliable loaded-set** (startup pins it
  to `router_preload_list[0]`, live example `mxbai-embed`; router mode can hold
  several loaded models). *Mitigation:* `/models` is the authority; treat
  `current_model` as a fallback only, and never as proof of absence.
- **Assumption:** the admission outcome for an unloaded model is unchanged
  because the current definitive-400 path already returns `None`
  (`_check_slot_availability` only 503s on `200` with zero free slots).
- **Assumption (Q3 = B):** LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW exposes the cached `/models` id
  snapshot in a form the synchronous resolver can read (directly or via an
  argument supplied by call sites). If it does not, that is a blocker to raise
  on this item rather than a reason to fork the cache.
- **Assumption:** "not loaded" polls carry no information for capacity
  signalling, so deleting them cannot degrade `/status` (which polls
  `srv.current_model`, i.e. a model it believes is loaded).
- **Scope-creep risk:** the startup `current_model = router_preload_list[0]`
  behaviour (and the resulting `mxbai-embed` warning) is a *separate* defect
  about loaded-model bookkeeping. Record as a linked follow-up rather than
  widening this item (see Appendix Q3).

## Dependencies / sequencing (Q3 = B)

- **Blocked by LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** — *Resolve the model id from `/models`
  instead of hard-coding Qwen3* (slice 4 of LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8). Supplies the
  TTL-cached `/models` id snapshot AC1/AC2/AC6 rely on.
- **Blocked by LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL** — *Document the model-resolution rule and
  400 semantics* (slice 5). Owns the `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` section
  AC4 extends, so this item must not race it.
- Sequencing note: both blockers sit in the LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 chain
  (`intake_complete`, serially blocked), so this item starts once slices 4 and
  5 are terminal. If slice 4 lands without a synchronously-readable snapshot,
  surface it as a blocker on this item rather than building a second cache.

## Out of scope

- Eliminating router `/slots` 400 responses in general (LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8)
  and the new per-query instrumentation deferred to LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5.
- `/health` reachability probing (already fixed in LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0).
- Changing `_discover_local_child_port()`'s discovery sources or caching.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded 2026-10-31 during the intake session for
LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K (agent: Map; session
`herdr-1793416675-4166126-26041`). All three were raised as OPEN QUESTIONs
because the item was filed with "scope to confirm at intake", and all three
were answered by the producer on 2026-10-31 (interactive reply).
**Final: Q1 = A, Q2 = B, Q3 = B.**

- **Q1 — How wide is the skip?**
  - **A)** Guard **every** proxy-initiated `/slots` poll through the single
    shared path, so no proxy surface can poll a definitively unloaded model
    (chat-dispatch availability check, per-model poller, status/SSE paths —
    the latter two only matter if their model argument can be a non-loaded
    name).
  - **B)** Guard **only** the chat-dispatch availability check
    (`_check_slot_availability`) that produced the `gpt120` evidence; leave the
    other call sites untouched.
  - **C)** Guard the two async poller call sites only
    (`_check_slot_availability` + `poll_slots_for_model`), leaving the
    status/SSE paths alone.
  - **Recommended: A** — the ACs are written at the resolver level, and a
    single guard prevents a future call site from re-introducing the noise;
    the status/SSE paths pass `srv.current_model` today, so A costs them
    nothing in the common case.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-31): A** — guard every proxy-initiated
    `/slots` poll through the single shared path (source: interactive reply).

- **Q2 — What is the authority for "currently loaded"?**
  - **A)** `srv.current_model` only (cheapest, already in hand; but it is
    pinned to `router_preload_list[0]` at startup and router mode can hold
    several loaded models, so it can neither prove absence nor list the loaded
    set).
  - **B)** The router's `/models` loaded set (existing
    `router_is_model_loaded()` / `router_list_models()`), behind a short-TTL
    cached snapshot; poll as today whenever the probe fails or the name is
    unresolved.

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Early-released local dispatch keeps prefilling in `llama-server` and starves the next dispatch

## Problem statement

The Option D early release (LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN) detours the client in under a
second, but it does not demonstrably stop the work it abandoned at
`llama-server`: in the measured 24 h window **285 of 1 092 backend prompt
evaluations (26 %) were never consumed by a proxy stream**, and **58 of 60**
residual `prefill_deadline` evictions started inside an *estimated*
abandoned-prefill window. Each fake-warm dispatch therefore appears to cost a
release *plus* a 120 s residual: the retry — which returns to the same
session-pinned slot — reports no prefill progress for its whole lease and is
evicted in turn.

The premise cannot be taken as given. Intake-time log inspection
(2026-10-31, current `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`) found 143
`Connection handling canceled` events, of which 49 could be joined to a task
id; **only 4 were followed by any further `prompt processing progress` line,
each at most one batch**, and none reached `prompt eval time` after the
cancel. The upstream cancel implemented by LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB does take
effect — so the *magnitude* (26 % of compute, 667 s median backlog) and the
*mechanism* (abandoned work runs to completion) must be decided on evidence
before a fix is chosen. That decision is AC1.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Owns the prefill-deadline and eviction metrics
  and pays for cloud fallback; needs the 26 % waste and the 1.96 user-class
  evictions/h explained and reduced, and needs the residual counts to stop
  being re-attributed every measurement cycle.
- **Agent sessions (herdr workers, `pi` sessions).** They are the retries: a
  dispatch starved behind abandoned work ends as a 503 detour, a longer
  latency, or a failed audit run.
- **Measurement analyst.** Re-runs
  `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py`; needs each release
  joined to the backend task it cancelled, so "prefills computed and thrown
  away" is a measurement and not the subtraction of two unrelated counters.

User stories:

- As an operator, when the proxy releases an accepted local dispatch early, I
  want the GPU work it abandoned to stop within a bounded, recorded time — and
  I want to see that bound in the logs — so compute is never thrown away
  silently.
- As an agent session, when my request is retried after an early release, I
  want it either to prefill immediately (on a free slot) or not to be admitted
  at all, rather than burn a 120 s lease with zero measured progress.
- As an analyst, I want the abandoned-prefill estimate to state its own
  provenance and error, so the 58/60 and 26 % figures are either confirmed or
  restated with evidence rather than quoted as fact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Mechanism decided (confirmed or refuted) with recorded evidence.**
  A committed record under `docs/dev/` (for example
  `docs/dev/abandoned-prefill-release-cancel.md`) reports, for a ≥24 h window,
  per post-acceptance release: release reason, proxy release timestamp, joined
  backend task id (where a join exists), whether a backend cancel was observed,
  the number of `prompt processing progress` lines after the cancel, the time
  from cancel to `slot release: … stop processing`, and whether a
  `prompt eval time` line was emitted for that task. The record states a
  verdict for each competing mechanism below, with the log lines that decide
  it, and either confirms or restates the 26 % (285/1 092) and 58/60 figures:
  - **H1 — the abandoned prefill runs to completion.** Discriminator: cancel
    events followed by many progress batches, and `prompt eval time` emitted
    for a cancelled task. *Intake sample argues against this (4 of 49, ≤1
    batch each) — it must still be measured over 24 h, not assumed.*
  - **H2 — the cancel lands only at a batch boundary.** Discriminator:
    cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution against observed
    `batch.n_tokens` (up to 8 192) at the measured prompt-eval rate (current
    log p10/p50/p90 = 86 / 158 / 536 tok/s), i.e. a bounded tail of roughly
    6–52 s rather than minutes.
  - **H3 — the 26 % is an accounting artefact.** Discriminator: reconcile
    `prompt eval time` (backend, *all* consumers) against
    `Stream finished … provider=local` (proxy) per hour, and enumerate
    non-proxy consumers of `llama-server` (direct calls in `scripts/`,
    benchmarks, health probes) that would be counted as "thrown away".
  - **H4 — the retry is queued behind a draining slot.** Discriminator:
    `slot launch_slot_` time for the retry task versus the abandoned task's
    `slot release`, joined through the proxy's session→slot assignment
    (`_slot_id_for_session` keeps a session on its slot, so a retry returns to
    the slot it abandoned).
  - **H5 — the residual is capacity, not starvation.** Discriminator: the
    event's prompt size and measured prompt-eval rate against the 120 s
    deadline (median event is a 78 213-token prompt; at 158 tok/s a full
    re-prefill is ≈495 s, at 536 tok/s ≈146 s), and whether any later dispatch
    of the same prompt ever reached `progress = 1.0`.

- **AC2 — The release's effect on the backend is bounded and observable.** A
  committed analyser (extend
  `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` or add a sibling)
  joins proxy post-acceptance releases to backend task lifecycles over a ≥24 h
  window and emits: releases with no observed backend cancel (count and
  share), the cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution, and the tokens
  actually evaluated after the cancel. Every release whose cancel cannot be
  joined is reported as unjoined rather than dropped. Target (assumption to
  confirm): **≤ 5 % of releases with no explained backend stop**, and a
  recorded p90 stop latency bound.

- **AC3 — The next dispatch is not starved by abandoned work.** In a
  post-change ≥24 h window (restart-segmented, from on-disk logs), the share
  of `prefill_deadline` events whose dispatch start falls inside an
  abandoned-prefill window falls from **58/60** to a recorded target
  (assumption: **≤ 20 %**), **and** no accepted dispatch expires its lease
  with zero `prefill_progress_measured` while its session's slot is still
  draining an abandoned task — either the retry is routed to a free slot, or
  it observes prefill progress inside its lease. Both halves must be reported;
  a bare `prefill_deadline` count can be gamed by reason conversion (248
  `measured_cache_deficit` releases in the same window).

- **AC4 — No warm-path or throughput regression.** Against the matched
  pre-change window: local completions per hour and large-warm completion
  latency (p50/p90) are not reduced, and `measured_cache_deficit` releases per
  hour do not rise, measured per
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`. Both windows are reported, with the
  deltas, not just a verdict.

- **AC5 — Tests and documentation.** Hermetic tests pin the new
  release→cancel accounting and any routing/accounting behaviour change (no
  live `llama-server` dependency). Documentation is updated to reflect the
  change, including code comments, `proxy/docs/routing.md` (the abandoned
  dispatch section), `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`, the
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()` docstring in the analyser (which currently
  asserts the opposite of `routing.md`), and
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` where the baseline moves. The full
  project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Out of scope (owned elsewhere, do not re-tune):** the prefill deadline
  (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds=120`), the cold-prefill budget
  (`local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens=25000`), the admission ladder's warmth
  pricing (LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27), and the slot count (LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5).
- **`llama-server` exposes no cancel API.** Cancellation is only observable as
  a closed socket, and the backend acts on it at its next socket write, so the
  effective granularity is one `n_batch` (up to 8 192 tokens observed). Any
  batch-size (`-ub`/`--batch-size`) change is a backend-config change and must
  be justified by AC1 evidence as a recorded decision — not tuned silently in
  this item.
- **No overlap with the annotation work.** LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM and its child
  LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK own the abandoned-slot identity/annotation
  (`abandoned_busy`, registry entries on every release path, including the
  Option D path's missing `abandoned_slot_id`); this item owns the
  *behaviour* — does the backend stop, and is the next dispatch starved.
  Implementation must not duplicate or contradict that annotation, and the
  Option D plumbing gap is reported to those items rather than fixed here.
- **Measurement integrity.** `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S = 43.1` in the
  analyser prices the abandoned backlog; the measured prompt-eval rate on the
  current log is p10 86 / p50 158 / p90 536 tok/s, so the 667 s median backlog
  estimate is likely overstated several-fold. Any correction must be recorded
  as a measurement change with its own evidence, and the 58/60 figure restated
  on both the old and the corrected basis (backwards comparable) rather than
  swapped.
- **Measurement windows** are ≥24 h, restart-segmented, derived from on-disk
  logs only (no in-process counters), per the existing
  `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` method.

## Existing state

- **The upstream cancel already exists.** LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (with
  LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK) made every abandonment path close the captured upstream
  stream through `_release_unserved_dispatch`, and records the abandoned slot
  identity for the status annotation. `proxy/docs/routing.md` claims the
  cancel is real: 42 of 82 `Connection handling canceled` events on 2026-10-28
  cancelled a task that never reached `prompt processing done`.
- **The Option D path does not use that plumbing.** In `proxy/proxy/router.py`
  the `MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError` handler calls
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch(...)` **without**
  `upstream_stream_cm` or `abandoned_slot_id` (the deadline path at
  `router.py:2220` passes `upstream_stream_cm=cm`), then closes the stream and
  client itself. So the 42/82 evidence was taken on a different code path than
  the one that produces most of the 389 post-acceptance releases, and the
  abandoned-slot annotation is not recorded for the Option D releases (that
  annotation gap is LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK's scope; here it is evidence, not
  work).
- **The analyser's model contradicts `routing.md`.**
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()` documents "A released dispatch is **not**
  cancelled at `llama-server`" and prices the *whole* remaining prompt
  (`tokens / 43.1`) as backend occupancy — the source of the 667 s median and
  of the 58/60 overlap figure.
- **Session→slot affinity makes the retry return to the draining slot.**
  `_slot_id_for_session` (`proxy/proxy/session.py`) keeps a session on its
  assigned slot, so the immediate retry after a 503 targets the same slot the
  release just abandoned. `slot_id=unknown` on every post-F4 eviction line
  means slot-level attribution is currently unavailable from the eviction log
  alone (it must be reconstructed from `launch_slot_`/`slot release` pairs).
- **Current live counts (intake sample).** `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`
  (3.7 h, 2026-10-31 00:41 → 04:21) holds 39 `local_eviction_after_acceptance`
  events; `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` holds 143 cancels, 121
  completed prompt evaluations and 34 batches of 8 192 tokens.
- **Queue-wait work overlaps but is a different question.**
  LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR / LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5 diagnose why *queue* waits expire
  at the 60 s budget (blocker class, guard projection); this item is about
  accepted dispatches starved by abandoned work they were never told about.

## Desired change

1. Decide H1–H5 on 24 h evidence and publish the decision record (AC1), with
   the 26 % / 58-of-60 claims confirmed or restated.
2. Make the release's backend effect attributable per dispatch (AC2), so
   "abandoned" stops being an estimate derived from a token-rate constant.
3. Remove the starvation path found by AC1 — at minimum: a retry must never be
   admitted into a slot that is still draining work the proxy itself abandoned
   without that fact being visible to admission and to the eviction log
   (AC3). The specific mechanism (route to a free slot, hold the dispatch out
   of "about to prefill" pricing, or bound the wait against the drain) is a
   decision for AC1's evidence, not for intake.
4. Prove no warm-path or throughput regression (AC4), and leave the
   documentation and tests consistent with the new measurement (AC5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — the `MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError` handler
  (≈ lines 1998–2120) and the deadline handler (≈ lines 2190–2260); the Option
  D release currently omits `upstream_stream_cm` / `abandoned_slot_id`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`, `_record_abandoned_slot`,
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup`.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_id_for_session` / `_slot_owners` (session
  affinity is what sends the retry back to the draining slot).
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` —
  `abandoned_prefill_windows()`, `backend_prefill_accounting()`,
  `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S`.
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`,
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the three
  records whose claims must agree after the change.
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_measured_cache_abort*.py` — the existing hermetic
  coverage the new tests sit beside.

## Related work

- LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O — the measurement item that produced the 26 % / 58-of-60
  evidence (`discovered-from` parent of this item).
- LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (completed) and LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK (completed) — the
  upstream cancel + abandoned-slot registry whose effectiveness this item
  re-verifies for the Option D path.
- LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2 (completed) — regression test: abandoned dispatch not
  reported saturated.

# Intake Brief: hydrator demotes in-progress items held by pane-less (driven/headless) sessions

## Headline

The Herdr **hydrator** treats "no herdr pane title contains this work-item ID" as "nobody is working this item" and releases the claim (`in-progress/* → open/*`) every 30 s — but driven/headless `implement` sessions (`implement.py drive` → `pi -p`, no pane) own legitimate claims, so their claims are reverted continuously (10 releases across 3 items in 27 minutes in the live log window). This item is the **defect dossier + fix specification** for the hydrator owner (code lives in the sibling ContextHub repository, `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`); it does not change code in this repository.

## Problem statement

`decideDemotion()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts:497`) returns `{status: 'open', stage: 'intake_complete'}` whenever the item is `in-progress` and no pane in the current workspace has a title containing its ID. That single-signal rule cannot distinguish *"the claim was abandoned"* from *"the claim is held by a live session that has no pane"*, so every claim made by a driven child session is reverted within one hydrator cycle while the session is still editing.

## Users

- **Driven/headless implement sessions** (`implement.py drive` / `phase` / `start`, `pi -p`) — the only writer of the claim, and the party whose claim is silently revoked.
  - As a driven session, I need my `in_progress` claim to survive while my process is alive, so `StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` does not fail mid-work and no second session is handed the same item.
- **Producer / operator** — relies on the invariant *actively worked ⇒ `in_progress`* to reason about the queue.
  - As a producer, I need `in_progress` to mean "someone is actually working this", and I need abandonment to still self-heal without manual intervention.
- **Other dispatching agents** (`wl next`, downtime worker) — consume the resulting queue.
  - As a dispatching agent, I must never receive an item another live session is editing (the duplicate-dispatch failure the invariant exists to prevent).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Defect dossier recorded** — `.worklog/analysis/LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK-hydrator-headless-demotion.md` exists and contains: the observed failure narrative, the exact code path (`hydrator.ts:497` `decideDemotion` → `applyDemotion` → `wl update --status open --stage intake_complete`), the evidence table (≥3 timestamped `released … (no matching pane)` lines with affected item IDs and their resulting status/assignee), and the affected populations (driven/headless sessions; herdr panes whose title lost the ID).
2. **Evidence is re-verifiable, not quoted from memory** — every log line and symbol cited in the dossier is reproducible by the documented commands (`rg "released " .worklog/logs/hydrator.log`, `rg -n "function decideDemotion" -A 20 packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` run in the owning checkout), and the dossier states the retention limit that makes older evidence unavailable (the live log holds only ~200 lines / one day, so the original 2026-10-30T20:49–20:52Z lines are already rotated away).
3. **Fix specification is implementable in one pass by the hydrator owner** — the dossier contains a specification naming: the additional claim signal to honour, the liveness test to apply to it (a *heldness* probe, never file existence — 39 of 40 `child-*.lock` files on this machine belong to dead processes), the preserved behaviours (pane match stays primary; a claim whose holder is dead is still released; a step failure stays fail-open toward no-demotion), the exact unit-test cases to add to `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`, and the docs to update (`docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, module header).
4. **Producer directive reconciled, not silently overridden** — the spec explicitly restates the producer's "keep it simple: a pane title containing the item ID means busy" directive (`WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ`) and explains why a second, mechanically verifiable signal is required for pane-less sessions, so the owner can accept or reject it knowingly.
5. **Secondary defects documented as separate facets** — the dossier records at least: (a) demotion leaves the previous `assignee` set, producing `open` items that are still on a scheduling hold (live example `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U`: `open/intake_complete`, `assignee=Map`, released at 2026-10-31T04:36:31Z); (b) the claimed `in_review` branch of `decideDemotion` would mark a live session's item `completed` (not observed; recorded as a risk of the same root cause); (c) a pane-based false release for a session whose pane title/ID drifted.
6. **Follow-up ownership is unambiguous** — the dossier states which store owns the fix and why (ContextHub `WL-` store owns `packages/herdr/`; this `LP-` store cannot create a worktree over that repo), and records the producer's decision on how the ContextHub implementation item is raised (created by this item, or left to the producer) in the Appendix.
7. **Validation criterion** — an independent reviewer can re-run the three documented verification commands and confirm each attested claim in the dossier without access to this session; every claim is either reproduced or explicitly marked "reported, not reproduced".
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (for this repository: the analysis dossier is the documentation deliverable; nothing else in `docs/` describes the hydrator, because it does not live here).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundaries.** The hydrator, its docs and its tests live in the sibling ContextHub repository; the lock protocol lives in the globally installed agent skills (`~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py`, installed from SorraAgents). Neither may be edited from an `LP-` worktree; this item records the defect and the spec only (see AC6).
- **Producer design directive.** Pane-title matching was chosen over tab-label matching after the producer rejected tab matching as unreliable ("It should be simple. Look for a pane in this workspace with the work item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy." — quoted in `ContextHub/docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md:58`, rework tracked by `WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ`). Any fix must keep that rule intact as the primary signal and add rather than replace it.
- **No new heartbeat/TTL.** The hydrator must stay kernel-authoritative where possible: no wall-clock claim expiry, no polling of a session's heartbeat, and no demotion-suppression that can outlive the claiming process (that would re-introduce the stuck-`in_progress` defect the hydrator exists to cure, `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`).
- **Budget.** A hydrator cycle already races a 5 s per-step budget inside a 20 s run watchdog (`HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS` / `HYDRATOR_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`); any added probe must be local filesystem I/O, not another `wl`/`herdr` spawn per item.
- **Fail-open asymmetry is deliberate.** An ambiguous or unavailable claim source must not demote (mirroring the existing fail-open on `wl`/`herdr` failure) — but an *affirmatively dead* holder must still release.
- **Scope.** Do not expand into redesigning dispatch, the worklist UI marker, or the drive orchestrator; record such opportunities as separate work items.

## Existing state

### Live evidence (2026-10-31T04:10–04:37Z, current log window)

Ten releases, three distinct items, all `in-progress/intake_complete → open/intake_complete (no matching pane)`:

| Time (UTC) | Item | Releases |
|---|---|---|
| 04:10:59, 04:11:29, 04:28:30 | `LP-0MVT1NVAJ007KUGO` | 3 (now `blocked/intake_complete`, no assignee) |
| 04:14:59, 04:15:29, 04:31:00, 04:31:30, 04:32:00, 04:36:31 | `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U` | 6 (now `open/intake_complete`, `assignee=Map` — stale hold) |
| 04:29:30 | `LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12` | 1 (later completed in_review by its own session) |

Historical evidence (2026-10-30T20:49–20:52Z, `LP-0MVRMOV8K0007NFO`, three releases interleaved with the live session's writes) is no longer in the log: `hydrator.log` retains only the current ~200-line window (13,796 bytes, all lines dated 2026-10-31), with no rotated archive — so evidence must be captured live (AC2).

### Mechanism

- Detection is a single signal: `herdr pane list --workspace <HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID>` → keep panes whose title contains the item ID (`extractWorkItemIdsFromText` / `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix` keep the ID as a trailing suffix).
- A driven child session is spawned as `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>"` with no pane, so it can never satisfy that signal; every claim it makes is released on the next 30 s tick.
- `applyDemotion` issues `wl update <id> --status <s> --stage <g> --json` only — it never clears `assignee`, so a released item can remain on a scheduling hold (non-empty assignee = hold per the global workflow).
- The per-child lock at `<worklog>/locks/child-<work-item-id>.lock` is kernel-authoritative while held (`flock`, released on exit/SIGKILL) and records `{agent, pid, session_id, started_at, token}`; the file **persists after release**, so it is a liveness source only via a heldness probe, never via existence or a `started_at` TTL.
- Current machine state: 40 `child-*.lock` files, **all** recording pids that are no longer alive — i.e. pure existence checks would suppress demotion forever.

### Consumers that break

- `StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` (intake/implement/plan) fails on a legitimately-held claim.
- `wl next` / the downtime worker can hand the same item to a second session while the first is editing (the duplicate-dispatch failure `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` exists to prevent).
- Per-child `implement.py` locking still serialises `start`/`finish`, so no store corruption has been observed — but worktree and claim are no longer a consistent pair.

## Desired change

A hydrator cycle decides "busy" from **two** independent signals and demotes only when both are negative:

1. *Pane signal (unchanged, primary)* — a pane in the current workspace whose title contains the item ID ⇒ busy.
2. *Claim-holder signal (new)* — the item is named by a **live** claim holder: its `child-<id>.lock` is currently flocked (probed non-blocking) or its recorded pid is alive **and** the probe is unambiguous ⇒ busy.

Everything else keeps today's behaviour: pane match wins, dep-blocked ⇒ `blocked`, `in_review` ⇒ `completed`, otherwise release to `open`/`intake_complete`; any ambiguity or probe error ⇒ no demotion (fail-open), an affirmatively dead holder ⇒ release as today.

## Fix specification (for the hydrator owner)

1. **New seam.** Extend the hydrator's injected deps with a `hasLiveClaimHolder(itemId): Promise<boolean>` (or a batch variant over the cycle's candidate list) so orchestration stays unit-testable without touching the filesystem, matching the existing `HydratorDeps` style.
2. **Decision input.** Give `decideDemotion()` a third context flag (`held: boolean`) and return `null` when `ctx.hasActivePane || ctx.held`; keep the `blocked` / `in_review` ordering untouched.
3. **Probe semantics.** Resolve the worklog root once per cycle (existing `getWorklogDir()`), list `locks/child-*.lock` once (no per-item spawn), and for each candidate attempt a non-blocking `flock` on its lock file:
   - acquire succeeds ⇒ nobody holds it: release immediately and fall back to the recorded `pid` liveness check (`process.kill(pid, 0)`), cross-checked against `started_at` to reject pid reuse;
   - acquire fails with `EWOULDBLOCK` ⇒ held ⇒ busy.
   Missing file ⇒ not held. Any other error (EACCES, malformed JSON, unreadable dir) ⇒ treat as held (fail-open, no demotion) and log a named reason.
4. **Log lines.** Every suppression and every release states the deciding signal, e.g. `[hydrator] kept <id>: live claim holder pid <pid> session <sid>` and `[hydrator] released <id>: … (no pane, claim holder dead)`, so the next incident is diagnosable from the log alone.
5. **Tests** (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`): pane match still wins; live holder + no pane ⇒ kept; dead holder + no pane ⇒ released to `open`; no lock file ⇒ released; malformed lock ⇒ kept + reason logged; `EWOULDBLOCK` ⇒ kept; probe throw ⇒ kept (fail-open); `held` never overrides the `blocked`/`in_review` branches; per-cycle lock listing happens once (no per-item spawn).
6. **Docs.** Update `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` (Design step 3 and the "Safety" list) and the module header to describe the second signal, its fail-open rules, and the explicit non-goal (no TTL/heartbeat).
7. **Producer sign-off gate.** If the producer prefers a worklog-native claim record (e.g. a claim token/assignee convention refreshed by `implement.py`) over reading the lock file, substitute that source behind the same seam — the decision is an Appendix open question, not an implementation detail.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `decideDemotion()` (line 497), orchestration cycle, `HydratorDeps`, `createProductionHydratorDeps().applyDemotion` (line 1030): add the claim-holder signal.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new decision and orchestration cases (1,348 lines today).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `getWorklogDir()` / `buildWlArgs()` already resolve the store root the lock probe needs.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — Design + Safety sections need the second signal.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py` — producer of the lock protocol (`<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`, metadata + `ENV_LOCK_TOKEN` re-entrancy); read-only contract for this fix.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — holds the lock for `phase_start`/`drive` lifetime (lines ~696–760); the population whose claims are being reverted.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/analysis/LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK-hydrator-headless-demotion.md` — the dossier this item produces (analysis-doc convention already used in this store).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/logs/hydrator.log` — evidence source and its retention limit.

## Related work

**This store (`LP-`)** — `LP-0MVRMOV8K0007NFO` (*[verdict] AC3 closure verdict, successor link and rollback note*, discovered-from parent): the session whose claims were reverted three times.

**ContextHub store (`WL-`, the fix's home)** — verified present in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`:

- `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI` (completed) — *Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane*: the feature that introduced the demotion rule, plus `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`.
- `WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` (completed) — pane-title active-detection directive quoted in **Constraints** ("It should be simple …"), and the selection-list marker.
- `WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US` (completed) — *Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items*: AC3 defines the `open`/`intake_complete` release target.
- `WL-0MTTSWE0G008M1VA` (deleted, folded into `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`) — claim-age timeout: the "no pane ⇒ stale regardless of age" rule this defect qualifies.
- `WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ` / `WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO` (completed) — per-step budgets and stdio isolation constraining the probe in **Constraints**.
- `WL-0MV25EE4E0028KDI` (completed) — hydrator docs/pane-title rationale, the doc to update.
- `WL-0MTWU4Y82001B3UH` (completed) — demotion audit-trail comment requirement (relevant to facet (a), stale `assignee`).
- `WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7` (completed) — *Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless `pi -p` vs herdr pane*: why driven sessions have no pane by design.

**Agent infrastructure (`SA-`)** — `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` (*actively worked ⇒ `in_progress`* invariant, the contract this violates); `SA-0MVOABYW00004978` (per-child lock rationale, `drive` duplicate-session RCA).

**Automated related-work report** (`find-related`, comment on this item) matched only proxy files in this repository — expected, since the hydrator and its tests live in ContextHub; those matches are noise and were not used.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — pid reuse.** A stale lock whose recorded pid now belongs to an unrelated process would suppress demotion indefinitely. Mitigation: require `started_at` ≤ process start time, or prefer the flock probe as authoritative; log the probe outcome.
- **Risk — cross-repo coupling.** The hydrator would depend on a lock format owned by the globally installed skills (SorraAgents). Mitigation: read it defensively (unknown/malformed ⇒ fail-open) and document the contract; or choose the worklog-native source (Appendix Q2, option C).
- **Risk — regression to stuck claims.** Suppression that outlives the holder re-creates `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`'s original defect. Mitigation: no TTL, kernel liveness only; explicit test for "dead holder ⇒ released".
- **Risk — evidence loss.** `hydrator.log` keeps only the live window with no rotation, so the dossier must capture its evidence at writing time (AC2); longer retention is recorded as a separate opportunity, not scope.
- **Risk — partial observation.** Facet (c) ("herdr pane whose pane id changed was released") is *reported but not reproduced*; the dossier must label it as such rather than assert it.
- **Assumption.** A driven child session's `implement.py` lock is held for the whole session lifetime (verified in `implement.py` around `_set_child_lock` / `phase_start`), so it is a faithful "session is alive" proxy.
- **Assumption.** Patch-level verification will happen in the ContextHub store; this item is validated by dossier quality (AC7), not by a green hydrator test run here.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Drive-orchestrator redesign, hydrator log rotation and `assignee`-clearing on release are adjacent opportunities; they are recorded as facets/candidates, not implemented under this item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope/home).** "Should this item stay report-only, or should it also raise the implementation item in the ContextHub store?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-31): B — "b, once created and synced delete this item."** Created `WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY` in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` (*[bug] hydrator demotes in-progress claims of pane-less driven sessions (no matching pane)*, stage `intake_complete`, effort Small / risk Medium) carrying the full brief, evidence, fix specification and all three answers; synced to `refs/worklog/data` (commit `141c91fb`, matching `origin`). This item is then deleted, per the same instruction. Source: producer reply on this item.
- **Q2 (claim signal).** "Which pane-less claim signal should the hydrator honour?" — **Answer (producer): A** — the existing per-child lock `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`, probed for *heldness* via non-blocking `flock` with a guarded pid-liveness fallback (never existence, never a TTL). Live example recorded: `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U` was `open/intake_complete` with `assignee=Map` after its 04:36:31Z release. Recorded as AC 7 of the successor item.

**Outcome:** superseded by `WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY` (ContextHub store) per producer decision Q1 = B; this item is deleted after that item was created and synced.

# Writer-side sidecar still absent at seed time post-fix — 0 found/restored over ≥24 h (LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB verdict)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the restored-prefix credit to actually fire (and,
secondarily, the snapshot/sidecar pair to stay coupled on disk), so that AC3
of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E can be answered with non-zero restored dispatches and
`found` seeds.

## Background (evidence, 2026-10-30)

The verification item LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB measured a ≥24 h post-fix window
(fix `5502ee44`, deployed 2026-10-29T12:58:32Z) and found the expected
signature absent:

- `cache_state=restored` dispatches: **0**; `slot_ratio_restored` events: **0**;
  `outcome=found` seeds: **0** (unchanged from the 155 h / 4,488-decision baseline).
- Seed outcomes shifted the wrong way: `missing_sidecar` 303 → **605** (98.1 % of
  617), `missing_snapshot` 392 → 12; guard outcomes still 0 (guard never reached).
- Writer-side health worsened: router-path slot saves 103/33 ok/fail (24 % fail)
  pre-fix → 34/65 (66 % fail) post-fix; eviction saves 9/33 → 42/64;
  `persistence skipped reason=slot_busy` 155 → 260. `ReadTimeout` dominates the
  failures (52 of 106 `slot_save` failures in-window).
- AC6 pairing at report time: 0 snapshots / 28 sidecars (all orphan, all saved
  post-deploy 04:02–19:01Z on 10-30) — no snapshot+sidecar pair on disk and
  orphan growth for post-deploy saves persists, 142 → 28 legacy orphans cleared.

Reproducible data: `docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-30.json` (+
`-full.json`), source logs `/var/log/llama-proxy` (`slot_ratio_seed outcome=…`,
`slot_save …`, `slot persistence skipped …`).

## Hypotheses to test (from the verdict)

1. **Eviction-sidecar write skipped.** `session._write_eviction_sidecar`
   returns early when `provider.get_recorded_prompt_prefix(model, session_id)`
   is `None` — sessions whose measured prefix was never recorded (e.g. usage
   block missing prompt_tokens, or prefix cleared) get a snapshot with **no**
   sidecar, which later seeds as `missing_sidecar`. Audit-traffic sessions
   dominate the 605 hits. Quantify how many eviction `saved=True` events are
   followed by a sidecar appearing on disk vs not, by session.
2. **Router-sidecar write skipped on 0-token fallback.**
   `provider.sidecar_cached_tokens` returns 0 (no usage, no recorded prefix,
   empty-message estimate fail) → the router writes no sidecar. Confirm the
   fallback estimate (`_estimate_prompt_tokens_for_routing`) can return 0 for
   real prompt shapes.
3. **Save/retire path divergence producing orphan sidecars.** A sidecar survives
   its snapshot (opposite of the AC3 coupling) — e.g. save resolves an endpoint
   dir path (`localhost-8080/`) while `_invalidate_session_and_slot` retires a
   root-style path, or `slot_id` vs `session_id` filename mismatch. Reproduce
   minimally and fix the divergence; the daily `cleanup-slot-cache.sh` removes
   pairs/orphans only, it never creates a survivor, so the proxy itself leaves
   them.
4. **Save-failure cliff.** 66 % router-save failure (`ReadTimeout`, `slot_busy`
   skip growth) starves the sidecar supply. Triage whether this is a timeout
   tuning, concurrency, or llama-server-side regression independent of the seed
   path.

## Acceptance criteria

- A minimal repro or direct log evidence pins which write path produced each
  observed `missing_sidecar` snapshot (router vs eviction), with counts for at
  least the 24 h post-fix window.
- Root cause identified and fixed so that a snapshot saved post-fix is paired
  with a sidecar (AC6-style pairing check: paired files present, no orphan
  growth for post-deploy saves).
- Post-fix ≥24 h window after the NEW deploy shows `outcome=found` > 0 and
  `cache_state=restored` dispatches > 0 (matching LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E AC3), or
  a documented, evidence-backed explanation of why the credit cannot fire with
  the current guard/prefix semantics.
- Verdict recorded in `docs/dev/` with exact command line and JSON artifact
  mirroring LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB.

## Notes

- discovered-from: LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB (which superseded LP-0MVK0E8NH007XCV3).
- The AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E remains unmet until this item closes.
- Do not "fix" a non-zero `prefix_mismatch`/`expired` if one appears — those
  guard outcomes are the *success* signal that the seed path runs past lookup
  (LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3); if they dominate, reopen the guard question with
  counts.

# Validate writer-side sidecar pairing fix — >=24 h post-deploy window (earliest = deploy + 24 h)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a >=24 h post-deploy window proving the fixed
snapshot/sidecar directory pairing makes the restored-prefix credit fire, so
AC3 of LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ (and AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E) can be answered
with real numbers instead of the pre-fix 0 found / 0 restored baseline.

## Scheduling (read first — every implement OR audit attempt)

**Status: deferred until the fix is actually deployed. The deploy is NOT tied to
a ship/release.** Producer decision (2026-10-31T11:20Z): the proxy restart is a
standalone operator action; do not wait for `/skill:ship`. The `Map` assignee is
the scheduling hold and stays until a restart is observed.

**Mandatory preflight — do this before claiming, before any phase, on every
implement or audit attempt:**

1. Find the production proxy and its start time:
   `ps -eo pid,lstart,cmd | grep 'uvicorn proxy.server:app' | grep ':8000'`
   The live proxy runs from `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy`; the
   `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.<ts>` rotation name records the restart
   instant.
2. Confirm the fix is in the deployed tree: the restart must post-date
   **2026-10-31T06:18:04Z** (commit `5c0f80f9`, on `dev`), and the main checkout
   must contain it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 5c0f80f9 HEAD`).
3. Decide:
   - **No restart since the fix** -> record a one-line comment with the current
     proxy start time, leave the item open with the scheduling hold, and
     **stop**. Do not claim, do not measure. (Wait again.)
   - **Restarted, but < 24 h ago** -> record the restart time and the earliest
     valid measurement time (restart + 24 h) in a comment, keep the hold, and
     stop.
   - **Restarted >= 24 h ago with the fix in the tree** -> proceed with the
     measurement (clear the scheduling hold when claiming).

## Background

The pre-fix measurement (LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB, 2026-10-29T12:58:32Z ..
2026-10-30T12:58:32Z) found 605 `missing_sidecar` seeds, 0 `found`, 0
`cache_state=restored` dispatches. LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ identified the cause:
llama-server writes `<--slot-save-path>/<basename>` (it rejects subdirectories)
while the proxy wrote the `.ratio.json` sidecar and checked restore under
`<root>/{host}-{port}/`. The fix makes save/restore/sidecar/seed all use the
shared root (an eviction save with no recorded prefix still saves its snapshot
but writes no sidecar, as documented in LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC).

Evidence for the pre-fix state:
`docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md`,
`docs/dev/slot-sidecar-attribution-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.json`,
`docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-30.md`.

## Procedure

1. Confirm the deployed tree contains the fix commit (`git log -1 dev`);
   confirm no proxy restart inside the window (a restart resets in-memory
   ratios; note it if it happens).
2. Run the measurement tool over the post-deploy window and an equal-length
   pre-deploy window, with pinned timestamps:

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py \
     --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
     --slot-cache-dir /home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache \
     --window "post-fix=<deploy>,<deploy+24h>" \
     --window "pre-fix=<deploy-24h>,<deploy>" \
     --json > docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-<date>.json
   ```

3. Attribute any remaining `missing_sidecar` seeds:

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py \
     --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
     --window "<deploy>,<deploy+24h>" --json
   ```

4. On-disk pairing: every `slot_*.bin` must have its `.ratio.json` in the same
   directory; no orphan growth for snapshots saved after the deploy:

   ```bash
   cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache
   echo "snapshots=$(find . -name '*.bin' | wc -l) sidecars=$(find . -name '*.bin.ratio.json' | wc -l)"
   find . -name '*.bin' -exec basename {} \; | sed 's/\.bin$//' | sort > /tmp/snaps
   find . -name '*.bin.ratio.json' -exec basename {} \; | sed 's/\.bin\.ratio\.json$//' | sort > /tmp/sides
   comm -13 /tmp/snaps /tmp/sides | wc -l   # orphan sidecars
   comm -23 /tmp/snaps /tmp/sides | wc -l   # orphan snapshots
   ```

5. State restored-vs-cold `dispatch_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 in the same context
   bucket, with sample counts.
6. Write the report under `docs/dev/` with the exact commands and JSON
   artifact, and link it from LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ and LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
7. If restored dispatches are still zero, say so honestly, explain the
   outcome counts, and file a follow-up instead of claiming success.

## Expected post-fix signature

- `slot_ratio_seed outcome=found` > 0 and `slot_ratio_restored` events > 0.
- `cache_state=restored` dispatches > 0.
- `missing_sidecar` near 0 for sessions saved after the deploy; any residual
  should be attributable with `scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py` (an
  eviction save with no recorded prefix still produces an unpaired snapshot).
- `missing_snapshot` may appear for legacy orphan sidecars until
  retirement/`scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` clears them.
- `prefix_mismatch` / `expired` become *possible*: a non-zero count is the
  success signal that the guard now runs; do not "fix" it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A post-deploy window of >=24 h contains more than zero `cache_state=restored` dispatches and more than zero `slot_ratio_seed outcome=found` events, with exact counts stated.
- On-disk pairing at report time shows paired files in the same directory and no orphan growth for snapshots saved after the deploy, with counts.
- `missing_sidecar` counts for the window are stated and are ~0 for post-deploy sessions; any residual is attributed with the raw counts.
- `dispatch_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 for restored dispatches are stated against cold dispatches in the same context bucket, with sample counts for both groups.
- A written report with the exact command line and a JSON artifact is added under `docs/dev/` and linked from LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ and LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
- If restored dispatches are still zero, the verdict says so honestly, explains the outcome counts, and files a follow-up item instead of claiming success.

## Risks / notes

- Snapshot-bearing traffic is thin (617 seed decisions in the pre-fix 24 h); if
  the post-deploy window yields too few restored samples, extend it rather
  than concluding early.
- Legacy orphan sidecars in `{host}-{port}/` predate the fix; the success
  signal is no orphan growth for **sessions saved after the deploy**, not an
  absolute zero.
- Do not credit local-prefill movement to this path unless `found`/`restored`
  are non-zero.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ (writer-side sidecar pairing fix)
- covers AC3 of LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ
- answers AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E
- validates: the fix committed by LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ
- baseline: `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md`,
  `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-attribution-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.json`

## Key Files

- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — windows, `cache_state` tables, bucket pairs, `seed_outcomes`.
- `scripts/attribute_missing_sidecar.py` — per-write-path `missing_sidecar` attribution.
- `docs/dev/slot-sidecar-pairing-fix-LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ.md` — the fix + pre-fix evidence.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy` — source logs.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache` — snapshot/sidecar inventory.

data.description:
discovered-from:LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0

## Summary

`implement.py finish` Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout's local `dev`
to the new commit specifically so the dev-push pre-push hook — which runs
`run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"` from
the main checkout — measures the **pushed** tree. When that fast-forward is
**refused** (`local_dev_fast_forward.method = "refused"`,
`reason = "commit_not_based_on_remote_tip"`, because local `dev` moved since
the worktree base), the hook instead runs the suite at the main checkout's
**stale** HEAD.

Consequence: the push is gated on a tree that does not contain the pushed
changes, and no full-suite cache entry is produced for the pushed commit. The
post-push read-only verification (`run_tests.py --summary --suite all`) then
reports `missing`. A red commit can reach `dev` and stay unverified until the
ship release gate re-runs the merged `dev`→`main` tree.

## Evidence (LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0, 2026-10-31)

- Finish pushed commit `ac8dc504`; `steps.local_dev_fast_forward` =
  `{"method": "refused", "reason": "commit_not_based_on_remote_tip",
  "local_tip": "0c5276fc...", "remote_tip": "0c5276fc..."}`.
- The push phase (pre-push guard verify `00:20:52` → pre-removal verify
  `00:21:20`) took ~28 s, while the full suite takes ~382 s — so the hook
  cannot have executed a fresh full suite.
- No `.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt` entry contains the new test file
  `proxy/tests/test_health_probe_router_slots.py`, proving no hook run
  measured the pushed tree.
- `python3 run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` immediately after the
  push returned `scopes.all = "missing"`.
- Contrast: concurrent finishes whose fast-forward succeeded produced fresh
  full-suite cache entries (e.g. `00:20:05`, 6773 passed) — i.e. the gate works
  when the fast-forward lands.

## Impact

Medium. The dev-push integration gate silently loses its purpose in exactly
the concurrent-advance scenario it runs in most often, so failures are deferred
to release time instead of blocking the push.

## Proposed fix (confirm at intake)

1. Gate on the pushed SHA: the hook already receives `local_sha`; run the suite
   against a temporary worktree/checkout of that SHA (or add a
   `run_tests.py --git-state-ref <sha>` mode that fingerprints and tests the
   pushed commit rather than the project-root HEAD).
2. Or, when the fast-forward is refused, have `implement.py finish` run the
   full suite in the worktree explicitly before pushing.
3. Or refuse to push when the main checkout cannot be advanced to the pushed
   commit, so the gate can never measure a stale tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — A test proves the dev-push gate tests the pushed commit when the
  main checkout's local `dev` cannot be fast-forwarded (stale/local-diverged
  scenario).
- **AC2** — After a push whose fast-forward was refused, a green full-suite
  cache entry exists for the pushed commit (no `missing` from
  `run_tests.py --summary`).
- **AC3** — Docs for the dev-push gate (`docs/dev/git-hooks.md`,
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) describe the stale-checkout
  behaviour and the fix.

# slots_500_triage.py crashes on any /slots 503 response

**Discovered from:** LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12 (AC1 static audit of `/slots` 400 call paths) — the audit could not use the documented measurement command. **Blocks:** LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8 (fresh 24 h router-responder `400 == 0` verification window), whose AC4 evidence is the responder split this tool produces.

## Problem

`scripts/slots_500_triage.py` aborts on **any** `/slots` response whose status code is not one of the three it pre-seeds in `stats`:

```
$ python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --summary
error: analysis failed: 'slots_503'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "scripts/slots_500_triage.py", line 118, in analyze_slots_500
    stats[f"slots_{status}"] += 1
KeyError: 'slots_503'
```

`stats` is a fixed-key dict (`slots_200`, `slots_400`, `slots_500`, …), but the parser feeds it **every** status the access log reports. `llama-server.1.log`, `.2.log` and `.3.log` currently contain child-responder `/slots … 503` lines (4 in total), so the documented full-corpus invocation fails today. Same risk for any future 502/429/unparseable status.

## Why it matters

- The AC4 verification for the parent epic (LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8) and the existing F3 triage workflow (`docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`) both rely on this script, and its `--log-dir` corpus mode is the documented form.
- A crash is worse than a wrong number: the tool exits 1 before emitting the microsecond-fast responder split, so a verification window can neither confirm `router-400 == 0` nor bound a residual class.
- Workaround used by the audit (read-only and **not** committed): an inline reimplementation of the same `_ACCESS_RE` responder split. That is not an acceptable long-term substitute for a repo script.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No crash on unexpected statuses.** `analyze_slots_500` tolerates **any** status code on a `GET /slots` line (503, 502, 429, unparsed/`"?"`): the per-status counters and the `slots_status[(responder, status)]` split are populated without a `KeyError`. A regression test drives a log fixture containing a `503` router line and a `503` child line through `analyze_slots_500` and asserts the payload is produced with those counts (no exception).
- [ ] **AC2 — Counters are not a closed set.** The `stats`/`slots_*` accumulation uses `Counter`/`defaultdict`-style defaults (or an explicit guard) so a future status code cannot crash the tool; the tool must not silently drop an unexpected status either — it is reported in the JSON under the responder split.
- [ ] **AC3 — Documented invocation works on the live corpus.** `python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --summary` exits 0 today and reports the child-503 events; record the run output (or the equivalent fixture-backed evidence) as a comment.
- [ ] **AC4 — Existing behaviour preserved.** The 200/400/500 counts, the 500 proximate-cause classification and the `--json`/`--compact`/`--summary` shapes are unchanged for logs without unexpected statuses (assert against an existing fixture so the F3 numbers in `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` remain reproducible).
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests + docs.** `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py` covers AC1-AC4; `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` notes that the responder split counts *every* status code (so 503/502 appear rather than aborting the run).

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — `analyze_slots_500` (`stats[f"slots_{status}"] += 1`, ~line 118) and the `stats`/`per_file_slots` initialisers at the top of the function
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py` — existing tests for this tool (extend, do not duplicate)
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` — responder-split documentation (per-file method section)

## Notes

- Reproduce with the current live corpus: `python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --summary`.
- Do not change the `_ACCESS_RE` responder classification (`router` = no `[pid]` prefix, otherwise the child pid) — the AC1 uphill audit and slice 6 both depend on it.
