# Coordinate restart-free 24 h measurement windows across concurrent verification items

**Headline:** Multiple open verification items each need a restart-free ≥24 h production
window, but every deploy/manual restart invalidates all concurrent windows. Chosen
mechanism: **A — a shared measurement calendar** (process record under `docs/dev/`),
scoped to future measurement items, plus attribution of the unattributed 2026-10-31
manual restart #2.

## Problem statement

Several open work items each require a **restart-free 24 h** production window, but a
proxy restart resets the in-process residency/lease state those windows measure — and
every deploy restarts the proxy. Restarts therefore invalidate *each other's* windows,
and each invalidation costs a full re-arm plus (often) a wasted dispatched session. One
restart-free 24 h window should serve every open measurement whose code is already
loaded, instead of one re-arm per item and restart-churn between them.

Observed on 2026-10-31 alone, inside re-arm #3's window of `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K`
(`2026-10-30T10:36:00Z → 2026-10-31T10:36:00Z`):

| # | Restart (UTC) | New pid | Attribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-10-30T23:10:49Z | 3797968 | `LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK deploy post-deadline re-dispatch fix (5b35dd80) — 24h measurement anchor` |
| 2 | 2026-10-31T00:37:53Z | 3938219 | `source=manual actor=unknown reason=manual` |
| 3 | 2026-10-31T00:41:57Z | 3944027 | `/health probe fix deploy (LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0, commit ac8dc504) — per LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6 deploy evidence` |

Restart #1 was another measurement item's own deploy anchor; #2 and #3 were unattributed
manual restarts four minutes apart. **Attribution established at intake:** restart #3's
pid (3944027) matches the deploy evidence recorded in `LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6` (commit
ac8dc504, /health probe fix) — only **restart #2** (pid 3938219) remains unattributed.

**State refreshed at intake (2026-11-02T03:30Z):** several windows quoted in the original
description have since expired or been superseded:

- `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` — re-arm #4 window `2026-10-31T00:42Z → 2026-11-01T00:42Z` (expired; re-arm needed)
- `LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK` — **completed** (post-deadline re-dispatch fix measured)
- `LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q` — writer-side sidecar pairing fix: deferred until fix deployed; `earliest = deploy + 24 h`
- `LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6` — window `2026-11-01T00:41:55Z → 2026-11-02T00:41:55Z` (expired)
- `LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57` — window `2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z` (expired, superseded)

**New in-flight windows** (post-dating the item): `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1` (release-lag fix,
run-not-before 2026-11-02T07:00Z, in-progress), and re-arm/measure items
`LP-0MVVXGMRN007NCJP` (blocked), `LP-0MVW8S74G004MFAQ`, `LP-0MVX157ZF007QJSU`. The
coordination problem is ongoing; the calendar (AC1) must be populated from the live
worklog at implementation time.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / verification dispatcher (herdr downtime worker)** — wants to arm a
  window once and have it serve all waiting measurements, not invalidate each other.
- **Verification agents running 24 h measurements** — want a stable, ownable window they
  can cite; a restart mid-window currently costs a re-arm and a wasted dispatch.

Example user story: "As the downtime dispatcher, I want one shared record of open
measurement windows so that deploying verification item A does not silently invalidate
verification item B's already armed 24 h window."

## Desired change — mechanism A: shared measurement calendar (chosen by producer)

A single "measurement window" record — a file under `docs/dev/` (candidate:
`docs/dev/measurement-windows.md`, or the existing `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` if it is the natural home) —
listing:

- every **open 24 h measurement item** (id, title, owner item),
- its **required deploy commit(s)** (fix commit + deploy evidence),
- the **current restart-free window** each one expects (anchor timestamp + end),
- a **batched-deploy convention**: new deploys land *before* a window opens, never inside one,
- a **manual-restart investigation convention**: unattributed `source=manual actor=unknown`
  restarts are investigated (per AC3) rather than ignored.

This is a **process/record mechanism, no code change** — the calendar makes windows
visible and batching the norm, so a restart during an open window is either avoided or
visibly recorded as invalidating the named items listed in the calendar. The interval
between app-wide deploys is the shared restart-free window.

**Future-only scope (producer decision):** expired/stale windows (re-arm needs) are
handled by their owning items' re-arm cycles, which should reference this calendar as
the coordination record. This item does **not** re-arm expired windows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1. A shared measurement calendar exists (file under `docs/dev/`) enumerating the
  currently open 24 h measurement items, their required deploy commits, and the
  restart-free window each currently expects — populated from the live worklog, not the
  stale 2026-10-31 list.
- AC2. The calendar mechanism is documented with a batching convention (deploys land
  before a window opens, never inside one) and a manual-restart investigation convention,
  so that a restart during an open window is either avoided or visibly recorded as
  invalidating the named items.
- AC3. The unattributed `manual` restart of 2026-10-31T00:37:53Z (pid 3938219) is
  investigated against proxy log archives / herdr logs around that timestamp; the cause
  (operator action, tooling, or incident) is recorded — or, if no evidence exists, the
  outcome "cannot be attributed with available evidence" is recorded. (Restarts #1 and #3
  are already attributed.)
- AC4. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- AC5. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README, relevant wiki/docs
  entries).

## Constraints

- Read-only with respect to the proxy's scheduling behaviour; no knob re-tuning.
- Must not weaken the existing AC2 rule on measurement items: a restart inside a window
  still invalidates that window (this item reduces the *frequency*; it does not license
  measuring across a restart).

## Existing state

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — supports `--restart`, `--reason "<text>"`, `--log-file`;
  no measurement-window awareness today. Manual restarts without `--reason` log
  `source=manual actor=unknown reason=manual`.
- Restart attribution is parsed from `proxy.log` lines (`Proxy restart attribution:
  source=... actor=... reason=...`) by `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`.
- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` exists (empty `entries: []`) — a possible machine-readable
  companion to the calendar, but not required by mechanism A.
- Prior art: `LP-0MVQ4WYOM006BLRE` (Preflight attestation and restart-free window
  certification, completed) and `LP-0MVT2QYXI0025U6C` (re-arm chore) — window-coordination
  precedents.

## Key Files:

- `docs/dev/measurement-windows.md` — **new** calendar file (AC1/AC2 home), or extend
  `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` if that is the existing natural home for
  window records (decide at implementation; the item's brief favours a dedicated file).
- `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` — measurement-window conventions used by the
  24 h items; cross-reference the calendar.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — restart-attribution parsing
  reused for AC3 investigation.
- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` — optional machine-readable mirror of the calendar.
- Live data for AC1 population: `wl search "24 h window" / "post-deploy"` — the open
  verification items (see Related work).

## Related work

- `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` (open) — 24 h AC4 resident-prefix admission verification; needs re-arm
- `LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q` (open, deferred) — writer-side sidecar pairing ≥24 h window
- `LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6` (in-progress) — router:500 == 0 over 24 h after /health fix
- `LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57` (open) — router:500 == 0 over 24 h after child-port fix
- `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1` (in-progress) — release-lag fix window closing 2026-11-02T07:00Z
- `LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK` (completed) — post-deadline re-dispatch ≥24 h window (restart #1 attribution)
- `LP-0MVVXGMRN007NCJP` (blocked) — re-measure 24 h window; record AC2 disposition
- `LP-0MVQ4WYOM006BLRE` (completed) — preflight attestation / window certification prior art
- `LP-0MVT2QYXI0025U6C` (completed) — window re-arm chore precedent

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** the calendar could grow into tooling (machine-readable store,
  linting, gates). Mechanism A is deliberately process-only; record any tooling desire as
  a linked follow-up, not scope.
- **Stale state:** the original quoted windows (2026-10-31 era) have expired; AC1 must be
  populated from the live worklog at implementation time, not the description's list.
- **AC3 may be unresolvable:** restart #2's `actor=unknown` cause may not be recoverable
  from archived logs; recording "cannot be attributed with available evidence" is an
  acceptable AC3 outcome (producer-approved).
- **Assumption:** no code change to the proxy's scheduling behaviour (constraint
  honoured); mechanism A is record/process only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which mechanism (A / B / C) should be implemented for AC2?" — Answer (producer):
  "**A** — measurement calendar (process)." Source: interactive reply 2026-11-02.
  Research: reviewed `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` (no existing gate), empty
  `downtime-coordination.json`, prior-art items. B and C rejected as adding complexity
  not yet justified.
- Q2: "Should the mechanism cover future measurement items only, or also handle the
  currently expired/stale windows that need re-arming?" — Answer (producer): "**future
  only**". Source: interactive reply 2026-11-02. Expired windows are re-armed by their
  owning items' cycles.
- Q3: "Restart #2 (pid 3938219, 00:37:53Z) — attribution source?" — Answer (producer):
  "**as recommended** — search proxy log archives / herdr logs around 00:37:53Z; if
  unresolvable record 'cannot be attributed with available evidence'." Source:
  interactive reply 2026-11-02. (Restarts #1 and #3 already attributed at intake:
  LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK deploy and /health probe fix deploy respectively.)

## Goal

**As an** operator running unattended `local-preferred` (pin-local) herdr workers,
**I want** the local prefill-thrash cooldown to expire in ~2 minutes instead of 10,
**so that** a single measured cold-prefix abort costs a pinned session a short retry
window rather than a ten-minute `429 Local admission refused` lockout, while
keeping the measured-cache early abort (F3, `LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN`) fully in force.

Operator decision 2026-10-31: this is the approved **interim** mitigation (of the
three options put to the operator, option B — the config-only change; option "A"
raising `local_measured_cache_abort_bound_tokens` / disabling the abort was
rejected because a 23-34 k prompt would then pay a 62-200 s prefill against a
120 s deadline, restoring the deadline-eviction thrash F3 exists to prevent, and
option "C" dropping the `local-preferred` pin was rejected because it cannot help
in the 06:00-10:00 UTC remote hole — see `LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135` and the new
structural-unavailability item).

discovered-from:LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135 (the defect that keeps the abort armed),
discovered-from:LP-0MVR7HJD0007RFEM (Option D / measured-cache abort epic).

## Observed incident (2026-10-31, herdr session `herdr-1793416360-4155786-6690`)

Diagnosis via the `proxy-log-skill`. The pane was dispatched pinned
(`X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`, `preference=local-preferred` on every
proxy line). Over 7 h 47 m it produced **~15 local turns and 113 refusals**
(100 x `429 Local admission refused`, plus `503`s). Refusal reasons for this one
session today:

| reason | count |
|---|---|
| `local_provider_cooldown` | 83 |
| `local_route_unavailable` | 13 |
| `prefill_thrash_cooldown` | 11 |
| `local_lease_active` | 5 |
| `eta_exceeds_budget` | 1 |

Every refusal cycle began with one abort that armed the cooldown:

```
08:16:32  measured_cache_abort session=herdr-1793416360-... total=23164 cache=0
          measured_new_tokens=23164 priced_new_tokens=2198 deficit_ratio=1.0
          bound_tokens=2000 elapsed_s=0.1 → cancelling local dispatch early
08:16:32  prefill_thrash_cooldown_started session=... cooldown_s=600
08:16:32  local_eviction ... reason=lease_evicted
… then, for the next 600 s, every retry:
          local_only_refused reason=local_provider_cooldown preference=local-preferred
          verdict=deferrable ... route=refused
          local_preference_resolved ... outcome=pinned
```

The session then sat in a 600 s refusal window, retrying roughly once a minute,
and was released only when the cooldown lapsed and the slot happened to still
hold its prefix (`07:07`, `10:57-10:58` produced the real turns).

Scope of the problem: **330 `measured_cache_abort` events across 28 sessions**
today, **249 of them at `deficit_ratio=1.0`** (cache entirely gone). Per hour:
05 h 82, 10 h 62, 04 h 51, 09 h 34, 07 h 31, 08 h 28. At 600 s per abort this is
the dominant source of pinned-client refusals on this host.

## Why 600 s is the wrong value here — and why this is a config change, not a rewrite

`local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` is documented in `proxy/config.yaml`
(~:2087-2100) as the quarantine armed after a measured-cache-deficit abort. Its
intent is to stop a session thrashing the GPU with repeated cold prefill attempts.
But a cold-prefix abort costs ~0.1 s (the abort fires on the first
`prompt_progress` event), while the cooldown it arms costs 600 s of *client*
downtime — a 6000x asymmetry. For a pinned client, which by contract receives
`429` rather than a remote fallback, that asymmetry converts a 0.1 s GPU saving
into a 10-minute outage.

The measured recovery time for the same session shows 600 s buys nothing: after
the cooldown lapses the prefix is still cold (`cache=0` again at 08:27, 08:37,
08:48, 08:58, 09:09) — the thrash defence does not protect the cache, it only
delays the next attempt. 120 s still suppresses a genuine retry storm (the
observed client retry cadence is ~60 s) while capping the outage at two minutes.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (value).** `server.local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` is `120` in
  `proxy/config.yaml`. No other cooldown, budget, deadline or abort knob changes
  value (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`,
  `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`,
  `local_measured_cache_abort_bound_tokens: 2000`,
  `local_measured_cache_abort_min_deficit_ratio: 0.25`,
  `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: true` all unchanged), asserted by a
  config test so an accidental re-tune is caught.
- **AC2 (armed duration).** The cooldown armed by a measured-cache-deficit abort
  is driven by that key, not by a literal: a unit/integration test sets the key
  to a distinctive value (e.g. `45`) and asserts
  `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started ... cooldown_s=45`, and that the local route
  is skipped with `reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` for that duration and no
  longer. No hard-coded `600` remains anywhere in the abort/cooldown path.
- **AC3 (defence retained).** The cooldown still *starts* on every
  `measured_cache_abort` (the thrash defence is not weakened, only shortened):
  the incident replay fixture asserts exactly one
  `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started` per abort, with `cooldown_s=120` at default
  configuration.
- **AC4 (abort behaviour unchanged).** `measured_cache_abort` decisions,
  `local_eviction_after_acceptance` fields and the warm-path contract are
  untouched: the existing `measured_cache_abort`, warm-path and replay tests
  pass unmodified. `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: 0` still restores
  pre-change behaviour exactly.
- **AC5 (docs).** The `proxy/config.yaml` comment block for
  `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` and `proxy/docs/routing.md` record the
  new default, the 2026-10-31 operator decision, the 0.1 s-vs-600 s asymmetry
  rationale, and that the real repair is the benefit gate in
  `LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135`, after which this value should be re-tuned upward
  (the item must leave a note saying so, not silently imply 120 is permanent).

## Out of scope

- The benefit gate that stops the abort firing for prompts that fit the budget —
  `LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135`.
- Bounding the number of pin-local refusals / escalating to remote —
  `LP-0MVUH9PL0005PW90`.
- The 06:00-10:00 UTC `model=plan` remote hole and its client-facing error.
- Slot-prefix stability (why the prefix is cold at all).

## Key files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — `server.local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` (~:2100),
  comment block (~:2087-2100).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — thrash-cooldown arm/release helpers.
- `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` — the decision (read-only here).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Assumptions

- 120 s is long enough to suppress the observed retry storm (client cadence
  ~60 s) and short enough that a pinned client recovers without operator help.
- Shortening the cooldown does not increase abort frequency in a way that costs
  more GPU time than it saves: each abort still costs ~0.1 s and the 120 s gap
  is two client retry intervals.
data.title: Interim: cut local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds 600s -> 120s so a pinned session's cold-prefix abort costs 2 minutes, not 10

## Goal

**As an** operator running unattended workers against this proxy,
**I want** the proxy to recognise when a model's whole provider chain is blocked by
*scheduled* gates it already knows the expiry of (`available_times` windows,
usage-limit resets, quota quarantines) rather than by transient failure,
**so that** the client receives a single meaningful, retryable error that says
*what* is unavailable, *when* it comes back, and *not to retry until then* —
instead of the opaque `503 All providers exhausted` it gets today, which it
retries every ~60 s for hours.

discovered-from:LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135, discovered-from:LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN.
Operator decision 2026-10-31: we deliberately do **not** want to add an always-on
remote provider to paper over the gaps — during the scheduled windows some
requests *must* be deferred. This item makes that deferral honest and actionable
rather than appearing as a failure.

## Observed behaviour today (2026-10-31, `model=plan`)

For `model=plan` there is **no eligible remote provider between 06:00 and 10:00
UTC**: `opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2` and `opencode-go-3` all carry
`available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`
(`proxy/config.yaml:516, 574, 632`), `munitoai-free` is
`usage_limit_reset_pending` until `2026-11-01T00:02:00Z`, and
`OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` is `quota_exhausted` with `resets_in` ≈ 17 days. So local
(`local-qwen3`) is the only candidate, and every refusal in that window is a hard
failure for the client:

```
08:16:32 Skipping provider=munitoai-free: usage_limit_reset_pending
         (reset_at=2026-11-01T00:02:00Z, reset_in=56727s)
08:16:32 Skipping provider=opencode-go-3: quota_exhausted
         (effective_headroom=0.0%, resets_in=1475316s)
08:16:32 Skipping provider=opencode-go-2: outside its available_times window (UTC)
08:16:32 Skipping provider=opencode-go:   outside its available_times window (UTC)
08:16:32 All providers exhausted for model=v1/chat/completions;
         unavailable={'local-qwen3': 59, 'munitoai-free': 56727,
                      'opencode-go-3': 1475436}
08:16:32 Returning first provider error response instead of generic exhausted
         message for model=v1/chat/completions (status=503)
```

The victim session (`herdr-1793416360-4155786-6690`, pinned) accumulated **113
refusals** and 10 hard `503`s over 7 h 47 m, and one recurrence produced
`~30` further failures between 06:02 and 09:19 — always the same sentence, never
any indication that the earliest possible recovery was the 10:00 UTC window edge.

### Why the two existing mechanisms do not cover this

1. **`_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (`provider.py:6247`) is
   sole-cause-only.** It returns `None` unless *every* recorded attempt is
   `status == "outside_time_window"` (`provider.py:6275-6288`). In the real
   06:00-10:00 case the diagnostics also carry `usage_limit_reset` /
   `quota_exhausted`, so the window-specific body never fires and the client
   falls through to the generic `all_exhausted` 503. The mixed-but-fully-planned
   case — the actual shape of every occurrence — is unhandled.
2. **`_compute_retry_after` (`provider.py:4608`) takes the MAX of its
   candidates** and includes every entry in the process-wide `_usage_reset_at`
   map. In the observed case the maximum is `opencode-go-3`'s 1 475 436 s
   (17 days), so the advertised wait is then clamped to
   `server.max_retry_after_seconds: 3600` (`config.yaml:1261`). The timer the
   client sees is therefore an artefact of the cap, not the real recovery
   instant: the honest answer was the 10:00 UTC window edge (≈ 3 h 44 m away),
   and for a `munitoai-free`-only case at 08:16 it was 16 h away while the client
   was told 3600 s.

Net effect: no `code`, `detail`, or `retry_at` distinguishes *"the fleet is
scheduled off and returns at 10:00 UTC"* from *"everything failed just now"*.
Both are `503 all_exhausted` with a cap-derived `Retry-After`.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (classification).** A new classifier separates a chain blocked
  **exclusively** by *known-until* gates from one blocked by *transient*
  failure. Known-until gate statuses are exactly: `outside_time_window`,
  `usage_limit_reset` (the reset instant is known), `quota_exhausted` (the reset
  interval is known) and `provider_budget_exhausted` (window rollover is known).
  Transient/unknown statuses are: `connection_error`, `http_error` / `HTTP <n>`,
  `empty_response`, `stream_error`, `stream_reroute`, `local_admission_reject`,
  and anything unrecognised. The new response applies **only** when every
  attempt is known-until and at least one provider was window- or reset-blocked;
  a single transient attempt keeps today's behaviour byte-identically.
- **AC2 (honest recovery instant).** The response advertises the **earliest**
  instant *any* entry in the chain becomes eligible — the minimum over window
  edges and known resets — not the maximum. Unit rows:
  (a) the 2026-10-31 08:16 chain ⇒ `retry_at` is the next `10:00` UTC window
  edge, not `now + 3600 s`, and not the 17-day quota reset;
  (b) `munitoai-free`-only at 08:16 (reset `2026-11-01T00:02Z`) ⇒ `retry_at` is
  that reset instant;
  (c) a chain whose earliest recovery is already past ⇒ treated as available now
  (fail-open; today's behaviour, never a stale `retry_at`).
- **AC3 (cap is honest, never silent).** `Retry-After` equals the body
  `retry_after`, as every other refusal does. When the true wait exceeds
  `server.max_retry_after_seconds`, the advertised `retry_after` is capped **and**
  the body carries the untruncated `retry_at` plus an explicit truncation flag
  (e.g. `retry_after_truncated: true`), so a client can choose to sleep through
  the window instead of polling every hour. No silent cap.
- **AC4 (stable discriminator, back-compatible).** The response carries a new
  stable `code` (e.g. `no_provider_available_in_window`) plus `retryable: true`,
  and a `detail` naming the earliest reopening provider and its gate. The
  existing prose `error` field keeps a value that older clients already
  understand (today's `All providers exhausted`), so no existing client
  string-match breaks. `EXHAUSTION_CODE_TIME_WINDOW`'s existing sole-cause
  behaviour is preserved exactly.
- **AC5 (no regression).** The sole-cause window response and the generic
  `all_exhausted` / `all_slots_exhausted` / `local_admission_reject` responses
  are unchanged for their existing triggers; their contract suites
  (`proxy/tests/test_admission_refusal_retry_contract.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`) pass unmodified.
- **AC6 (observability — one line an operator can act on).** One log line at the
  chain end names every blocked entry, its gate class and the instant it
  reopens, plus the aggregate `retry_at`, so the condition is diagnosable without
  joining skip lines:
  `chain_planned_unavailable model=plan retry_at=2026-10-31T10:00:00Z blocked=[opencode-go:window@10:00Z, opencode-go-2:window@10:00Z, opencode-go-3:quota@<iso>, munitoai-free:usage_reset@<iso>]`.
  One line per request, not per entry, and no new per-provider vocabulary.
- **AC7 (pinned clients get this too).** A `local-preferred` request whose local
  route is refused inside a known-until window receives this response (or an
  equivalent that carries the same `retry_at`/`code`), rather than a bare
  `429 Local admission refused` with an unrelated local-capacity timer. The
  incident shape (`X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`, local refused, remote
  all window/quota blocked, 08:16 UTC) asserts the client is told `10:00Z`.
- **AC8 (fail-open).** Any unparseable window, missing reset instant, unknown
  gate status, or internal exception resolves to today's generic exhausted
  response — never to a fabricated `retry_at`. A provider with no computable
  reopening instant disqualifies the classification (falls back), it is not
  guessed.
- **AC9 (no chain-hold regression).** The chain-hold/wrapper that replays cycles
  still bounds itself by the real wait and does not spin: replaying a
  known-until-exhausted chain must not schedule its next cycle earlier than the
  advertised `retry_at` (bounded by the existing hold caps), asserted in the
  overnight-exhaustion end-to-end suite.
- **AC10 (docs).** `proxy/docs/routing.md` and the `available_times` comment
  block in `proxy/config.yaml` document the classification, the earliest-instant
  rule, the truncation flag, and the operator decision that scheduled gaps are
  deferred-and-reported rather than papered over with a permanent remote
  provider.

## Out of scope

- Adding or re-timing any provider's `available_times` so the gaps disappear —
  explicitly rejected by the operator on 2026-10-31.
- Making a pinned client fall through to remote, or capping how many refusals it
  may accumulate (`LP-0MVUH9PL0005PW90`).
- The measured-cache abort / thrash cooldown (`LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135`,
  `LP-0MVWC8JCG007GAPW`).
- The body/header surface owned by `LP-0MVSS435600370D6` (capacity verdict on the
  admission-reject payload) — this item must compose with it, not replace it.

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_exhausted_response` (:6126),
  `_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (:6247, the sole-cause gate at
  :6275-6288), `_compute_retry_after` (:4608), `_refusal_retry_timing` (:4830),
  `_budget_window_retry_after` (:4660), `_seconds_until_next_window`,
  `_record_quarantine_attempts`, `_providers_outside_window`,
  `EXHAUSTION_CODE_*` (:6006-6010), the chain-end call sites (:12236, :14535).
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — canonical reason vocabulary (:113).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `max_retry_after_seconds` (:1261), the `available_times`
  comment block (:505-516).
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_refusal_retry_contract.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`.

## Assumptions

- Window edges and usage-limit resets are the *only* known-until gates whose
  expiry this proxy can compute reliably; anything else must fail open (AC8).
- Advertising a long `retry_at` (hours) is safe for existing clients: they either
  honour `Retry-After` (bounded by the existing cap) or ignore it as today.
- The earliest-instant rule is the right semantics for a *client* even though the
  chain-hold wrapper benefits from the conservative maximum; the two are kept
  separate (AC9), not merged into one number.
## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| New response shape breaks older clients that hard-match `503 All providers exhausted` | The prose `error` field retains the existing string (AC4); new fields are additive only. |
| The earliest-instant rule could expose a short-lived recovery (seconds) that the chain-hold wrapper would spin on | AC9 asserts the hold wrapper stays bounded by the advertised `retry_at` (existing cap logic untouched). |
| A provider with a partially-parsed window could misclassify the chain | AC8 fail-open: any unparseable/missing data disqualifies the classification. |
| `Retry-After` cap truncation could still cause retries after the cap expires | The body `retry_after_truncated: true` flag lets clients choose a longer sleep. |
| Scope creep into pinned-client refusal handling (AC7) | Scoped to error vocabulary only; the 3-refusal bound stays in LP-0MVUH9PL0005PW90. |

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (incident evidence,
operator decision 2026-10-31) sufficed to draft this brief. Checks performed
instead of asking:

- Q: has this classification/earliest-instant rule been proposed before?
  Answered by `wl search` — the closest completed items
  (LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4 max-based `retry_after`, LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G exhaustion
  `code`, LP-0MU56ZFII004L7OO sole-cause window 503) predate it and are the
  mechanisms this item corrects/extends; no item covers the mixed known-until
  chain. Duplicate check performed — no overlapping item found.
- Q: is a permanently-on remote provider acceptable to cover the scheduled gap?
  Answered by the operator directly on 2026-10-31: no — gaps are
  deferred-and-reported, not papered over.
- Q: which recovery instant should a client trust? Answered by the incident
  evidence — the earliest instant any chain entry reopens (AC2); the
  conservative maximum stays with the chain-hold wrapper (AC9).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF0N9SA0071LWM** – Chain-hold on budget-window exhaustion: hold for the free-tier 60s window rollover, not 0s (completed)
- **LP-0MU56ZFII004L7OO** – Exhaustion: emit time-window-specific 503 only when every provider was window-skipped (completed)
- **LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08** – Chain-hold: bound hold duration by the real retry_after (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 00z, 0mvuh9pl0005pw90, abort, ac1, ac2 (+358 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 0mvwbd91z004u135, 0mvwc8jcg007gapw, abort, ac1, ac2 (+350 more)
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: 0mvr7in0o000dpxn, 0mvss435600370d6, 0mvwbd91z004u135, 0mvwc8jcg007gapw, abort (+343 more)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-02 — `plan` skill (herdr-downtime dispatch): decomposed into 7 children in test-first dependency order (see completion comment); added dependency edges test→impl and impl→dependent impls/docs; ran the six automated review stages (no changes were required to intent; AC-T2/AC10a rewritten to restate parent AC2/AC10 near-verbatim so the coverage matcher recognises them); AC coverage review = proceed (100% covered), stage advanced to `plan_complete` by `apply_coverage_review`.

## Goal

**As** the implementer of the measured-cache benefit gate, **I want** the
decision-level rows for the gate written and failing first, **so that** the
gate's continue/abort verdicts, its comparator budget and its input provenance
are pinned before any production code changes.

Parent AC1, AC10, and the unit half of AC6. **Test-first**: this item precedes
the decision implementation (the `[impl]` benefit-gate item depends on it).

## Scope

Add the benefit-gate rows to `proxy/tests/test_measured_prefill_abort_decision.py`
(split into a sibling module only if that file becomes uncomfortable to read).
Every row **names its rate basis** in its docstring/assertion message (parent
AC1), so a future recalibration that re-breaks the incident fails loudly rather
than silently.

Determinism: clear/seed the rolling calibration through `proxy.prefill_eta.reset()`
and synthetic observed samples (the `_seed_varied` pattern in
`proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py`). The "shipped default fit" row
relies on the **uncalibrated** default `DEFAULT_PREFILL_MS_PER_TOKEN = 3.9`
(14 380 × 3.9 ms = 56.08 s), so it needs no seeded window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — incident row (parent AC1(a); D2 → `abort=False`).**
  `total=14380 cache=0 priced_new_tokens=48`, shipped config (uncalibrated
  default fit) ⇒ `abort=False`, `detail="within_eta_budget"`,
  `measured_eta_s ≈ 56.1` (±0.5 s), `budget_s == 114.0`. The docstring records
  the measured host range (38.8 s at 371 tok/s … 84.6 s at 170 tok/s) and an
  accompanying assertion shows the row still continues at the p25 rate
  (84.6 s < 114 s).
- **AC2 — huge-prompt row (parent AC1(b)).** `total=56000 cache=0
  priced_new_tokens≈100` (seeded so the p75 uplift applies) ⇒ `abort=True`,
  `detail="deficit_over_bound"` — today's behaviour preserved for the
  population the feature exists for. Both the shipped default fit (218.4 s)
  and the measured median (150.9 s) are recorded in the test and both exceed
  the 114 s comparator.
- **AC3 — the comparator is the prefill-deadline budget (D1).** Three rows:
  (i) `budget_safety_fraction=0` ⇒ `budget_s == local_prefill_deadline_seconds`
  (120 s) and the AC1 row still continues; (ii) a deadline tuned low enough to
  make the incident prompt exceed the comparator (e.g.
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 40` ⇒ 38 s) ⇒ `abort=True`, proving the
  comparator is deadline-derived; (iii) the admission wait budget never decides
  the verdict — with `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30` (and a
  `budget_seconds=30`-shaped admission evidence) the AC1 row still continues.
- **AC4 — gate input provenance (parent AC10).** With `priced_new_tokens=48`
  and `total=14380 cache=0`, `measured_eta_s >= 30` (the measured-rate floor),
  never ≈8 s; a companion assertion feeds `48` as though it were the measured
  deficit and asserts both `measured_eta_s` and the verdict change — so the
  optimism inversion that caused the incident cannot be reintroduced through
  the gate's input.
- **AC5 — fail-open on a missing budget (parent AC6).** Absent, `0`, negative,
  non-numeric or otherwise unreadable `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` /
  `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction`, a non-mapping config, and an
  unusable ETA estimator each resolve to `abort=False` with a `detail` that is
  **not** `deficit_over_bound`; a missing budget never manufactures an abort.
- **AC6 — existing decision rows unchanged.** Every pre-existing row in
  `test_measured_prefill_abort_decision.py` (warm path, ratio floor,
  monotonicity, `enabled` spellings, malformed config, never-raises) passes;
  only rows whose expectation the gate genuinely changes may be updated, and
  each such update carries an inline comment explaining why.
- **AC7 — the changed-scope test gate is green** (`/skill:test`, changed
  scope).

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_measured_prefill_abort_decision.py` — the decision rows.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` — calibration seeding/reset
  pattern to reuse.
- `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` — module under test.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `estimate_prefill_seconds` (`~893`),
  `_deadline_budget_seconds` (`~1293`), `DEFAULT_PREFILL_MS_PER_TOKEN` (`162`).

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the decision implementation.

## Deliverables

Decision tests that fail on today's code and encode the AC1(a)/AC1(b)/AC10/
AC6 verdicts, ready to be turned green by the implementation item.

data.description:
## Goal

**As** an operator running pinned `local-preferred` workers, **I want**
`decide_measured_cache_abort()` to abort only when the measured cold prefill
genuinely cannot complete inside the request's own prefill-deadline budget,
**so that** a mid-size prompt that fits the budget is never cancelled into a
600 s thrash cooldown and an endless `429 Local admission refused` loop.

Parent AC1, AC5 (continue detail), AC6, AC10. **Test-first**: the decision rows
item is written first and this item turns it green.

## Scope

Add a third, **benefit** gate to the decision, evaluated *after* the existing
ratio floor and token bound (both keep their current semantics):

1. price the **measured** deficit `measured_new = total - cache` with
   `proxy.prefill_eta.estimate_prefill_seconds(model, measured_new,
   cached_ratio=0.0, config=...)` — the same call the admission guard makes,
   including its configured conservative p75 uplift for prompts ≥
   `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens` (D3 (a)). Never price it
   from the admission-priced `new_tokens`;
2. compare that ETA against the comparator budget
   `budget_safety_fraction × local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (114 s shipped),
   falling back to `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` when the fraction is `0`
   (D1 (a)). The admission wait budget (`budget_seconds`, 60 s) is **not** the
   comparator;
3. `abort=True` only when `measured_eta_s > budget_s`; otherwise `abort=False`
   with `detail="within_eta_budget"` (D2 (a) — no extra margin test beyond the
   comparator's own 5 % safety fraction).

`AbortSettings` gains the gate's inputs — `model`, `config`/resolved budget and
an injectable ETA estimator for deterministic tests — and keeps its fail-open
construction: an unreadable deadline, fraction or estimator resolves to
*continue*, never to a more aggressive abort. `AbortDecision` gains
`measured_eta_s`, `budget_s` and the rate basis so the dispatch log line can
report why a deficit was tolerated (parent AC5). Budget resolution lives in
`proxy.prefill_eta` behind a small public helper wrapping
`_deadline_budget_seconds`, so the advertised threshold can never drift from
the enforced one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — parent AC1 restated (benefit gate: abort only when waiting cannot
  succeed).** The abort decision prices the measured deficit with the same
  calibrated prefill rate model the admission gate uses
  (`proxy.prefill_eta.estimate_prefill_seconds`) and aborts **only when that ETA
  exceeds the request's local prefill budget** — the prefill-deadline budget
  `budget_safety_fraction × local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (114 s shipped),
  falling back to `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120 s) when the fraction is
  `0`. The admission wait budget `budget_seconds` is **not** the comparator, and
  the ETA is priced from the **measured** `total - cache`, never from the
  admission-priced `new_tokens`. Enforced order: ratio floor → token bound →
  ETA budget, so an abort requires all three.
- **AC1b — vocabulary.** `DETAIL_WITHIN_ETA_BUDGET = "within_eta_budget"` is
  added alongside the existing `detail` values — one new `detail` token, no new
  reason token, no new response header, no refusal-body change.
- **AC2 — the pinned rows are green.** The incident row (`total=14380
  cache=0`) continues with `within_eta_budget`; the 56 000-token row still
  aborts with `deficit_over_bound`; the AC10 provenance row shows
  `measured_eta_s >= 30` and never ≈8 s.
- **AC3 — comparator resolution is single-sourced.** A public
  `prefill_eta` helper wraps `_deadline_budget_seconds` (fraction × deadline,
  `0` ⇒ fall back to the deadline); the admission wait budget
  (`budget_seconds` / `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) is never consulted by
  the gate.
- **AC4 — ETA provenance.** The ETA is computed from the measured deficit with
  `cached_ratio=0.0` (a deficit is by definition uncached); `priced_new_tokens`
  continues to gate only the token bound and never prices the ETA.
- **AC5 — fail-open (parent AC6).** Missing/partial/non-numeric measurement, an
  unusable priced value, an unreadable or non-positive deadline/fraction, an
  unusable estimator, an unreadable config, or any internal exception all
  resolve to *continue*; `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: 0` still restores
  pre-change behaviour exactly (no `return_progress` injection, no capture, no
  early release).
- **AC6 — never raises.** `estimate_prefill_seconds` is called inside the
  module's existing `try` so the never-raises contract is preserved even for a
  pathological config or an estimator stub that raises.
- **AC7 — warm path untouched (parent AC2).** `cache ≥ 0.99 × total` still
  returns `below_deficit_ratio_floor` **before** any ETA work; the existing warm
  and replay tests pass unmodified.
- **AC8 — the changed-scope test gate is green** (`/skill:test`, changed
  scope).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` — `decide_measured_cache_abort`,
  `AbortSettings`, `AbortDecision`, the new `within_eta_budget` detail.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `estimate_prefill_seconds` (`~893`),
  `_deadline_budget_seconds` (`~1293`), `resolve_config` (`~398`).
- `proxy/tests/test_measured_prefill_abort_decision.py` — the pinned rows.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` — existing deadline-budget
  expectations that must stay green.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the decision-rows item. Blocks the wiring item.

## Deliverables

The benefit gate in production code with a fail-open construction, the
`within_eta_budget` detail, the ETA/budget fields on the decision, and the
public comparator-budget helper — all decision rows green.

## Goal

**As** an operator, **I want** the incident shape replayed end to end in the
test suite **so that** a pin-local prompt that fits the budget is served
locally with no thrash cooldown and no `429`, while a genuinely doomed prompt
keeps today's early detour.

Parent AC3, AC4, AC8, and the integration half of AC7. **Test-first**: written
before the wiring item, which depends on it.

## Scope

Extend `proxy/tests/test_measured_cache_abort_wiring.py` (release, cooldown and
eviction assertions) and `proxy/tests/measured_prefill_window_replay.py` (the
incident fixture), reusing the `proxy/tests/prefill_thrash_replay_harness.py`
style so the replay drives the real preview/peek path rather than a mock of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — incident replay fixture (parent AC8).** A fixture built from the five
  recorded aborts (total 14 380, `cache=0`, priced 48, admission wait budget
  60 s, deadline 120 s, `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`) at default
  configuration asserts **zero** `measured_cache_abort` and **zero**
  `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started` events, and records the resulting local
  dispatch as explicit numbers — `measured_eta_s ≈ 56` (shipped fit) against
  `budget_s = 114`, with the measured range (38.8–84.6 s) in the assertion
  message — so a future tuning change that re-breaks the case fails loudly.
- **AC2 — pin-local turn served locally (parent AC4).** `local-preferred` +
  ~14 k cold prompt + admission `decision=admit` under a 60 s wait budget +
  llama-server reporting `cache=0` ⇒ `200` with `X-Local-Route: local`, zero
  `local_only_refused` lines, zero `429`s and zero `prefill_thrash_cooldown_*`
  lines.
- **AC3 — parent AC3 restated (no cooldown for a benefit-neutral abort).** An
  abort the benefit gate declines never emits `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started`;
  an abort it allows emits exactly one with `cooldown_s` from
  `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds`. Integration assertion: the AC1(a)
  request produces zero `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started` lines, AC1(b) exactly
  one. Both assertions live in the same module and drive the real
  `_record_prefill_thrash_cooldown` arming site.
- **AC4 — deadline-path contract unchanged (parent AC7).** For a gate-allowed
  abort the `local_eviction_after_acceptance` snapshot still carries `total`,
  `measured_cache`, `priced_new_tokens` and `elapsed_s`, and the request still
  detours to the remote provider — asserted by the existing tests, extended only
  where the gate changes which fixture reaches that branch.
- **AC5 — warm path (parent AC2).** A warm stream (`cache ≥ 0.99 × total`)
  still continues with no eviction and no cooldown; the existing warm-path
  replay assertions pass unmodified.
- **AC6 — the changed-scope test gate is green** (`/skill:test`, changed

## Goal

As a drive operator, I want one shared, table-driven classifier that turns a
failing `finish` report into `{kind, step, reason, message}`, so `phase_drive`
can tell a transient infrastructure refusal from a genuine gate failure instead
of treating every failure as a gate failure (parent AC1).

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts through all layers end-to-end — the `finish`
subprocess's structured `steps` payload, `phase_parent._run_finish`'s report,
and the classifier `phase_drive` consumes — with unit tests and the reference
doc's vocabulary table updated in the same slice.

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - Add module-level constants **next to the emitters** (adjacent to
    `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` / `phase_finish`):
    - `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` — frozenset of `(step, reason)` pairs (the
      allow-list from the parent item's **Assumptions**).
    - `FINISH_GATE_REFUSALS` — frozenset of `(step, reason)` pairs for the
      known gate failures (`tests: tests_failed`, `build: build_failed`,
      `worktree_placement: *`, `diff: no_changes`, …) — recorded for
      documentation/consistency only; classification of anything not in
      either set is `unknown`.
    - `FINISH_FAILURE_KINDS = ("infrastructure", "gate", "unknown")`.
  - Add `classify_finish_failure(finish_report: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]`
    returning `{kind, step, reason, message}`:
    - resolves `(step, reason)` from the report's structured `steps`
      (precedence: `main_checkout_lock` → `main_checkout_guard` →
      `local_dev_fast_forward` → `push` → `build` → `tests` →
      `ancestry_assertion`), never from prose;
    - `kind = "infrastructure"` only for an explicit allow-list hit;
      `"gate"` for an explicit gate-list hit; otherwise `"unknown"`
      (fail-safe: `unknown` is never `infrastructure`);
    - tolerates `None`, `{}` and non-dict input → `kind="unknown"`.
  - `phase_parent._run_finish`: call `_invoke_implement("finish", …, parse_on_failure=True)`
    and **keep the `None` sentinel** — `_run_finish` still returns `None` on
    failure, but records `report["finish_failure"] = classify_finish_failure(parsed)`
    on the parent report before returning.
  - Record a structured `steps` entry for the `finish` failure exits that have
    none today (the `AncestryAssertionError` handler ~6958 and the generic
    `RuntimeError` push/build/commit handlers), so classification never parses
    prose.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — new `TestFinishFailureClassifier`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — seed the "Drive failure recovery"
  classification vocabulary table (completed in the docs item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One module-level vocabulary constant, colocated with the emitters,
   enumerates every `(step, reason)` pair the shipped `finish` code can emit;
   a table-driven test asserts the `kind` mapping for each entry.
2. A `(step, reason)` pair that is not listed classifies as `unknown`, never
   `infrastructure` (table-driven test covers the fail-safe direction).
3. `classify_finish_failure(None)`, `classify_finish_failure({})` and a
   non-dict argument each return `kind="unknown"` without raising.
4. `phase_parent._run_finish` invokes `finish` with `parse_on_failure=True`,
   still returns `None` on failure (sentinel pinned by a regression test), and
   the returned parent report carries `finish_failure` with the correct
   `step`/`reason`/`kind` for a scripted failing finish report.
5. Every `finish` failure exit that previously carried no structured `steps`
   entry (ancestry assertion, generic push failure, generic `RuntimeError`)
   records `{success: false, reason}` in `steps`, so no classification path
   depends on `report["message"]` prose.
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC1 traceability.** **Single classifier for finish failures.** `phase_drive` classifies each failing `finish` as `infrastructure`, `gate` or `unknown` through one shared, table-driven classifier over an explicit `(step, reason)` vocabulary, derived from the `finish` subprocess report (threaded out of `phase_parent`'s `_run_finish`). Unit test: a table-driven test asserts the mapping for every refusal reason the shipped code can emit, and that an unlisted reason classifies as `unknown` (fail-safe, never `infrastructure`). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the three module-level constants beside `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push`
   and `phase_finish`, with a comment stating the drift rule (a new `_refuse`
   reason must be added to the table in the same commit).
2. Write the failing table-driven test first (`TestFinishFailureClassifier`),
   enumerating the emitted pairs; then implement `classify_finish_failure`.
3. Thread `parse_on_failure=True` through `_run_finish`, keeping the `None`
   sentinel and adding `report["finish_failure"]`; add the sentinel regression
   test.
4. Add the missing structured `steps` entries in `phase_finish`'s failure
   exits; assert them in a test.
5. Seed the reference doc vocabulary table.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `classify_finish_failure` (new),
  `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` / `FINISH_GATE_REFUSALS` / `FINISH_FAILURE_KINDS`
  (new), `phase_parent._run_finish` (~7558), `phase_finish` failure handlers
  (~6780–6980), `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` (~3595–3740).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `TestFinishFailureClassifier`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Drive failure recovery" table.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Vocabulary drift** — a future `_refuse` reason is added and silently
  classifies as `gate`, re-creating the discard hazard. *Mitigation:* the
  constant sits next to the emitters; the table test enumerates every emitted
  pair; `unknown` fails safe.
- **`parse_on_failure=True` alters the placement-guard path.** *Mitigation:*
  the `None` sentinel is kept and pinned by a regression test.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice; every other child consumes
`classify_finish_failure` / `finish_failure`.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC1 (primary) — the single table-driven classifier; supplies the
`finish_failure` evidence payload that AC5's reporting slice consumes.

## Notes

- **Canonical source.** Code and docs live in `~/projects/SorraAgents`
  (`skill/implement/…`, `tests/…`, `docs/dev/…`); implementation runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree for this work item's id. The installed
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` tree is a runtime copy and must **not** be
  edited — run `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing.
- **Work-item location.** This work item lives in the `llm-manager` worklog
  (where the incident's epic `LP-0MVRO3AHN002UM1Q` is tracked) while the code
  lives in SorraAgents — the same cross-repo pattern as `LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4`.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator driving an epic unattended on a contended host, I want a
transient infrastructure refusal (`local_dev_diverged`, main-checkout lock
held, push transport drop) to be retried on its **own** bounded budget with
backoff instead of consuming the finish-attempt budget, so a refusal that
clears seconds later no longer discards a committed slice (parent AC2).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `phase_drive`: classify `parent_report["finish_failure"]` on every
    `finishing_failed` report.
    - `kind == "infrastructure"` → increment `infra_retries[child]`, emit a
      `children_driven` entry with `result: "infra-retry"`, sleep the injected
      backoff, `continue` (re-run `parent`, which re-runs `finish`; **never**
      spawn a session). `finish_attempts[child]` is **not** incremented.
    - `kind in {"gate", "unknown"}` → existing bounded path unchanged.
  - New `--infra-retry-limit N` argparse flag (default `5`, non-positive
    clamped to 1) plumbed into `phase_drive` as `infra_retry_limit`.
  - New report keys: `infra_retries` (dict child → count),
    `infra_retry_limit` (int). Existing keys keep their meaning/types.
  - Backoff: `_drive_infra_backoff_delay(attempt)` → `min(2 * 2**(attempt-1), 30)`
    seconds, with an injectable delay callable (`sleep`/`delay` parameter on
    `phase_drive`, default `time.sleep`) so tests pass a zero-delay recorder.
  - `max_iterations` bound accounts for `infra_retry_limit` so the loop still
    always terminates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `--infra-retry-limit` is present in `implement.py drive --help` and in the
   usage block; the default is `5`; a non-positive value is clamped to `1`.
2. An infrastructure refusal increments `infra_retries[child]` and leaves
   `finish_attempts` without an entry for that child (test asserts both).
3. Scripted harness returning three infrastructure refusals then success ends
   with `success: true`, the child recorded as `finished`,
   `infra_retries[child] == 3`, `infra_retry_limit == 5`, and
   `finish_attempts` empty for that child.
4. Each infrastructure retry emits a `children_driven` entry with
   `result: "infra-retry"` carrying `step`, `reason` and the attempt number,
   and spawns **no** session (`sessions_spawned` unchanged).
5. Exhausting `--infra-retry-limit` does not retry unboundedly: the loop falls
   through to the existing reconcile/reset path and stops with a message naming
   the failing `step` and `reason`.
6. The backoff schedule is bounded and injectable: a unit test asserts
   `[2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30]` seconds for attempts 1–6 and that no test sleeps.
7. `max_iterations` includes the infrastructure budget, and a
   always-refusing harness terminates (test in the regression item asserts the
   exact `parent` invocation count).
8. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
9. **Parent AC2 traceability.** **Infrastructure refusals do not consume the finish-attempt budget.** They are bounded separately by a new `--infra-retry-limit` (default `5`) with a bounded backoff between attempts; a refusal that clears within that budget lets the same `finish` succeed and the chain continue. Test: a scripted harness returning N infrastructure refusals then success ends with `success: true` and the child `finished`, and `finish_attempts` does **not** count the infrastructure attempts (`infra_retries` does). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the scripted-harness test first (3 infra refusals → success) against
   the extended harness from the test-harness item; it must fail.
2. Add `--infra-retry-limit` and `infra_retry_limit` plumbing plus report keys.
3. Branch on `finish_failure["kind"]` before the `finish_attempts` increment;
   emit `infra-retry`, record the delay, `continue`.
4. Add `_drive_infra_backoff_delay` and the injectable delay hook.
5. Extend `max_iterations`.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` finish-failure branch
  (~8940–9100), `_drive_infra_backoff_delay` (new), `_emit_phase_report`
  (~8270), argparse block (~9630), usage block (~42).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — infra-retry budget tests.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — CLI-flag and loop-bound coverage.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Over-eager infrastructure classification hides a real gate failure.**
  *Mitigation:* explicit allow-list only (classifier item); `unknown` is never
  infrastructure; the budget is small and bounded; the chain still stops with
  the real reason.
- **Repeated retries re-run the changed-scope suite on a contended host.**
  *Mitigation:* default bound 5, exponential backoff capped at 30 s, no extra
  session spawn.

## Dependencies

- `Classifier: finish refusal vocabulary and threading` — supplies
  `finish_failure` / `classify_finish_failure`.
- `Test harness: refusal scripting and commit-carrying worktree` — supplies the
  scripted `finish_failure` reports and the zero-delay recorder.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC2 (primary) and AC6 (the loop bound accounts for the new budget).

As the owner of an already-committed child slice, I want drive to never
`reset --hard` a worktree that carries commits — parking the tip on a named
`refs/wip/<child-id>` instead — so my work cannot be discarded (parent AC3).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_reset_child_worktree(worktree_path, parent_branch=..., child_id="")`
    gains a **pre-destructive preservation gate** that runs after the existing
    isolation gates (linked-worktree check, `--show-toplevel` match) and
    **before** any `git reset --hard` / `git clean -fd`:
    - compute `git -C <wt> rev-list --count <parent_branch>..HEAD` (fall back
      to `merge-base --is-ancestor <parent_branch> HEAD`);
    - when the worktree is ahead of the parent branch: create
      `refs/wip/<child-id>` at `HEAD` with `git update-ref`, then return
      `{"success": False, "reset": False, "preserved_ref": "refs/wip/<child-id>",
      "preserved_commit": <tip>, "reason": …}` — no destructive command runs.
  - `phase_drive`: on a refused reset carrying `preserved_ref`, record
    `report["preserved_refs"]` (list of `{id, ref, commit}`), comment the ref +
    commit on the child, and stop the chain naming the real step/reason. No
    session is spawned for that child.
  - `_emit_phase_report` prints `preserved_refs` in the human summary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With a worktree whose `HEAD` is ahead of the parent branch,
   `_reset_child_worktree` returns `success: False`, `reset: False`,
   `preserved_ref == "refs/wip/<child-id>"` and `preserved_commit` equal to the
   worktree tip; neither `git reset --hard` nor `git clean -fd` ran.
2. `git rev-parse refs/wip/<child-id>` resolves to the tip after the refused
   reset, the original commit is still reachable from the worktree branch, and
   the ref does **not** appear in `git branch` output or `git worktree list`.
3. The preservation ref is created **before** any destructive command: a
   refused reset leaves the ref in place and the worktree byte-identical.
4. A worktree that is only uncommitted-dirty (no commits ahead) still takes the
   existing reset path and succeeds — behaviour unchanged, and the reset still
   uses `git clean -fd` **without** `-x` (ignored files such as the
   `node_modules` symlink survive; test asserts the flag).
5. `phase_drive` reports `preserved_refs` for the refused child, comments the
   `wip/<id>` ref and commit hash on the child, spawns no session for it, and
   the chain-stop message names the failing `finish` step and reason.
6. The existing isolation gates (main-checkout refusal, missing worktree,
   `--show-toplevel` mismatch) are unchanged and still covered by their current
   tests.
7. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
8. **Parent AC3 traceability.** **A worktree carrying commits is never reset.** `_reset_child_worktree` refuses when the child worktree's `HEAD` is ahead of the parent branch; the tip is preserved on `refs/wip/<child-id>` **before** any destructive git command, and the ref + commit hash are reported in the drive report and commented on the child. Test: a real in-repo git worktree fixture proves (a) ahead-of-parent → no reset, `wip/<id>` resolves to the tip, original commit still reachable from the worktree branch; (b) only-uncommitted-dirty → existing reset still happens. Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the ahead-of-parent refusal test and the uncommitted-only regression
   test first (they must fail), using the `commit_carrying_worktree` fixture.
2. Add the preservation gate between the isolation gates and the reset.
3. Thread `child_id` into `_reset_child_worktree` from `phase_drive`.
4. Record `preserved_refs`, comment on the child, extend `_emit_phase_report`.

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_reset_child_worktree` (~8148),
  `phase_drive` reset path (~9028–9095), `_emit_phase_report` (~8270).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `TestNonTerminalResetForRetry`
  (~646) extended with preservation cases.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Stale `wip/<id>` refs accumulate.** *Mitigation:* created only when a
  commit would otherwise be discarded; named in the report and the child
  comment; cleanup documented in the skill reference (docs item).
- **A ref name colliding with a real branch.** *Mitigation:* `refs/wip/<id>` is
  a fully qualified ref outside `refs/heads/`, so it never appears in `git
  branch` or worktree discovery.

## Goal

As a producer triaging a stalled drive, I want `reset-for-retry` to apply only
to a worktree that holds **no** commits, and its audit comment to name exactly
what was discarded (a file list, never a commit hash), so a retained commit is
never implied to have been thrown away and an uncommitted discard is fully
documented (parent AC4).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `phase_drive`: the `reset-for-retry` path is only reachable when
    `_reset_child_worktree` succeeded, which (after the preservation-gate item)
    implies the worktree carried no commits ahead of the parent branch. Pin that
    invariant in the code with an explicit guard/assert and in a test.
  - `_reset_for_retry_comment`: build the "discarded" section from the actual
    removed paths (`git clean -fd` output and/or `git status --porcelain=v1`
    captured before the reset), list them as a file list, and state explicitly
    that no commit was discarded. The comment must contain **no** commit hash
    token.
  - `_reset_child_worktree`: return the pre-reset `status --porcelain` paths in
    the result (`discarded_paths`) so the comment is evidence-based rather than
    inferred from `clean` stdout alone.
- Interpretation note to record on the parent: the parent item's "re-queue a
  finish-only retry rather than a session reset" is satisfied by the
  infrastructure-retry path (an infra refusal re-runs `parent` → `finish`
  against the preserved commit without spawning a session); a **gate** failure
  on a commit-carrying worktree stops the chain, because a finish-only retry
  would contradict parent AC6 (one attempt at the default bound).

1. A commit-carrying worktree whose `finish` exhausts the gate bound produces
   no `reset-for-retry` entry in `children_driven`, spawns no session, and
   reports `preserved_refs` for that child (test asserts all three).
2. `_reset_for_retry_comment` lists the discarded paths individually (one per
   line or a comma-separated list) derived from the pre-reset `git status
   --porcelain` / `git clean` output, and the comment body matches no 7–40
   character hex token that could be read as a commit hash (test asserts
   against a regex and against the preserved commit hash value).
3. When the worktree held no commits, the comment explicitly states that no
   commit was discarded, and its discarded-file list matches the files the
   reset actually removed (fixture comparison).

   continues with a fresh session.

## Goal

As a producer triaging a stalled drive, I want every drive verdict message and
child comment to name the failing `finish` step and reason — plus the
main-checkout lock holder and/or the offending paths and competing work item
when the report carries them — instead of the generic

genuine gate failure without excavating subprocess stdout (parent AC5).

    plus optional `"; lock held by <holder>"` and
    `"; offending paths: <paths>; competing work item <id> (pid <n>)"`.
  - Use it in every drive verdict:
    - `infra-retry` (report message + `children_driven` entry + child comment),
    - `reset-for-retry` (report message + child comment),
    - `terminal-reconciled` (report message + child comment),
    - chain-stop / `failed_child` messages (bound exhausted, reset refused,
      reset-then-fail-again, status-reset failure).
  - Read the evidence from the threaded `finish_failure` payload:

discovered-from:LP-0MVK6XGOF000C45C

## Summary

A local dispatch aborted by the measured cache-deficit guard
(`measured_cache_abort … reason=measured_cache_deficit`) returns the same
retryable **503** the prefill-deadline path returns. Outside the cold-start
grace window that 503 takes the generic *provider* path, so the proxy calls
`mark_provider_unavailable("local-qwen3", provider_cooldown_seconds=60)`. The
abort therefore cools the **whole `local-qwen3` entry for 60 s for every
session**, not just the session/prompt that lost the cache. With several
concurrent sessions on this host the entry cooldown is re-armed before it can
expire, so `prefer-local` work is starved of local capacity indefinitely while
the GPU sits idle.

This is a critical availability defect: it produced **0 % local utilisation**
for the interactive session and only 4 of 43 requests local overall in the
2026-10-31 12:46–12:58 window (see evidence), despite local being healthy.

## Problem statement

The cache-deficit abort is scoped (correctly) to one session + one prompt
fingerprint: `_record_prefill_thrash_cooldown(session_id, …, fingerprint=…)`
arms a per-session, per-prompt window
(`local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 600`). But the *same* abort returns a
retryable 503 into the fallback loop, and the fallback loop's HTTP-error
handling quarantines the provider **entry**:

```
2026-10-31 12:50:00 measured_cache_abort session=audit-LP-0MVK6XGOF000C45C-parent-8329aaca
    reason=measured_cache_deficit total=11375 cache=3889 measured_new_tokens=7486
```

Two independent scopes fire from one event: the per-session/prompt 600 s thrash
window (correct) and an entry-wide 60 s quarantine (the defect). The entry
quarantine is what the `Skipping provider=local-qwen3 … in cooldown` lines on
*other* sessions' requests report — 100 occurrences on 2026-10-31 alone.

Aggravating factor: each abort also records the owning slot as abandoned for
900 s (`abandoned_slot_recorded … ttl_s=900`), so
`/llama/local/status` publishes `local_abandoned_slots=2` and
`capacity_hint=abandoned_busy` while llama-server is idle. Capacity therefore
looks consumed for 15 minutes after a 1-second abort.

## Why the deficit fires at all (context, not a second defect)

The proxy prices `new_tokens` from its cached-prefix expectation
(`cached_ratio` 0.90–0.97) and llama-server then re-prefills 3–8x that
(measured_new 7,486–27,691 vs priced 999–11,230; `deficit_ratio` 0.32–1.00).
That is the documented Qwen3.x hybrid/SWA checkpoint invalidation
("forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data") combined with
three concurrent sessions interleaving on a 2-slot pool. Per `AGENTS.md` that
re-prefill is expected behaviour for this architecture, so the abort will keep
firing during contention; the fix must therefore stop it from escalating into a
cross-session local outage.

## Users

- **Primary user — any `prefer-local` agent session.** Wants local capacity when
  it is genuinely available; currently one neighbour's cache deficit removes it.

  > As an agent session routed `prefer-local`, I want a neighbour's
  > measured-cache abort to affect only that neighbour's prompt, so that my own
  > request still reaches local when the GPU is free.

- **Secondary user — the operator.** Wants local GPU utilisation to reflect real
  capacity, and wants cooldown signals to mean "local is broken", not "someone
  else's prompt missed the cache".

  > As the operator, I want `local-qwen3 in cooldown` to disappear from logs for
  > deficit aborts, so that a cooldown skip is trustworthy evidence of a real
  > local fault and `/llama/local/status` capacity reflects reality.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — no entry quarantine from a deficit abort.** A
      `measured_cache_deficit` early release no longer marks the `local-qwen3`
      provider entry unavailable: no `mark_provider_unavailable` call and no
      `local_provider_cooldown` skip token is produced by that path. Covered by
      a proxy test that drives the abort and asserts a **different** session's
      subsequent `prefer-local` request is not refused with
      `local-qwen3 in cooldown`.
- [ ] **AC2 — the aborting prompt is still refused.** The aborting session's own
      prompt is still refused for the configured
      `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` (per-session + per-prompt
      fingerprint window unchanged), asserted by the same test or a sibling one.
- [ ] **AC3 — genuine local faults keep their quarantine.** A non-deferral 5xx,

## Desired change

1. **Carry the reason on the 503, then honour it in the fallback loop.** Mark the
   deficit-originated 503 distinctly (an exception/marker plus a response
   header set by the router's error builder — `_build_backend_error_response`
   already supports headers such as `X-Session-Fallback-Reason`, so a
   `X-Local-Dispatch-Reason: measured_cache_deficit` style marker follows that
   precedent). In `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`, treat that marker like the
   cold-start case: no `mark_provider_unavailable`, no failure-counter bump, and
   return the retry hint so `Retry-After` still reaches the caller. Only the
   marked 503 is exempt; every other 5xx/connection error keeps its behaviour
   (AC3).
2. **Name the detour on the request.** In the HTTP-error branch
   (`provider.py:14253–14295`) set `fallback_reason` to the new token (rather
   than `HTTP 503`) and add it to `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS` so the
   request-level token is accepted rather than rejected as an unknown reason.
   *Interpretation recorded for AC5:* because the fix removes the *entry*
   cooldown, the distinct token belongs on the aborting request's fallback
   reason, not on a surviving `Skipping provider=… in cooldown` line. The
   implementer must also keep the aborting session's own refusal observable via
   the existing `prefill_thrash_cooldown` skip token (AC2).
3. **Release the abandoned-slot marker on the abort's own release path.** The
   deficit abort cancels the upstream stream and can resolve the slot identity
   (`_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` already receives
   `abandoned_slot_id` / `upstream_stream_cm`), so clearing (or shortening the
   TTL of) that slot's abandonment entry once the cancel is confirmed makes
   `capacity_hint` honest within seconds rather than 900 s (AC4).
4. **Document** the new semantics in `proxy/config.yaml` and
   `proxy/docs/routing.md` (AC6).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — masking genuine local faults.** Mitigation: restrict the exemption to
  the deficit-originated 503 (a dedicated marker/exception type), never to "any
  503 from local"; AC3 asserts the other faults keep quarantining.
- **Risk — a marker that silently disappears.** If the marker is only a header set
  on the router's response, any intermediary (or a future response-rebuilding
  path) can drop it. Mitigation: prefer an explicit in-process marker on the
  dispatch/request in addition to the header, and test the header path.
- **Risk — thrash storms.** Removing the entry cooldown means the same big prompt
  can retry sooner; the per-session/prompt 600 s window still bounds it. AC2
  asserts the second attempt from the same session+prompt is still skipped.
- **Risk — abandoned-marker release races.** Clearing the marker while
  llama-server still processes the cancelled task would under-report genuine
  busy capacity (see `LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2`). Mitigation: shorten the TTL only
  after the cancel is confirmed, and keep `slots_detail`/`stale` semantics
  untouched.
- **Assumption.** The 503 is the only vehicle for the deficit abort; verified in
  `router.py` (`MeasuredCacheAbortDetourError` → `_build_backend_error_response`
  → 503). If a second path exists it needs the same treatment.
- **Assumption.** `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` is the value that re-arms
  before expiry under concurrency; the fix removes the call rather than tuning
  the value.
- **Risk — AC4 undoes the draining-slot annotation.** `LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM`
  exists precisely so a cancelled-but-draining slot is never reported idle or
  saturated. Deleting the abandonment marker on abort (rather than releasing it
  once the slot is confirmed free) would reopen that defect. Mitigation: release
  only on confirmed slot release, keep the `abandoned_busy` vocabulary intact,
  and record which AC4 option was chosen in the commit note.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Fixing the underlying Qwen3.x re-prefill cost, the
  admission pricing model, or the herdr reservation bug are *not* in scope; file
  or link them separately (`WL-0MVWEZF4Z004UNYT` already covers the last).
