# Extend the status builder's live-work attribution during prefill (72 residual saturated-without-live-work polls)

Follow-on item filed from the **LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1** verification verdict (2026-11-01 night window), **re-targeted 2026-11-02 after log-analysis evidence corrected the attribution** (see Evidence below).

**Verdict (unchanged):** EXPECTED IMPROVEMENT ACHIEVED: NO — 72 saturated-without-live-work polls (0.41 %) remain, up from the 12-poll / 0.11 % AC4 residual baseline (+60 polls) though down from the 247-poll / 2.12 % pre-fix baseline. The abandoned_busy annotation IS firing (367 polls / 2.06 %), so the shift is real. Of the 72 residual polls, 65 were **tool-attributed** to `session_evicted` (nearest event within the 600 s lookback), 1 to `no_progress_watchdog`, 1 to `prefill_deadline`, and 5 were unattributable (2026-11-01 22:12:58, 22:13:00 ×2, 23:02:37, 23:03:32).

## Problem statement

A slot that is genuinely busy prefilling a real local dispatch reports `capacity_hint=saturated` with empty live-work fields (`local_in_flight_requests=0`, `local_owner_session_id=None`, `local_active_query=false`) on fresh slot detail, so consumers cannot tell the slot is doing live work. The measured residual is 72 polls / 0.41 % of the 2026-11-01 night, all attributable to status-builder attribution lag during prefill rather than to the post-cancel draining-ghost class the abandoned_busy fix (LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM) already closes.

## Evidence (log-analysis, 2026-11-01 night episode 05:26–05:33)

The original "session-eviction path" reading was a **nearest-event mis-attribution** — the eviction was not draining when the residual polls were read:

1. 05:26:46.361 `Evicted 2 expired/invalidated session(s)` → `lease_released` ×2 (`session_evicted`). Both slots were **already free 7 s later**: 05:26:53.850 status reads `available_slots=2`, `capacity_hint=idle`, `in_flight=0`. No draining ghost existed from this eviction.
2. 05:27:10.829 a NEW local dispatch begins: `[local] POST slot=0 session=herdr-1793585223-1761548-25344` (large ~107K-token full-prompt reprocess; lease_extended_during_prefill at 05:27:22/05:28:07/05:28:19) — the slot is genuinely busy with live work.
3. The first residual poll (05:31:18.459) is 6 ms BEFORE `Stream started: provider=local session=herdr-1793596937-2342287-16191 turn=993bed20` (05:31:18.465) + `prefill_progress_measured` (31K tokens) — a second live local dispatch starts at that exact second.
4. All 65 residual polls (05:31:18 → 05:33:07) read `available_slots=1`, `capacity_hint=saturated`, `local_in_flight_requests=0`, `local_owner_session_id=None`, `local_active_query=false`, `slots_detail_stale=false`: a busy slot whose in-flight/owner attribution the status payload does **not** reflect during prefill.
5. Same shape reproduces live (2026-11-02 09:06): `available_slots=1` + `saturated` + `in_flight=0` + `owner=None` for several seconds while slot prefill for a REAL dispatch is in flight (owner + in_flight appear ~9 s later). Also observed: `available_slots=2` + `saturated` with fresh detail (09:06:41) — the counts-stale family (LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA).

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Reads `/llama/local/status` to decide whether the machine is genuinely busy. A `saturated` hint from a prefilling slot misdirects triage and hides real saturation (alarm fatigue).
- **Routing policy / dispatchers** (including the herdr downtime worker). `saturated` steers work to cloud/remote providers; a false `saturated` from live work causes avoidable paid fallback and, historically, starvation of the downtime dispatcher (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).
- **Measurement analyst** re-running `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`. Needs every residual poll attributable, otherwise the next re-measurement is as unexplained as this one.

User stories:

- As an on-call operator, when a slot is prefilling a real local dispatch, I want the status payload to say so (owner/in-flight set), so I don't misread capacity.
- As the herdr downtime worker, when a slot is doing live prefill work, I accept `saturated`; when it is not, I want a signal that distinguishes it, so I don't fall back to paid providers needlessly.
- As a measurement analyst, I want the widened attribution reason set to cover every residual poll, so re-measurements reach zero or full attribution.

## Goal (re-targeted)

Reconcile **slot-occupancy vs in-flight/owner attribution in the status builder** so a slot that is genuinely busy with live local work (prefill in progress for a real dispatch) reads its live-work attribution (`local_in_flight_requests`/`local_owner_session_id`/`local_active_query` or an equivalent signal) instead of `capacity_hint=saturated` with empty live-work fields. This is **NOT** the post-cancel draining-ghost the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM fix targets — extending `abandoned_busy` to the session-eviction path would not close this class.

## Work

1. Root-cause the status-builder lag: why does a slot prefilling for a real local dispatch read `in_flight=0` / `owner=None` (busy slot, but no live-work attribution)? Check against the counts-stale family LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA first (the 09:06:41 `available_slots=2` + `saturated` shape may be the same family).
2. Fix the status builder (or the residual classifier) to attribute live work during prefill — truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM must not be weakened (`some` live work must still read `saturated`).
3. Re-run the measurement over a comparable night (same invocation shape as `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-01_night-post-deploy/run_measurement.sh`) to confirm the residual drops toward 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A slot prefilling a real local dispatch never reports `capacity_hint=saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` / empty owner on fresh slot detail; it either carries the live-work attribution or reads a live-work hint.
- AC2: A pool with live work still reads `saturated` (truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM unweakened) — existing deterministic tests pass unchanged.
- AC3: Over a fresh closed night window, saturated-without-live-work polls are 0, or every residual is attributed with the widened reason set.
- AC4: The 5 unattributable polls from the 2026-11-01 night are either attributed via extended evidence (see LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR) or provably absent.

## Constraints

- Truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM must not be weakened: a pool with live work must still read `saturated` (`some` live work, even unfinalised during prefill, is still live).
- Do not duplicate LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR (attribution extension for unattributable polls) — reference it; AC4 here is bounded by "or provably absent".
- Measurement windows must be comparable in invocation shape to the 2026-11-01 night run (`run_measurement.sh`) and free of proxy-process restarts inside the window (the 2026-11-01 window's first 86 min were served by an earlier process).

## Existing state

The abandoned_busy annotation (LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM, landed on `dev`) already annotates post-cancel draining slots — 367 polls / 2.06 % read `abandoned_busy`. The residual class under this item is distinct: a **busy** slot (live prefill) whose live-work fields the status builder leaves empty. The counts-stale shape (`available_slots=2` + `saturated` with fresh detail) is tracked separately in LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA and may or may not be the same family (overlap check required before re-measuring).

## Desired change

The status payload for a slot prefilling a real local dispatch must expose its live-work attribution (or an equivalent live-work hint) instead of `saturated` with empty owner/in-flight fields — either in the status builder (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`) or, if root-cause shows the read path is stale, via the residual classifier's widened reason set.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — capacity hint status builder (live-work attribution during prefill)
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — measurement tool / residual classifier
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — slot-polling helpers (multi-slot iteration, per LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L)
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-01_night-post-deploy/verdict.txt` and `saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv` — evidence (72 rows; 65 mis-attributed to `session_evicted`)
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md` — documented `abandoned_busy` semantics (update on behaviour change)

## Risks and assumptions

- (Risk) The `available_slots=2` + `saturated` shape may belong to the counts-stale family (LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA); if root-cause confirms overlap, do not duplicate that fix inside this item — link it and keep this item's scope to prefill attribution.
- (Risk) Fixing attribution inside the builder while keeping `saturated` truthful for genuinely busy pools (AC2) is the core tension; existing deterministic tests are the guard.
- (Risk) A re-measurement night with a proxy-process restart inside the window invalidates comparability; pick a restart-free window.
- (Risk) AC4 depends on LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR (currently blocked); if it stays blocked, satisfy AC4 via "provably absent" under the widened reason set.
- (Assumption) The 09:06:41 `available_slots=2` + fresh-detail shape is the counts-stale family until proven otherwise.
- (Scope-creep guard) Any additional residual classes discovered during root-cause go to new linked work items, not this item's scope.

## Related work

- discovered-from: LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1 (verification item whose verdict this files)
- LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM — original draining-slot annotation fix (this is a different residual class)
- LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR — attribution extension for unattributable residual polls (reference, do not duplicate)
- LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM — truthful-status contract
- LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA — counts-stale family (overlap check required)
- LP-0MRO4U5O1008TLFU / LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L — multi-slot polling tests/fix for `poll_slots_for_model()` (completed; polling iteration context)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No interview required — the item was re-targeted with sufficient evidence by the LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1 verdict session and the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM implementation session before this intake. Evidence above is the answer record (log-analysis timestamps and live reproduction 2026-11-02 09:06, sourced from `/var/log/llama-proxy` and the status payloads cited in the Evidence section).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR** – Attribute saturated-without-live-work residual polls (blocked)
- **LP-0MRO4U5O1008TLFU** – Write multi-slot tests for poll_slots_for_model() (completed)
- **LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L** – Fix poll_slots_for_model() to iterate all slots (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: 0mvutyhg7001s6bm, abandoned, absent, ac1, ac2 (+175 more)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, 0mvutyhg7001s6bm, abandoned, absent, ac1 (+170 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, abandoned, absent, ac1, ac2 (+166 more)

## Plan (2026-11-02, plan skill)

### Root cause confirmed (log-analysis of `/var/log/llama-proxy`, 2026-11-01/02)

The residual is a **per-session dispatch-record teardown race**, not a stale read
path and not a missing attribution reason:

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py::_decrement_local_active_queries` closes a *turn*
by writing `local_dispatch_records[(endpoint, session_id)]["active"] = False` and
`expires_at = now + lease_timeout`, logging `lease_renewed`. When the next turn
of the **same session** has already re-acquired that shared record key, the late
teardown of turn N clears turn N+1's live-work attribution for its whole
prefill:

```text
05:31:07,383  Stream finished: ... provider=local session=herdr-1793596937   (turn N ends)
05:31:07,675  [local] POST ... (turn N+1 admitted, same session, same record key)
05:31:08,008  lease_renewed session=herdr-1793596937 timeout=30s            (turn N teardown, LATE)
05:31:13,015  local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0 (0 active dispatch records)
05:31:18,459  status_request avail=1 hint=saturated in_flight=0 owner=None slots_detail_stale=false latency_ms=3000
05:31:18,465  Stream started: provider=local session=herdr-1793596937       (first byte after 10.8 s prefill)
```

Control: polls at `05:33:4x` (same session, prefill with **no** teardown inside
it) read `local_in_flight_requests=1`, `local_owner_session_id=herdr-1793596937-…`.

`_release_local_dispatch` carries the mirror hazard: it `del`s the record
unconditionally, so a late abandonment release can delete a newer dispatch's
record outright.

### Attribution of the 72 residual polls (parent AC4)

- **65/72** (`05:31:18` → `05:33:07`): the cross-turn teardown race above, one
  looping agent session (`herdr-1793596937-…`) whose turn boundaries recur every
  7-18 s. The `session_evicted` cause in the tool's CSV is the 600 s
  nearest-event mis-attribution already documented on LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1.
- **5/72** ("unattributable"): the **same class**, now attributed:
  `22:12:55,240 [local] POST` → `22:12:55,282 lease_renewed` → polls
  `22:12:57`-`22:13:00`; `23:02:16,450 [local] POST` → `23:02:16,478
  lease_renewed` → poll `23:02:37,677` (`Stream started` `23:02:37,680`);
  `23:03:3x` same shape. AC4 is satisfied by attribution, so this item does not
  depend on the blocked LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR.
- **1/72** (`01:28:48`, `available_slots=0`): `prefill_deadline` attribution
  stands.
- Secondary contribution: the status handler samples live-work attribution
  **before** the `/slots` query, so a 3 s poll can pair fresh busy detail with an
  attribution snapshot taken before the dispatch was admitted (the
  `latency_ms=3000` / `2843` rows).

### Deviation from the predicted fix site (documented assumption)

The "Desired change" predicted the fix in `proxy/proxy/observability.py` or in
the residual classifier. Root cause places it in the **dispatch-record
lifecycle** (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, a predicted Key File) —
the status builder and the classifier are both reporting the registry correctly.
Fixing the classifier would only annotate a false payload, which the truthful
status contract (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM) forbids. No producer question is raised:
the goal ("a slot prefilling a real local dispatch must expose its live-work
attribution") is met by the source fix, and AC1/AC2 are unchanged.

### Features (children, test-first, single phase)

| # | Item | Type | Depends on |
|---|------|------|------------|
| 1 | Regression test: late turn teardown must not clear a newer dispatch's attribution | task | — |
| 2 | Scope dispatch teardown to its own dispatch | bug | 1 |
| 3 | Sample live-work attribution after the slot query | bug | 1 |
| 4 | Carry live-work evidence columns in the residual CSV | task | — |
| 4b | Record per-poll attribution for the five 2026-11-01 unattributable polls | task | — |
| 5 | Document per-dispatch live-work attribution semantics | docs | 2, 3 |
| 6 | Re-measure a restart-free night window and record the verdict | task | 2, 3, 4 |

Child ids: 1 `LP-0MVZ3V87D007R6JA`, 2 `LP-0MVZ3V8J1006YGFN`,
3 `LP-0MVZ3V8UR003KCSZ`, 4 `LP-0MVZ3V96D007A825`, 4b `LP-0MVZ3YV7L0056IVL`
(created by the AC-coverage review), 5 `LP-0MVZ3V9HZ0011S44`,
6 `LP-0MVZ3V9T800872B8`.

**Phasing decision:** one phase. The item is Small (~10 h expected) and every
child is a vertical slice of the same observable contract, so no phased rollout
is required; child 6 must run after child 2/3 are deployed to `dev` and served by
a proxy process that starts before the measured window.

### Scope boundary

- The **counts-stale pair** (cache-served `available_slots` alongside a fresh
  `saturated` hint — 71 of the 72 rows also show `available_slots=1` with fresh
  detail) stays with LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA. Child 6 reports that figure separately
  and does not claim it fixed here.

# Goal (test-first)

Pin the defect this parent was filed for with a deterministic, hermetic test, so
the fix (sibling item) cannot regress it.

## Defect being pinned

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py::_decrement_local_active_queries` marks the
session's **shared** per-session dispatch record `active=False` and logs
`lease_renewed` when a *turn* ends. A back-to-back next turn of the **same
session** acquires the same `(endpoint, session_id)` record key. When the
previous turn's teardown lands *after* that admission (measured 0.3-0.6 s later
in production), it clears the newer dispatch's live-work attribution for the
whole prefill, so `/llama/local/status` reports `capacity_hint=saturated` with
`local_in_flight_requests=0`, `local_owner_session_id=None`,
`local_active_query=false` on **fresh** slot detail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A hermetic test (no live proxy, no backend, no shared files/sockets)
  acquires a local dispatch for session `S`, acquires a second dispatch for the
  same session `S` (back-to-back turns), then runs the **first** dispatch's
  teardown (`_decrement_local_active_queries`) and asserts the surviving record
  still reads `active=True` with a future `expires_at`.
- AC2: The same test derives the status live-work view from the record registry
  exactly as `get_llama_local_status` does and asserts
  `local_in_flight_requests == 1` and `local_owner_session_id == S`.
- AC3: The test fails on the current code (red before the fix) and its failure
  message names the ordering ("teardown of turn N ran after admission of turn
  N+1") so a future regression is diagnosable.
- AC4: The retained-lease contract is pinned alongside: after the **last**
  dispatch's teardown the record is `active=False` with `expires_at > now`
  (post-stream lease retention must not regress — LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM AC1), and
  `_release_local_dispatch` on an abandoned dispatch must not delete a newer
  dispatch's record.
- AC5: Deterministic and fast: no sleeps beyond 0.1 s, no wall-clock
  dependencies, runs in the changed-scope gate via `/skill:test`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py` — existing home for dispatch-record
  accounting ACs (AC1-AC4 of LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O); add the new case here.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_decrement_local_active_queries`, `_release_local_dispatch`.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — the live-work fields the assertion mirrors
  (`local_in_flight_requests`, `local_owner_session_id`, `local_active_query`).

## Evidence (from the parent's log analysis)

```text
2026-11-02 05:31:07,383  Stream finished: ... provider=local session=herdr-1793596937  (turn N ends)
2026-11-02 05:31:07,675  [local] POST ... (turn N+1 admitted, same session)

2026-11-02 05:31:13,015  local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0 (0 active dispatch records)
2026-11-02 05:31:18,459  status_request available_slots=1 capacity_hint=saturated
                         local_in_flight_requests=0 local_owner_session_id=None

2026-11-02 05:31:18,465  Stream started: provider=local session=herdr-1793596937  (first byte after 10.8 s prefill)
```

# Goal

Make live-work attribution **per dispatch**, not per session turn, so a slot that
is genuinely prefilling a real local dispatch always carries its attribution
(AC1 of the parent) and the truthful-status contract is not weakened (AC2).

## Root cause (confirmed by log analysis, 2026-11-02)

`_decrement_local_active_queries` (normal end-of-stream teardown) writes
`local_dispatch_records[record_key]["active"] = False` +
`expires_at = now + lease_timeout` and logs `lease_renewed`. `record_key` is
`(endpoint, session_id)`, so the teardown of turn N clobbers the record already
re-acquired by turn N+1 of the same session whenever the teardown lands after
the admission (measured 0.3-0.6 s later, repeatedly, in production).
`_release_local_dispatch` has the mirror hazard: it `del`s the record
unconditionally, so a late abandonment release can delete a newer dispatch's
record entirely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A teardown (both the normal-end `_decrement_local_active_queries` path
  and the `_release_local_dispatch` abandonment/explicit-release path) affects
  **only the dispatch that owns it**: a later dispatch on the same session key
  keeps `active=True`, its `expires_at` and its attribution.
- AC2: A slot prefilling a real local dispatch never reports
  `capacity_hint=saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` / empty owner on
  fresh slot detail — it carries the live-work attribution.
- AC3: Retained-lease semantics unchanged: after the last teardown the record
  remains `active=False` with a future `expires_at` (`lease_renewed`), so slot
  retention and the post-stream cooldown behave exactly as before.
- AC4: `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` no longer falsely resets
  `local_active_queries` for this case (no `counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0
  (0 active dispatch records)` warning for a healthy back-to-back session), and
  the recovery path still zeroes a genuinely leaked counter.
- AC5: Truthful status unweakened (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM): a pool with live work
  still reads `saturated`; abandoned work still reads `abandoned_busy`;
  abandonment paths still emit `lease_released reason=<reason>`; the existing
  dispatch/lease/capacity test suites pass unchanged.
- AC6: The only observable behavioural deltas are the corrected in-flight
  counts; any change to admission/prefill-gate inputs is measured and recorded
  in a comment on this item (no cap or budget change).

## Minimal implementation

Two candidate mechanisms — the implementation picks one, guarded by the sibling
test item:

1. **Per-dispatch token** — the acquisition path already receives `request`;
   stamp a dispatch id on the record and on the request state, and have every
   teardown no-op when the id no longer matches (idempotent, also fixes the
   `_release_local_dispatch` delete hazard).
2. **Per-session live-dispatch refcount** — acquisition increments, teardown
   decrements, `active = count > 0`; ordering-insensitive. Must keep the
   `expires_at` safety net so a leaked increment cannot wedge the pool, and the
   recovery loop must reconcile the count.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (~L4180-4260),
  `_decrement_local_active_queries` (~L3062-3135), `_release_local_dispatch`
  (~L4293), `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` (~L6480-6656).
- `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_race.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_generating_only_pool.py` — existing guards.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — consumes the record registry for the payload.

# Goal

Close the second-order read-path skew: the status handler samples live-work
attribution **before** it queries `/slots`, so a dispatch admitted during the
slots query (which can take up to the 3 s `STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) yields a
payload that pairs **fresh** busy slot detail with **stale-empty** attribution —
`saturated` + `local_in_flight_requests=0`.

## Evidence

`2026-11-02 05:31:18,459 status_request ... capacity_hint=saturated
local_in_flight_requests=0 ... slots_detail_stale=false latency_ms=3000` — the
poll ran for 3 s, the live-work snapshot was taken at its start, and the local
dispatch's admission (`[local] POST` 05:31:07,675 / first byte 05:31:18,465)
fell inside that window. Same shape on `2026-11-01 23:02:37,677`
(`latency_ms=2843`).

This is complementary to the primary teardown-race fix: that one removes the
attribution loss, this one removes the sampling skew, so AC1 of the parent
("never `saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` on fresh slot detail")
holds by construction rather than by timing luck.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `get_llama_local_status` derives `local_in_flight_requests`,
  `local_owner_session_id` and `local_active_query` from a record-registry read
  that is not earlier than the served slot detail, so a dispatch admitted during

# Verify the ≥24 h restart-free proxy window and unblock the measurement child

**Follow-up to:** LP-0MVZ2EPI3006Y0WN (restart performed, window not yet armed)

## Why this item exists

The proxy has been restarted onto a build containing the starvation fix
(`9f3b9c06`), but the ≥24 h **restart-free** window that LP-0MVZ2EPI3006Y0WN
AC4 requires cannot be closed inside the deploy run — it is a time gate, not a
code change. This item owns that time gate so the deploy item does not claim
completion before the window genuinely exists.

## Anchor (as of the deploy run)

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Live proxy pid at anchor | **3698721** |
| Start (ps lstart) | **2026-11-02T10:39:24Z** (log boot marker `10:39:25.932`) |
| Restart attribution | `reason=LP-0MVWBXDZA00494HK live verification: deploy slices 2-3 (unloaded-model /slots skip)` |
| Deployed tree HEAD | `8ca1f24f` (docs-only over `579e2cc3`), contains `9f3b9c06` |
| Earliest the window can close | **2026-11-03T10:39:24Z** (anchor + 24 h) |

The anchor is the **newest** restart, not LP-0MVZ2EPI3006Y0WN's own restart: that
restart (pid 3684928, boot `2026-11-02 10:38:10.853`) was superseded ≈72 s later
by the concurrent live-verification deploy above, which rotated its log segment
aside as `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-11-02_103922`.

## What to do

1. **Do not restart the proxy to "freshen" the window.** If a restart has already
   happened (legitimate deploy, crash recovery), **re-anchor** on the new restart
   and record the reason — never measure across a restart and never silently
   tolerate one (per `docs/dev/measurement-windows.md` §1).
2. Wait until at least `2026-11-03T10:39:24Z`, then run the verification below.
3. If a restart occurred inside the window, re-anchor and restate the new
   earliest close time (the window restarts, it does not accumulate).

## Verification commands

```bash
# 1. Which process is actually serving 8000 (ignore test "twin" processes on other ports)
PID=$(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*:8000 .*pid=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
ps -o pid,lstart,etimes,cmd --no-headers -p "$PID"

# 2. Deployed tree still contains the fix
git -C /home/rgardler/projects/llm merge-base --is-ancestor 9f3b9c06 HEAD && echo "fix is ancestor: OK"
git -C /home/rgardler/projects/llm log -1 --format='%H %ci %s'

# 3. Health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/health | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['status'],d['llama_server_running'],d['tts_server_running'],d['tts_server_healthy'])"

# 4. Exactly one boot inside the window (a second marker means a restart happened)
grep -c "Starting LLama Proxy Server" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log

# 5. ≥ 24 h elapsed  (86400 s)
ps -o etimes= -p "$PID"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window closed on the anchor.** `ps -o etimes=` for the port-8000
  process is ≥ `86400` s and `ps -o lstart` matches the anchor
  `2026-11-02T10:39:24Z`, proving ≥24 h of uninterrupted uptime.
- **AC2 — No restart inside the window.** Exactly one
  `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker exists in the live window's log
  (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`), and no restart entry for the window
  appears in the window-start/end record.
- **AC3 — Build provenance re-proven.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor 9f3b9c06 HEAD`
  succeeds against the checkout the proxy runs from, and the deployed HEAD hash
  and `git log -1` line are quoted in the record.
- **AC4 — Health and services.** `/health` reports `status: healthy`,
  `llama_server_running: true`, `tts_server_running: true`,
  `tts_server_healthy: true`, with the raw JSON quoted.
- **AC5 — Window recorded.** A comment states window start, window end, elapsed
  duration in hours, and quotes the command outputs. A re-anchored window states
  the re-anchor reason and the discarded partial window length.
- **AC6 — Measurement child unblocked and notified.** The `depends-on` edge from
  `LP-0MVW8S8OZ00449YR` to `LP-0MVZ2EPI3006Y0WN` is resolved and that item is
  commented with the window boundaries, the deployed commit, and the log
  segments to read so its AC1 can cite the deploy evidence.
- **AC7 — Parent closed out.** `LP-0MVZ2EPI3006Y0WN` is moved to `in_review`
  with AC4/AC5 marked satisfied by this item's evidence (its AC1–AC3 are already
  satisfied by the deploy record).

## Constraints

- **Never** use `killall`/`pkill` on `python3`/`uvicorn`/proxy names; restart only
  via `/skill:start-proxy` (`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart --reason
  "<item id>: <what is being deployed>"`).
- Match the serving process by the **port-8000 listener**, not `pgrep` by name —
  test harnesses spawn "twin" uvicorn processes on other ports.
- No code change is expected; this is a read-only verification item.
- Coordination: register/refresh the window in `docs/dev/measurement-windows.md`
  (owned by `LP-0MVWC0FAT0018PMW`) rather than starting a second calendar.

# Rotation on restart strands the adopted llama-server's log in the rotated-away file

**discovered-from:** LP-0MVZ2EPI3006Y0WN (deploy run, 2026-11-02)
**Prior fix this appears to regress/leave uncovered:** LP-0MVECX47Z004LJAQ
*"Adopted llama-server loses its log sink, freezing llama-server.log"* (completed).

## Observed (2026-11-02, reproduced twice)

A proxy-only `start-proxy.sh --restart` preserves the running llama-server
(`Preserving running llama-server (unchanged local backend config)`) and the new
proxy adopts it:

```
2026-11-02 10:40:19,765 - INFO - Adopted running llama-server (model=router parallel=1 router_mode=True); preserving warm prompt cache
```

The restart also **rotates the log directory**, so `llama-server.log` is renamed
to `llama-server.1.log` and a fresh `llama-server.log` is created. The adopted
process keeps the **pre-rotation inode**, so its output continues to append to
`llama-server.1.log`, while the path the proxy watches stays frozen:

```
$ ls -la --time-style=full-iso llama-server.log llama-server.1.log
-rw-rw-r-- 1 rgardler rgardler 6696738 2026-11-02 10:44:38  llama-server.1.log   <- growing
-rw-rw-r-- 1 rgardler rgardler    2257 2026-11-02 10:39:48  llama-server.log     <- frozen (2257 bytes)

$ sleep 5 && ls -la llama-server.1.log llama-server.log
llama-server.1.log: 6700006 (10:44:42)      # +3,268 bytes in 5 s
llama-server.log:      2257 (10:39:48)      # unchanged
```

`/health` reports the consequence:

```json
{"llama_log_source_healthy": false, "llama_log_age_seconds": 277.4}
```

(the age keeps growing). The 2,257 bytes in the new `llama-server.log` are the
new proxy's *own* failed host-first spawn attempt, not the adopted backend's
output.

## Impact

- Log-based diagnostics for the local backend are silently unavailable after any
  restart that preserves llama-server — the common agent-restart path.
- `_update_slot_progress_from_log()` consumes the frozen tail and feeds stale
  values into the slot status payload.
- Any measurement that reads `llama-server.log` for the window under-measures or
  reads the wrong file — directly relevant to the prefill-recovery measurement
  family (`LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2`, `LP-0MVW8S8OZ00449YR`).
- `llama_log_source_healthy: false` is visible in `/health`, but nothing alerts
  on it, so operators trust a window that is blind on the llama side.

## Suspected cause

LP-0MVECX47Z004LJAQ fixed re-attaching the adopted process's stdout to the new
proxy's log sink, but re-attachment targets the **old file object / inode**. When
the restart rotates the file first, the re-attached sink writes to the renamed
inode (`llama-server.1.log`) while the reader/watcher resolves the path
(`llama-server.log`). Re-attachment therefore needs to happen *after* rotation
and/or to reopen by path rather than inheriting the pre-rotation descriptor.


**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `rotate_llama_logs()`, `start_llama_server()`, `_try_adopt_running_llama_server()`, `_verify_adopted_log_relay()`, `_log_has_live_writer()`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — startup / `_ensure_model_ready()` adoption ordering and `/health` fields
- `proxy/tests/test_log_relay_adoption.py` — existing adoption/rotation relay tests (regression home)
- `docs/dev/measurement-windows.md` — AC5 measurement safety note
- `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` — AC5 measurement safety note

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Reproduction pinned.** A regression test reproduces the sequence
  "llama-server running → proxy restart with log rotation + preserved backend"
  and asserts the adopted backend's output lands in the watched
  `llama-server.log` (not a rotated-away sibling).
- **AC2 — Watched path is live.** After such a restart, `llama-server.log`
  receives the adopted backend's output continuously (file size advances) and
  `/health` reports `llama_log_source_healthy: true` with
  `llama_log_age_seconds` below the staleness threshold.
- **AC3 — No rotation split.** Either the rotation is deferred until after
  re-attachment, or the adopted backend is re-pointed at the new path, so no
  live output is ever stranded in a `.N.log` sibling.
- **AC4 — Diagnostics surface the failure.** When the log source is unhealthy,
  the proxy logs a WARNING naming the frozen path, the live inode's actual path
  (resolved via `/proc/<pid>/fd/1`) and the remediation, so the condition is
  self-explaining rather than visible only as a `/health` boolean.
- **AC5 — Measurement safety note.** `docs/dev/measurement-windows.md` and
  `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` record that a window's llama log
  may live in a rotated sibling after a restart-with-preserve, with the command
  to resolve the real path (`readlink /proc/$(pgrep -f 'llama-server.*--models-preset' | head -1)/fd/1`).

## Constraints

- Do not restart llama-server merely to "fix" the log: preserving the warm
  prompt cache is deliberate (`--keep-llama-server` default).
- No blanket `killall`/`pkill`; restarts only via `/skill:start-proxy`.
data.title: Rotation on proxy restart strands the adopted llama-server's log in the rotated-away file (llama-server.log frozen, /health llama_log_source_healthy=false)

# `implement.py start` cannot resume from inside a worktree (relative path resolves against cwd)

**discovered-from:** LP-0MVWBXDZA00494HK (slice 5 live verification of LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K)

## Problem

`implement.py start <id>` is documented as idempotent — a driven child session, or any
session resuming pre-created work, must be able to run it from inside the worktree
("`start` resumes the pre-created worktree idempotently"). It cannot: the resume check
resolves the worktree path against the **current working directory**.

- `worktree_path_for()` returns a **repo-relative** path (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`).
- `phase_start()` computes `abs_wt_path = str(Path(wt_path).resolve())` and tests
  `_is_worktree(Path(abs_wt_path))`.
- When `start` is invoked from inside that worktree, `Path(wt_path).resolve()` becomes
  `<worktree>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (does not exist) → `resumed = False` →
  `git worktree add` fails ("already exists"/"already checked out") → the run aborts with
  `Failed to create worktree …`, having already claimed and then released the item
  (status reset to `open`).

## Observed (2026-11-02, LP-0MVWBXDZA00494HK)

```
$ cd .worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVWBXDZA00494HK-live-verification-skip-signal-replaces-u
$ python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py start LP-0MVWBXDZA00494HK --allow-orphaned-stashes
INFO: Claiming work item LP-0MVWBXDZA00494HK...
INFO: Creating worktree at .worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVWBXDZA00494HK-live-verification-skip-signal-replaces-u from branch dev...
ERROR: Failed to create worktree at … from dev
```

Note `.git` **is** a file in that directory, so `_is_worktree()` on the *correct* absolute
path returns True. Running the same command from the main checkout succeeded and reported
`"resumed": true`.

## Impact

Every driven child (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`, cwd = its pre-created worktree) that follows
the documented leaf flow (`start` → … → `finish`) fails at `start` and must fall back to
`finish`-only or a manual claim, and the same is true for a human resuming a run inside the
tree. The failure also briefly claims and releases the item, which is noisy in the worklog.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the canonical worktree path against the **main checkout root** (`_get_repo_root()`),
never against cwd, before the `_is_worktree()`/`git worktree add` decision — mirroring the
`repo_root` rule already enforced for `.implement_state.json`. Add a regression test that
runs `phase_start()` with cwd set inside the existing worktree and asserts
`resumed: true` and no `git worktree add`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `implement.py start <id>`, run with cwd **inside** the item's existing worktree, resumes
      it (`resumed: true`), leaves status `in_progress`, and never attempts `git worktree add`.
- [ ] A regression test pins the cwd-inside-worktree case (and the existing
      main-checkout case still passes).
- [ ] Invoked from the main checkout the behaviour is unchanged.

## Key files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `worktree_path_for()`,
  `phase_start()` (Step 7 worktree create-or-resume), `_is_worktree()`
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/tests/` — regression test home
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — document the cwd-independence of the resume path
data.title: implement.py start cannot resume from inside a worktree (relative path resolves against cwd)

data.comment:
question: A sibling item LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 (intake_complete) proposes **deleting** `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` (git rm + repo-wide config-fast/cheap sweep) and claims, via its coverage matrix, that every surviving assertion is duplicated in pytest. This item's intake proposes **repairing** the harness in place to assert today's single-config contract (AC1–AC6, fixing LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA staleness). The two completed intakes contradict each other and cannot both be implemented (delete vs rewrite the same file), so consolidation onto exactly ONE item requires the producer's decision.

Evidence check (I verified before asking): the sibling matrix is correct that the mode-selection, base-only key, per-slot and Web-UI assertions are already covered (proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py::test_config_overlays_gone + test_slot_pool_fixed_at_2, tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh, proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py). **However it misses one gap:** this harness is the ONLY coverage of start-proxy.sh's shell-level `--restart` preserve-vs-restart decision — `grep -rln "Preserving running llama-server"` matches only `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` and `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`; proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py covers the Python hash helper (`_config_file_sha256` / `merged_config_sha256`), not the shell branch that consumes the signature file and its KEEP_LLAAMA logic. Deleting the harness drops that shell-level coverage unless follow-up work adds a pytest test for it.

Options (producer pick; my recommendation is B):
- **A. Repair in place (this item).** +~4.9h small/low. Rewrites fixtures/assertions to the single-config contract and keeps the only shell-level restart-decision coverage. LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 + LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8 closed as duplicates.
- **B. Delete (sibling item LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29).** +~1.6h small/low. `git rm` the harness + config sweep; **add a follow-up** pinning start-proxy.sh `--restart` preserve/restart at the shell level so the merged-config signature keeps a consumer test. This item + LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8 closed as duplicates.
- **C. Something else** (e.g. repair + pytest wrapper collecting the harness in the default suite — the wrapper is currently out of scope on both items).

**Recommended: B** — the harness asserts a removed surface and its fixture scaffolding is a maintenance liability; the one genuine gap (shell restart decision) is better covered by a small focused pytest test than by a 567-line sandbox harness. Either way, LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8 (in-progress, no ACs) and the non-chosen item must be closed as duplicates.

Measured window numbers (AC1–AC4 of the record) — the ≥24 h window opened
2026-10-22 21:48:05 (LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF) and closed 2026-10-23 21:48:05.
Artifact: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`.
Lease-gate decision from the same window: LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB.

| Metric | Baseline 2026-10-19 07:23 → 10-20 07:23 | Before 10-21 21:48 → 10-22 21:48 | After (window) 10-22 21:48 → 10-23 21:48 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `local_idle_admit` | 0 | 0 | **31** |
| Local serve share | 2.34 % | 10.79 % | 2.04 % |
| `large_context_bypass` | 1,284 | 1,790 | 3,702 |
| Remote fallback events | 17,005 | 6,953 | 12,888 |
| `local_dispatch_denied` | 2,635 | 1,584 | 1,731 |
| Local prefill slot-seconds | 50,187 | 16,653 | 3,314 |

**AC2 (idle-admitted vs non-idle, same bucket):** 31 admits, **0 paired local
dispatches** — the treatment sample is empty, so the bucket comparison is
unmeasurable (`ac2.idle_admitted_*` empty; `non_idle_first_byte_ms` n=278,
p50 5,752 ms / p90 45,716 ms).

**AC3 (denials / timeouts):** denials 66.0 → 72.1 per hour (**+9.3 %**, over the
5 % band); zero timeouts attributable to idle-admitted requests (3 coincident,
55 unrelated). Both are consequences of the ~2× heavier after window.

**AC4 (interactive tier):** before window had no `priority=`-tagged `high`
dispatches (n=0) → unmeasurable; after window `high` n=85, p50 2,467 ms /
p90 28,600 ms, and `idle_admitted_by_priority` is empty (no idle-admitted
dispatch reached first byte, so none can be blamed at that tier).

**AC5 recommendation:** the tool returns **`measure`**, not
`enable_by_default` ("only 0 idle-admitted dispatch sample(s); need >= 5").
The zero is mechanistic, not a sampling hole: 22 of the 31 admits dispatched
and were cancelled at `prefill_deadline_exceeded` (`progress=0`) and 9 were
refused by `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` — the override admits prompts it cannot

**Why the last audit was right to call AC2/AC4 partial.** `routing_idle_admit_refused` — the admit-time prefill-feasibility refusal shipped by LP-0MVRCLPVI0057116 — contains `routing_idle_admit` as a substring, so the parser counted every refusal as an admission. In the post-fix after window that is **9,186 refusals counted as admissions against 76 real admissions (120×)**, and every refusal became a phantom "unpaired admit": AC2 could never pair, and the fixture made the window look unmeasurable even where convertible requests existed. Refusals are now a distinct event (`kind: idle_admit_refused`), reported as `ac1.local_idle_admit_refused`, `ac1.idle_admit_refused_by_reason` and `event_counts.idle_admit_refused`, never as admissions.

**Second window pair (the measurement of record for AC2/AC4).** The 2026-10-22→23 window genuinely cannot answer AC2/AC4 (0 idle-admitted conversions; its before side predates the `priority=` instrumentation), so both are measured on the eligibility-fix pair, override live throughout: before 2026-10-22 21:48 → 2026-10-25 23:00 (73.2 h, pre-fix) vs after 2026-10-25 23:00 → 2026-10-31 10:00 (131.0 h, fix live). New artifact: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-31.json`.

**AC2 — 76 admits, 7 paired, per-bucket comparison with sample counts** (bucket edges 16,384 / 32,768 / 65,536 / 131,072 tokens):

| Bucket (tokens) | idle n | idle p50 / p90 (ms) | idle slot-s | non-idle n | non-idle p50 / p90 (ms) | non-idle slot-s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0–16,384 | 0 | — | — | 2,133 | 2,946.0 / 16,300.1 | 13,529.3 |
| 16,384–32,768 | 0 | — | — | 1,312 | 4,352.8 / 51,684.2 | 18,473.3 |
| 32,768–65,536 | 5 | 26,193.9 / 44,161.7 | 115.3 | 272 | 4,795.2 / 35,547.2 | 3,988.2 |
| 65,536–131,072 | 2 | 17,850.8 / 29,275.7 | 35.7 | 33 | 2,225.6 / 5,405.4 | 109.0 |
| **all** | **7** | **26,193.9 / 42,941.2** | **151.0** | **3,750** | **3,276.6** | **36,099.8** |

The trade AC2 asks for is now a measurement, not a claim: an idle-admitted request holds the slot **~8× longer to first byte** (26.2 s vs 3.3 s) and the 7 of them consume 151 s of slot time, in exchange for local service instead of a remote provider. 69 of the 76 admits never reached a local dispatch inside the 60 s correlation window (refused later, client-cancelled, or detoured), stated so the 7-sample comparison is not over-read.

**AC4 — interactive tier improves, with no overlap to blame:**

| Interactive (`priority=high`) | before | after | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dispatches (n) | 63 | 648 | — |
| p50 first byte | 16,161.5 ms | 3,589.1 ms | **−77.8 %** |
| p90 first byte | 74,058.2 ms | 43,526.6 ms | **−41.2 %** |

Latency improved rather than regressed (the eligibility fix stopped dispatching prompts that could never reach a first byte, which had been occupying slots ahead of interactive work); the noise band is a one-sided harm test, so a decrease is not harm.  reconstructs the 7 idle-admitted prefill intervals (2 same-tier, 5 cross-tier by the admitting request's priority) and **0 of 648 interactive-tier dispatches started inside one** — no regression and no overlapping evidence to attribute one to, stated explicitly instead of implying a same-tier cause.

The tool's AC5 recommendation on this pair is `tune` (the after window carried 30.5 % more remote fallbacks); AC5's recorded outcome stays `measure` + LP-0MVRCLPVI0057116.

## AC2–AC4 — Verdict: the failure mode is a snapshot ↔ sidecar lifecycle gap, NOT either guard

Full write-up (counts, tables, code references, caveats):
`docs/dev/slot-ratio-seed-verdict-LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3.md`.

### Confirmed failure mode

Of **4,488** seed decisions over **155 h**, every one failed **at the lookup**:

- `missing_sidecar` **3,402 / 4,488 = 75.80 %** (31 sessions)
- `missing_snapshot` **1,086 / 4,488 = 24.20 %** (4 sessions)
- **guard branches reached: 0** (`found`, `expired`, `model_mismatch`,
  `prefix_mismatch`, `empty_ratio` all exactly 0)

By construction in `seed_cached_ratio()` those guard branches are only reachable
*after* a `slot_<session>.bin` candidate exists **and** a readable, versioned
sidecar is found next to it. A zero guard total across 155 h therefore means the
guard was **never evaluated on real traffic** — the seed path never got that far.

### The two alternative modes, ruled out with their own counts

- **Prefix mismatch (`prefix_matches`): 0 / 4,488 (0.00 %).** Not rare —
  unreachable, per the above. So the "rewritten system prompt / client-compacted
  front" hypothesis is *not* what is blocking the credit.
- **Expired sidecar (24 h TTL): 0 / 4,488 (0.00 %).** Independently, every
  sidecar that did exist was young: `missing_snapshot` `age_s` p50 **1.26 h**,
  p90 **14.1 h**, max **16.05 h** (24 h window: p50 0.92 h, max 2.69 h), all far
  below the 86,400 s default. The TTL could not have suppressed a single
  decision — AC4's age distribution is included here for completeness even
  though `expired` is not the confirmed mode.
- **Lookup miss (recorded at intake as "unlikely, directory names matched") —
  confirmed**, in a sharper form than directory drift: the reader resolves the
  right path; the **writer does not keep the snapshot and its sidecar
  together**.

### Writer-side causes (code + counts, verified by inspection)

1. **Eviction saves never write a sidecar.** `write_slot_ratio_sidecar()` has
   exactly one caller — the request-completion path in `proxy/router.py`.
   `session.save_evicted_session_snapshot()` (the AC6 tenancy-reclaim save)
   writes only the `.bin`. **98 successful eviction saves across 32 sessions** in
   the window, overlapping **17 of the 31** `missing_sidecar` sessions: those
   snapshots are structurally unseedable whatever the guard does.
2. **The request-path sidecar write is conditional** on
   `_measured_prompt_tokens > 0`, so a snapshot saved from a request whose usage
   block was not measured gets no sidecar. This is the plausible source for the
   affected sessions with no eviction save; the outcome line cannot separate the
   two (see the follow-up item below).
3. **Sidecar lifetime is not coupled to its snapshot's**: written after the
   snapshot in a separate best-effort step, deleted only from
   `_invalidate_session_and_slot()` when a caller passes a filename, and never
   pruned by retention — `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` globs
   `"$SLOT_CACHE_DIR"/slot_*.bin` (root only, non-recursive) and ignores
   `.ratio.json`, so it reports "No slot files found" while **139 orphan sidecars
   accumulate on disk with 0 snapshots**. A session whose sidecar outlived its
   snapshot reports `missing_snapshot` on *every* subsequent request (this is why
   a handful of sessions produce thousands of identical failures).

### AC3 — the implied fix, and why it satisfies AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304

**None of the four candidate guard relaxations is implied** — "fingerprint the
non-system messages only", "stable prompt-prefix anchor", "credit the last saved
overlapping messages" and "re-evaluate the TTL default" all loosen a guard that
**never executed**, so each leaves the observed 0 % restored-prefix engagement
exactly where it is.

Implied fix — **writer-side lifecycle coupling**:

1. write the sidecar on the **eviction** save path too (the session's last
   recorded prompt prefix and prompt-token estimate are already available via
   `record_prompt_prefix`);
2. write it on the request path even when no usage block was measured, deriving
   `cached_tokens` from that recorded prefix/estimate instead of skipping it;
3. delete the sidecar wherever the snapshot is deleted (one helper used by every
   unlink site) and make retention recurse into endpoint subdirectories and
   prune orphan sidecars;
4. leave `prefix_matches()`, the TTL default and the credit arithmetic
   **unchanged**.

**AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 still holds**: the fix repairs artefact *pairing*,
not the guard. Credit is still applied only after the stored message
fingerprints prefix-match the incoming messages, under the same
measured-tokens × safety-margin cap (AC3 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304). A genuinely
changed prompt still earns nothing; a genuinely reusable prefix finally gets
evaluated at all. Revisit the guard only *after* this fix, from new counts: if
`prefix_mismatch` appears in volume once pairs exist, the guard is then the
binding constraint and the data will say so directly.

### Expected post-fix signature (feeds this item's re-measurement AC)

`missing_sidecar` ≈ 0 for eviction-saved sessions; `missing_snapshot` ≈ 0;
`found` > 0 and `cache_state=restored` dispatches > 0 for the first time;
`prefix_mismatch` / `expired` become *possible* and their counts become the next
measurement's question.

### Follow-ups filed from this analysis (discovered-from LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3)

- **LP-0MVTFITHI00948Y5** — log the resolved snapshot/sidecar paths in
  `slot_ratio_seed`, so the residual per-session split of `missing_sidecar` is
  attributable from logs.
- **LP-0MVTFJ04T001VW47** — `cleanup-slot-cache.sh` is non-recursive and never
  prunes orphan sidecars.

### Caveats

- The counts prove the **stage** conclusively; the sub-cause split per session is
  inferred from code + tallies, not logged (the follow-up above closes that).
- Local-prefill movement in this window must **not** be attributed to the seed
  path: engagement was 0 throughout.

data.comment:
## Implementation complete — commit `5502ee44` pushed to dev

### What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `proxy/proxy/session.py` | `save_evicted_session_snapshot()` now writes the sidecar after a successful save (`_write_eviction_sidecar`) using the session's recorded prompt prefix; every snapshot unlink now goes through `_retire_slot_snapshot` / `_retire_session_slot_snapshots`, which retire the `.bin` **and** its `.ratio.json` for the named filename *and* every candidate path (root layout + `{host}-{port}` subdirectories) |
| `proxy/proxy/router.py` | request-path sidecar write is no longer gated on `_measured_prompt_tokens > 0`; it derives the count via `provider.sidecar_cached_tokens()` |
| `proxy/proxy/provider.py` | new `get_recorded_prompt_prefix()` + `sidecar_cached_tokens()` (measured → prefix-matched recorded measurement → router prompt estimate → 0 = write nothing) |
| `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` | `write_slot_ratio_sidecar()` accepts precomputed `fingerprints` (the eviction path has no request body). `prefix_matches()`, `ttl_seconds()`, `ratio_from_sidecar()` and `SIDECAR_VERSION` are untouched |
| `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` | walks the root **and** one level of endpoint subdirectories, deletes each snapshot with its sidecar under both retention rules, and prunes orphan sidecars (previously the root-only glob printed `No slot files found` and exited early against 139 orphans / 0 snapshots) |
| `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` | 15 new tests (eviction pairing, unmeasured-usage save, retirement coupling, cleanup-script retention) |
| `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` | 7 new shell assertions (pair deletion, subdirectory scan, orphan pruning) |
| `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md` | resolved lifecycle coupling, token-count rule, what still earns nothing, expected post-fix signature, retention behaviour |

### Chosen token-count rule (AC5 risk note)

`cached_tokens` is never invented: (1) the usage block's `prompt_tokens` when measured (unchanged); (2) else the previously recorded **measured** prefix, only when its fingerprints prefix-match the saved messages (a genuine lower bound); (3) else the router's own estimator (`_estimate_prompt_tokens_for_routing`), which counts message text only and therefore under-counts rather than inflating credit; (4) else **no sidecar**. - \`~/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/manifest.txt\` — per window: boundary, exact CLI command, output dir, headline numbers, measured coverage and any gap (AC3, AC5). Blocks for \`post24\`/\`now24\`/the ref24 fragment were written by the tool itself, so the recorded command is the command that ran.

### Reproducible tooling (committed)

\`scripts/proxy_usage_window_archive.py\` (\`coverage\` / \`archive\` / \`run-window\`, all \`--json\`) + \`tests/test_proxy_usage_window_archive.py\` (22 tests) + \`docs/dev/proxy-usage-evidence-windows.md\`. Rationale: parent AC6 requires every quoted number to be reproducible from a committed command, and the archive step (copy + integrity verification + manifest) is the part that must happen *at measurement time*. It reuses the already-tested \`scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py\` discovery/coverage rather than adding a second parser, and drives \`analyze_proxy_usage.py\` unmodified (scope respected: no skill-code changes).

### Scope notes / assumptions recorded

- The live \`proxy.log\` and \`llama-server.log\` are **not** archived: their content no longer intersects any of the four windows (verified by the coverage map), so copying them would only have added ~12 MB of out-of-window data.
- \`llama-server.log*\` segments carry no per-line timestamps in this deployment; archive inclusion uses the rotation date in the filename, and the live file is never ranged.
- The \`now24\` window is complete (24.0 h) and is the reference window downstream should use in place of \`ref24\`.
- Retention remains unaddressed as a systemic fix (archive-on-write or longer retention) — that is a deployment decision beyond this item; the operational lesson is recorded in the doc: run \`archive\` in the same session as the measurement.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Completed — pushed to dev in commit e21d2af5 (worktree cleaned up, `dev` fast-forwarded).

**What changed**
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: `_await_first_byte_with_prefill_monitor()` now takes the `Request` (plus `dispatch_session_id`) and polls `request.is_disconnected()` on the existing prefill poll cadence (`local_dispatch_lease_prefill_poll_seconds`, default 10 s — no new background task). On a *confirmed* disconnect it calls the new synchronous `_release_client_disconnect_dispatch()` and raises `ClientDisconnectedDuringPrefillError`. The per-tick probe is skipped when polling is disabled (`poll_seconds <= 0`), where the reaper verdict path covers the case.
- `_release_client_disconnect_dispatch()` (new, contains **no `await`**): deletes the dispatch record (legacy and per-endpoint key forms), pops the session's `local_prefill_in_flight` marker, frees the slot assignment, cancels the captured upstream stream (`stream_cm`) and wakes the contention queue (the two awaiting steps run as detached tasks). Logs `lease_released session=… reason=client_disconnect endpoint=…`. Idempotent: a missing record/marker is a silent no-op.
- `proxy/proxy/disconnect_reaper.py`: `mark_client_disconnected()` / `client_disconnect_observed()` record the reaper's confirmed verdict on the ASGI scope key `llama_proxy.client_disconnected` before cancelling the in-flight task (a cancelled task cannot re-probe the connection). Fail-closed: only an explicit `True` counts.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`: passes the request to the monitor; new `except ClientDisconnectedDuringPrefillError` branch finishes the counter accounting via `_cleanup_after_request(..., disconnected=True)` and returns 499 without marking the backend not-ready or recording a 5xx; new `except asyncio.CancelledError` branch releases synchronously on the reaper verdict, schedules the counter cleanup as a detached task, then re-raises. `_cleanup_after_request()`'s `disconnected` branch now also pops a surviving prefill marker (the `disconnect` reason is kept for the stream-end path).
- Docs: `docs/llama-router.md` (new "Client-dead mid-prefill recovery" section) and `proxy/docs/routing.md` (lease / orphan-recovery section).

**AC status**
- AC1 (regression test, release within 300 s, another session admitted): `test_router_prefill_client_disconnect_releases_and_admits_another` + `test_monitor_releases_on_confirmed_disconnect` (asserts elapsed well under 300 s and that `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` admits the next session immediately).
- AC2 (distinct log reason + upstream cancelled): `test_client_disconnect_release_frees_every_hold`, `test_monitor_keeps_a_slow_but_live_prefill` (counter-case) and the router-level 499 / no-5xx / no-cooldown test.
- AC3 (cancellation-interrupted cleanup): release made non-awaiting; `test_client_disconnect_release_is_cancellation_proof` and `test_router_prefill_reaper_cancel_releases_on_confirmed_verdict`.
- AC4 (live confirmation on the deployed proxy): **pending deployment** — it cannot be verified against the running pre-deploy build without reproducing the wedge and blocking this session's own local admissions. Post-restart verification: kill a client mid-prefill, expect `client_disconnect_during_prefill` plus `lease_released … reason=client_disconnect` within one poll interval (<= 10 s), a subsequent admission from another session with no `local_dispatch_denied reason=local_lease_active`, and `/llama/local/status` `local_prefills_in_flight` back to 0.
- AC5 (docs): done as above (code comments + both routing docs).
- AC6 (full suite): green at the pushed commit — cached post-push full run reported `4990 passed, 15 skipped in 344.88s`.

**Assumptions recorded**
- The release decrements no per-request counters: `_cleanup_after_request` remains the single owner of those decrements (`local_active_queries` is pool-wide, so a double decrement would free another session's capacity).
- Only an explicit `is_disconnected()` `True` (or the reaper's recorded verdict) releases, so a live but slow (>180 s) prefill is never cut short; the 90 s deadline, 180 s no-progress watchdog and 900 s ceiling all still apply.
- Record/marker mutations are single statements with no `await`, so skipping `local_dispatch_records_lock` in the release cannot interleave with a lock holder on the event loop — that is what makes the release cancellation-proof.
- Worktree hygiene: `implement.py start` warned about 13 pre-existing orphaned stashes on the main checkout; they were left untouched (not triaged, not deleted) as they are outside this item's scope.

## Producer decision required — evidence from the completed 24 h window (2026-10-25)

The 24 h post-deploy measurement (**LP-0MVM83F6X0005V8S**, pasted on
LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2, commit `458c7fc6`) now answers the question this item was
filed to resolve.

### What changed since this item was written

- **The wedge is gone.** 525/525 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` → `lease_released
  … reason=prefill_deadline` pairs released in **0.0 s**, no unreleased
  sessions, so no session can hold the gate for hours after a cancelled
  dispatch. The incident shape (`progress=None alive=False` renewal for ~4 h)
  did not recur.
- **Denials by a productive holder remain the dominant lease-active shape.**
  93 `reason=local_lease_active` fallbacks in 24 h (766 in the 24 h pre-fix
  baseline). Where I sampled them (e.g. `herdr-1792789684-1790656-13656`
  holding ~19 min while others queued 60 s), the holder was decoding — a
  fairness/monopoly shape, not a zero-decode wedge.
- **The remaining zero-service hours are a different defect**, at the
  admission end, not the lease end: 1,125 dispatch attempts vs 90 local
  streams served, 14 hours with ≥10 attempts and no local stream, each attempt
  cancelled at the deadline (525 in 24 h). That is tracked by
  LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG / LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I / LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE, not here.

### The decision this item's AC1 asks for

Either:

- **(A) Restate the AC — recommended.** The measurable, fix-attributable target
  is the **wedge signature**: a lease owner that produces no first byte *and*
  no llama-server prefill progress beyond a bound. Under that definition the
  fix passes (0.0 s releases, no unreleased sessions). Literal "zero
  `reason=local_lease_active` fallbacks" is unachievable at sustained
  multi-session demand on a 2-slot pool and conflates a productive holder with
  a wedge.
- **(B) Treat it as a defect — lease fairness.** Cap consecutive renewals
  without a first byte per request, or per-request lease cycles, so a single
  session cannot hold the gate for ~19 min while others queue 60 s. Scope as
  its own work item; it is orthogonal to the wedge fix.

On (A) the wording change belongs on **LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2 AC3** (which quotes
"zero `reason=local_lease_active` fallbacks" verbatim); on (B) I can file and
start the fairness item.

### Metadata change made while recording this

Removed the inverted dependency edge `LP-0MVLHMCN6003GAMD → LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6`
(this item "depended on" its own parent epic, which deadlocked the epic: the
parent cannot close until this child is terminal while this child was blocked
by the parent). The parent/child relationship already expresses that the epic
needs this decision. This item keeps its inbound edge from

adopted: the measurable, fix-attributable target is the **wedge signature** (a
lease owner that holds the local gate with no client-visible first byte beyond
a bound), not literal zero `reason=local_lease_active` fallbacks. Option B
(lease fairness) is tracked separately as **LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0**.

### AC1 — MET

Decision recorded here, and the restatement propagated to both places this AC
required (commit `e0d2ccb3` on `dev`):

1. **LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2 AC3** — description amended: the AC now reads "zero
   **wedge-attributed** lease-active denials", names `ac1.wedge_denials` as
   the metric, and records the restatement + the fairness-item cross-link.
2. **The verification script's AC1 verdict** —
   `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` no longer derives AC1 from the
   report figures. `measure_wedge_denials()` classifies every
   `local_dispatch_denied` by the named owner's **continuous prefill-hold
   chain** (`lease_extended_during_prefill` every ~10 s; ended only by a
   genuine `lease_released`; deadline/`lease_renewed` churn deliberately does
   not end a chain, which is exactly the incident shape):

   | Class | Meaning |
   |---|---|
   | `wedge_denials` | owner held ≥ `--wedge-bound-seconds` (default 300 s = the AC's ≤5 min) with no first byte — **the verdict metric** |
   | `productive_holder_denials` | owner had already delivered a local first byte (fairness) |
   | `short_hold_denials` | unproductive owner, hold shorter than the bound (fresh prefill) |
   | `stale_owner_denials` | denial names an owner with no live hold |

   `verdict_met = (wedge_denials == 0)`. Thrash hours and the
   `reason=local_lease_active` volume moved to `ac1.diagnostics` (admission-side,
   LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG / LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I / LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE).

Implementation (Map, commit da5bba21):

**Design decision (recorded assumption, producer may override):** implemented the warm-start priming gate as the primary fix plus `--stagger-seconds` as a complementary control — the 2026-10-23 log already had a 60 s stagger active yet request 1 never completed a local prefill, so stagger alone cannot fix a first-request-that-never-lands.

**AC1 — warm-start gate:** `--warm-start` / `--no-warm-start` (default **ON for `--sweep`**, OFF otherwise). After each slot-count restart one small single-turn priming request ('Say Hi', `WARM_START_MAX_TOKENS=20`, per-attempt timeout 120 s) must complete with a local `X-Resolved-Model` (the harness-visible `cold_start.is_cold() == False` proof). Bounded retries (`--warm-start-attempts`, default 3; retry delay 15 s); persistent failure raises `WarmStartError` and **no measured request is sent** — the run fails fast with a diagnostic naming `proxy/cold_start.py: is_cold()`, `local_dispatch_denied` and `backend busy (health check timeout)`. The proxy guard itself is untouched (no changes to `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py`).

**AC2 — stagger:** hard-coded `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S = 60.0` removed; `--stagger-seconds N` (default 0 = all at once) spaces *measured* starts by `N × idx`; requests still run concurrently once started; warmup pass never delayed.

**AC3 support — auditability:** per-request `started_at`/`ended_at` are now recorded and `contention.max_concurrent_local_streams` (peak concurrent local streams) is derived, so 'local share > 0 with >= 2 concurrent local streams' is verifiable from `slot_<N>.json`; each run artefact also carries a `warm_start` block (attempts, completed_locally, resolved_model) and `config.stagger_seconds`; the summary report prints both.

**AC4 — tests:** new `tests/test_slot_benchmark_warm_start.py` (20 tests): gate passes only on a local completion, retries remote/transport failures, fails fast after the bounded budget with the diagnostic, gate runs before any measured request, abort path sends zero measured requests, stagger math + run-level laundelays, CLI defaults/validation/help, peak-concurrency metric. Existing `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` fixture updated for the new metric.

**AC5 — docs:** `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` (flag table + 'why the gate exists' + peak-local metric), `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` reopen condition #1 (now marked implemented, exact re-run command + audit keys), `RESULTS_NOTE.md` limitations.

**AC3 (live re-run) — NOT executed in this session:** the sweep restarts the proxy/llama-server, which would terminate the agent session driving it (pi itself is served by that proxy). It requires a quiet window and `scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py` green, then: `python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark --sweep --resume 2 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 --warm-start --stagger-seconds 0`. data.comment:
Implemented and pushed to dev in commit 4fa52f48 (branch wl-LP-0MVMBM1Y3001TPRT-parse-routing-skip-provider-context-line, rebased onto dev ba4f1a18; full suite green at the pre-push gate).

What changed:
- **AC1** `log_parser.py`: new `routing_skip_provider_context` prefix parsed into a `provider_context_skip` event carrying `provider`, `provider_type` (the line's `type=`), `session`, `reason`, `estimated_tokens`, `limit`, plus `src_file`/`line_no`/`raw` evidence (`LogEvent.line_no` is set generically by `iter_events`).
- **AC2** `aggregation.py`: `AnalysisResult.provider_context_skip_events` (+ per-provider / per-limit properties). Documented attribution precedence in `_attribute_fallback`: own `routing_skip_local` > own `routing_skip_provider_context` (`own_provider_skip`) > own session-bearing `Fallback triggered` > nearest session-less `Fallback triggered` (legacy) > `lease_denied` > `unattributed`. Rationale: a local-side skip explains why local was unused; provider-context skips are downstream chain-step ceiling hits and are reported separately, so nothing is lost.
- **AC3** `reporting.py`: new `## Provider context skips` section (count, % of all skip events, category-relative Standard/Low split, provider+type breakdown, ceiling `limit` values, estimate median/p90/max, and a `not logged` note), rendered only when the window has such events; header summary bullet; `--json` `provider_context_skips` object.
- **AC4** `recommendations.py`: new medium-severity "Provider entries skip prompts above their context ceiling" rule driven by the events (count, share of fallbacks, fast/cheap split, `limit` values), threshold `PROVIDER_CONTEXT_SHARE = 0.10` of fallbacks (lower than the 0.20 routing-preference reasons because this is a direct size signal); degrades to skips-as-whole-signal when a window has no fallback lines.
- **AC5** fixtures + tests in `tests/fixtures.py`, `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` (parser, precedence, non-inflation of demand counts, report section, JSON, recommendations).
- **AC6** `REFERENCE.md` (Outputs, How it works, Interpreting the report, Limitations, attribution precedence incl. the merged LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES states) and `SKILL.md` output description.
- **AC7** audited consumers: `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` now counts provider-context skips per provider and per `limit` (JSON + Markdown); `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` now tracks them per day and per session (JSON + Markdown). Both extended with tests. `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py` needs no change — the line explicitly records no cooldown / no slot or persistence involvement, so it is not slot evidence. `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` is a one-off analysis script pinned to the 2026-10-18 era windows (LP-0MVDU4FDE003RQHS) and is not a maintained consumer; left unchanged.
- **AC8** absent `limit=` tolerated everywhere (parser, report `not logged`, recommendations, both consumers).

Live check over the 2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52 window: 1,738 provider-context skips parsed (24.8% of 7,011 skip events), all attributed to `munitoai-free` with `limit=150000`, estimate median 201,353 / p90 265,053 / max 322,357; the new recommendation fired at 17.5% of fallbacks. (The item's 8,828 figure came from an unfiltered raw grep across rotated files; the in-window event count is 1,738.)

data.author: pi-agent
data.comment:
## Implementation notes (all 8 ACs)

**AC1 — shared helper + emit sites.** New module `proxy/proxy/turn_id.py`: `new_turn_id()` (8 hex), `bind_turn_id(request)` (idempotent; ContextVar + `request.state` mirror), `get_turn_id()`, `turn_field()` (returns `" turn=<id>"`, or `""` when no turn is bound so pre-change lines keep their byte-identical shape), `reset_turn_id()`. Field `turn=` is appended **last** on every listed line kind:
- `provider.py`: `routing_skip_local` (prefill-thrash cooldown + warm/cold skip), `routing_skip_provider_context`, `routing_hop`, `Fallback triggered` (all 3 success paths, via `_fallback_evidence`).
- `router.py`: `Stream started: provider=local`, `Stream finished: reason=client_disconnect`, `local_dispatch_denied`, `dispatch_first_byte_ms=`, `dispatch_first_byte_timeout`, `Stream error: ... provider=local`.
- `proxy_remote.py`: `Stream started`, `ttft_seconds=`, `Stream error`, `[remote] upstream error`.
- `router_helpers.py`: `[local] POST` / `[remote] POST` (`log_request`), `Stream finished` (streaming, incl. deferred-usage flush) and the buffered (`stream=false`) terminal line.

**AC2 — stability + uniqueness.** Bound once per client request at `_run_chain_cycles` (covers both chain wrappers and chain-hold retries), `proxy_to_local`, `proxy_to_remote`, and `log_request` (idempotent — nested calls keep the id). Held in a ContextVar (one task per request under uvicorn, so ids never leak between turns) + mirrored on `request.state`. Also part of the deferred-finish stream key, so two interleaved turns of one session cannot complete each other's `Stream finished` line.

**AC3 — skill consumption.** `log_parser`: `RE_TURN` + `LogEvent.turn` populated on stream_started / stream_finished / stream_finish_error / fallback / routing_skip / provider_context_skip / dispatch_denied / local_dispatch / ttft. `pair_ttft_to_streams` and the new `pair_stream_events` pair exactly by id first, then per-session FIFO for id-less lines; `compute_busy_stats` uses them. `_attribute_fallback` prefers the evidence carrying the first remote stream's turn. `reporting.py` documents the exact-attribution semantics in the fallback note and the busy-time method line.

**AC4 — skill tests.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` gains two interleaved turns of one session (`turn=` lines with distinct reasons); new `tests/test_turn_correlation.py` (20 tests) proves exact pairing for fallback→stream, skip→stream and TTFT→stream, exact stream start/finish and busy-stats pairing, that legacy lines without ids still parse and pair by the existing FIFO paths, and that the turn's own line wins over a later same-session line.

**AC5 — proxy tests updated.** `test_provider_fallback.py` (`turn=` asserted on the fallback line), `test_routing_preference_logging.py` (new parametrised test: `routing_skip_local` and `routing_skip_provider_context` carry the id for all 4 preference cases), `test_dispatch_log_measurement_fields.py` (new end-to-end tests: one local request stamps the SAME id on `[local] POST`/`Stream started`/`dispatch_first_byte_ms`/`Stream finished`; the `local_dispatch_denied` line carries it), `test_contention_queue_profile.py` (trailing `turn=` does not break `reason=` parsing), `test_model_audit_plan_routing.py` (live audit extracts `turn` per routing line). New `proxy/tests/test_turn_id.py` (16 tests: helper semantics, per-turn uniqueness across concurrent tasks, deferred-finish keying, legacy absence).

**AC6 — other log consumers audited (no change required).** Applied each consumer's own regexes to `turn=`-suffixed lines: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` (fallback/skip reason bounded by the next `key=` → OK), `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py` (`_FALLBACK_RE` trailing-group + `_STREAM_RE` capture `session` before the suffix → OK), `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (RE_DISPATCH → 55656.5), `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` (`_FINISH_RE`/`_START_LOCAL_RE`/`_DENY_RE` → OK), `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` (skip/provider_skip/denied → OK), `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (substring + `entry=munitoai\b` → OK; untracked analysis script, not modified). `proxy/proxy/ui.py` log tail is a pure pass-through (only `slot_log_filter` session/slot regexes), verified unaffected.

**AC7 — docs.** `REFERENCE.md`: new 'Per-turn correlation id' contract block (field format, stability, parsing, exact-attribution semantics + legacy fallback), busy-time step and a Limitations entry updated. `SKILL.md`: explicit 'no behavioural change' note (same sections/columns/JSON keys; only pairing improves).

**AC8 — verification.** Skill suite 625 passed / 1 skipped; full proxy suite 5978 passed / 22 skipped / 50 xfailed; `run_tests.py --scope changed` PASS; deterministic daily path smoke-tested end-to-end against a synthetic log dir (report.md + CSVs produced, session attributed `own_skip`/`context_too_large` from the turn's own evidence).

data.comment:
## Implementation notes (AC mapping)

**AC1/AC2 — emit path** (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`): new module constant `TOKENS_MISSING = "tokens=missing"`. Emitted in exactly the three places a terminal `Stream finished` line can be written without usage:
- `_flush_deferred_stream_finish` (deferred flush on `[DONE]` / end-of-stream when `expect_usage=True` but no usage chunk arrived);
- the immediate finish-chunk emit when `expect_usage=False` (providers that never report usage);
- `log_non_stream_usage` for a completion-shaped buffered body with no `usage` (an error/other body still logs nothing, so no fake stream is invented).
Populated usage is untouched: a present `usage` object still renders `tokens=p/c/t` in the same position, and the deferred flush now always places the token field directly after `reason=` (also fixing a pre-existing dropped-token-field edge when the parts list had length 1).

**AC3 — analyser**: `log_parser.RE_TOKENS_MISSING` parses the marker onto the `stream_finished` event as `usage_missing=True` (never matched by `RE_TOKENS`, so no fabricated count). Window-level `streams_without_usage` (pre-existing) now has a per-session counterpart on `SessionStats` (`streams_with_usage` / `streams_without_usage`) populated by `_SessionBuilder`; `reporting` renders a **Streams without usage — by session** table in the *Total tokens* section when any session is affected, and the per-session CSVs carry both counts.

**AC4 — limitation text**: the *Notes and limitations* entry now names `tokens=missing` as the cause of missing context/response figures (and notes that pre-marker logs omit the field entirely).

**AC6 — consumer audit (verified, no code change needed)**:
- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` — only `estimated_tokens=`/`new_tokens=` regexes; no `tokens=p/c/t` reader.
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py` — no `tokens=` regex at all.
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` — derives context from `routing_check`/`estimated_tokens=` lines only.
- `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` (found by the repo-wide scan, not in the AC list) — matches `tokens=(\d+)/(\d+)/(\d+)`, so `tokens=missing` simply does not match; verified no `int()` cast of an unmatched group.
- `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` — untracked/out-of-repo scratch script with no `tokens` handling at all.
Repo-wide scan for `tokens=(` found no consumer that captures a non-numeric token value.

**AC7 — docs**: `REFERENCE.md` documents the marker (emit sites, position, consumer behaviour, `usage_missing` field, per-session table/CSV columns) and `proxy/README.md` mentions it in the parsed-line list.

**AC5 — tests**: proxy suite `proxy/tests/test_local_stream_usage_tokens.py` (new `TestTokensMissingMarker` class: deferred flush, repeated flush, remote stream, buffered reply, non-completion body, marker-never-overrides-populated) and `proxy/tests/test_console_stream_chunk.py` updated; analyser suite `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py::TestTokensMissingMarker` (parser marker, populated unchanged, counted + excluded from totals, per-session/per-provider counts, report table, limitation text, CSV columns) with new fixtures in `tests/fixtures.py`.

**Scope decision**: the buffered (`stream=false`) no-usage path is marked too — otherwise the "streams without usage" count would silently under-report the exact invisibility this item removes. A non-completion body is deliberately not turned into a `Stream finished` line.

Targeted runs before the gate: `proxy/tests` 5968 passed / 22 skipped / 50 xfailed; `tests/` 438 passed; analysis skill suite 613 passed.
