data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implementation summary (LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES)

## Proxy emit sites (AC1-AC4)
- Three emit helpers (`_handle_streaming_success`, `_build_fallback_success_response`, `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion`) take `session_id=` and `budget_evidence=` keyword args and append the evidence suffix after `reason=`: `session=<uuid|unknown> attempt=<n>` plus `limit=`/`remaining=`/`waited=` when the reason starts with `rate_limited`.
- 8 call sites threaded (the plan note said 7): remote cycle 3 (`_budget_session_id`), local cycle 5 (`_session_id`: streaming success, reasoning promotion, promotion-after-empty-retry, success path, success-after-HTTPException-retry).
- `attempt=` is a per-session 1-based fallback ordinal (`_fallback_attempts`), not a per-request index: the log timestamp alone cannot distinguish two fallbacks from one session in the same second, which AC2 calls out. Unknown sessions share the `unknown` key so even session-less lines are numbered. The counter is dropped on session invalidation (`clear_cached_ratio_for_session`).
- Budget evidence comes from the already-computed `BudgetDecision` (`limit_rpm`/`remaining`/`waited_seconds`) captured at the two `fallback_reason = "rate_limited"` points; the fallback *decision* logic is untouched.
- AC4 verification: new fields go after `reason=`; the three end-anchored consumers (`log_parser.RE_FALLBACK`, `munitoai_budget_eval.FALLBACK_RE`, `slot-persistence-correlate._FALLBACK_RE`) were already flagged at plan time and are updated here.

## Skill consumers (AC5)
- `log_parser`: `RE_FALLBACK` reason is now terminated by the next `key=` token (or end of line), and parses `session`, `attempt_index`, `budget_limit`, `budget_remaining`, `budget_waited`. Absent fields degrade to `None`, so pre-change rotated logs parse unchanged.
- `aggregation`: new `FALLBACK_ATTRIBUTION_*` states and `SessionStats.fallback_attribution`. Precedence: own `routing_skip_local` (unchanged) -> own `Fallback triggered` -> nearest **session-less** line within 60s (legacy logs only) -> `lease_denied` when the session has `local_dispatch_denied` evidence -> `unattributed`. Sessions without remote use are `no_remote_fallback`. The fix for the reported regression: a session-bearing line belongs to the session it names, so no session inherits a neighbour's `rate_limited`.
- `reporting`: `fallback_attribution` CSV column, a `Session fallback attribution` summary line covering every state, JSON `fallback_attribution` map, and the limitations text rewritten as a log contract + precedence description.
- `recommendations`: reason-count evidence appends an attribution-coverage sentence only when lease-denied/unattributed sessions exist (so fully-attributed windows are unchanged).
- `REFERENCE.md`: new log-contract block (fields, order, backward compatibility) and a per-session attribution-precedence bullet replacing the old "lines carry no session UUID" limitation.

## AC7 audit of the other consumers
- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`: `_FALLBACK_REASON` was end-anchored -> now bounded by the next key=value; stale "carry no session id" attribution-limit text updated (it already extracted `session=`).
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`: `_FALLBACK_RE` end-anchored -> bounded; new test proves a session-bearing line still counts in `concurrency_fallbacks_in_window`.
- `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`: `FALLBACK_RE` end-anchored -> bounded; new test file `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_budget_eval_parse.py`.
- `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`: audited, no change needed — its `reason=([a-z_]+)` extractor is not end-anchored; test added asserting trailing fields still parse.
- `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`: audited — no `Fallback triggered` parsing (docstrings only), no change.
- `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`: audited — presence check (`"Fallback triggered" in line and "from=munitoai-free"`) only, no reason regex; untracked local analysis script, no change needed.
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py`: audited — zero references to `Fallback triggered` (pass-through log tail), unaffected.

## Tests (AC6)
- Skill: new parser tests (session/attempt/budget, `session=unknown`, legacy degradation), a `TestFallbackAttribution` class (own-fallback, own-skip precedence, no-inheritance regression, legacy nearest-line, lease-denied, no-remote-fallback, counts cover every session, report/JSON/CSV exposure, recommendations coverage note), fixtures for the session-bearing shapes, and an availability-classification test that a session-bearing `local_lease_active` line still feeds `lease_active_fallbacks`.
- Proxy: `TestFallbackLogEvidence` (all three emit sites, `session=unknown`, per-session ordinal increments, per-session independence, budget evidence only for `rate_limited*`, wire-level `proxy_with_remote_fallback` line shape), contention-queue parse test, and a stricter `local_admission_guard` assertion (session=/attempt= present).

data.comment:
## Implementation progress (AC coverage)

**AC1 — measured `tokens=` on local terminal lines.**
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` injects `stream_options.include_usage=true` into local
  streaming requests (supported by the deployed llama.cpp b8782/e97492369 build:
  `tools/server/server-task.cpp` parses it and emits an OpenAI-compatible
  `usage` block with `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`).
- llama.cpp emits that usage block in a **separate chunk after** the
  `finish_reason` chunk, so `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py::log_response_chunk`
  now defers the `Stream finished` line by one chunk when `expect_usage=True`
  and emits it as `Stream finished: reason=<r> tokens=p/c/t session=…
  provider=local model=…`. A stream that never delivers usage is flushed
  unchanged at `[DONE]` or by `flush_pending_stream_finish()` in the loop's
  `finally`, so no terminal line is ever lost.
- Client-visible stream is byte-compatible: when the client did not ask for
  usage itself, the usage-only chunk is logged but not forwarded
  (`is_usage_only_chunk`).
- Non-streaming path: `log_non_stream_usage()` logs the same line with
  `stream=false` for buffered local replies (both the buffered branch and a
  buffered 2xx reply to a streaming request).

**AC2/AC3 — usage-driven cache credit and the cold cap.**
- `proxy/router.py::_update_session_and_slot` already extracts usage from the
  collected SSE text; with `include_usage` requested, `update_cached_ratio()`
  and `record_prompt_prefix()` now fire for local streams with measured values
  (verified by `test_router_records_measured_usage_for_local_streams`).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_stream_usage_tokens.py::test_sequential_turns_stay_local_under_the_cold_cap`
  proves the intended semantics: turn 1 (30K) routes local; after its measured
  usage the 40K-total / ~13K-new turn 2 still routes local (new tokens below the
  38K cold cap), while the counterfactual without the measurement is skipped
  with `large_context_bypass`.

**AC4 — usage-analysis skill.**
- `log_parser.py`: parses the measured tokens and the new `stream=false`
  marker (`LogEvent.streamed`).
- `aggregation.py`: per-session token totals are now tracked per **serving**
  `(provider, model)` (`SessionStats.tokens_by_model`), so `token_by_model`
  attributes each stream to the provider that served it rather than to the
  session's initial provider; buffered (`stream=false`) replies contribute
  tokens without entering stream/busy pairing; new window counters
  `streams_finished`, `streams_without_usage`,
  `streams_without_usage_by_provider`.
- `reporting.py`: the `## Total tokens` section reports the measured-usage
  coverage and a **Streams without usage** line split by provider, the by-model
  table is documented as serving-provider attribution, real local prompt sizes
  are now measured, and the limitation text names `include_usage` and the
  usage-less count. JSON summary gains `streams_with_usage`,
  `streams_without_usage`, `streams_without_usage_by_provider`.

**AC5 — other `tokens=` consumers audited.**
- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`: parses only `estimated_tokens=`/`new_tokens=`
  (word-boundary regexes); no `tokens=p/c/t` handling → unaffected.
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`: `_STREAM_RE` matches
  `Stream (started|finished): …provider=local…session=` with a lazy `.*?`, so
  the added `tokens=` field cannot break it; no token arithmetic → unaffected.
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`: its docstring stated the
  `tokens=p/c/t` payload "is not emitted in this deployment" — updated to say
  local streams report measured usage since this item (blanks now mean a
  usage-less/legacy line, reported as "streams without usage").
- `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (untracked, main checkout): greps only
  `routing_check`/eviction fields via `^\d{4}-…` line parsing; contains no
  `tokens=` handling → unaffected.

**AC6 — tests.** `proxy/tests/test_local_stream_usage_tokens.py` (emit path,
client-stream compatibility, usage-only chunk detection, non-streaming line,
router accounting, cold-cap regression) and
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_local_token_usage.py` (+ fixtures)
for parsing, serving-provider attribution, usage-less counting and report
rendering.

**AC8 — full suite.** `run_tests.py --scope full --force` → `success: true`,
rc=0, 0 failures at the final tree.

Children 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 each cut through code + tests + docs/observability. Child 1 is intentionally a test-only slice (the regression oracle for AC4); this is the documented test-first exception, not a horizontal production layer.

None blocking. Two deferred to measurement rather than guessing: whether the 20–30k band rate still holds (child 6 measures it), and the remote-spend impact of detouring >25k new-token prompts (child 6 records it).

### What the measurement found (7.4 h interim, 11:46:50 → 19:11) and what was fixed

The budget half is working: **0** over-budget admissions (1 089 `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusals at admission), deadline events **22 / 7.4 h = 2.97/h vs 24.3/h baseline (−88 %)**, wasted prefill tokens **25k/h vs 151k/h (−83 %)**, provider-exhaustion errors **17/h vs 53/h**, upstream 503s **0**.

But the AC7 eviction counter — which AC4 requires to be zero — read **116**, and **94 of those were false positives**: every one had `estimated_tokens=0 new_tokens=0 elapsed_s=0.0` and fired on `Session … invalidated, creating new`. ## Planning Complete — pool-4 snapshot evaluation decomposed into 7 children

**Decision path:** `plan_helpers.plan-if-needed` returned `decision: plan` (effort Medium, risk Medium). The approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (approval is only requested for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk), so the plan proceeded straight to the six automated review stages and the AC-coverage review.

### Seed finding that shapes the whole plan (verified during planning)

`session_slot_pool_size` is **not** a snapshot-retention knob in this codebase. It is:

- the llama-server `--parallel` / `-np` value (`proxy/config.yaml:1649` → `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py:1603` `LLAMA_PARALLEL` → `start-llama.sh`), so per-slot context is `262,144 // pool` minus 4,096 headroom: **N=2 → 131,072 (clamp 126,976), N=3 → 87,381, N=4 → 65,536**;
- the concurrent dispatch-lease cap (`router_helpers._try_acquire_local_dispatch`);
- the slot-ID space (`session._slot_id_for_session`), and the persistence on/off gate (`session._slot_persistence_enabled`, `pool > 0`).

Snapshot files are already **per session** (`slot_<session>.bin`) and their on-disk retention is governed by `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` (age / size / keep-recent), not by the pool size. A bare `2 → 4` therefore shrinks per-slot context and contradicts AC5 rather than widening a retention pool. The plan therefore front-loads a semantics child (C2) and records the producer question below, instead of assuming the answer.

### Children (test-first, dependency order)

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|------------|
| C1 | `LP-0MVOG8SYO006R49J` — Snapshot save/restore benchmark harness (offline, test-first) | task | — |
| C2 | `LP-0MVOG8T9F0031JP5` — Define pool-4 semantics and bake-off protocol | task | — |
| C3 | `LP-0MVOG8TK6002EWZU` — Measure save/restore cost per band under load | task | C1, C2 |
| C4 | `LP-0MVOG8TUM005705R` — Bake-off replay of the 2026-10-24 thrash window | task | C2, C3 |
| C5 | `LP-0MVOG8U4D0026YCL` — Pool-4 go/no-go decision record | docs | C3, C4 |
| C6 | `LP-0MVOG8UE60050SKA` — Ship pool-4 retention and eviction semantics (**if go**) | feature | C5 |
| C7 | `LP-0MVOG8UNX003Z9WN` — Report restore-hit rate and snapshot pool occupancy (**if go**) | feature | C5 |

### Parent AC coverage

- **AC1** (benchmark) → C1 (harness + offline tests) + C3 (measurement run).
- **AC2** (go/no-go with evidence) → C4 (replay/reuse uplift + restore-success rate) + C5 (verdict).
- **AC3** (if go: config + retention/eviction + report fields) → C6 (config, retention/eviction) + C7 (report/observability).
- **AC4** (if no-go: record blockers) → C5.
- **AC5** (no live slot/ctx change) → C2 (states the mechanical constraint), C5 (invariant statement), C6 (executable guard test).
- **Tests** (bake-off harness + save/restore micro-benchmark + pool>2 retention unit tests + report-schema tests) → C1, C4, C6, C7.

Deterministic coverage review: `recommendation: proceed`, coverage 100 %.

### Vertical-slice check

Every child is an end-to-end slice of its own kind: C1 ships code + offline tests + doc; C3/C4 ship run + committed JSON artefact + comment evidence; C5 ships the decision doc + parent update; C6 ships config + tests + docs; C7 ships parser + report section + schema tests + reference doc. Phasing is cumulative rather than layered, and each child is independently reviewable.

### Reuse (no duplicate work)

- `LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE` ("quantify llama-server slot save/restore cost for virtual slots", open, children `LP-0MVKU0RG0002WWF2`… still `intake_complete`) covers save/restore cost at the 38K/72K/100K/124K bands and a virtual-slot prototype. That is a **partial overlap** with AC1 only: AC1's 10k/25k/40k/60k+ bands, the under-load condition, the 0.0015 s/token timeout comparison, the pool-4 bake-off (AC2) and the ship path (AC3) are not covered there. C1 is explicitly instructed to merge with `LP-0MVKU0RG0002WWF2` if it lands first rather than build a second harness; the item is not closed as a duplicate because its scope is broader than the spike's.
- `proxy/tests/prefill_thrash_replay_harness.py` + `fixtures/prefill_thrash_2026_10_24.jsonl` (replay pattern for C4), `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` and `kv_memory_table.py` (C1/C3), `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` and `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py` (C1/C7), `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` from `LP-0MQMC4MNU002QJK4` (C6 retention), and the eviction-save path `session.plan_eviction_snapshot` / `save_evicted_session_snapshot` (C6) are all reused, not rebuilt.

### Assumptions recorded (not requirements)

- The production GPU host is available for C3 during this item; if not, C3 records the blocker and the decision record falls back to the replay evidence with an explicit confidence note.
- The 2026-10-24 fixture and its measured baseline (26.1 % aggregate, 15.6 % median for >20k prompts, 28/227 fully cold) stay the AC2 reference window.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (to producer, OPEN QUESTION):** Does AC5 ("no change to live slot count or per-slot ctx in this item") forbid reading "`session_slot_pool_size` 2 → 4" literally (4 live slots at 65,536 per-slot context), and therefore require the go-path to be a *decoupled* retained-snapshot pool (2 live slots, more retained snapshots)?

## Parent AC2 verdict + AC4 blockers + AC5 assertion — from C5 `LP-0MVOG8U4D0026YCL`

**Decision: NO-GO** on widening the session-slot snapshot pool (`session_slot_pool_size` 2 → 4).

Decision record: `docs/slot-snapshot-pool-evaluation-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` (commit 5cc8d9b9, pushed to `dev`).

### AC2 — go/no-go with evidence

C2 §4.3 requires all six gates to pass; the comparable arm (candidate B — live slots 2, decoupled retained-snapshot pool of 4, LRU) fails **G1** and **G2**. G3–G6 pass.

| Gate | Pass condition (C2 §4.3) | Measured (arm1) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 reuse uplift | >20k median >= 31.2 % **and** aggregate >= 36.1 %, paired delta > 0 | 15.5 % / 25.83 %, delta 0 | **fail** |
| G2 restore success | restore success >= 90 % **and** busy+cooldown exclusions <= 20.0 % | 100 % success; **56.1 %** exclusions (170/303) | **fail** |
| G3 no geometry drift | live slots 2, clamp 126,976 | 2 / 126,976 | pass |
| G4 cost bounded | restore within `min(3.0 + 0.0015·tokens, 60)` | 0.04–0.09 s | pass |
| G5 no regression | disk <= 20 GiB (G5 pair "local serve share") | 2.17–9.88 GiB; local serve share 0.2982 unchanged | pass |
| G6 reproducibility | deterministic replay | byte-identical JSON; arm0 = 26.1 % / 15.6 % baseline | pass |

Evidence: C3 `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_snapshot_bands_20261028/summary.json`; C4 `proxy/benchmarks/results/pool_bakeoff_2026_10_24/summary.json`.

Break-even, numerically: pool widening pays only if >20k median reuse is **>= 31.2 %** and aggregate reuse **>= 36.1 %**, while busy+cooldown suppression stays **<= 20.0 %** of persistence decisions — because a cold prefill of the window's dominant prompts costs 19.96 s (10k) → 480.8 s (60k+) while a restore adds 0.02–0.09 s.

### AC4 — measured blockers (also recorded on C5)

- **Reuse uplift absent (G1 blocker):** arm1 aggregate 25.83 % vs 36.1 % required; >20k median 15.5 % vs 31.2 %; per-session delta 0. The LRU pool of 4 evicts 16 snapshots the per-session baseline keeps (restore opportunities 44 → 39).
- **Suppression (G2 blocker):** `skip_when_busy` + cooldown suppress **56.1 %** (170/303) of persistence decisions vs the 20.0 % ceiling. Diagnostic arm with the gate relaxed recovers +8.73 pp median (24.33 %) — still short of G1.
- **Not blockers:** restore latency 0.02–0.09 s (400×–2 000× inside the adaptive timeout, 0 timeout-exceeded); restore failures 0 (100 % success); disk 6.46 GiB = 32.3 % of the 20 GiB cap.
- **Admission reality:** 687/1,016 attempts (67.6 %) exceed the 126,976 clamp; median window prompt 148,753 tokens.

### AC5 — invariant asserted

**The decision keeps the live slot count (**2**) and per-slot context clamp (**126,976**) unchanged.** Candidate A (literal `session_slot_pool_size: 4`) would change both (2 → 4 live slots; 126,976 → 61,440) and is therefore called out in the record as a **supersession of AC5 requiring producer sign-off** — it is not a bake-off arm and is not adopted.

### AC3 — no config delta ships

NO-GO: no configuration delta, no retention/eviction semantics, no observability fields ship from this evidence. `LP-0MVOG8UE60050SKA` (C6) and `LP-0MVOG8UNX003Z9WN` (C7) remain **blocked**. Note the C2 §5 producer open question only gated a *go*; a no-go is recordable without it.

- Virtual slots (candidate C): `LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE`
- Slot-count re-evaluation (N=2 verdict, preserved by this decision): `LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8`

`proxy/router_helpers.py`: `resolve_session_tenants()` (default = slot count, `0` disables, malformed → slot count, never unlimited), `resolve_tenancy_idle_seconds()` (default = `local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds`, i.e. the adaptive lease base; non-positive/malformed → default rather than an instant lapse), and `evaluate_session_tenancy()` returning `TenancyDecision(admitted, reason, occupants, tenant_limit)`.

## Implementation complete — fixture harness

**Files:** `proxy/scripts/capture_prefill_thrash_window.py` (new capture tool, .gz-aware), `proxy/tests/fixtures/prefill_thrash_2026_10_24.jsonl` (new, 647 KB, 1 978 records + header), `proxy/tests/prefill_thrash_replay_harness.py` (new harness: loader, profile seeders, `replay()`, `ReplayResult`, JSON serialiser), `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_window_replay.py` (new, 12 tests).

**Measured baseline (the executable oracle):** 1 978 local admission attempts; **125** deadline-cancelled attempts (**81** distinct cancelled prefills); **778 863** wasted prefill tokens (≈ the parent's ~780k ✓); **33** economic/idle-bypass admissions, all oversized (>25k new tokens). Replay of the fixture through today's uncalibrated path admits 1 978/1 978 and marks 999 attempts admitted-and-doomed — the defect reproduces rather than being asserted.

**AC2 figure reconciliation (documented deviation):** the parent's prose baseline is 160 events / ~45 tasks / ~780k tokens for this window. Retained logs support **125** events for 18:38–23:47 (164 for 17:37–00:00) and **81** distinct cancelled prefills, so the ≥150-attempts and ~45-tasks numbers in AC2 are **not reproducible** from the retained logs; the ~780k token figure **is** (778 863). The checked-in fixture is therefore pinned as the oracle and the thresholds restated against it (125 attempts / 81 tasks / 778 863 tokens). Every later child asserts against the fixture, so parent AC4 keeps an executable baseline; the >700k floor from AC2 is retained as an assertion.

**Modelling decisions (in the module docstring):** (1) the pinned calibration profile prices the 20–30k band at its measured p75 rate (270 t/s) because the estimator fits one coefficient per context bucket and the 20–30k/30–40k/48k bands share the 16k–64k bucket — a bucket-linear fit cannot express the measured knee; (2) per-slot prefill progress was unobservable throughout the window (`prefill_progress_unobservable`, progress=None/0), so the fixture records `prefill_tokens_computed: null` and the harness models discarded volume as `min(new_tokens, 90 s × band_rate)` per distinct cancelled prefill instead of inventing a measurement.

**ACs:** AC1 ✓ fixture + documented capture command (regeneration is byte-identical, verified by re-running the capture). AC2 ✓ baseline reproduced (with the documented figure restatement above). AC3 ✓ structured `ReplayResult` + `replay_result_to_json`. AC4 ✓ 647 KB < 2 MB, no prompt text/credentials, pytest style, behaviour assertions. AC5 ✓ `test_harness_is_not_imported_by_any_production_module` asserts behaviourally via a sentinel attribute on every admission-path module.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Implementation complete — cold-prefill budget enforced on all admission paths

**`prefill_eta.py`:** the flat cap (`new_tokens > cold_prefill_budget_tokens` → `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`) is now the FIRST bound inside `evaluate_admission`, hoisted **above** the `no_budget` (high-priority) and `insufficient_samples` (uncalibrated) early returns — so it prices GPU compute rather than queue patience and can never be skipped. Percentile pricing now engages from `eta_percentile_min_tokens` (20000) instead of the hard-coded 32 768. A third, deadline-relative bound refuses when `eta_prefill > budget_safety_fraction × deadline` (114 s at 120 s) with `reason=prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`, which is what stops a band-slow prompt slipping past the flat cap. `AdmissionDecision` carries `new_tokens`, `budget_tokens`, `deadline_budget_seconds`; `_deadline_budget_seconds()` is the single source of truth for that threshold. `record_guard_decision` logs the token evidence (`new_tokens`/`budget_tokens`/`deadline_budget_s`) and now also emits for a budget refusal, which carries no priced ETA.

**`provider.py`:** removed the `wait_budget <= 0` early return in the guard (the shared `evaluate_admission` already returns `no_budget`/inert for the wait bound, so never-queue semantics are preserved while the cap still binds for `high`). The idle/economic bypass now consults the **same** `evaluate_admission` through `_idle_admission_budget_verdict()` — no duplicated budget maths — and on refusal keeps skipping local and logs `routing_idle_admit_refused reason=prefill_budget_exceeded` (plus a `routing attempt` record) so the refusal is attributable rather than looking like an idle block. The reserve endpoint needs no change: `admission_reserve.evaluate_admission is prefill_eta.evaluate_admission` (asserted in a test).

**Tests:** `proxy/tests/test_cold_prefill_budget.py` (new, 25 tests) — AC1 boundary (24 999/25 000 admitted, 25 001 refused), new-vs-total tokens, high priority, uncalibrated bucket, budget 0 rollback; AC3 all four paths (queue guard, direct free-slot guard, idle bypass admitted/refused, reserve endpoint sharing the implementation); AC4 114 s safety maths, 25k fast-band admitted, band-slow 25k refused, safety fraction 0 rollback, percentile floor 20k vs 32 768; AC5 warm 47k/549 new tokens; AC2/AC7 the refusal logs `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded` with evidence and produces no `prefill_deadline_exceeded`/`lease_released`; AC8 observe logs `decision=reject enforced=false` without refusing, off stays inert; AC6 fixture replay admits **zero** of the 600+ measured >25k cold prompts, all with `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`, `admitted_and_doomed == 0`, and the pre-change baseline test still passes.

**Regression note:** child 2's `test_budget_key_does_not_change_the_admission_decision_yet` asserted the *pre-enforcement* behaviour and is now obsolete; it was replaced with `test_shipped_config_resolves_every_new_knob` (config surface only — behaviour is owned by this child's suite). 1 301 prefill/admission/idle/reserve/routing/provider tests pass.

No code was written for this child; status was reset to `open` and the worktree removed. This comment records what a resuming session needs, including the **partial coverage that already landed from the sibling epic** LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG.

Its module docstring already says it owns the "post-acceptance eviction reporting (LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D AC7)" convention. **Extend this module rather than adding `local_eviction.py`** — the child sketch predates it.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py::_record_local_eviction(...)` — one chokepoint that emits the event and plans the KV snapshot save. Five call sites already route through it: `lease_evicted` (x3: disconnect/deadline/orphan reclaim paths), `slot_assignment_freed` (inactive-record idle sweep), `tenancy_lease_expired` (orphan sweep).
- Vocabulary `EVICTION_REASONS` = `lease_evicted`, `slot_assignment_freed`, `resident_prefix_evicted_by_tenant`, `tenancy_lease_expired`.

### Still missing (this child's real work)

1. **Reasons** `prefill_deadline`, `no_progress_watchdog`, `idle_timeout`, `orphan_cleanup` are absent from the vocabulary and are not emitted. Today those paths only log `lease_released reason=…` (INFO/WARNING) — which must stay unchanged (AC6).
2. **Evidence fields** — dispatch records (`router_helpers.py` ~line 2361 and ~line 1641) carry no `estimated_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `slot_id`, `llama_task_id` and no `first_byte_seen` flag. Enrich at creation and set `first_byte_seen` where the first chunk arrives in the local streaming loop (`router.py` around `_await_first_byte_with_prefill_monitor`).
3. **AC3 classification** — the current code classifies by *path*, not by flag (e.g. the inactive-record idle sweep emits `slot_assignment_freed`). Post-first-byte evictions must keep today's level; only accepted-and-unserved records become ERROR.
4. **Idempotence** — guard against the same record emitting twice when a release path runs more than once (e.g. disconnect racing the deadline release).
5. **Counter** — `local_evictions_after_acceptance` (total + per-reason), monotonic, plus a Prometheus counter and a `/admin/metrics` JSON block alongside `guardrail_metrics`. Note `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` currently has **no** `llama_local_*` counters to copy from — the pattern must be established here.
6. **Tests** — `proxy/tests/test_local_eviction_after_acceptance.py`: one test per reason (exactly one ERROR event with all fields, none at WARNING/INFO), the inverse (a pre-acceptance budget/ETA refusal emits nothing and does not increment), counter increments once per eviction, and the metrics exposure.

data.comment:
## Implementation complete — post-acceptance eviction ERROR events + counter

**Shared sink (extended, not duplicated).** Per the previous handoff I extended `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` rather than adding a second `local_eviction.py`: the vocabulary now includes all six AC1 reasons (`prefill_deadline`, `no_progress_watchdog`, `idle_timeout`, `orphan_cleanup`, `lease_evicted`, `slot_assignment_freed`) via `EVICTION_REASONS_AFTER_ACCEPTANCE`, and `record_eviction_after_acceptance(srv, session, reason, record, *, endpoint, elapsed_s)` emits exactly one ERROR line `local_eviction_after_acceptance session=… reason=… estimated_tokens=… new_tokens=… eta_prefill_s=… elapsed_s=… slot_id=… llama_task_id=… endpoint=…`, increments the counter, and is **idempotent per record**. Unknown evidence is emitted as `unknown`/`0`, never omitted (AC2).

**Classification by flag, not by path (AC3).** `first_byte_seen` is set on the dispatch record when the first chunk arrives (`router.py`, next to the `stream_cm` pinning), and the emitter suppresses the event for served dispatches — so a lease expiring after a served response stays at today's level. The `idle_timeout` sweep is exercised explicitly to prove path-independent classification.

**Record enrichment (AC2).** Both record-creation sites (`_increment_local_active_queries`, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`) now spread in `_dispatch_evidence(body_json, model_name, session_key)` — `estimated_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s` (from the shared estimator), plus `slot_id`/`llama_task_id`/`first_byte_seen` placeholders and `endpoint`. Captured once at acceptance, never recomputed at release.

**All six paths wired.** `prefill_deadline` (`_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`), `lease_evicted` (client-disconnect release), `no_progress_watchdog` (deferred watchdog loop, record carried through the deferred tuple), `idle_timeout` (inactive-record sweep), `orphan_cleanup` (orphan sweep) and `slot_assignment_freed` (`server._release_lease_on_session_eviction`, record captured before release). Existing `lease_released … reason=…` lines are byte-for-byte unchanged (AC6), which a test asserts explicitly.

**Observability (AC5).** `local_evictions_after_acceptance_total` (total + per-reason, monotonic, reset on process restart) via `admission_events.eviction_after_acceptance_counters()`, a Prometheus counter `llama_local_evictions_after_acceptance_total{reason}` in `metrics.py`, and a `local_evictions_after_acceptance` block in the `/admin/metrics` JSON beside `guardrail_metrics`.

**Tests.** `proxy/tests/test_local_eviction_after_acceptance.py` (new, 21 tests): per-reason ERROR event with every evidence field and none at WARNING/INFO; unknown-evidence rendering; served-dispatch suppression; idempotence across racing paths; the **inverse** (a real budget refusal emits nothing and leaves the counter at 0); counter increments once per eviction with the per-reason breakdown; Prometheus wiring (behavioural spy — this repo ships a `prometheus_client` test shim, so the rendered text is not the production registry); `/admin/metrics` block; legacy `lease_released` level/name preserved; and per-path wiring through the real release functions (deadline, disconnect, idle sweep, first-byte suppression, evidence-at-creation).

**Regression:** 1 273 lease/dispatch/watchdog/slot/disconnect/admission/metrics tests pass; full `proxy/tests` run in progress before the finish gate.

## Implementation complete — usage-report eviction metrics + threshold/triage rule

**Parser (`log_parser.py`).** New `local_eviction_after_acceptance` event kind with its own field regexes (`estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `elapsed_s`, `slot_id`, `llama_task_id`). Because it shares the `local_eviction` prefix, the branch is matched **before** the tenancy branch — AC1's "never a fallback for neighbouring lines" — and a test asserts the two events keep distinct kinds. Tolerates `unknown` for `eta_prefill_s`/`slot_id`/`llama_task_id`; a line with no `reason` is skipped rather than guessed. `LogEvent` gains `new_tokens`/`eta_prefill_seconds`/`elapsed_seconds`/`llama_task_id` (`eta_prefill_seconds` deliberately distinct from the admission guard's string-valued `eta_prefill_s` so the events can never be conflated).

**Aggregation + JSON (AC2).** `AnalysisResult.eviction_after_acceptance_events` collected as its own bucket; `summary_to_json` now emits `local_evictions_after_acceptance` (total) and `local_evictions_after_acceptance_by_reason` (all six reasons addressable), both **additive** — a test asserts the pre-existing keys (`local_admissions`, `local_evictions`, `local_admission_reject`, `local_idle_admit`, `errors_by_type`, …) still exist, and an empty window yields `0`/`{}` rather than omitting the keys.

**Text report (AC3).** The residency section prints the counter, a per-reason share table and the alert threshold inline ("**Alert threshold: >0** … file a critical `test-failure` work item"); the section is absent when empty, so `--quiet` behaviour is unchanged.

**Docs (AC4/AC5).** `proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` gains a "Post-acceptance evictions (alert threshold + triage rule)" section: threshold **>0** for within-budget prompts, the exact `check_or_create.py` triage invocation, the "don't dismiss as churn" reasoning (served dispatches are already suppressed upstream) and the band-calibration guidance. `proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md` gains the matching operator steps including the five-value rollback set.

**Tests.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_post_acceptance_eviction_report.py` (new, 19 tests + 1 skip): full/partial/absent line parsing, per-reason parsing, kind separation from `local_eviction`, no-reason rejection, aggregation bucketing, summary keys (present, zero-when-absent, additive), report text and emptiness, and the SKILL/runbook documentation assertions. Whole usage-analysis suite: **518 passed, 1 skipped**.

## Interim post-deploy measurement — 11:46:50 → 19:11 (7.4 h of the 24 h window)

Analysis commands (the re-run set, window-aware):
```bash
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --start "2026-10-25 11:46:50" --end "2026-10-26 11:46:50" --output-dir ~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-25-postdeploy --json
# plus a raw log scan for the exact event streams below (see this comment's methodology note)
```

### AC1 — window
Certified window **2026-10-25 11:46:50 → 2026-10-26 11:46:50** (recorded, operator restart). This sample covers **11:46:50 → 19:11 (7.4 h)**; the full 24 h is not yet elapsed, so AC2 verdicts are **interim, not certified**.

### AC2 — scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` rate (primary gate)

| Window | Events | Rate | Gate (≤10 % of baseline) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 baseline (fixture-restated, LP-C0MVN90F4F00249RC) | 125 / 5.15 h | 24.3/h | — | baseline |
| Post-deploy interim (7.4 h) | **22** | **2.97/h** | ≤2.4/h (fixture) / ≤2.96/h (prose 160/5.4h) | **FAIL-margin** (12 % of fixture baseline) |

**Decomposition of the 22:** 10 (45 %) are sibling-epic audit loads (`audit-LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG-*`, `audit-AH-*`, session `01a172f6…` driven by LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG audit runs), i.e. test traffic, not user traffic. User-traffic residual = **12 events / 7.4 h = 1.6/h** ≤ 2.4/h → PASS. All 22 share the same shape: accepted (new_tokens ≤ 25 000, usually warm), **zero prefill progress for the full 120 s** (`lease_extended_during_prefill progress=None alive=False`, `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold waited=30s progress=0`) — head-of-line blocking behind another session's prefill on the second slot, not the admission maths (ETAs said 7–68 s for the small ones). This residual is owned by the scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG; follow-up LP-0MVO7J5AF005W1FI filed.

### AC3 — eviction counter (parent AC7)

**FAIL (interim).** `local_evictions_after_acceptance` = **116** over 7.4 h:

| reason | count | characterisation |
|---|---|---|
| `slot_assignment_freed` | **94** | **false positives** — every event has `estimated_tokens=0 new_tokens=0 eta_prefill_s=unknown elapsed_s=0.0`, fired on `Session … invalidated, creating new` for sessions with **no** dispatch record. Root cause: `_release_lease_on_session_eviction` looked records up under the legacy string key while production records are `(endpoint, session_id)` tuples → `record=None` → emitter fired un-evidenced; the per-endpoint lease was also leaked until its timeout. Fixed in **LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D** (commit `fc3c6e2e`, in `dev`, awaiting push). |
| `prefill_deadline` | **22** | genuine accepted-unserved evictions → 10 audit-load + 12 user-traffic HOL (see AC2); triage rule fired, follow-up LP-0MVO7J5AF005W1FI filed (owned by LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG scheduler). |

**AC7 triage rule invoked:** interval counter non-zero for within-budget prompts → defect signal; the 94-event false-positive class is being fixed (LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D); the 22-event class is a second-slot HOL defect owned by the scheduler epic. **The window must re-base after the false-positive fix restarts the proxy** (a restart clears in-process counters) — re-run the commands above from the new restart timestamp (see LP-C0MVO7F2L… comment on LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D).

### AC4 — waste + client impact

| Check | Baseline | Post-deploy interim | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wasted prefill tokens (sum of cancelled dispatches' `new_tokens`) | 778 863 / 5.15 h (≈ **151k/h**, fixture) | **183 832 / 7.4 h (≈ 25k/h)** | **PASS** (~6× reduction; all waste now from HOL-cancelled warm prompts, not budget-thrash) |
| Client-visible provider-exhaustion errors (`All providers exhausted`) | 394 / equal 7.4 h pre-window (53/h) | **128** (17/h) | **PASS** (rate −68 %) |
| Upstream `status=503` | 4 / 7.4 h pre-window | **0** | **PASS** (no increase) |
| `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusals at admission | 1 814 pre / 7.4 h | 1 089 | informational — cap refusing at admission, and refusals fell despite 2.5× the requests |

### AC6 — rollback decision
**Keep the change** (budget 25000 / deadline 120 / percentile-min 20000 / safety 0.95). The budget half works (zero over-budget admissions; deadline rate −88 % vs baseline; waste −83 %). The counter failures are instrumented false positives (being fixed) plus a second-slot HOL defect that is a scheduler problem, not an admission-budget problem — rolling back would restore the thrash without fixing the HOL. No rollback applied.

### Remaining to certify
1. The false-positive fix (LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D) must land on `dev` and the proxy restart — record the new restart timestamp as the re-based AC1 window.
2. Re-run the two commands over the complete re-based 24 h (after it closes), tabulate the four AC2 checks again (expect: `prefill_deadline` ≈ 0–16 user-traffic events for the full window, i.e. the HOL residual only; `slot_assignment_freed` ≈ 0; eviction counter = genuine only).
3. Record final verdicts here + parent AC4.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## Precondition wording corrected — compare 60 % against the log-derived `local_busy`, not "GPU busy"

Correction recorded by `LP-0MVUIMMOY00945D5` (child of `LP-0MVSPWLLP008AQXZ`,
which made the log-derived figure the decision-facing local utilisation).

**What is being corrected.** The AC0 trace above reads *"A comment records the
measured >60% GPU busy for a full night"*. Read literally, ">60 % GPU busy"
points at the **power-based hardware** figure, which is **not** local model
utilisation. The number this gate must compare against 60 % is the log-derived
**`local_busy`** — the `dispatch → finish` slot union. No AC text is rewritten
by this comment (ACs and status are unchanged); this is the binding
interpretation to apply when the gate is resumed.

### Which number to compare against the 60 % bar

| Source | Figure | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Report `## Local model utilization`, row `Busy time — upper bound (dispatch → finish)` | log-derived `local_busy` (`dispatch → finish` union) | **decision figure — compare this to 60 %** |
| Report row `Busy time — lower bound (decode only)` | decode-only union (labelled lower bound) | context / bracketing |
| Report row `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` | power-based GPU activity over the 15 s `gpu:computing:bool` samples | **hardware-only telemetry — never the gate number** |
| `--json` → `summary_to_json()["local_busy"]` | `definition: "dispatch_to_finish"`, `busy_pct`, `busy_seconds`, `decode_busy_seconds`, `prefill_busy_seconds`, `upper_bound_label`, `lower_bound_label` | **decision figure (machine-readable)** |
| `--json` → `summary_to_json()["gpu_busy"]` | `computing_fraction`, `busy_pct`, `busy_seconds`, `idle_seconds`, `total_seconds`, `smoothed_power`; `null` when Prometheus is unreachable | separate key, hardware-only |
| CLI stdout summary | `local model busy (dispatch → finish) X%` **and** `, GPU busy — power-based (hardware, not local model utilisation) Y% (Ns)` | the first is the gate figure |

### Shipped labels and keys (from `LP-0MVUIM7A50053EFN`, commit `5bef959a`)

- The hardware row stays labelled `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)`; it is
  never presented as the local utilisation figure.
- The note under the table now reads: *"It is **hardware activity, not local
  model utilisation**: it counts GPU work outside the proxy's slot accounting
  (other workloads, non-local requests) and misses proxy-served work during log
  gaps. The decision figure for local model utilisation is the log-derived
  `local_busy` (`dispatch → finish`) above; this row is supplementary hardware
  telemetry …"*.
- `scripts/reporting.py::_gpu_busy_json` and `scripts/gpu_busy.py` docstrings
  state the power figure is supplementary hardware telemetry, not a
  local-utilisation signal.
- JSON key names (`local_busy`, `gpu_busy`) and their sub-keys are unchanged;
  the change was additive labelling only. `gpu_busy` remains best-effort
  (`null` on Prometheus failure) — a report never fails because monitoring is
  down.
- Busy definition reference: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`
  → *Local model utilization (busy time)* (`BUSY_DEFINITION =
  "dispatch_to_finish"`, `BUSY_UPPER_BOUND_LABEL` /
  `BUSY_LOWER_BOUND_LABEL`) and *GPU busy time from power (Prometheus)*.

### Why the distinction changes the gate reading

The two figures differ substantially on every measured night. For the
2026-10-29 22:00 → 2026-10-30 06:00 window recorded above: log-derived
`local_busy` = 1h 09m = **14.5 %**, while `GPU busy — power-based (hardware)` =
2h 05m = **26.2 %** of the same 8 h. A decision taken on the hardware figure
would read a 14.5 %-busy night as roughly a quarter contended — inflating the
apparent proximity to the 60 % bar and risking a "gate passed" record on the
wrong number. Compare **14.5 %**, not 26.2 %, on that window.

### How to resume the gate (self-contained)

1. Generate the report for a complete night window:
   `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --start '<YYYY-MM-DD> 22:00:00' --end '<YYYY-MM-DD+1> 06:00:00'`
2. Take `local_busy` / `Busy time — upper bound (dispatch → finish)` from the
   `## Local model utilization` section (or `--json` → `local_busy.busy_pct`).
3. Compare **that** percentage to 60 %. Quote the `GPU busy — power-based
   (hardware)` row only as hardware-side context, explicitly labelled as not
   local model utilisation.
4. Record the window, the `local_busy` percentage and the arm-decision on
   `LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN` before any configuration change.

This comment does not change this item's lifecycle: it remains `status: open`,
`stage: intake_complete`, `assignee: Map` (scheduling hold) and
`needs-producer-review: true`, with its acceptance criteria untouched.

data.comment:
Implementation (pre-commit summary) — the direct/lease local-only refusal no longer routes through the exhaustion builder.

**Change (2 code sites in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`)**
- Direct free-slot local-only branch (`_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`, after `_local_preference_pins_local`): returns `_build_local_only_refusal_response(attempt, config, preference=_preference)` instead of `_build_exhausted_response(...)` → the shared builder the queue/lease `refused_local_only` branches already use. Its explicit `_log_local_only_refusal(_direct_reason)` call is removed because that builder emits the single `local_only_refused` line itself — now with `preference=<parsed intent> verdict=<deferrable|too_large>`, so the line count stays exactly one per refusal.
- `_build_local_only_refusal_response` detail is now reason-agnostic and truthful for every exit that reaches it: `local admission refused: the request is pinned to the local route (X-Local-Preference: local-only / local-preferred) and the local capacity guard refused it; no remote provider was used`. The previous text asserted 'the projected wait exceeds the wait budget', which was false for the deadline/safety-budget and cooldown/lease reasons. No field/header added or removed.
- `_build_exhausted_response` (and its `_local_admission_reject_payload` → `_build_local_admission_reject_response` variant) is untouched: a `prefer-local` guard refusal whose remaining chain is genuinely exhausted keeps `error: "All providers exhausted"` + `code: local_admission_reject` byte-compatibly (AC3).

**Tests (TDD: the 4 new/extended assertions were red first)**
- `test_local_admission_guard.py`: `test_direct_local_only_refusal_is_not_chain_exhaustion` (status 429, `error == "Local admission refused"`, no exhaustion prose anywhere in the body, `code == local_admission_reject`, detail names the pin intent + refusal, `verdict == deferrable`, full `X-Local-*` header set), `test_both_local_only_refusal_paths_answer_with_one_shape` (queue vs direct: identical body key set, identical error/code/detail, identical header set), `test_exhausted_chain_keeps_the_exhaustion_prose` (AC3 regression: genuine exhaustion still says "All providers exhausted" with `local_admission_reject`, and the pin prose never leaks onto it).
- `test_admission_reserve.py`: the queue-path `test_pin_local_refuses_429_when_guard_would_fall_back_remote` (both wire spellings) now also asserts the AC1/AC2/AC6 prose — remotes available and never called (`calls == []`), so 'All providers exhausted' would be factually wrong.
- `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`: deleted `_VERDICT_NOT_APPLICABLE` — the free-slot row `admission_guard_free_slot` now asserts `body[verdict] == deferrable` for both spellings (this was LP-0MVSS435600370D6's AC3 deliverable, satisfied by routing the branch through the one builder).

**Docs (AC5)** — `proxy/docs/routing.md`: `code` bullet now contrasts `local_admission_reject` with the three exhaustion codes; new `error`/`detail` bullet states the refusal prose and that 'All providers exhausted' is reserved for a genuinely exhausted chain; new 'Client action on a local_admission_reject' block (retryable:true → honour retry_at/Retry-After and resend pinned local; retryable:false → compact to budget_tokens; allow remote via `prefer-local`/`remote-ok`; never read the refusal as 'all providers are down'); the stale 'direct free-slot admission-reject 429 does not carry verdict yet' sentence is corrected. `proxy/README.md` gets the matching note in the All Providers Exhausted section.

**Assumption recorded:** the pin-local refusal body no longer carries the `diagnostics` array the exhaustion payload attached (the queue path never did — AC1 requires one shape, and `reason`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, the ETA/budget numbers and the token evidence all remain). Clients discriminate on `code`/`retryable`/headers, so this is additive-in-spirit only.

**Verification:** full suite green — `run_tests.py --scope full`: 6693 passed, 20 skipped (5 pre-existing `live`/snapshot skips + 4 too-large promotion skips). Refactor step skipped (`--no-refactor`) — the diff is two small, reviewed sites.

## Implementation notes (LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ)

### Gap analysis against already-landed work (Step 4.2/4.3)

A duplicate check found the **refusal line itself already exists**: `_log_local_only_refusal()` and the `local_only_refused` token were introduced by LP-0MVRMC275000R2W6 and extended with `verdict=` by LP-0MVSMINPR006SWT6. Those items are not duplicates of this one — neither fixed the false fallback line (AC1) nor gave the refusal line the dispatch context / decision evidence an operator needs to attribute a 429 to `local-only` (AC2). So the remaining gap was implemented here, on top of the existing single token, rather than adding a second one.

**Documented deviation from AC2/AC3's illustrative token name.** AC2/AC3 name the token `local_only_refusal` ("e.g." in AC2). I kept the already-shipped, already-documented and test-pinned token **`local_only_refused`** — emitting a second token would violate AC3's own "countable by a single stable token" and would regress LP-0MVRMC275000R2W6's documented contract. Everything else AC2 asks for was added to that line (context + evidence + `route=refused`).

### What changed

- **AC1 — truthful fallback line** (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`, direct free-slot guard block): `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` moved **after** the pin predicate, so it is emitted only when the request really falls through. A pin-local refusal emits the refusal line instead and never claims routing.
- **AC2 — attributable refusal line** (`_log_local_only_refusal`): now carries `session=`, `provider=`, `priority=`, `new_tokens=`, `budget_tokens=`, `eta_prefill_seconds=`, `budget_seconds=` and the constant `route=refused`, each appended only when supplied. The builder gained a `context=` argument, and every refusal site threads the dispatch context:
  - direct guard (`provider.py` direct block) — decision evidence from `_local_admission_evidence()`, parsed `preference`;
  - contention-queue `refused_local_only` branch and lease `refused_local_only` branch — session/provider/priority;
  - spent-deferral exits (`_build_deferral_refusal_response`) and the pre-loop choke point (`_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote`) — session (+ resolved provider where one exists), via the new `_refusal_dispatch_context()` helper.
  - The guard's own `local_admission_guard decision=…` line is untouched.
- **AC3 — docs** (`proxy/docs/routing.md`): the exit table row states that the fallback line belongs to a real fall-through only, and the refusal section now documents the countable token, all of its fields, and the "no line claims routing that did not happen" rule.
- **AC4 — tests**: new coverage in `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` (direct refusal attribution + no false fallback line, prefer-local fall-through regression, contention-queue refusal context, queue-exit and lease refusal context), the not-local line matrix in `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py` now splits the direct-guard exit by preference (fall-through row vs refusal row), and `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py` pins the documented token/fields and the truthful fallback claim.
- No change to the 429 response contract (body/headers) or to `prefer-local` behaviour.

Decomposed into the smallest sequence of end-to-end slices that each ship code +
tests + docs-in-code, test-first first.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Delivers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | GPU telemetry test fixtures and busy-counter guards (LP-0MVT1NVAJ007KUGO) | task | — | `/slots` + Prometheus API fixtures with a deliberate gap; `gpu_busy_percent` guard extended to the new CLI. Test-first slice. |
| 2 | Publish slot occupancy metrics from the proxy (LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL) | feature | 1 | `llama_slots_{total,busy,in_flight_tasks,sample_timestamp_seconds}`, `llama_slot_busy{slot}`, sampler loop (10 s, configurable), no-write-on-failure semantics. |
| 3 | Combined computing-workload recording rule (LP-0MVT1O4O1004ND6L) | feature | 2 | `gpu:computing_workload:bool` + `promtool test rules` cases; power-only `gpu:computing:bool` kept for comparison. |
| 4 | GPU utilisation CLI with honest unknown share (LP-0MVT1O52G000LMC6) | feature | 1,2,3 | `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py`: computing/idle/**unknown** split, mean/max power, peak busy slots, `--json`, `proxy.log`-absent proof. |
| 5 | Document GPU telemetry, calibration and retention (LP-0MVT1O7AU002CM7P) | docs | 2,3,4 | `monitoring/README.md` slot series + CLI usage + 90 d retention + calibration/re-measure + `busy_pct` comparison; full-suite gate. |

Phasing rationale: child 1 is the verification harness every later slice consumes
(satisfies the test-first ordering rule); child 2 is the tracer bullet (a real
series visible on `/metrics` end-to-end on day one); 3 and 4 add the shared
definition and the query path; 5 documents only what actually shipped. Each slice
is vertical — code, tests, config, operational verification — with user-facing
prose deferred to slice 5 so the docs describe reality rather than a plan.

## Evidence gathered while planning (this host, 2026-10-29)

- `curl localhost:8000/metrics | grep llama_slots_` → only the two existing
  counters (`llama_slots_query_failures_total`, `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total`).
  No slot gauges exist today — AC1 is genuinely open.
- `curl localhost:8000/slots` → 404, confirming the proxy is the only working
  `/slots` path (parent Appendix Q2).
- `GET :8080/slots?model=mxbai-embed` → `[{"id":0,"n_ctx":256,"speculative":false,"is_processing":false}, ...]`:
  this build publishes **no `id_task` and no `next_token` while idle**, so the
  in-flight count must fall back to `is_processing` and say so (child 2).
- `GET /slots` for the large model timed out (HTTP 000) through the router — the
  timeout/500 risk in the brief is real; the sampler must reuse the coalesced
  path and never write gauges on failure.
- Reusable code confirmed: `observability._fetch_slots_payload` (TTL 1 s,
  single-flight, 5 s failure backoff), `observability._query_slots_detail`,
  `router_helpers._resolve_local_slots_target` (child-port discovery),
  `metrics.py` optional-`prometheus_client` pattern, and
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` as a reference reader
  (approach only — no cross-directory import).

## Duplicate-work check

`wl search` over "slot occupancy metrics", "gpu utilisation cli", "prometheus
slot", "in-flight tasks", "gpu telemetry sampler", "unknown coverage gpu".
No item duplicates these acceptance criteria:

- **LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC** (completed) — made log-derived GPU busy/prefill visible
  *in the usage report*. Different deliverable (no Prometheus series, no CLI).
- **LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4** (completed) — power-based GPU busy time inside the
  usage report; consumes `gpu:computing:bool`. Our combined rule is new.
- **LP-0MVSQT7YC0045HFW** (in-progress, idea) — investigating
  `gpu_metrics` as a true GFX-activity signal; explicitly says to check this item.
  Adjacent, not duplicate: it may later *change the signal source*, it does not
  build the slot series, the CLI or the gap accounting. Linked below.
- **LP-0MVSPWLLP008AQXZ** (open, idea) — argues the log-derived busy figure should
  be decision-facing because power-only overstates local utilisation by ~27
  points. Our child 2/3/4 deliver the attribution split that makes that
  divergence measurable; linked below, not duplicated.

## Decisions recorded (agent, from repository and host evidence)

1. **Sampler lives in the proxy** (parent Appendix Q2 confirmed) — no new daemon,
   no new port, reuses child-port discovery and the coalesced `/slots` cache.
2. **Failure means "no write"**, not zero: gauges stay absent/stale and
   `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` does not advance.
3. **`llama_slots_in_flight_tasks`** = assigned tasks per payload (`id_task >= 0`
   when published, else `is_processing` count). On this build it coincides with
   the busy count; the series is kept because a build that queues tasks will
   report higher. Documented in the metric docstring.
4. **Label-matching trap** for the recording rule: power (`instance=localhost:9100`)
   and slots (`instance=localhost:8000`) come from different scrape jobs, so a
   naive `and`/`on(instance)` join yields nothing. The rule must use
   label-agnostic matching, proved by a `promtool` case with those distinct labels.
5. **Coverage maths** for `unknown`: expected = window ÷ queried step; observed =
   samples where `up{job="llama-proxy"}` / `up{job="node-exporter"}` /
   `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` prove the pipeline was alive;
   unknown = expected − observed; computing + idle + unknown sum to 100 %.
6. **Parent ACs normalised**: the AC block was re-wrapped so each criterion is a
   single line. Content is unchanged (verified: 8 bullets before and after, text
   byte-identical apart from removed hard wraps); this removes a truncation bug
   where multi-line ACs were parsed as their first line only, which made AC
   coverage checks unreliable for this item and its children.

## Appendix additions (planning session)

- **Q7: Is `llama_slots_in_flight_tasks` a distinct measurement on this
  llama.cpp build, or a duplicate of the busy count?**
  **Recommended:** keep the series, define it as assigned tasks per payload with
  an `is_processing` fallback, and document the equivalence.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the deployed build answers
  `GET :8080/slots?model=mxbai-embed` with
  `[{"id":0,"n_ctx":256,"speculative":false,"is_processing":false}, ...]` — no
  `id_task`, no `next_token` while idle. Older/richer builds publish `id_task`,
  so the metric is defined against that field with the fallback today. Source:
  live probe of `localhost:8080/slots`, `observability._query_slots_detail`,
  `_slot_context_tokens` (same "honest null" handling for removed fields).
- **Q8 (OPEN QUESTION for the producer, non-blocking): does the "computing"
  definition stay `power >= 90 W AND at least one slot busy` while
  LP-0MVSQT7YC0045HFW investigates `gpu_metrics` as a true GFX-activity signal?**
  **Recommended:** keep the power+slot definition as briefed (AC3), because it is
  the only definition with a deployed, tested series today; revisit only if that
  investigation produces a usable activity series, in which case the recording
  rule swaps its power term and the CLI keeps its gap/unknown accounting.
  — Answer: not yet answered; planning proceeds on the recommendation, which the
  producer may override without invalidating children 1, 2, 4 or 5 (only child 3's
  power term would change).

## Assumptions

- Prometheus (90 d retention) stays the store; no second rotating store.
- The CLI is wanted rather than "PromQL is enough" (parent Appendix Q3) — PromQL
  cannot express the `unknown` share honestly.
- Reported resolution is bounded by the 15 s scrape interval and stated in output.
- "True GPU utilisation" in the daily usage report remains a follow-up item, not
  scope here.

A window much shorter than the live `llama-server.log` therefore shows engine ≫ proxy as a **windowing artefact**. Rather than silently mislead (or expand scope to relabel unrelated figures), the section and REFERENCE Limitations state it explicitly (`engine_cross_check.window_approximation`, tested). 1. `## Engine cross-check` section in `report.md`, rendered immediately after `## Prefill vs decode`: proxy-inferred prefill slot-seconds vs engine `prompt eval time` seconds, and proxy decode slot-seconds vs engine `eval time` seconds, each with absolute delta (s) and delta % of the engine figure, plus sample counts.

4. Honest degradation: missing logs / no eval lines / non-Qwen3 ports / no proxy-side phase samples render `_Unavailable — <phase>: <reason>_` reusing the parser's named `empty_window_reasons` vocabulary, with `-` deltas and `null` JSON deltas — never `0`/`100%` (tested).

Warning recommendation `medium`, escalated to `high` at 2x the threshold. **Fix (2 connected defects in `proxy/proxy/server.py::_release_lease_on_session_eviction`):**

1. The dispatch-record lookup now matches **every key shape** for the evicted session — the legacy bare `session_id` string and per-endpoint `(endpoint, session_id)` tuples (`_dispatch_key_session_id`) — and captures the record *objects* before release.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implementation summary (LP-0MVO9F877008ZCP7).

New module `proxy/proxy/backend_rss.py` resolves llama-server RSS without a host process handle; `/admin/metrics` and `/metrics` both publish through it.

Resolution chain (additive — the host-pid path is kept):
1. Container path (when a container is configured/detected): `podman inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' <name>` -> container init pid -> summed RSS of its process tree; fallback to the container cgroup `memory.current` (the number `podman stats` reports). Container name: `server.llama_container_name` -> `PODMAN_LC_CONTAINER` -> auto-detect when the configured start script is a podman wrapper (`llama`).
2. Host path: summed RSS of the llama-server process tree (router + per-model children — the ~99% under-report case). Uses the tracked `llama_process.pid` only when it is a genuine backend process (never a `podman exec` wrapper); otherwise discovers pids by scanning `/proc` for `llama-server --port <llama_server_port>` — this covers the adopted-server case (`_AdoptedLlamaProcess.pid = 0`).
3. All /proc reads are stdlib (`statm`, `stat`, `cmdline`, `cgroup`), so psutil is not required.

Freshness (AC1): `/metrics` now refreshes the gauges itself (TTL 5 s, `llama_rss_refresh_seconds`), off the event loop via `asyncio.to_thread`, so the 15 s Prometheus scrape keeps `llama_process_rss_bytes` fresh with no `/admin/metrics` poll. Loaded-model labels come from `backend_rss.ensure_models` (router `/models`, cached 30 s with a negative cache so a failure is never retried per scrape).

Fail-soft (AC3/AC4): every failure path is swallowed; the scrape still returns 200, the last known-good value is kept instead of being re-zeroed (only a backend that has never resolved stays at 0), and each failure reason is logged ONCE per process lifetime (thread-safe resolution under a module lock).

AC2: per-model attribution keeps the documented equal-split heuristic; 14 new tests, including one asserting the labelled values sum within 10% of the process total.

AC5: restored `monitoring/llama_memory_alerts.yaml` (75%/90% of 90 GiB on `llama_process_rss_bytes`), registered it in `prometheus.yml` `rule_files` and `REQUIRED_RULE_FILES`, removed `llama_process_rss_bytes` from `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` (comment updated), and updated the `prometheus.yml`/README notes plus `monitoring/README.md` with the series source and verify commands.

Live check on this host (read-only, current dev build data): router tree = 43.13 GB via `/proc`, matching `ps` sums exactly (0% deviation); discovery found the router pid by port despite the adopted handle (pid=0).

Assumptions recorded: (a) AC5 restore-the-alert branch chosen (per the plan decision), keeping the original 90 GiB thresholds; (b) equal-split attribution retained, the `loaded_models` over-listing remains out of scope per the item Notes; (c) cgroup `memory.current` fallback includes page-cache share, only used when the process tree is unreadable (`--no-mmap` keeps the difference tiny).

# Plan Complete — decomposition into 4 features (all gated on the upstream fix)

Decomposed LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X into 4 child items in test-first order. Effort/risk
pre-check returned `decision: plan` (Small / Medium); the plan-approval gate
returned `request_approval: false` (approval is reserved for Extra Large **and**
High+ risk), so the six automated review stages ran without an approval pause.
AC-coverage review: **proceed, 100 %** (7/7 parent ACs covered, no gaps, no
conflicts, no auto-created stubs).

> **Every child is `blocked`.** SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB (SorraAgents) is still at
> `plan_complete` with its own children blocked, so the resolution rule this
> item verifies is not installed. The cross-store edge cannot be expressed with
> `wl dep add` (`Work item not found`), so each child records the blocker in its
> description and carries `status: blocked`. This parent is set to
> `stage: plan_complete` + `status: blocked` for the same reason — unblock both
> levels once the upstream runner emits the `.pi/skills/*/tests` command.

## Features (execution order)

| # | Child | Type | Parent ACs | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Drift guard: resolved full-suite command set must include hidden skill tests (LP-0MVT26OX9006WLCZ) | task | AC5 | upstream |
| F2 | Prove the dev-push gate refuses a failing skill test (LP-0MVT26S4J0021ST3) | task | AC2, AC3 (comment) | F1, upstream |
| F3 | Document skill-test coverage, split counts and the no-pin rule (LP-0MVT26TOD006UT2I) | docs | AC1, AC3 (docs), AC4 (runtime), AC6 | F1, F2, upstream |
| F4 | Verify finish loop unchanged and full suite green (LP-0MVT26XYN003Z29E) | task | AC4 (finish loop), AC7 | F1, F2, F3, upstream |

**Why test-first.** AC5's guard is the only durable defence against the risk this
item exists for (a later `suiteCommands` pin or resolver change silently
re-blinding the gate). Landing it before the proof and the docs means the
assertion — not prose — defines what "enforced" means; the enforcement proof
(F2) then exercises the real gate, and the docs (F3) describe exactly what the
test asserts. Every child is a vertical slice of the gate surface (assertion /
runtime proof / documentation / integration check), because this item makes **no
product-code change** in this repo.

## Plan-level decisions recorded (not silent assumptions)

- **D-P1 — Enforcement proof method.** AC2's "observe the push being refused" is
  satisfied by a scratch branch plus an **uncached** full-scope gate run, and, if
  a hook-level proof is wanted, the stdin push simulation documented in
  `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`. A red tree is never pushed to `origin/dev` or `main`
  (F2 AC5). Rationale: pushing red would break the shared branch and the
  pre-push gate would refuse it anyway.
- **D-P2 — Single documentation touch.** All documentation lands after the
  upstream fix (F3) so the three counts and the runtime are measured once
  against the real gate; no interim docs edit that would need a second pass.
- **D-P3 — Runner resolution in the guard test.** The test resolves the runner
  exactly like `.githooks/pre-push` (repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
  first, then `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) and **skips with an
  explicit reason** when neither exists, rather than failing in environments
  where the skill is not installed (F1 AC5). A skip is visible in the report;
  the alternative (hard failure) would make the guard unrunnable on a bare
  checkout.
- **D-P4 — Numbers are re-measured, never carried over.** The 5 264 / 529 figures
  in this brief are evidence, not fixtures: F2 publishes the repo, skill and
  combined counts measured at implementation time, and F4 asserts the combined
  total equals their sum (duplicate-collection guard).

## Six automated review stages

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — all 7 parent ACs map to children (AC1 →
   F3 AC5 "Decision recorded"; AC2 → F2; AC3 → F2 AC4 + F3 AC1; AC4 → F4 AC1 +
   F3 AC3; AC5 → F1; AC6 → F3; AC7 → F4 AC2). No invented ACs; child AC first
   lines were aligned with the parent AC wording so coverage resolves cleanly.
   **Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: 7/7 mapped, no contradictions.**
2. **Completeness** — every child has Goal, Minimal implementation, Acceptance
   Criteria, Key Files, Dependencies and Deliverables; `**Key Files:**` blocks
   are bullet lists (the parser ignores inline paths on the header line) and all
   paths pass `validate_key_files_format()` (directory entries and
   extension-less paths such as `.githooks/pre-push` were replaced with real
   files). **Finished Completeness review: fields complete, Key Files valid.**
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — test-first order (F1 → F2 → F3 → F4) wired as
   6 `wl dep` edges; all four also depend on the cross-store upstream item,
   which `wl dep` cannot record, so it is in the descriptions plus `status:
   blocked`. **Finished Sequencing & dependencies review: order coherent,
   blocker recorded.**
4. **Scope sizing** — each child is a single-session deliverable (approx. 1–3 h);
   no child mixes assertion, proof and documentation. **Finished Scope sizing
   review: no oversized or overlapping child.**
5. **Acceptance & testability** — every child AC is pass/fail observable: test
   passes, gate exit code, named command in output, counts compared, doc line
   present. **Finished Acceptance & testability review: all ACs verifiable.**
6. **Polish & handoff** — descriptions are copy-pasteable for the implement
   skill, name the exact files and the blocker, and avoid stale numbers.
   **Finished Polish & handoff review: ready for implementation once unblocked.**

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required: the intake brief (and its producer
decision round) already fixed the two contested points, and the remaining
questions were answered by existing repository/Framework evidence.

- **Q: Which enforcement route is implemented here?** Answer (producer,
  2026-10-27, recorded in the brief's AC1 table and comment
  LP-C0MVQJSW91001Y4LK): option 3 — a generic upstream fix in the test skill
  (SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB); no repo-local workaround. Final: upstream route only.
- **Q: Coverage breadth — all `.pi/skills/*/tests` or just proxy-usage-analysis?**
  Answer (producer, same round): **all**, glob form. Final: all skill test
  directories (F1 asserts the proxy-usage-analysis command today; the upstream
  rule is generic).
- **Q: Does this item have anything implementable before the upstream item
  ships?** Research (this session): installed

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Design decisions (all fail-open, no new configuration knob):

1. **Deadline bound is now occupancy-inclusive.** `prefill_eta.evaluate_admission` compares `projected.projected_seconds` (own prefill + occupied gate) against `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` instead of the own ETA alone. Both bounds (queue budget and deadline) therefore read the same single number, so they cannot disagree about the wait a newcomer faces. The reason stays `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline` (one logging/header convention).
2. **Occupant service is priced from the occupant's own evidence.** New `router_helpers._live_prefill_remaining_seconds()` sums `max(0, eta_prefill_s - (now - started_at))` over active, pre-first-byte dispatch records, excluding the requesting session's own record and other endpoints. `eta_prefill_s` is the calibrated ETA captured at admission (`_dispatch_evidence`); `started_at` is `time.monotonic()`. It is injected into `projected_wait_seconds(..., occupant_prefill_seconds=...)` as `max(symmetric floor, measured)` — measured evidence can only raise the floor, never lower it, so absent/malformed records keep the previous verdict byte-for-byte.
3. **Both guard paths plus /reserve.** `_prefill_admission_guard` (queue and direct free-slot) and `POST /llama/local/reserve` share the projection so their verdicts cannot drift.
4. **Two existing test fixtures retuned, not weakened.** `test_prefill_eta_occupancy.py` and `test_admission_reserve.py` pin the *budget* bound; their fixtures project ~112 s, which now (correctly) also trips the 90 s default deadline. Both fixtures set `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 300` so the deadline is clear of the assertion under test — the budget path keeps being the thing they test.
5. **No new knob.** Rollback remains `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off` and `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 0` (both test-covered). Documented in `proxy/config.yaml` and `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

Evidence: full suite green via the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope full --force`), ruff clean on every touched module. New tests in `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py` cover the measured residual shape (own ETA ~7 s, occupant remaining ~113 s, 120 s deadline), the projection helper (multi-occupant, elapsed, own-session exclusion, endpoint scoping, malformed evidence), floor preservation, both guard paths, /reserve agreement and the fail-open cases.

## Implementation + control-run evidence

**Deliverables**
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — window measurement tool (reuses `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` for dot/dash/`.gz` discovery, per-line timestamp filtering and the coverage verdict; follows the `scripts/dispatch_latency_verification.py` pattern).
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py` — 19 import-based unit tests (synthetic logs, no production log needed).

**AC3 control run (reproduces the pre-fix baseline exactly)**
```
python3 scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py --since '2026-10-23 00:00' --until '2026-10-23 06:29:13' --label control-prefix
```
- status polls: **9,484** (recorded 9,484)
- `slots_stale`: **7,543 / 9,484 = 79.53 %** (recorded 79.5 %)
- `capacity_hint`: idle 1,069 / saturated **8,415**
- `capacity_hint=saturated` + `available_slots=0`: **7,807 = 82.32 %** (recorded 82.3 %)
- `saturated` without live local work: 1,773 (18.69 % of polls)
- local dispatches: 59 (15 sessions, 4 herdr sessions)
- coverage: covered, no gaps

**Derivation finding (documented in the tool docstring)** — the recorded baseline was labelled the "2026-10-22 20:00→07:00" night, but its poll total is exactly the *content* of one rotated file, `proxy.log.2026-10-23_00.gz` (00:00:00→06:29:12); the file name encodes the rotation hour, not its span. Its 82.3 % saturated figure is the `available_slots=0` subset (7,807), not the raw `saturated` count (8,415). The literal 20:00→07:00 window is a different, wider population: 17,299 polls, 71.24 % stale, 70.85 % saturated-with-no-available-slot. Both are reproducible; the narrower window is the baseline's own population and is therefore the control.

**Post-fix sanity sample (not this item's AC, for the measurement child)** — `2026-10-26 20:00 → 2026-10-27 07:00` (`--window-closed`): 10,704 polls, stale 34.38 %, saturated 600 (5.61 %), saturated-without-live-work 82, local dispatches 138, herdr downtime dispatches 19 (`downtime-dispatches.log` covers it: 2 deduped by `(itemId, dispatchedAt)`), coverage covered.

**Verdict semantics** (AC1/AC2): exit 0 for a covered window (targets reported, not fatal unless `--fail-on-target-miss`), exit 0 + `EMPTY` for an empty-but-covered window, exit 3 + `COVERAGE GAP` for a between-file hole, a missing window head, a missing tail when `--window-closed`, or a window outside retained logs.

**Assumption recorded**: herdr downtime dispatch counting reads `<shared-worklog>/downtime-dispatches.log` (resolved through a worktree's `.git` file to the main checkout). That log is bounded/rolling (~100 rows, earliest retained 2026-10-25 03:12 local), so it cannot cover the 2026-10-23 control window — the tool reports `covered=false` and states that 0 means "not retained", never "no dispatches".
