## What shipped
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` § `X-Local-Preference`: the `local-only` row now states enforcement is structural on **every** exit, not only the admission guard.
- New section **"Local-only is enforced on every exit from the local route"**: the loop-head choke point (`_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` at the head of both dispatch cycles, \(`_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` / `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`), the reason-recording contract (`_note_local_fallback_reason` → header/body/`reason=`), and the 19-row exit→token table (`X-Local-Fallback-Reason` per exit, with the log line each one emits).
- `local_only_no_local_route` documented as a **refusal** for a chain with no local entry — never a remote fall-through.
- `X-Local-Route` section: `refused` carries the exit's reason token (identical to body `reason`); `prefer-local` falls through exactly as before; `remote-ok` strips local structurally; replaced the stale `remote_ok`/`cached_tokens_skip` example values with the implemented tokens and the `no_local_provider` default.
- Per-reason retry contract: replaced the stale "remaining non-admission skips still fall through … being closed by …" paragraph with the shipped behaviour, and added the honest caveat that on structural `local-only` refusals the advertised `Retry-After` is the shared 1-second floor until the real-expiry mapping lands (LP-0MVQ23B80009OZ9V, still blocked).

## Tests
- New docs-contract test `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`: parses the exit→token table and asserts the documented token set equals the emitted vocabulary (matrix rows ∪ `admission_reserve.LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS` ∪ admission-guard reasons), plus the no-local-route refusal wording and the `prefer-local`/`remote-ok` statements.
- Full suite green at the pushed commit: 6188 passed, 16 skipped, 3 xfailed (dev-push gate, cached entry verified read-only afterwards).

## Assumptions (documented, please flag if wrong)
- Documented `local_concurrency_limit` (fast-mode fallback policy with local slots busy) and the `local_route_unavailable` generic token (exit that recorded no reason, e.g. plain post-dispatch slot-exhaustion 503) even though AC1's enumeration does not name them: both are real, implemented refusal tokens, and omitting them would leave the table incomplete.
- Per-entry `max_context_tokens` is documented under `context_too_large`: on a *local* entry the ceiling composes into the warm cap, so that is the token a local-only client actually sees (the remote-only `provider_context_exceeded` path is a remote-entry skip, not a local-route exit).
- First push attempt was blocked by the live-repo guard (a sibling child session was mid-commit in the main checkout); the retry pushed successfully and the cached full-suite evidence is green.

# Plan — 7 children, two vertical slices + measurement + docs

Decomposition of LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (effort Small, risk High; pre-check decided `plan`, approval gate `request_approval=false` — not XL+High, so no approval pause).

## Dependency order (test-first)

| # | Item | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2 — Regression test: abandoned dispatch not reported saturated | task | — |
| 2 | LP-0MVT2KSC6004UZSD — Regression test: cooldown scope and free-GPU release | task | — |
| 3 | LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK — Abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel on abandonment | feature | 1 |
| 4 | LP-0MVT2KSXY002O75C — Fingerprint-scoped cooldown with free-GPU release | feature | 2, 3 |
| 5 | LP-0MVT2KVVS002YZT8 — Add cooldown-skip metrics to capacity verification tool | feature | — |
| 6 | LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037 — Re-measure one comparable night and publish before/after | task | 3, 4, 5 |
| 7 | LP-0MVT2KWF0000QTSM — Document abandoned-work status and cooldown scope | docs | 3, 4 |

## Vertical slices

- **Phase A (AC1)** — items 1→3: mocked-snapshot regression first, then the abandoned-slot registry + upstream cancel + status annotation + hint extension. Cuts through code, tests, observability (log lines) and the status payload.
- **Phase B (AC2)** — items 2→4: cooldown scope regression first, then the fingerprint-keyed window and the free-GPU release. Cut after Phase A because a "GPU is free" release is only sound once abandoned work is excluded from the capacity signal.
- **Phase C (AC2 before/after, AC4)** — items 5→6: additive metric, then the overnight re-measurement with artifacts under `~/proxy-usage-reports/`.
- **Phase D (AC5)** — item 7: the two doc sections rewritten and code comments swept.

**Between phases:** review the next item's description against what actually landed, update it, then start. Item 7 must be reviewed after 3 and 4 land so it documents the mechanism that shipped, not the one planned.

**Docs phasing decision:** AC5 is one coherent rewrite of two existing sections, so it is a single trailing item rather than spread horizontally across the code items; each code item still owns the inline comments at the paths it changes (an explicit AC in items 3, 4, 5, 7).

## Test-first note (build must stay green)

Each test item is created **before** its implementation item and is that item's declared prerequisite (the convention used by LP-0MVSAM2AV0077UAE → LP-0MVSAMN14001DMTY). The test items are deliberately scoped so the harness can be added and the *control* cases pass on today's code; the defect assertions that must go red are the ones the paired implementation turns green in the same commit sequence. If a red assertion cannot be added without breaking the suite gate, the implementation item may land the assertion and the fix together — recorded as a noted deviation, not a silent one.

## Appendix: plan questions, answers and decisions

**Q (plan → evidence, no producer round trip): does the parent's "Existing state" description match the code?**
Answer (plan, code inspection 2026-10-29): yes, and it sharpens AC1. `_release_unserved_dispatch` (the shared core of `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch` and `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`) pops the dispatch record and the prefill marker but **never closes the record's `stream_cm`** — so the deadline branch only `client.aclose()`s. By contrast `_release_client_disconnect_dispatch` *does* pop `stream_cm` and closes it detached (`_spawn_detached_release(_close_stream_cm(...))`), which is why the disconnect reason already cancels and the deadline reason does not. `compute_capacity_hint` has no notion of abandoned work; `_prefill_thrash_cooldowns` is a bare `dict[session_id → deadline]`. Source: `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (3091-3260, 1120-1330, 3503-3660), `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (1646-1760), `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (11291-11348).

**Q (plan, resolves the intake's OPEN QUESTION 1 — AC1 mechanism): "cancel upstream" or "exclude from the signal"?**
Decision: **hybrid** (adopting the intake's advisory recommendation; AC1 grants the latitude and requires the choice to be documented, not pre-approved). Close `stream_cm` on every abandonment path that holds a handle — the deadline and session-eviction paths gain the mechanism the watchdog/disconnect paths already have — **and** record the abandoned slot identity in a TTL registry that the status payload exposes. The cancel attempt reduces the ghost window; the annotation guarantees AC1's measured outcome even if this llama-server build only aborts at a write point. Item 3 carries a bounded, read-only investigation that records which of the two actually aborts, per reason, in `proxy/docs/routing.md`. Not signed off by the producer: the AC delegates the mechanism choice.

**Q (plan, resolves the intake's OPEN QUESTION 2 — AC2 mechanism): fingerprint scoping, size band, or release-on-free-GPU?**
Decision: **fingerprint scoping + free-GPU release** (adopting the intake's advisory recommendation). A size band is rejected: two different 60 k prompts share a band, so it would still veto unrelated work. A bare free-GPU release is rejected as circular *while ghosts exist*, but is sound after item 3, hence the AC1-before-AC2 dependency edge. Fail-open rule recorded in item 4: when a fingerprint is not available at either the arming site or the gate site, the gate keeps today's session-wide behaviour — the gate never stops engaging by accident.

**Q (plan, resolves the intake's OPEN QUESTION 3 — sequencing vs LP-0MVSAMN14001DMTY): does AC2 conflict with "the gate engages at every local-dispatch entry"?**
Decision: **no**; this item narrows *what* the gate refuses, the sibling owns paths that *bypass* it. Item 4 explicitly forbids touching dispatch-entry coverage and requires the sibling's engagement test to be re-run as a regression. No dependency edge to the blocked sibling is added — it must not gate this work.

**Q (plan, new): does AC1's annotation need a new `capacity_hint` value, and is that safe for consumers?**
Decision: **yes for the controller, safe by convention.** The parent constraint forbids folding abandoned work into `idle`, so a distinct additive hint value (candidate `abandoned_busy`) is the only way `saturated` can keep meaning "live, proxy-owned decode work" while the pool is genuinely occupied. Existing hint values keep their meanings, and `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`'s `saturated`-without-live-work metric needs **no redefinition** — it drops to ~0 because the ghost stops being labelled `saturated`. The herdr `downtime-worker.ts` contract (ContextHub, other repo) admits only on `idle`, so a new non-`idle` value is conservative for it; item 7 documents the rule that consumers must treat unknown hint values as busy. **AC1 mechanism table + bounded investigation finding** (delivered by LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK; also written into `proxy/docs/routing.md` under "Abandoned local dispatches").

| Abandonment reason | Mechanism | Log line |
|---|---|---|
| `prefill_deadline` | **Cancel**: the captured upstream stream `cm` is closed through the shared `_release_unserved_dispatch` core (plus the record's pinned `stream_cm` fallback); the slot is recorded as abandoned | `lease_released … reason=prefill_deadline` + `abandoned_slot_recorded` |
| `session_evicted` | **Cancel** the pinned `stream_cm` of each released record in `_release_lease_on_session_eviction` (it holds no handle through `_release_local_dispatch`), **annotate** whatever could not be cancelled | `lease_released … reason=session_evicted` + `abandoned_slot_recorded` |
| `no_progress_watchdog` | **Cancel** the record's `stream_cm` (existing, LP-0MVIQ0FJC000YLX0) + **annotate** | `lease_released … reason=no_progress_watchdog` + `abandoned_slot_recorded` |
| `client_disconnect` | **Cancel** the record's `stream_cm` (existing, LP-0MVLFVY6K003VYEL) + **annotate** | `lease_released … reason=client_disconnect` + `abandoned_slot_recorded` |
| `orphan_cleanup`, `measured_cache_deficit` | **Cancel** + **annotate** through the same shared core | `lease_released … reason=<that reason>` |

**Investigation finding (read-only, 2026-10-28 `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`):** a real abort IS achievable and observable on this build, including mid-prefill. Of 82 `Connection handling canceled` events, **42 cancelled a task that never reached `prompt processing done`** — i.e. the abort landed during prefill, not at the prefill→decode transition. The sequence is always `Connection handling canceled` → `stop: cancel task, id_task = N` → `slot release: … stop processing`. Reason: `return_progress` makes llama-server write to the socket throughout the prefill, and it acts on the closed socket at that write. So the deadline path's pre-fix `client.aclose()` (downstream only) was the defect; no new llama-server capability is needed. Because the backend can still lag the close, the registry annotation carries AC1's measured outcome independently — the annotation is additive and never a silent discount, so a genuinely busy GPU still reports `saturated`.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
**AC2 mechanism decision (as implemented by LP-0MVT2KSXY002O75C)** — recorded in the parent per the item's deliverable.

Chosen: **prompt-fingerprint scoping + free-GPU release**, exactly the Appendix recommendation, over a size band or a bare release.

- **Scope**: the window is keyed by `(session, prompt fingerprint)`, where `_prefill_thrash_fingerprint(body_json)` is a 32-hex-char SHA-256 prefix over `json.dumps(messages, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))`. Message order is significant; a payload with no usable `messages` yields `None`. Arming sites (deadline, measured cache-deficit) and the gate/cелеар sites derive it from the same parsed body — no body re-read on the hot path.
- **Fail-open, both directions**: a `None` fingerprint at the arming site arms the session-wide (empty-fingerprint) window; a `None` fingerprint at the gate consults **every** window of the session. A site that cannot fingerprint therefore never loses the gate — it only loses the narrowing.
- **Free-GPU release** (`_release_prefill_thrash_cooldown_on_free_gpu`): released only on positive evidence — no `active` dispatch record, a **known/fresh** `/slots` snapshot (`proxy.residency` view), and **no processing slot at all** (a ghost still processing blocks it, which is why AC1 had to land first). Logged as `prefill_thrash_cooldown_released session=… reason=free_gpu cooldown_remaining=Ns`. Everything unknown answers "not free", so the gate can never be released on a guess.
- **A size band was rejected**: two different 60 k prompts share a band, so it would keep vetoing unrelated work — the measured defect (336 of 916 skips with a free GPU, 241 of them for 21 `herdr-*` sessions).
- **Gate engagement untouched**: the same single gate entry (`provider.py`, before the concurrency/queue gates) still refuses, with the unchanged `routing_skip_local … reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` contract. The sibling item LP-0MVSAMN14001DMTY owns entry coverage; its engagement test does not exist yet (that item is still blocked), so there is nothing to re-run there — the existing refusal/route matrix tests (`test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`, `test_routing_preference_logging.py`) pass unchanged.

Test adjustment recorded (deliberate, not silent): the prerequisite test item's `test_different_prompt_is_still_skipped_when_evidence_is_stale` asserted the *session-wide* behaviour that this item removes. It was renamed to `test_failing_prompt_is_still_skipped_when_evidence_is_stale` and now dispatches the **failing** prompt, which is the AC's actual requirement ("the free-GPU release is not a blanket disable"); the unrelated-prompt case is asserted by `test_different_prompt_is_dispatched_locally_on_a_free_gpu`.

Window by reason: `measured_cache_deficit` **248**, `prefill_deadline` **60**, `no_progress_watchdog` 60, `lease_evicted` 7 (0 `slot_assignment_freed`, 0 `idle_timeout`). Deterministic, ordered rules (recorded in the report payload and the doc):

1. **occupancy** — another tenant in the pool inside the dispatch window (another session's `lease_extended_during_prefill`, another session's `provider=local` stream finishing, or `local_in_flight_requests ≥ 2`).
2. **predicted-warmth** — no other tenant **and** admission priced ≤ 10 % of the prompt as new compute **and** the evidence contradicts that price (no backend progress at all inside the lease, or a same-prompt cluster measured ≥ 4× the priced compute).
3. **capacity** — no other tenant and an honest cold price (> 10 %).

| window | occupancy | capacity | predicted-warmth | measured capture? |

| 22-event baseline | 6 | 13 | 3 | no (pre-F4) |
| 114-event fix window | 17 | 49 | 48 | no (pre-F4) |

Second-slot head-of-line blocking is a minority cause — consistent with LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27.

**Predicted warmth dominates (43/60) and is measured for the first time:** 0 of 60 events produced a single `prefill_progress_measured` line inside their own dispatch window, so the backend never reported a first `prompt_progress` event and the priced warmth was never realised. Where a retry of the same prompt had measured, the price was wrong by two orders of magnitude (priced 173 → measured 35 267).

**Contributing mechanism — abandoned-prefill backlog:** 58 of 60 dispatches started **inside an abandoned-prefill window** (49 preceded by a `measured_cache_deficit` release, 9 by a `prefill_deadline`; median 667 s of estimated remaining backend work at the retry's start). Filed as **LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2** (`discovered-from:` this item): cancelling or bounding abandoned backend work is a dispatch change, explicitly out of this evidence item's scope.

- **Path (a) is not met:** 47 user-class `prefill_deadline` evictions in 24 h (1.96/h) with the scheduler epic, the budget/deadline work and Option D all live. The occupancy-only residue (a) was written for is 9 events (0.38/h across all classes); the other 51 are predicted-warmth (43) and capacity (8).
- **Evidence for a (b) re-scope:** (i) the residual is no longer occupancy-shaped (15 % occupancy / 72 % predicted-warmth / 13 % capacity); (ii) the rate to gate on is restart-stable (1.96/h overall, 1.76/h and 3.10/h per segment) against 1.62/h pre-fix and 3.46/h at the fix window; (iii) the dominant class is already being *converted* (248 early releases), so any threshold must count `prefill_deadline` + `measured_cache_deficit` together; (iv) the abandoned-prefill backlog is an identified mechanism a dispatch-path fix can move, so this is not a GPU-capacity floor.
- Consumers: verdict item **LP-0MVRMOV8K0007NFO**; parent AC4 comment on **LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I**.

### Limitations (recorded, not hidden)

`llama-server.log` has no wall-clock timestamps → attribution is proxy-log-only and the backend accounting is window-level only; the abandoned-prefill duration is an estimate (tokens ÷ 43.1 tok/s), never a verdict class; the two comparison windows have no measured-prefill capture, so their predicted-warmth share rests on price + the `progress=0` signature (the report says so via `attribution.capture_available`/`capture_caveat`); `slot_id=unknown` on every post-F4 eviction line, so attribution is pool-level, not slot-level.

## AC3 closure verdict — path (a) is NOT met; the AC3(b) re-scope proposal is put to the producer

**Verdict.** Parent AC3 path **(a)** — *"the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance"* — **is not met**. Path **(b)** therefore applies, and the AC3(b) re-scope proposal below is put to the producer with `wl reviewed LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I true`.

**No parent AC4 text, threshold or AC is changed by this item.** Parent AC4 is re-scoped only after an explicit producer reply is recorded on this item (AC3).

### 1. Evidence the verdict rests on

All figures below come from the measured window recorded by the sibling measurement item **LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O** (`completed`): dataset `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-2026-10-29.json`, report `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`, tool `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` (both on `dev`, commit `56d853be`).

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Window | `2026-10-29 14:08:10` → `2026-10-30 14:08:10` UTC (24.0 h; 52 log files, 353 286 in-window lines, 318 duplicate lines dropped) |
| Restart segments (re-base events, segmented not discarded) | `14:09:25` (75 s in) and `10:35:09` (20.4 h in) |
| `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` | **60** total — **47 user-class** (1.96/h) / 13 `audit-` (0.54/h); 22 distinct sessions (15 user) |
| Cause attribution (per-event, deterministic rules) | **occupancy 9 (15 %)**, **capacity 8 (13 %)**, **predicted-warmth 43 (72 %)**; by class: user 7 / 5 / 35, audit 2 / 3 / 8 |
| Signature carried over from the baseline | `progress=0` in **60 of 60** events (717 `lease_extended_during_prefill … progress=None` lines and ≥1 `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold … progress=0` per victim), exactly as in the 22-event baseline (22 of 22) |
| Event shape | p50 prompt 78 213 tokens, p50 priced `new_tokens` 2 348 (p50 priced cached ratio **0.946**), p50 `eta_prefill_s` 46.4, p50 `elapsed_s` 120.2 |
| Comparison windows (same tool, same classifier) | 22-event baseline 7.40 h: 22 total / **12 user** (1.62/h); fix window 24 h: 114 total / **83 user** (3.46/h) |

**Both landings (a) was conditioned on are live, and the count is not zero:**

| Change | Commit | State |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduler epic **LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG** (occupancy-aware admission, child LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE) | `8b7ab7a2`, committed `2026-10-25T23:44:00Z` | `completed`/`done`; in `HEAD` throughout the window (3.6 days before it opened) |
| Option D (predicted-warmth early abort), fix epic **LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27**, F4 `LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN` | `1908f431`, live from the `2026-10-29T00:10:19Z` restart | fix epic `completed`/`in_review` (2026-10-30T14:40Z); the window is entirely post-deploy (14.0 h after the restart) |
| F5 **LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD** (+ its post-deploy delegate **LP-0MVS03KCV005BTGE**) | docs `f40cc5d4` | `completed`/`done` — the fix's own ≥24 h post-deploy window measured with no fabrications |

So (a) is not merely "still pending": in a 24 h window with both changes live, 47 user-class evictions occurred. (a) is **falsified for the occupancy hypothesis it was written for**: second-slot head-of-line blocking accounts for 9 of 60 events (15 %), and zero of those 9 had another session's *lease* extended inside the window (all 9 qualified through `local_in_flight_requests` reaching 2).

### 2. Three findings that shape the (b) proposal

1. **The rate is a sustained residual, not a burst.** User-class rate 1.76/h over the 20.43 h segment and 3.10/h over the 3.55 h segment (1.96/h overall) — above the 1.62/h pre-Option-D baseline, below the 3.46/h fix-window rate.
2. **The reason conversion masks it (AC5).** Alongside the 60 deadline evictions the same window records **248 `measured_cache_deficit` releases** (94 user-class, 3.92/h; 154 audit), plus `no_progress_watchdog` 60 and `lease_evicted` 7. A bare `prefill_deadline` threshold can therefore be met by converting events into early releases; any re-scoped criterion must count both reasons together.
3. **The surviving mechanism is a dispatch-path defect, not admission maths.** 58 of 60 events started inside an abandoned-prefill window (49 preceded by a `measured_cache_deficit` release, 9 by a `prefill_deadline`; median 667 s of estimated remaining backend work at the retry's start). Backend-vs-proxy accounting for the aligned day `2026-10-29` shows 1 092 completed `llama-server` prompt evaluations against 807 consumed local streams → **285 prefills (26 %) computed and thrown away**, filed as **LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2** (`discovered-from` the measurement item).

### 3. AC3(b) re-scope proposal (recommended: b2)

Replace the parent AC4 eviction clause *"zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions"* with:

> **(b2 — recommended) An agreed residual threshold with a cause-shape guard.** Over a ≥24 h window starting at the first proxy restart that carries the **LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2** (abandoned-prefill) fix — deploy commit and restart timestamp recorded on the tracking item *before* the window opens, and every restart, config load or slot-count change inside it recorded as a segment boundary —
> 1. **Rate:** user-class (non-`audit-`) `reason=prefill_deadline` evictions **≤ 0.5/h** (≤ 12 per 24 h), measured with `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` against the recorded baseline (22 / 7.40 h), fix-window (114 / 24 h) and this window (60 / 24 h);
> 2. **Cause shape:** occupancy-attributed events **≤ 25 %** of all events (currently 15 %) — if occupancy regains dominance, the scheduler scope must be re-opened instead of this threshold used to sign the residual off;
> 3. **Conversion accounted:** the rate is reported together with `reason=measured_cache_deficit` (currently 248 / 24 h) and per restart segment, so a fall in one reason can never be read as the residual disappearing;
> 4. **Capacity floor:** if capacity-attributed events reach ≥50 % of the window, the criterion is **not** certified — that is a GPU-provisioning decision, not another admission change.

**Why 0.5/h:** it is ~¼ of the measured 1.96/h, ~3× below the 1.62/h pre-Option-D baseline and ~1/7 of the 3.46/h fix-window rate — the level at which this residual is a tail rather than a standing rate. It is also certifiable with a tool that is already on `dev` against a recorded baseline, so the sign-off is one reproducible command, not a fresh analysis.

**Why not zero** (the honest reason, which is why this is a re-scope and not a relaxation dressed up): (a)'s zero was written when the cause was believed to be occupancy head-of-line blocking that a scheduler could eliminate. Measurement now shows 72 % of the events are a warmth *pricing* error that a retry re-enters at the same price, plus a 26 %-of-compute abandoned-prefill backlog; 51 of the 60 events are outside the class the scheduler epic targeted, so a zero target would stall the sign-off indefinitely on a class no dispatch fix can remove entirely.

**Alternatives if the producer prefers another shape:**

- **(b1-split)** Keep a zero target but split it by cause: **zero user-class occupancy-attributed events** (currently 7 / 24 h) — exactly what the scheduler epic promised — plus the (b2) threshold for the predicted-warmth and capacity classes.
- **(b1-strict — not recommended)** Keep zero and re-point the criterion at the LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 fix. Zero has now been falsified twice (after the scheduler epic, and after Option D), so it would gate the residual on an event class the fix does not address.

**Why a further re-scope is warranted** (the item's own re-scope-fatigue risk): parent AC4 has been re-scoped once (2026-10-25, producer option (b)). This proposal does not move the goalposts on the same facts — the facts changed. The measured cause composition is no longer the occupancy shape the criterion was written for, and both landings the literal criterion names are live, so the criterion as written can never be satisfied by the fix it points at.

### 4. Measurement plan for the re-scoped criterion

1. Record the LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 deploy commit + restart timestamp on the tracking item before the window opens; re-base (segment, never discard) on any restart/config/slot-count change inside it.
2. Run `analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py --start … --end … --json --output docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-<date>.json` over the ≥24 h window, plus the two documented comparison windows, with the same classifier.
3. Report the user/audit split and per-hour rates, the `prefill_deadline` **and** `measured_cache_deficit` counts, attribution totals (overall and per session class), distributions and restart segments, with the exact invocation recorded.
4. Certify only if clauses (1)–(4) of (b2) hold over the *same* window; otherwise the residual stays open with the failing column recorded.

### 5. AC4 — rollback note re-affirmed with the fresh window's numbers

> **AC4 — Rollback note.** No rollback recommended: the budget change is working (−88 % deadline rate, 0 over-budget admissions, −83 % wasted tokens); rolling back restores the thrash without touching this residual.

Re-affirmed against the fresh (post-scheduler, post-Option-D) window:

| Claim | Fresh-window value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Deadline rate down | user 1.96/h vs the 24.3/h baseline (125 events / 5.15 h) = **−91.9 %**; all-class 2.50/h = −89.7 % | holds (stronger than −88 %) |
| Zero over-budget admissions | **2 772** `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusals in the window; **0** admitted-then-evicted events with `new_tokens > 25 000` (max 23 135) | holds |
| Wasted tokens down | 292 466 vs 648 008 admission-priced tokens = **−54.9 %** (all-in, adding 208 470 tokens of partial prefill burned by early releases: 648 008 → 500 936 = −22.7 %) | holds |
| No new client-visible failure | **0** `503` / provider-exhaustion lines in the 353 286 in-window lines | holds |

The residual the rollback would *not* touch is the same one it did not create: 43/60 predicted-warmth and 8/60 capacity events, plus the abandoned-prefill backlog — none of which is a budget or deadline-maths effect. Rolling back restores the 24.3/h thrash and 648k wasted tokens/day for no residual benefit. **AC4 stands.** (Verified 2026-10-30 with an eviction-scoped grep over the recorded window; commands in §2 of `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`.)

### 6. AC status after this comment

- **AC1 — met.** The 22-event / 7.4 h measurement (12 user, `progress=0` signature, audit split) is re-confirmed against the fresh window and referenced from a parent AC4 comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D (posted with this verdict).
- **AC2 — met.** `depends-on` edge to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG is present (`wl dep list` verified) and that epic is `completed`/`done` (landed `8b7ab7a2`, 2026-10-25T23:44Z).
- **AC2b — met.** Successor link recorded in this item's description and in the related-to comment below; the superseded occupancy hypothesis is stated explicitly; deliberately **not** a `wl dep add` edge (that would set this item `blocked`).
- **AC3 — verdict recorded, proposal put to the producer, parent flagged; closure gated on the producer reply.** This item is deliberately **not** marked `completed`/`in_review`: AC3 says it closes only on the matching condition, and that condition is now the producer's decision plus the re-scoped criterion. This is a gating stop, not an abort.
- **AC4 — met.** Re-affirmed in §5 and in the parent AC4 comment.

### 7. OPEN QUESTION for the producer (blocking the closure of this item and of LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I)

Which restatement of parent AC4's eviction clause is agreed?

- **(b2, recommended)** threshold ≤0.5 user-class/h with the 25 % occupancy-shape and 50 % capacity guards, counting `prefill_deadline` + `measured_cache_deficit` together; or
- **(b1-split)** zero for the occupancy class plus the (b2) threshold for the warmth/capacity classes; or

A comment on this item is sufficient as the explicit producer reply; parent AC4 is then re-scoped on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D and this criterion is applied to the post-fix window. Until the reply arrives, `needsProducerReview` is set on LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I and on this item, and neither may be advanced to `in_review`.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
intake findings (root cause confirmed, brief written, 2 questions open)

**Root cause confirmed** — `.githooks/pre-push` gates the tree of the *push cwd* (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` → `--project-root`), never the pushed `local_sha` from stdin. `implement.py finish` normally makes the two coincide (Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout to the new commit, Step 6 pushes from `repo_root`). The non-fast-forward retry breaks it: `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` rebases **in the worktree** (rewriting the commit) then retries `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)` (`implement.py:4737`) from the main checkout, which still holds the pre-rebase commit. Nothing re-points the main checkout at the rebased commit (`_sync_parent_branch` runs only after a successful push).

**Correction to the reported evidence** — a cache hit cannot come from an "unrelated tree" by accident: `test_cache.compute_git_state` keys on `HEAD` sha + content hash of dirty paths, and `cache_key` adds the suite command. A hit means the gate verified the *pre-rebase commit* (the tree the main checkout was fast-forwarded to), not "an unrelated tree". The retry is therefore silently gating the wrong **commit**, which is worse than a random cache collision because it is deterministic.

**Still unexplained (instrumentation target, AC3)** — the whole finish took ~68 s, and git runs the pre-push hook *before* contacting the remote, so the non-fast-forward rejection must have come after it: neither push appears to have executed the suite. A cache hit on the retry cannot explain the first attempt. AC3 (gate evidence naming root + `HEAD` + pushed sha + executed/cached) is the intended way to make this diagnosable; it is explicitly not a separate root-cause hunt here.

**Duplicate-work check** — `wl search` found LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9 (stale main checkout when the Step-5 fast-forward is *skipped*; same root cause, different trigger). Partial overlap only: that item does not cover the rebase-retry path, gate evidence, or a retry-path regression test. Per the intake duplicate procedure the brief is scoped to the differences and cross-links the sibling; no new duplicate item created. Also referenced: LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK (gate activation, completed), LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ (pre-activation period, completed), LP-0MVQ239VQ001RXZ0 (discovered-from).

**Review stages** — completeness: added AC5 (no fail-open), AC6 (docs) and AC7 (full suite) to the original 4 ACs; capture fidelity: original seed context preserved, evidence correction recorded above; related-work & traceability: `find-related` report attached plus manual cross-links; risks & assumptions: added temp-worktree dependency risk, stricter-gate false-refusal risk, cache path-independence assumption (verified in `test_cache.py`), scope-creep note; polish: brief is copy-paste ready, issue type corrected `chore` → `bug` (broken gate behaviour, matching the sibling item).

## Post-deploy ≥ 24 h measurement — all four ACs met (2026-10-30)

**Window:** `2026-10-29T14:08:10Z → 2026-10-30T14:08:10Z` (24 h), entirely inside the post-F4 deploy window. Reference column = the same parser run over the documented baseline window `2026-10-26T09:06:07Z → 2026-10-27T09:06:07Z`; it reproduces the parent's figures exactly (114 deadline evictions / 648,008 tokens / 252 large prefills / 177 under 10 s), so the two columns are like-for-like.

### AC1 — Deploy evidence (met)

- **Post-F4 restart:** `2026-10-29T00:10:19Z` — proxy log line `Rotated previous proxy log aside: proxy.log.2026-10-29_001015 (pre-restart window preserved)`. Dev tip at that restart was `52085f09` (2026-10-29T00:07:08Z), which contains F4 `1908f431` (landed 2026-10-28T05:49:43Z).
- **Capture went live at that restart:** the first `prefill_progress_measured` line ever recorded is `2026-10-29T00:10:30Z`; every log file covering earlier dates contains **0** (e.g. `proxy.log.2026-10-28_16.gz` = 0).
- **Currently-running process is also post-F4:** started `2026-10-30T10:35:07Z`; 162 `prefill_progress_measured` lines in `proxy.log`.
- **Knob on (not disabled):** `server.local_measured_cache_abort_enabled = True`, `bound_tokens = 2000`, `min_deficit_ratio = 0.25` (`python3 -c "import yaml;print(yaml.safe_load(open('proxy/config.yaml'))['server'])"`).
- **Capture live in the window:** 1,098 `prefill_progress_measured` lines, 345 distinct large (≥ 20k) measured dispatches.

### AC2 — Reason split recorded (met)

Eviction records (`local_eviction_after_acceptance`) in the 24 h window:

| reason | count |
|---|---|
| `measured_cache_deficit` | **248** |
| `prefill_deadline` (residual) | **60** |
| `no_progress_watchdog` | 60 |
| `lease_evicted` | 7 |

Commands (eviction-scoped: the same `reason=` string also appears on the `measured_cache_abort` and `lease_released` lines of the same event, so raw `grep -o | wc -l` triple-counts):

```bash
zcat -f /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* \
  | awk '$0 >= "2026-10-29 14:08:10" && $0 < "2026-10-30 14:08:10"' > /tmp/window.log
grep 'local_eviction_after_acceptance' /tmp/window.log | grep -c 'reason=measured_cache_deficit'   # 248
grep 'local_eviction_after_acceptance' /tmp/window.log | grep -c 'reason=prefill_deadline'         # 60
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24 \
  --output-dir ~/proxy-usage-reports/measured-prefill-postdeploy --json   # wasted_prefill_tokens=292466
```

`docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` step 3 has been corrected to the eviction-scoped form.

### AC3 — Wasted-token reduction (met)

| Metric | Reference | Post-deploy |
|---|---|---|
| `prefill_deadline` evictions | 114 | 60 |
| Wasted tokens, baseline-comparable metric (admission-priced `new_tokens` of deadline evictions) | **648,008** | **292,466** (**−54.9 %**) |
| `measured_cache_deficit` releases | — | 248 (858,903 admission-priced tokens abandoned early) |
| Measured deficit per release (p50 / p90 / max) | — | 17,844 / 51,855 / 87,948 tokens |
| Actual prefill compute wasted by the new path (Σ `min(measured_deficit, elapsed × 43.1 tok/s)`) | — | 208,470 tok |
| All-in discarded prefill compute (deadline priced + early-abort partial prefill) | 648,008 | 500,936 (**−22.7 %**) |
| Early-release latency `elapsed_s` (p50 / p90 / max) | 120.1 / 133.9 / 136.0 | **3.8 / 64.2 / 118.0** |

Method: the baseline metric is the `wasted_prefill_tokens` definition already used by the usage analyser (AC3 of LP-0MVR7DAXH004GAQQ) — Σ admission-priced `new_tokens` over `prefill_deadline` evictions — so both columns come from the same definition. The early-abort class is additionally priced at the 43.1 tok/s prompt-eval p10 used by the F5 replay model (`min(measured_deficit, elapsed_s × 43.1)`); at this window's own p10 (63.7 tok/s) it is 308,111, which makes the all-in comparison more conservative, not less.

**Doomed-class check:** 239 of the 248 releases had a measured deficit above the entire remaining 120 s budget (120 s × 43.1 tok/s = 5,172 tokens), i.e. under the pre-F4 path they would have burned the slot to the deadline and been evicted — they are the fake-warm/partial-reuse class the parent targets, not work that could have completed.

**Honest caveat on AC2's latency claim:** the abort is not always "seconds": 51.6 % of releases were under 5 s, but 26 of 248 (10.5 %) took ≥ 60 s and 4 took ≥ 100 s, because the *first* `prompt_progress` event itself arrives late for very large prompts (that subset's prompt p50 is 67,849 tokens, p90 80,430). Still bounded well below the 120 s deadline, but the tail is real and worth knowing for the parent's AC2 wording.

### AC4 — No warm regression (met; reduction explained)

The absolute predicted-warm count *does* fall (large ≥ 20k with first byte < 10 s: 118 → 48; all large: 177 → 108). Evidence that this is composition, not regression:

1. **Zero warm aborts.** Measured `cache/total` across the 248 releases: p50 0.324, p90 0.663, **max 0.748** — none in the ≥ 0.99 warm band (the 0.25 deficit-ratio floor makes that structural). No warm dispatch was released by the new path.
2. **The warm label was over-optimistic.** Measured ground truth for the window: of 345 large measured dispatches, 88 (25.5 %) are genuinely warm (≥ 0.99), 141 in 0.90–0.99, 90 in 0.50–0.90, 111 < 0.50. Pre-F4 the *prediction* labelled 149 of 252 completed large dispatches (59 %) warm; the post-deploy count tracks the measured share, so most of the drop is the inflated label collapsing, not warm work disappearing.
3. **Warm latency profile unchanged / better.** Large warm service time p50 2.67 s → 3.13 s, p90 26.8 s → 15.0 s; share reaching a first byte under 10 s 79.2 % (118/149) → 81.4 % (48/59).
4. **Large-prompt volume rose; completions fell because doomed dispatches left the pool.** Large local attempts 334 → 381 (+14 %) on 34 % more local streams (13,663 → 18,263 `ttft_seconds` lines; audit-session log volume 10,826 → 35,553 lines). Of the 381 attempts, 211 were released early (144 `measured_cache_deficit`, 54 `prefill_deadline`, 12 `no_progress_watchdog`, 1 `lease_evicted`) versus 82 evictions pre-deploy — so the completed population shrank while warm dispatches kept completing at the same rate.

### Deliverable

`docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` now carries a "Measured result — first post-deploy window" section with this table, the reproduction commands and the two caveats (abort tail; compositional warm-count reduction), plus the corrected eviction-scoped reason-count commands. No code changed; headless report artefacts: `~/proxy-usage-reports/measured-prefill-postdeploy/{report.md,errors.json,*.csv}`.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implementation started (worktree wl-LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ-occupant-remaining-priced-from-new-token).

Design decision (documented deviation from the plan formula, driven by AC1): the plan wrote progress = min(1, elapsed / eta_prefill_s) against the record's optimistic admission ETA. That formula re-introduces the very defect being fixed: the moment an occupant passes its optimistic ETA, progress caps at 1 and the remaining term converges to 0 — the measured 00:28:55 cold 65-89k-token case. AC1 explicitly requires the opposite ('an occupant past its ETA with 60k unpriced new tokens reports a large remaining service, not ~0'). Therefore progress is measured against the CONTENDED full service of the occupant's whole new-token load: full = estimate_prefill_seconds(model, new_tokens, 0, contended=True), progress = min(1, elapsed / max(full, eta_prefill_s)), remaining_new = new_tokens * (1 - progress), remaining_s = estimate_prefill_seconds(remaining_new, 0, contended=True). Uncalibrated contended window => contribute 0.0 (never a guessed multiplier), preserving fail-open.

TDD decomposition collapse: the three sub-items (LP-0MVSD3F2W006LX02 unit tests, LP-0MVSD4O3T007CZRW re-price, LP-0MVSD518N0021FR5 update occupancy tests) are delivered together in one green commit. A red tests-only commit cannot pass the changed-scope/push gate, so the slice is intentionally committable as a whole; the sub-items will be closed against the commit hash.

data.comment:
Implementation complete (pending commit/push). AC evidence:

- **AC1** `log_parser.py`: `LogEvent` gains additive `rate_bucket`, `contended_samples`, `eta_occupancy_s` and reuses the shared `new_tokens` on `local_admission_guard`; `ttft_source` ("local"/"remote") distinguishes the first-byte path. Tests cover a contended line, a `rate_bucket=solitary_fallback` line, and a pre-change line where all four fields stay `None` while the pre-existing fields parse unchanged.
- **AC2** `aggregation.admission_breakdown()` splits verdicts by `rate_bucket` and by the conversion-harness bands; `reporting.summary_to_json` exposes them as the additive keys `local_admission_by_rate_bucket` and `local_admission_by_token_band` (per-band `admit`/`reject`/`converted`/`unconverted`/`conversion_share`). Buckets/bands with no verdict are omitted, never zero-filled. Conversion joins a session's `decision=admit` to a later **local** first byte only (remote first bytes never convert a local admission); a band with no admitted session reports `null`, not `0.0`.
- **AC3** No test fixture gained a field; `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` (469 tests, incl. the guard/contention/report suites) passes unchanged.
- **AC4** Quickstand run over a synthetic slice completed and printed the table. Invocation (also documented in `SKILL.md`):
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /tmp/rate-bucket-check --start "2026-10-28 09:00:00" --end "2026-10-28 12:00:00" --output-dir /tmp/rate-bucket-out --quiet`
  Output: rate-bucket table `contended 0/1`, `solitary 1/0`, `solitary_fallback 1/0`; band table `8k-20k` 1 admit / 0 converted, `20k-32k` 1 admit / 1 converted (share 100.0%), `<8k` 0 admit / 1 refuse. `--json` returned the same split under the two new keys.
- **AC5 (report)** New conditional section `## Admission verdicts by rate bucket and prompt band` (omitted when the window has no guard decision).

Assumptions recorded:
1. Band edges are the harness's (`scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py`); `tests/test_admission_rate_bucket_report.py` loads the harness **by file path** (the skill's own `scripts/__init__.py` shadows the name `scripts` on `sys.path`) and asserts both band tables, the unknown label and the boundary mapping match, so drift fails the test.
2. Docs touched outside the Key Files list (`REFERENCE.md` JSON-key/report-section docs, `SKILL.md` new section + the AC4 invocation) because the new keys and section are operator-visible.
3. The start-phase dirty tree was the unrelated stray `=` file plus an untracked `gpu_busy.py`-family change set from another item; per the Key-Files-aware gate it was left untouched in the main checkout.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
**Cause determination (C1) — which gap the 2026-10-26 incident exposed**

Harness: `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` ("Post-deadline in-request local re-dispatch" section) — injected clock + stale-`/slots` stub, no real sleeps. Evidence re-read from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-26_131429`.

**Verdict: hypothesis (ii) — the in-request local re-dispatch bypasses the provider gate — is CONFIRMED. Hypothesis (i) (session-id arm/check mismatch) is REFUTED for the incident session, but is REAL for header-less sessions and, additionally, the arm/check *fingerprint* components disagree today.**

1. **Bypass path (confirmed).** After `prefill_deadline_exceeded` the router releases the lease and returns a backend error response (`_build_backend_error_response`). `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` then runs its local retry loops — `local_slot_exhaustion_retry` (provider.py `_dispatch_local` call site) and `local_http_retry` (the `status_code >= 500` branch) — which call `_dispatch_local(ptr_local, …)` → `proxy_to_local` **directly**, without re-entering the local-branch gate. That matches the log exactly: `[local] POST` at +150 ms / +147 ms after each `lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`, no `routing_skip_local`, no provider-cooldown line. The gap matches config: `local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts: 2` and `local_slot_exhaustion_retry_delay_seconds: 0.1` (`proxy/config.yaml`). Pinned red by `test_in_request_redispatch_after_the_deadline_is_not_admitted` (fresh active record + marker re-armed at +0.15 s, next session denied again).

2. **Session key parity (incident shape = OK).** The incident request carried `x-client-request-id` + `x-session-affinity` and the router logged `Session header resolved: source=session_id`; `_resolve_session_id_header` (provider.py's resolver) returns the same id the router armed the window under. The green control `test_the_gate_engages_when_the_incident_session_is_checked` proves the gate refuses the attempt and logs `routing_skip_local … reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` whenever it is consulted — so the missing skip lines in the incident are the bypass, not a key mismatch.

3. **NEW gap (a): header-less sessions can never engage the cooldown.** `_handle_session` → `session_manager.get_or_create(None)` *generates* a session id, which router.py arms under, while provider.py's gate resolves the request headers itself and gets `None` → `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining(None)` is always 0. Red: `test_a_header_less_session_cannot_engage_the_gate`.

4. **NEW gap (b): the fingerprint components disagree (post-2026-10-29).** Since LP-0MVT2KSXY002O75C the window is keyed `(session, prompt fingerprint)`, but router.py arms it from the `body_json` `_handle_session` has already rewritten to the *delta* messages it is about to prefill, while provider.py fingerprints the *original* request body. For any continuing session (the incident's had 5-8 messages) the digests differ, so the gate looks up a key nobody armed and never skips — the same non-engagement one level down. Red: `test_delta_arm_fingerprint_matches_the_gate_check_fingerprint`.

**Recommendation for C2:** make the post-deadline detour terminal for local *within the request* (the primary contract of AC6 — e.g. the retry loops consult the thrash gate before re-dispatching, or the request carries a `prefill_deadline` detour marker), and close (a)/(b) so the cooldown is not silently un-engaged for anonymous/continuing sessions. Cooldown-only fixes cannot satisfy AC6 for header-less requests, and capping renewals (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0 shape) leaves the gate un-engaged.

**Regression pin (green today):** `test_same_session_reacquisition_hold_is_bounded_within_300s` — a legitimate same-session re-acquisition extended every poll by the in-flight signal is still released by the no-progress watchdog at ≈190 s simulated (≤300 s), without weakening the 180 s watchdog or the 10 s sweep cadence (parent AC3 / this item's AC4, AC7).

Red-first encoding: the four failing assertions are `xfail(strict=True)` so this test-only slice lands green; C2 removes each marker as it fixes the gap. Verified red for the intended reason via `PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--runxfail run_tests.py --suite pytest --scope changed --no-cache`.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
C2 implementation (verified against C1's red-first tests, now unmarked and green).

Cause determination (the OPEN QUESTION from intake, answered):
- **Bypass is real (hypothesis ii).** provider.py's chain gate runs once per chain resolution; the in-request local retry loops (local_slot_exhaustion_retry / local_http_retry, and ui.py's direct dispatch) re-enter proxy_to_local *after* that decision, so the armed 600 s window produced zero skip lines for the affected session.
- **Arm/check key mismatch is also real (hypothesis i), in two independent forms:** (a) a header-less request arms under the session id the *router generated*, which no gate site can re-derive from headers; (b) router.py armed from the post-delta body_json while provider.py fingerprints the original client body, so a continuing session's two digests never matched (post-2026-10-29 fingerprint scoping).

Changes:
1. AC1 — the gate now sits at the acquisition choke points: `proxy_to_local` refuses before any local resource is acquired (covers the anonymous `_increment_local_active_queries` path and ui.py's direct dispatch) and `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` refuses before the record is created. Both log `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` with `entry=router_dispatch`/`entry=lease_acquire`; the response is the retryable 503 backend_error shape (deliberately NOT local_lease_active/no_slots_available, which would make provider queue for a slot the gate refuses). The free-GPU release stays at provider.py's chain entry — the choke point is deterministic by design.
2. AC2 — `_mark_local_dispatch_terminal(request)` on prefill_deadline_exceeded (and the measured-cache-deficit twin) makes local terminal *for that request*; refused as `reason=post_deadline_terminal`. The marker lives on the Request object, so concurrent requests from the same session are unaffected (session cooldown covers those).
3. AC2 — `_prefill_thrash_fingerprint` is now turn-scoped (messages after the last assistant message), so the router's delta body and provider.py's original body agree; router.py additionally captures the *original* client fingerprint before `_handle_session` rewrites the body, and all three arm/clear sites use it.
4. AC3 — `_release_unserved_dispatch` ordering is now documented and pinned: record + local_prefill_in_flight marker removed first, upstream stream closed and *awaited* (bounded by `server.disconnect_cleanup_timeout`, default 5 s, replacing the hard-coded 5.0) before returning, so no stale-marker re-extension.
5. AC4 — unchanged watchdog/sweep; the choke point removes the re-acquisition path that made the 308 s hold possible (C1's ≤300 s bound test green).

Behaviour change recorded (AC5): the first-byte clear remains wired and fingerprint/size-scoped, but because the gate now refuses a cooling-down session *before* dispatch, a live window is in practice released by expiry or the free-GPU proof. test_router_successful_first_byte_clears_the_cooldown was re-pinned accordingly (spy on the clear with the original fingerprint + estimated size, plus 'a success on prompt P must not release the window armed by prompt Q').

Tests: 4 C1 xfail(strict) markers removed (gate engagement, header-less, delta fingerprint, marker re-extension) all green; added 8 tests (choke point + log + rollback knob + fail-open, request-scoped marker end-to-end and concurrency isolation, router-level refusal for both reasons, turn-scoped fingerprint scope, release ordering with a recording stream, close-timeout config). Docs: proxy/docs/routing.md cooldown section + refusal matrix row.

## Intake blocked on producer decisions (Map, 2026-10-29)

The intake brief is drafted and written to this item's description (problem statement, measured evidence, 5 ACs, constraints, key files, related work, Appendix). Three decisions need the producer before the AC set can be frozen — the item's own description poses the first one ("calibrate or label"), and nothing in the repo answers it.

### Q1 — Semantics of the published field

`prefill_eta_seconds` on `/llama/local/status` is published as the **cache-cold reference-prompt cost** (all publication sites pass `cached_ratio = 0.0`) but is consumed as an expected wait. Options:

- **(a)** Keep `prefill_eta_seconds` as the cache-cold reference bound; add explicit labelling fields (`prefill_eta_kind`, assumed cached ratio, reference tokens) + documentation.
- **(b)** Rename to `prefill_eta_cold_bound_seconds`; publish a served-distribution estimate as `prefill_eta_seconds` (breaking change for external dispatchers).
- **(c)** Add per-request query parameters (`?prompt_tokens=&cached_ratio=`) so a dispatcher gets its own request's cost.

**Recommended:** (a) — fixes the misreading for every consumer without breaking an external payload contract, and leaves the conservative guard semantics untouched; (c) can follow as a linked item.

**Explicitly NOT recommended:** scaling the coefficients to match the observed `prompt eval time` distribution. That distribution is dominated by cache-warm remainders (66 % of dispatches warm, `cached_ratio` p50 0.957; median 999 new tokens evaluated), so matching it would make the admission guard admit cache-cold large prompts it currently refuses — a GPU-wasting safety regression.

### Q2 — Metric ownership / repository boundary

The M3 fix requires editing `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`log_parser.py`, `reporting.py`, `REFERENCE.md`), which the project AGENTS.md puts off-limits "unless explicitly instructed".

- **(a)** Authorise the `.pi/` edit in this item (recommended — the proxy log-line change and the parser change must land together to be verifiable in one window).
- **(b)** Split the metric fix into a child item for a separate approval trail.

### Q3 — Tolerance for a bound

`PREFILL_ETA_MATCH_TOLERANCE_PCT = 25` is two-sided and applied to a cross-population comparison, so it will always report `over_predicts` for a cache-cold bound.

- **(a)** Replace it with a one-sided "bound must not be violated" test (recommended: `bound_holds` when observed p90 ≤ predicted p50, with counts; `inconclusive` below 30 observed samples), retaining the 25 % two-sided tolerance *only* for the new matched per-dispatch figure.
- **(b)** Keep the current two-sided verdict and rely on the prose caveat.

### Gate state

- Effort/risk estimate is **not** run: `orchestrate_estimate.py` gates on `stage in (intake_complete, plan_complete)`, and the stage is deliberately left at `idea` until Q1–Q3 are answered (the ACs are conditional on Q1).
- Assignee released; `needs-producer-review` set.

- **Commit fad873c7** (LP-0MVSD5RJW008F1IB: Implementation complete) — follow-up found during post-push verification: the matched-accuracy pair split mis-read the guard line's `enforced` token. On the decision line `enforced` means "the refusal was applied" (it is `false` for every admit), so grouping `enforced=false` as "observe policy" mislabelled 711 of 715 real pairs. The split is now decided by the `policy=` token (`admitted_pairs` / `observe_pairs`) and an **enforced refusal is never a pairing candidate** (it refused that request, so a later first byte in the same session belongs to another request) — those records are counted as `enforced_refusals`.

### What shipped

- **AC1 matched accuracy** — `prefill_eta_error.matched`: guard `eta_prefill_s` (own-prefill term) joined by `session=` to that dispatch's `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms`; 25 % two-sided tolerance; unmatched dispatches counted, never folded in.
- **AC2 labelling** — payload (top level + every slot) publishes `prefill_eta_kind=reference_cold_bound`, `prefill_eta_assumed_cached_ratio=0.0`, `prefill_eta_reference_tokens`; one-sentence statement in `docs/llama-router.md` (§ Published prefill-ETA semantics) pinned by a test.
- **AC3 one-sided bound** — `bound_holds`/`bound_violated`/`inconclusive` (observed p90 ≤ predicted p50, floor 30 samples) replaces the two-sided `over_predicts` wording for the cross-population comparison; legacy JSON keys retained.
- **AC4 de-poisoned reference** — `local_admission_guard_reference_window_samples` (shipped 20, `0` = documented rollback to the last dispatch) makes the published reference a rolling **median**; `local_admission_guard_reference_max_tokens` (`0`/absent = uncapped) is the optional ceiling.
- **AC5 docs** — `prefill_eta.py` docstrings/constants, `handlers.py`, `observability.py`, `REFERENCE.md`, `SKILL.md` (M3 wording), `docs/llama-router.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/config.yaml`.
- **AC6 poll-log context** — `status_request` now appends `prefill_eta_reference_tokens`, `prefill_eta_calibrated`, `prefill_eta_rate_bucket`, `prefill_eta_samples`, `prefill_eta_kind`, `prefill_eta_assumed_cached_ratio`; parsed into `status_request_events`; existing `RE_STATUS_*` regexes, the `prefill_eta_error` JSON keys and `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` are pinned unchanged by regression tests.

### Measured figures (24 h window 2026-10-30 00:23 → 2026-10-31 00:23, real logs)

`analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24 --json`:

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Bound vs served remainder | predicted p50 **27.5 s** (n=18 123 polls) vs observed p90 **19.66 s** (n=1 003) → **bound_holds** (margin 7.84 s) |
| Matched per-dispatch | 714 pairs (714 admitted, 0 observe-policy; 834 enforced refusals excluded; 79 of 793 dispatches unmatched): predicted p50 **7.0 s** vs observed p50 **3.16 s** → median relative error **+29.2 %** → **over_predicts** (just outside the 25 % tolerance) |

Interpretation: the published bound is **not** violated on real traffic (the old metric asserted a +700 % "over-prediction" that was purely a cross-population artefact), and the guard's own per-request pricing is ~29 % conservative at the median — the safe direction, so no coefficient change was made (see the item's explicit constraint). A future window can decide whether a modest tightening is warranted; that would be a new item.

Note: today's logs predate the proxy restart, so the enriched poll fields only appear once the proxy is restarted with this code; the matched figure needed no new fields (it joins existing `local_admission_guard` and `dispatch_first_byte_ms` lines) and is therefore already measured on live data.

### Decisions taken during planning

1. **No decomposition into children.** The item is a single test-only slice whose eight matrix rows all land in the same three shared suites (`test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`, `test_local_admission_guard.py`, `test_admission_reserve.py`) plus the retry-docs assertions. Splitting rows into child items would fragment one change-set across shared fixtures, and no child would be independently verifiable or independently deliverable — the "vertical slice" test fails for every candidate cut. This is the same reason the epic's own plan (LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY, decision 3) recorded this item as intentionally horizontal.
2. **No rename of `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`.** The option allowed by the deliverable ("rename semantics or add a sibling file") is declined: a rename breaks citations in `proxy/docs/routing.md`, in sibling work items (LP-0MVRMC0Z500883O0, LP-0MVRMC2HT004NPO6) and in `test_local_admission_retry_docs.py`, for no behavioural gain. The file keeps its name; its module docstring is retitled to "local-pinned refusal matrix (`local-preferred`, legacy `local-only` alias)" — cheaper, and it preserves git history for the 12 landed rows.
3. **Preference becomes an axis, not a second table.** Adding `local-preferred` / legacy-`local-only` as a parameter axis over the existing `_ExitRow` table reuses 12 exit fixtures instead of restating them; a duplicated exit description is precisely the drift this matrix exists to catch.
4. **The verdict vocabulary is imported, not re-declared.** Tests assert through the production `local_capacity_verdict(...)` helper and the production retry-timing helper so a rename in LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ fails in one place. Only the incident regression pins literals (the 2026-10-28 log numbers).
5. **Status held at `blocked` on completion.** The three prerequisite children are still `open`/`blocked`, so the item is left `status=blocked, stage=plan_complete` instead of the skill's `status=open` transition — `open` would make it dispatchable for implementation before its dependencies exist. Deliberate, reversible, and recorded here.

### Six automated review stages

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — each AC traces to a stated requirement (AC1←"each row asserts", AC2←incident regression deliverable/parent AC7, AC3←gate requirement, AC4←readability, AC5←docs scope, AC6←suite green). No contradictory or invented AC found; AC4 needed a testable expression, added as a parametrisation-id note (see stage 5) rather than as a changed AC.
2. **Completeness** — required fields present; `**Key Files**` validated syntactically and against the real files (`test_local_admission_retry_docs.py` confirmed to exist, i.e. no predicted-only path). Added `Existing state` so the four files' reusable fixtures are discoverable.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — the dependency edges are coherent (vocabulary → verdict → chain → tests) and the test item is correctly last. Test-first ordering is not violated: the three prerequisite children each land their own tests with their slice; making this matrix a prerequisite would deadlock the graph. Recorded explicitly in `## Dependency & sequencing`.
4. **Scope sizing** — one deliverable increment (see decision 1); no child creation needed.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — every AC is pass/fail decidable. AC4 ("test names state the behaviour") was made concrete by requiring behaviour-composed parametrisation ids for the new rows while leaving the 12 landed per-exit ids unchanged.
6. **Polish & handoff** — description reads top-to-bottom as goal → matrix → per-row detail → dependency → existing state → reuse notes → open question → ACs → key files; section headings follow the sibling children's convention.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required, and **no questions were directed to the producer** — the item arrived from the producer-authored epic with a full matrix, deliverables, ACs and predicted key files, and every open point was answerable from repository evidence. Items considered, and where each was settled:

- Q (internal): How is "no remote dispatch" observed at each layer? Answer: `patch("proxy.server.proxy_to_remote", ...)` at reserve level and `patch("proxy.provider._get_proxy_to_remote", ...)` at dispatch-loop level. Evidence: `test_admission_reserve.py` ≈443/489/530/604/642, `test_chain_hold.py`.

**Intake paused — 3 producer questions (Q1–Q3).** Draft brief written to the description; stage left at `idea` pending answers. Duplicate check performed: no *full* duplicate, but **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3** (open) already requires the same hook invariant for the non-fast-forward retry path — see Q2.

Evidence gathered before asking: `.githooks/pre-push` captures the pushed refs on stdin but **discards `local_sha`** (only `remote_ref` is used); the gate runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` i.e. the push cwd = main checkout; `test_cache.compute_git_state()` keys on `HEAD` + dirty-path content, so a stale+dirty checkout has its *own* valid fingerprint and a prior green run there is a legitimate cache hit; `implement.py` Step 5 only logs a warning when the fast-forward is skipped and still pushes from `repo_root`; `tests/test_git_hooks.py::_hook()` always sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`, so no test can express 'pushed commit ≠ checked-out tree'; the main checkout is currently clean.

**Q1 — fix shape and repository.** Which do you want?
- **A:** repo-local fail-closed guard in `.githooks/pre-push`: refuse a `refs/heads/dev|main` push when the checkout's `HEAD` ≠ the gated `local_sha`, naming both SHAs, the tree path, the recovery step; regression test in `tests/test_git_hooks.py`; framework improvement as a linked follow-up.
- **B:** repo-local "gate the pushed commit": check out `local_sha` into a throwaway detached worktree inside the hook, run the suite with `--project-root <worktree>`, mirror the cache entry so it lands at the pushed commit.
- **C:** framework-only (`implement.py`: push from the worktree / verify the pushed commit / name the verified tree in the finish report) — needs explicit authorisation to edit agent-infrastructure files, tracked under a SorraAgents item.

**Recommended:** A — smallest deterministic change, testable in the existing hermetic sandbox, no worktree lifecycle inside a git hook, and it composes with B/C later.

**Q2 — overlap with LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3.** That open item already requires "`HEAD` ≠ pushed `local_sha` must never silently verify the wrong tree: gate it correctly or refuse with an actionable message" (retry path). This item's guard would satisfy both.
- **A:** transfer this item's distinct ACs (dirty-main-checkout reproduction test; cache entry keyed to the pushed commit) onto LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 and close this item as a duplicate.
- **B:** keep both; implement the shared guard **once** under whichever is scheduled first and link the other as verification-only.

**Recommended:** B — the triggers are distinct regression scenarios worth naming in tests, but only one implementation should exist.

**Q3 — strictness when `HEAD` == `local_sha` but the tree is dirty.**
- **A:** run the gate anyway, warning that the tree is not the pushed commit.
- **B:** refuse — a dirty tree's fingerprint can never equal the pushed commit's clean fingerprint, so `run_tests.py --summary` at the pushed commit stays `missing` and the evidence AC is unmet (excluding project-declared expected-dirty paths; none declared here).

**Recommended:** B — the main checkout is clean here, so a clean-tree precondition is not a routine blocker.

Note: the effort/risk estimate is deliberately not run yet — the skill gates on `intake_complete`, and the AC wording depends on these answers.

All commands were run against the **real** clone (`.githooks/pre-push` v4), not the
hermetic sandbox.

From the main checkout (`HEAD=2aafe4d9`, clean), pushing a sha that is **not** the
checked-out `HEAD`:

```
$ stale=$(git rev-parse HEAD^)
$ printf 'refs/heads/wl-x %s refs/heads/dev %s

ERROR: pre-push gate refuses this push: the tree it would measure is not the pushed commit.
  pushed commit  (refs/heads/dev): ec5d96a913ab8056d677bb060117ae654c2e3d5a

exit=1   (returned in <1 s — the runner was never invoked)
```

Both shas, the gate tree and the recovery step are named; the command returns
immediately, so no suite ran. ✔

Dirty-tree refusal (same hook, matching sha, uncommitted paths) was exercised during
the guard child's development and is covered by
`tests/test_git_hooks.py::test_dirty_tree_at_matching_sha_is_refused`.

### AC1 — a green `dev` push still leaves full-suite evidence at the pushed commit

Both pushes this epic made are backed by a **full-scope, exit-0** cache entry keyed to
the pushed commit's clean git state (`test_cache.compute_git_state()` = `HEAD` + dirty
content; a clean tree at commit X always yields the same key):

| pushed commit | what it is | cache entry (`scope`/`exit`) |
|---|---|---|
| `903497fb` | LP-0MVU94IPT009SICZ regression tests (pushed from its worktree) | `full` / `0` — `.worklog/cache/539485692ef040eca5c1dae87ba4b986` |
| `47bed454` | LP-0MVU94RN9006Z28Y docs (pushed through the **guarded** gate) | `full` / `0` — `.worklog/cache/07da0e64ddcb0592d10dbfe305841400` |
| `ec5d96a9` | next `dev` push (other session, guarded) | `full` / `0` — `.worklog/cache/d24a2c4a292a1d7dcf5cd10255b1e7b1` |
| `50167e00` | the guard's own landing push (**bootstrap**, see below) | none |

`run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` resolves the git state from the checkout it
runs in, so the positive case is captured from a clean checkout at the pushed commit
(throwaway detached worktree at `47bed454`, reading the main checkout's cache):

```
$ git -C /home/rgardler/projects/llm worktree add --detach /tmp/verify-47bed454 47bed454
$ cd /tmp/verify-47bed454 && git status --porcelain | wc -l     # clean
0
$ python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json --project-root /tmp/verify-47bed454
{

}
```

pushed commit exists and is reportable. ✔

keyed to their own git state; the three without are commits that were rewritten by a
concurrent rebase (never itself pushed) or the bootstrap push below. The mechanism is
not narrowed by the guard.

- Routine green path unaffected: `47bed454` was pushed **through the guard** (the main
  checkout had been fast-forwarded to it and was clean, so the gate ran the full suite

Implementation matches the expected behaviour: refusal is fast, loud and actionable;
a green `dev` push still produces evidence keyed to the pushed commit; the only gap is

Implementation notes (deferral 429 on queue budget expiry):
- Converted the contention-queue exits in `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (`_cq_action == "fallback"`, direct local gate) and the lease-queue exit (`_lease_action == "fallback"`) into an exit-time refusal via the new `_build_deferral_refusal_response()`, which defers to `_local_preference_pins_local()` (no new preference logic) and to the one builder `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (no new payload). The loop-head lease-active remote walk is now guarded for a pin-local deferrable request, so it never runs.
- Timing: the queue exit records the queue's *measured remainder* (`_contention_queue_remaining_seconds(config, elapsed)`: full window for the never-enqueued depth cap, 1 s floor once the budget is spent) and feeds it to `_refusal_retry_timing` through `advertised_retry_after`; the lease exit keeps the lease remainder. Both are recorded through `_note_local_fallback_reason()`, so header and body agree on `fallback_after_queue` / `local_lease_active`.
- Refusal is returned before the next candidate is resolved, so no remote dispatch, no attempt/cooldown/usage-limit state and no lease is written; a remote-less (private) chain now gets the retryable 429 instead of 'All providers exhausted'.
- prefer-local / remote-ok / absent-header behaviour is byte-identical (predicate false, caller's original `continue` unchanged).
- Tests: queue rows pinned in `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (explicit retryable/Retry-After/retry_at/verdict/timing fields, no double stamp, plus a remote-less chain case) and `test_local_admission_guard.py` (enqueue-once, depth restored, no lease/grant leak, single stamp, refusal before remote resolution).

## Implementation notes (pre-commit)

### Wiring

- `_build_local_only_refusal_response(attempt, config=None, preference=None)` computes the classification **once** via `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(reason=..., new_tokens=..., budget_tokens=...)` (lazy import, module convention) and uses that single `CapacityVerdict` for **both** `payload["verdict"]` and the log line (D1/D2/D3).
- `_log_local_only_refusal(reason, preference=None, verdict=None)` appends `verdict=%s` **only** when supplied; the free-slot/exhausted caller keeps its byte-identical two-key line (D5, boundary respected).
- Preference threaded from the choke point `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote` and both `refused_local_only` branches (queue + lease) (D6). Direct callers default to `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY`.
- No timing, queue, lease, header or promotion change; `_build_exhausted_response` / `_build_local_admission_reject_response` untouched.

### xfail flip (AC7)

Removed the verdict xfail markers in `test_admission_reserve.py` (4), `test_local_admission_guard.py` (6) and `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (1) in the same change that adds the behaviour.

### Three defects in the test children surfaced by the flip (fixed here, documented)

1. `test_incident_refusal_body_carries_the_deferrable_verdict` asserted `body["retry_at"] == expected.retry_at` — `retry_at` is stamped from `now`, so a recomputed expectation is never string-equal. It now compares the parsed instants within 2 s (the value is still recomputed from `_refusal_retry_timing`, not re-specified).
2. `test_choke_point_refusal_logs_one_verdict_line` priced the *incident* prompt (31 246 new tokens vs a 25 000 cap) while asserting `deferrable`; with token evidence over the cap the shared helper correctly returns `too_large`. The cooldown fixture now prices a within-budget prompt so the cooldown is the only blocking signal (the helper stays the single classifier — no second rule in `provider.py`).
3. `test_refused_local_only_branch_routes_through_the_helper_once` drove the **free-slot** path (concurrency (0,1)), which returns the out-of-scope exhausted payload, so the spy recorded zero calls. It now drives busy slots (1,1) + queue policy → the actual `refused_local_only` queue branch its docstring names.

### Discovered gap → LP-0MVSS435600370D6

The matrix row `admission_guard_free_slot` takes the direct free-slot branch that returns `_build_local_admission_reject_response` (explicitly out of this slice's boundary), so its 429 has no `verdict`. The row still declares `expected_verdict=deferrable` but its verdict assertion is skipped (`_VERDICT_NOT_APPLICABLE`, documented in the test) and the follow-up **LP-0MVSS435600370D6** owns wiring that payload. 11/12 rows assert the verdict green today.

### Preference drift re-pinned

The logged `preference=` is now the **parsed** value, so a legacy `local-only` header logs `preference=local-preferred` (the alias child LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 landed). Re-pinned the two refusal expectations in `test_routing_preference_logging.py` and documented the change in `proxy/docs/routing.md` (line format, body `verdict` field, out-of-scope note).

data.comment: Evidence from LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL (2026-10-28), relevant to this item: `gpu_busy_percent` is **not** pinned from boot on kernel 7.0.0-34 — it responds to load within seconds (0 % idle → 55 → 83 → 99 % during decode, decaying afterwards) — but it **saturates at ~20 W**: over 7 days of Prometheus history it reads ≥ 90 % in 93.8 % of samples against 28.1 % at compute power (≥ 90 W), i.e. 45 % false-busy, longest continuous saturated run 5.3 h (mean busy 98.9 % in the 20–40 W band, 2.3 % in the 0–20 W band; Pearson r = 0.28). So it behaves as a bang-bang 'GPU powered' indicator, not a graded utilisation measure. That makes a real GFX-activity accumulator (`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`, v3.0, live on this host) the remaining credible route to a true utilisation figure — the reason this item exists. Also note `amdtop` (zyoung11/amdtop, linux.go:151) renders exactly this counter, so it inherits the same defect.

data.comment:
Implementation complete (pre-commit summary) — session 01a19190-b683-7259-9e27-f64fd652ecb7

**Shipped values:** `proxy/config.yaml` now declares
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30` and `contention_queue_max_depth: 2`.
The surrounding comment block records:
- the 60 s-era evidence (3.3 h window 2026-10-22: 180 queue events, 38 wins /
  142 losses, all losses at the full 60 s, 8 705 s dead wait; retained wins by
  budget 20 s → 24 %, 30 s → 34 %, 45 s → 60 %);
- the ≥ 24 h pre-flip baseline required by the parent's AC1 trigger, with the
  measured numbers from `docs/dev/contention-queue-sweep-baseline-2026-10-31.json`
  (24 h window 2026-10-30 05:00 → 2026-10-31 05:00: 351 queue events, 214 wins
  (61 %) / 137 losses (39 %), 8 222 s loss wait = 342.6 s/h, 124 wins (57.9 %)
  at/below 30 s, 73 of 137 losses `reason=local_lease_active`);
- the 7-day / ≥ 1 000 queue-event observation window and the three flip
  criteria (dead wait/h −≥ 50 %, residual win share ≥ 20 %, remote volume
  < +20 % relative);
- the two-line rollback (60 / 8) plus proxy restart.

**Single budget (AC2).** No new knob and no second constant: the guard and
`POST /llama/local/reserve` both price against
`prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds` → `_get_contention_queue_config`. Code-level
defaults for an absent key (router `wait 60` / `depth 4`) are kept and
documented as the inert no-config fallback (an absent
`contention_queue_policy` resolves to `fallback`, so nothing queues).
`router.py`, `prefill_eta.py` and `admission_reserve.py` comments now state
that contract; `prefill_eta.py`'s module docstring and the startup ordering
note say 30 s.

**Tests (AC4).** Updated `test_{cheap,fast}_config_declares_queue_policy`
(30 / 2) and added, all reading the shipped config through the real resolver:
- `test_shipped_sweep_reaches_one_resolver_and_both_caps` — depth 2 passes the
  [1, 16] clamp unchanged; `wait_budget_seconds(merged, "medium"/"low") == 30.0`,
  `"high" == 0.0`;
- `test_shipped_sweep_caps_reach_the_provider_queue_wait` — provider hands
  `(30.0, 2)` to the queue wait end to end;
- `test_swept_depth_two_third_waiter_falls_back_without_enqueueing` — two
  parked waiters, the third returns immediately, depth stays 2;
- `test_swept_budget_expires_at_thirty_seconds` — fake clock/wait primitive
  asserts the wait is bounded by 30.0 s (no real sleep);
- `test_shipped_swept_budget_drives_the_guard_refusal_payload` — the 429 body
  and `X-Local-Admission-Budget` both report 30.0;
- `test_reserve_prices_against_the_shipped_swept_budget` — 12k-token request
  refused at 30 s, admitted under a 60 s control;
- `test_status_publishes_the_shipped_swept_budget` — `/llama/local/status`
  publishes `prefill_budget_seconds == 30.0`.

Ruff clean; the touched suites pass (contention queue, admission guard,
reservation, llama-local status, prefill budget config).

**Discovered, not fixed here (LP-0MVWADQ06004GLV7):**
`contention_queue_eta_promotion_seconds` is 30 — equal to the new wait budget —
so the ETA-ordering starvation promotion can no longer fire before expiry.
Changing it would be a behavioural change beyond the two swept values (AC7),
so it is recorded separately and noted in the config comment.

**Not in this item:** docs (`proxy/docs/routing.md`, `README.md`) are the
blocked docs child LP-0MVT114HU009UNML; deployment/restart happens in the
observation child after a quiet-window restart, not here.
