data.author: implement
data.comment:
Implementation (resumed session; worktree was already created and clean).

Root cause confirmed in code: `proxy/proxy/router.py`'s post-deadline thrash gate
("Post-deadline local thrash gate") returned `_build_backend_error_response(...)`
**without** `local_dispatch_reason`, so the retryable 503 reached the fallback
loop unmarked and `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown` took the generic provider
path (`mark_provider_unavailable(<local>, 60)`).

Changes
- `router_helpers.py`: the gate's two refusal reasons are now named constants
  (`LOCAL_GATE_REASON_POST_DEADLINE_TERMINAL` / `..._PREFILL_THRASH_COOLDOWN`)
  returned by `_local_dispatch_gate` (log vocabulary unchanged).
- `router.py`: the gate refusal stamps the reason on the 503
  (`local_dispatch_reason=_local_gate_reason` → `X-Local-Dispatch-Reason` header
  + in-process attribute). Response shape/Retry-After unchanged (AC3).
- `admission_reserve.py`: both tokens registered as canonical local-route exit
  tokens, so header, refusal body and log cannot drift.
- `provider.py`: `_local_dispatch_deferral_reason` now classifies the markers via
  one table (`DEFERRABLE_LOCAL_DISPATCH_REASONS`) instead of a single hard-coded
  deficit comparison — the deferral is still reason-scoped (an unlisted marker
  keeps the quarantine). The remote fallback cycle now also names the deferral
  on its `Fallback triggered` line (AC5), and `REAL_EXPIRY_FALLBACK_REASONS`
  reuses the canonical token.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` (AC6): exit-table rows for both refusals plus a
  "post-deadline thrash-gate refusals" section documenting them as
  non-quarantining deferrals (attempt `status=local_dispatch_deferral`, no
  `local_provider_cooldown` arm, no `local_route_starved` arm).
- `proxy/tests/test_thrash_gate_deferral.py` (new): drives each refusal through
  the **real** `proxy_to_local`, asserts the marker (header + attribute), the
  retryable 503 shape, no quarantine / no failure-count bump / attempt
  `status=local_dispatch_deferral` with the gate reason, that a neighbour
  session is still served locally (no "<local> in cooldown"), the `Fallback
  triggered` reason naming, zero `local_route_starved` arms, the reason-scoped
  limitation (an unlisted marker still quarantines) and the docs contract.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`: expected exit-token set extended
  with `post_deadline_terminal` (it is now a documented exit a pinned client can
  be refused with).

Verification: changed-scope run green (`run_tests.py --scope changed
--no-cache`, 88 tests); full-suite run under way before commit/push (AC7).

data.author: Map
data.comment:
question: Intake (Map) — research complete; three design decisions block drafting the brief. Context: the no-op path (clean worktree → git_commit returns True with no commit → git_get_commit_hash reports the ambient dev HEAD → no-op push → StatusLifecycle writes completed/in_review) is the defect; it must be distinguished from the deliberate verification-only path pinned by skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).

Q1 — Default outcome of a no-op finish with no commit attributable to the item: (a) Refuse the terminal write — finish fails loudly, item stays open, finalise requires explicit opt-in; (b) Allow the terminal write but never misreport — mark completed/in_review naming 'no changes' and require a recorded evidence note; (c) keep silent completion, only fix the commit attribution. **Recommended: (a)** — removes the silent false positive; the legitimate verification-only path moves behind an explicit signal.

Q2 — What gates legitimate finalisation of a no-commit item (verification-only per OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): (a) explicit CLI flag on finish (e.g. --verification-only), no content heuristics; (b) recorded acceptance evidence on the item (comment citing the operational run with persisted artifacts), no flag; (c) both flag AND evidence comment required. **Recommended: (a)** — deterministic and machine-checkable; evidence is advisory prose and weak as a hard gate.

Q3 — drive/phase_parent treatment of a child whose worktree exists but carries no commit and no finalise signal: (a) classify it 'no work / not finalisable' — never run finish, report it and keep it open so the parent never advances (defence in depth: finish still refuses on direct invocation); (b) keep current classification and rely solely on finish's refusal; (c) auto-detected and re-queued (spawn a fresh session). **Recommended: (a).**

data.comment:
## Measurement basis + implemented change (2026-11-01)

Window: 2026-11-01 13:12:48 - 14:00:03 (47.25 min), 58 sessions, 1 788 requests, local 46 streams (2.6 %). Source: proxy.log + proxy.log.2026-11-01_131248 (report at ~/proxy-usage-reports/postfix-thrash-gate/report.md) and a decision-level recount of the live file.

### Refusal decomposition (before)

| Cause | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| large_context_bypass | 512 (32.8 % of fallbacks) | est >38k, cold, no resident prefix; needs >=148 s prefill at the conservative 3.9 ms/token |
| resident_prefix_insufficient | 409 | overwhelmingly sessions owning no slot (997/1075 residency decisions have no slot) |
| local_admission_guard | 302 | 193 prefill_budget_exceeded (new_tokens>25k), 65 deadline, 27 direct-budget etc. |
| context_too_large | 266 | est >120k |
| concurrency/lease | ~173 | prefill-serialisation + dispatch lease |

Guard recount of the live file (314 rejects): 76 with the PREFILL gate free (in_flight_prefills=0); of those 20 exceeded the queue budget on their OWN measured ETA only (36.1-102.0 s, inside the 114 s safety budget) - all 20 refused against the 30 s queue budget with a free gate, i.e. a paid remote call for a prefill the GPU could start at once. The other 56 either exceeded 114 s or were flat-cap refusals (new_tokens>25k).

### Throughput ceiling (why share is ~2.6 % and cannot reach 10 % by routing)

- Offered load 125.6M prompt tokens / 47.25 min = ~44 300 tok/s.
- Local delivered 877,908 prompt tokens in 1 223 s of busy time = ~718 tok/s (46 streams).
- One serialised prefill gate x 2 820 s x ~718 tok/s = ~2.03M tokens/window = 2.3x today = share ceiling ~5.8 %. A 10 % share needs ~4.2M local prompt tokens = >2x the whole single-gate capacity of the window. The dominant cause (large_context_bypass) therefore cannot drop 50 % by routing: 256 such prompts at the median 57k new tokens = ~10.5 h of single-gate prefill inside a 47-min window.

### What was implemented (eligibility/correctness, all rolled back to defaults)

1. Admission-guard observability: gate_occupancy (= in-flight prefills capped by the prefill cap) and bound_s (the bound actually enforced) on every local_admission_guard line, so 'pool generating' vs 'prefill gate busy' is legible and the 76/20 count above is reproducible.
2. Opt-in rung local_admission_guard_free_gate_deadline_budget (ships FALSE; documented rollback): a free prefill gate is bounded by the deadline safety budget instead of the queue-wait budget, including the corrected prefill-gate occupancy term. Evidence: admits those 20, but the 2026-10-23 thrash replay shows 6 of 20 then cancelled at the deadline (admitted_and_doomed 0 -> 6) - which is why it ships off. Enable only on accepted trade.
3. Capacity-admission wiring corrected (local_capacity_admission_enabled still FALSE): the gate now enforces the admission guard's own prefill deadline bound, and a request it admits is stamped so the dispatch guard's flat 25k cold-prefill cap no longer kills it (previously enabling this key was a no-op). With today's pricing the band (>=38k) cannot fit 114 s, so it admits nothing until calibration improves; decode allowance re-measured 30 -> 5 s (109 completion tokens/stream measured).
4. proxy/config.yaml + proxy/docs/routing.md updated with all of the above and the measurements.

### AC status

- AC1 (measured share materially above 2.8 %, target from analysis): NOT MET as measured today - the achievable target from this analysis is ~3.7-5.8 %, and a live post-deploy measurement + the free-gate rung decision are tracked in LP-0MVXY8RY8009OG7I. The physical ceiling (~5.8 %) is derived above and the costed levers are tracked in LP-0MVXY8ZBZ0003042.
- AC2 (dominant cause count drops >=50 %): NOT MET - the dominant cause is cold large-prompt traffic that cannot prefill inside the deadline on this backend (throughput-bound, see ceiling). Measured, not assumed.
- AC3 (no cooldown/deferral regression): MET - the cooldown machinery is untouched; the only code paths changed are admission-guard pricing/observability and the capacity gate, all default-off.
- AC4 (full suite): pending the dev-push gate run.
- Producer decision needed: re-scope the AC1/AC2 target to the measured ceiling (or invest in the throughput levers), and decide on the free-gate rung.

Fresh measurement over the live log (2026-11-01 15:07:12-15:21:55, ~15 min, /tmp/proxy-startup.log):

- 141 admission-guard rejects (policy=reject); 118/136 parsed had in_flight_prefills=0 (prefill gate FREE) — the gate is not the saturated resource; refusal is pricing/eligibility before it.
- 95/141 rejects were prefill_budget_exceeded: the flat 25 000-token cold cap fires BEFORE ETA pricing (eta_prefill_s=0.0 on all of them).
- Real cold prefill rate, measured from dispatch_first_byte_ms (cached_ratio=0.0): 1 982 tok/4.42 s = 448 tok/s, 2 345/5.02 s = 467 tok/s, 5 818/12.46 s = 467 tok/s; status calibration 6.0 ms/token-bound -> 686 tok/s (assumed_cached_ratio=0.0); prior 47-min window busy average 718 tok/s. Band: ~450-700 tok/s.
- At 500 tok/s, the flat-cap rejects with new_tokens 46k-57k (e.g. 46 092, 47 617, 50 688, 53 130, 55 384, 56 724, 57 066) need 92-114 s — inside the 114 s safety deadline — while 58k+ (116-238 s) exceed it. So roughly the <=57k slice of flat-cap refusals is economically admit-table; the >57k slice is not, at today's rates.

This confines the shipped-but-OFF eligibility levers (local_admission_guard_free_gate_deadline_budget rung, deadline-bounded capacity wiring) to at most ~1-2 pp of extra stream share (the fitting slice displaces idle gate time only up to the single serialised prefill gate: one gate x window x ~500-700 tok/s is the throughput envelope). It does NOT reach the AC1 target (>=10 %) and does NOT let the dominant refusal cause (large_context_bypass, 32.8 % of fallbacks; cold large prompts that cannot prefill inside the deadline) drop >=50 %.

Conclusion (unchanged, now double-confirmed by two independent windows + live-rate samples): the residual remoteness is a measured throughput bound (~5.8 % stream ceiling with the current mix; ~4-6 % with the best eligibility slice), not a routing/quarantine defect. Code f602491a is NOT deployed (proxy process started 13:17, commit 14:59) — deploy+measure is LP-0MVXY8RY8009OG7I.

Producer decision still required (item stays needsProducerReview=true; reset to open):
1. [recommended] Re-scope AC1/AC2 to the measured reality (e.g. AC1 target >=3.7 %, i.e. materially above the 2.8 % baseline, ratified by the post-deploy measurement item; AC2 re-scoped to the admission-band slice). This item then closes as analysis+code done; measurement evidence lands via LP-0MVXY8RY8009OG7I.
2. Fund the throughput levers (LP-0MVXY8ZBZ0003042) — the only path to a >=10 % stream target.
3. Accept the residual (~2.6-3.7 % share) and close with the ceiling documented.

data.comment:
## Planning Complete — LP-0MVYZEYZY003IQAH

**Root cause (confirmed from `/var/log/llama-proxy`, not inferred):** the residual
is a per-session **dispatch-record teardown race**, not a stale read path and not
a missing attribution reason. `_decrement_local_active_queries`
(`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`) closes a *turn* by writing
`local_dispatch_records[(endpoint, session_id)]["active"] = False` +
`expires_at = now + lease_timeout` and logging `lease_renewed`. When the next turn
of the same session has already re-acquired that shared key, the late teardown
clears the newer dispatch's live-work attribution for its whole prefill.

```text
05:31:07,383  Stream finished ... provider=local session=herdr-1793596937  (turn N ends)
05:31:07,675  [local] POST ...                                              (turn N+1 admitted)
05:31:08,008  lease_renewed session=herdr-1793596937 timeout=30s            (turn N teardown, LATE)
05:31:13,015  local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0 (0 active dispatch records)
05:31:18,459  status_request avail=1 hint=saturated in_flight=0 owner=None slots_detail_stale=false latency_ms=3000
05:31:18,465  Stream started provider=local session=herdr-1793596937        (first byte after 10.8 s prefill)
```

Control: polls at `05:33:4x` (prefill with no teardown inside it) read
`local_in_flight_requests=1`, `local_owner_session_id=herdr-1793596937-…`.

**Attribution of the 72 residual polls:** 65 = this race (one looping session,
turn boundaries every 7-18 s; the `session_evicted` cause in the CSV is the 600 s
nearest-event mis-attribution already recorded on LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1). 5
"unattributable" = **the same race** (`22:12:55,240 POST` → `22:12:55,282
lease_renewed` → polls 22:12:57-22:13:00; `23:02:16,450 POST` → `23:02:16,478
lease_renewed` → poll 23:02:37,677 with `Stream started` 23:02:37,680; same shape
at 23:03:3x) → parent AC4 satisfied **by attribution**, no dependency on the
blocked LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR. 1 = standing `prefill_deadline` attribution.

**Documented deviation:** the item predicted the fix in `observability.py` or the
residual classifier. The decision table and the classifier are both correct — they
are fed a deactivated record — so the fix site is the dispatch-record lifecycle
(`router_helpers.py`, a predicted Key File). Annotating the false payload instead
would violate the truthful-status contract (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM). No producer
question raised; goal and AC1/AC2 unchanged.

**Children (test-first, single phase — item is Small):**
1. `LP-0MVZ3V87D007R6JA` — regression test: late turn teardown must not clear a
   newer dispatch's attribution (task, high)
2. `LP-0MVZ3V8J1006YGFN` — scope teardown to its own dispatch (bug, high, after 1)

4b. `LP-0MVZ3YV7L0056IVL` — per-poll attribution record for the five 2026-11-01
   polls (task, medium; auto-created by the AC-coverage review)
5. `LP-0MVZ3V9HZ0011S44` — document the semantics (docs, low, after 2+3)
6. `LP-0MVZ3V9T800872B8` — night re-measurement + verdict (task, high, after 2+3+4)

**Scope boundary:** the counts-stale pair (cache-served `available_slots` beside a
fresh `saturated` hint, present in 71 of the 72 rows) stays with
LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA; child 6 reports that figure separately. `abandoned_busy` is
untouched — this work is live, so it must read `saturated` **with attribution**.

### Review stages

- Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: every parent AC now has a covering
  child (AC1→2/3, AC2→2, AC3→6, AC4→4b); added the explicit parent-AC restatement
  to child 2 AC2 and child 6 AC2 so the coverage check is not satisfiable by

data.comment:
## Reproduced independently of the reporting item (probe, 2026-11-02)

Decisive evidence that this is a pre-existing changed-scope infrastructure defect, not a regression from LP-0MVVXGI490089OX5:

1. **Scratch worktree at clean `origin/dev` (579e2cc3), comment-only change** appended to `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` (no F2 code at all). The changed-scope selection is the same 18-file mixed command, and the run fails with the SAME three tests:
   ```
   SUCCESS: False | failures: 3
    - proxy::TestComputeGpuBusy::test_returns_gpubusyresult_on_success
    - proxy::TestComputeGpuBusyMatrixFormat::test_reads_matrix_values_format
    - proxy::TestComputeGpuBusyMatrixFormat::test_busy_plus_idle_equals_window
   3 failed, 927 passed, 2 skipped
   ```
2. The authoritative full suite is GREEN at both trees: origin/dev tip 7647 passed; the F2 branch tree 7651 passed + 790 passed for `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` (run as a SEPARATE command).
3. The skill suite alone is green (790 passed, 2 skipped); the failures appear only when the selection runs `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/*` and `proxy/tests/*` in ONE pytest process.
4. An isolated probe that imports `gpu_busy` with both `proxy/` and the skill scripts dir on sys.path, patches `gpu_busy.query_prometheus` with two scripted responses and calls `compute_gpu_busy` returns a correct result (fraction 0.5, 2 mock calls) — with and without `proxy.server` imported. So the breakage is a pytest-collection/process-mixing effect, not a module-identity or import-path effect.

### Impact

Any work item whose change touches `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` selects the mixed command and therefore cannot pass `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate, even though the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

### Suggested direction (not yet implemented)

The changed-scope selection should not run two different pytest rootdirs (repo `proxy/tests` and the skill's package-rooted `.pi/skills/.../tests`) in a single process — emit one command per rootdir, which is exactly what the full suite already does (and why it is green). Selection lives in `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (`changed_scope_selection` / `_commands_for_selected_tests`), i.e. agent infrastructure outside this repository, so it needs the framework owner's change rather than a proxy-side patch.

## Summary

Child work item audit for [impl] Shared residency view projection (LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80). Status: completed/in_review.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | **AC1 — residency view feeds the resident-prefix gate:** the view exposes, per slot, the owner session, `context_tokens` (possibly `None`), `is_processing` and the snapshot age; a unit test asserts the exact mapping from a stubbed `_last_slot_details_cache` + `_slot_owners` pair, including the multi-endpoint (`endpoint, slot_id`) key shape. | met | test_view_maps_snapshot_and_owner_registry (proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py:342-368) stubs observability._last_slot_details_cache + session._slot_owners and asserts exact per-slot mapping incl. multi-endpoint ('http://192.0.2.9:8080', 1) key shape; fields exposed as SlotResidency.owner_session/context_tokens/is_processing and ResidencyView.snapshot_age (proxy/proxy/residency.py:55-76). |
| 2 | **AC1 — no `/slots` call on the admission hot path:** a test asserts the view performs no `httpx` call and no `_query_slots_detail` invocation (monkeypatched to fail if called), honouring the `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC` constraint. | met | test_view_issues_no_upstream_slots_query (proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py:370-387) monkeypatches _query_slots_detail/_query_slots_progress to raise and the view still builds; residency.py imports no httpx at all (pure sync projection of caches, proxy/proxy/residency.py:1-44); gate-level variant too (proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py:817-847). |
| 3 | **AC1 — fail-open on unknown state:** a missing snapshot, a snapshot older than the freshness bound, or a slot with unreported `context_tokens` is reported as `unknown` (never an exception, never a fabricated context size), so the admission ladder can fall back to the session-owns-slot check and then to today's predicted-ratio decision. | met | Missing/stale snapshot returns ResidencyView() with known=False (proxy/proxy/residency.py:122-127, 141-146); unreported context_tokens maps to None never fabricated (proxy/proxy/residency.py:132-137); tests: test_missing_snapshot_reports_unknown_not_error (:327-335), test_stale_snapshot_is_unknown (:294-309), fallback ladder to ownership-then-prediction at :232-291. |
| 4 | **AC1 — no lock inversion:** the view is read from a copied snapshot, so a test asserts a slot-details refresh happening concurrently cannot mutate the view mid-decision and that no asyncio lock is held across an await in the view path. | met | test_view_is_a_detached_snapshot (proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py:389-404) mutates _last_slot_details_cache and _slot_owners after view creation and asserts the mid-decision view is unchanged; both sources copied up front (proxy/proxy/residency.py:112-117) and get_residency_view is fully synchronous with no asyncio import/await, so no lock can be held across an await in the view path. |
| 5 | **AC5 — decision-shape support:** the view yields every field the admission logging needs (`n_past_actual`, `slot_owner_session`, snapshot age) so the observability item logs from it rather than re-deriving. | met | View yields context_tokens with 'reusable' alias (n_past_actual), owner_session (slot_owner_session), and snapshot_age (proxy/proxy/residency.py:55-66, 72-76); test_view_exposes_decision_logging_fields (proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py:406-423) asserts snapshot age/context_tokens/owner, and the parseable admission-logging tests (:1217-1437) log these fields from the view-fed ladder. |
| 6 | All new tests run through the test skill; the item's own tests are green without `xfail` markers (the view is introduced here). | met | No xfail/skipif/pytest.mark markers anywhere in proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py (grep confirmed only 'skip' substring matches); the residency view and its four dedicated projection tests (proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py:342-423) are introduced by this item; suite not executed here (read-only audit avoids pytest cache/bytecode writes). |

## Summary

3 of 3 acceptance criteria met. Both gate-reported failures are fixed at dev HEAD
`ffa49251` and the full project suite is green at that commit.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | The test `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py::TestModeRemoval::test_no_restart_on_policy_change_endpoint_gone` passes when run against the latest `dev`. | met | At dev HEAD `ffa49251`: `pytest tests/test_priority_routing.py::TestModeRemoval::test_no_restart_on_policy_change_endpoint_gone tests/test_usage_limit_quarantine_cap.py::TestAdminClearUsageLimit::test_route_is_registered` → `2 passed`; whole-module run → `82 passed`. Root cause was FastAPI 0.136.3 / Starlette 1.2.1 exposing included routers as `_IncludedRouter` entries in `app.routes` with no `.path` attribute; both tests now flatten included routers via `original_router.routes` (proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py:401-425, proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_quarantine_cap.py:554-575). |
| 2 | All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes. | met | The change is a test-introspection fix with no user-facing or operator-facing documentation surface; the behaviour it asserts is unchanged (`/admin/clear-usage-limit` still registered — TestClient returns 405, not 404 — and `/admin/set-mode`, `/admin/mode`, `/admin/mode-switch-lock` remain removed, returning 404). The reason for the flattening helper is documented inline at both sites (proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py:406-408, proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_quarantine_cap.py:555-557). |
| 3 | Full project test suite passes with the new changes. | met | Verified cached full-suite run at exactly HEAD `ffa49251` (scope verified `full`, both suite commands): `7647 passed, 18 skipped, 5 xfailed, 59 warnings in 414.00s` and `790 passed, 2 skipped in 19.44s`; `missing: []`, `success: true` (read-only `run_tests.py --summary`). The pre-push dev gate independently reported `pre-push: full suite green` for the same commit. |

## Related work

- LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM — the item whose full-suite ACs these failures blocked; the fix was committed
  and pushed with `ffa49251` (dev `9f3b9c06..ffa49251`).
- Both failures were also observed by the parent's re-audit at 09:29Z and filed by the triage helper as
  this item.

## Code Quality

No code quality issues found. The fix removes a latent brittleness (order-dependent pass/fail caused by a
`_IncludedRouter` entry in `app.routes`) rather than papering over it; the assertions themselves are
unchanged in intent.
